chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Annual Rates & Limits
chunks.content:
Administrator Settings | Annual Rates & Limits
The Annual Rates & Limits page displays various regulatory rates and limits in a centralized location for informational and reference usage.
Table of Contents
IRS Contribution Limits
Health Savings Account
PCOR Fees
The page includes informational tables of IRS-published annual limits and PCOR fee rates, with breakdowns by-year. This information is published by DataPath and updated in accordance with IRS guidelines. The information displayed on this page is read-only.
IRS Contribution Limits
The IRS Contribution Limits section features collapsible tables of the IRS-published limits for benefits.
Health Savings Account
The Health Savings Account subsection of IRS Contribution Limits contains a table displaying a history for HSA Contribution Limits.
The table contains the following information:
Effective Date –This is the effective date of the rates displayed in the table’s row. The effective date for HSA Contribution Limits is the first day of the calendar year (eg, 01/01/2022, 01/01/2023/, 01/01/2024, etc.).
Single – This column displays the HSA contribution limits for account owners with individual HDHP coverage. Contributions made by individuals with Single coverage above the posted rate for the calendar year would be deemed excess contribution and possibly be subject to penalties and excise tax.
Family – This column displays the HSA contribution limits for account owners with Family HDHP coverage (EE+SP, EE+SP+Ch, EE+Ch, Fam, etc.). Contributions made by individuals with Family coverage above the posted rate for the calendar year would be deemed excess contribution and possibly subject to penalties and excise tax.

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Annual Rates & Limits
chunks.content:
55+ Catch Up – This column displays the maximum allowable HSA catchup contribution amount for eligible individuals 55 and older. Contributions made above the combined applicable Single/Family rate and the allowable catchup rate for the calendar year would be deemed excess contribution and possibly subject to penalties and excise tax.
Note that the limits published and displayed in this table are informational only and will not impact participant elections in the Summit.
PCOR Fees
This collapsible section features a table of the Annual Patient Centered Outcome Research (PCOR) Fees.
PCOR Fee Rate  – This displays a list of PCOR Fee Rates
After – This is the date on which the PCOR Fee Rate corresponds to; eg. if the “After” value is 9/30/2023, then the accompanying $3.22 PCOR Fee Rate applies after that date.
This information is read-only.
PCOR Fees are assessed for IRS-indicated plans, including Medicare, Group Health, and Self-Funded plans. The current year’s fee rate will apply when assessing fees via the Patient Centered Outcome Research Fees Report.
For further information, please refer to the Administrator Settings section in FAQs.

chunks.title: PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
chunks.content:
PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
This page outlines the best practices for:
Remitting and managing ACH and credit/debit card premium payments
Preventing chargebacks and returns
Managing chargebacks and returns
Table of Contents
ACH and Credit/Debit Card Management and Remittance
DataPath ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Policy
1. Overview
2. ACH Payment Returns
3. Credit/Debit Card Chargebacks
4. Your Responsibility as a TPA
5. Timing of Fund Movements
6. Communication Process
7. Compliance and Limitations
8. DataPath ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Policy Summary
Managing Credit/Debit Card Chargebacks
Change Chargeback Receipt Status to NSF
Create a Chargeback Receipt Custom Notice
Managing ACH Returns
Remittance Offsets
ACH and Credit/Debit Card Management and Remittance
The flexibility of Summit Premium Billing allows participants to make ACH and credit/debit cards via the Participant Portal and mobile app. The following are suggested best practices for managing ACH and card payment remittances and communications.
Remit to Entity – Remit premium payments directly to the employer, instead of the carrier. The employer will be responsible for remitting coverage premiums to the carrier, and in the event of a premium return or chargeback, it will be the employer’s responsibility to recover the returned or charged back premium amount from the carrier.
 *Note: TPAs should consult with their legal counsel to determine whether this remittance structure is included in the TPA/employer service agreement and complies with their policies and procedures, and state law.)
Remittance Scheduling – If premium payments are remitted less frequently than a monthly basis, TPAs should consider reducing the remittance frequency to allow more time to address and manage any disputes before the next remittance is sent to the receiving entity.

chunks.title: PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
chunks.content:
Employer and Carrier Communications – Provide clear communication to the remittance receiving entity (employer or carrier) which states that premium ACH returns and chargebacks returns will be offset from future remittances. Include internal applicable return and chargeback policies and practices as appropriate.
Participant Communications – Modify the coupon book cover letter to request that the participant contact the TPA prior to submitting a premium payment credit/debit card dispute with the financial institution. This will allow time for the TPA to address billing or payment disputes.Include the TPA contact information in the coupon cover letter. 
Similarly, modify the ACH Notification to request that the participant contact the TPA prior to submitting a premium payment ACH return with the financial institution.
Be sure to include TPA contact information in these participant communications.
DataPath ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Policy
1. Overview
Because DataPath partners with third-party financial institutions and payment processors, DataPath must follow their rules and federal regulations. DataPath cannot contest or stop returns or chargebacks once they are initiated.
The following explains what happens when payments are reversed and what responsibilities Third Party Administrators (TPAs) hold in those situations.
2. ACH Payment Returns
ACH (bank account) payments made through the DataPath platform are processed under the National Automated Clearing House Association (NACHA) rules. DataPath acts as a Third-Party Sender, while our clients (TPAs) are considered nested third parties.
If an ACH payment is returned by the participant’s bank for any reason (e.g., insufficient funds, account closed), DataPath:
Cannot dispute the return,
Will debit the TPA for the returned amount, and
Will notify the TPA with participant details and the reason for the return.
Why this happens:

chunks.title: PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
chunks.content:
ACH return rights belong to the participant and their bank. Once a return is issued, it is final. Because DataPath has already forwarded the funds to the TPA, the return creates a negative balance that must be recovered.
3. Credit/Debit Card Chargebacks
Payments made by credit or debit card are processed through ACI Speedpay, a trusted bill payment provider. These payments are subject to Speedpay’s terms of service, card network rules (Visa, MasterCard, etc.), and the Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA).
If a participant disputes a payment with their card issuer:
The dispute is processed directly between the cardholder and their bank.
Speedpay must accept all chargebacks and automatically deducts the funds from DataPath.
DataPath will then debit the corresponding TPA for the chargeback amount.
The TPA will be notified with the participant’s information, date, and amount.
Why this happens:
Under federal law, cardholders can dispute payments for up to 60 days. The full chargeback process may take up to 150 days to resolve. DataPath cannot intervene in or prevent this process.
4. Your Responsibility as a TPA
As a TPA, you are responsible for:
Working with employers or participants to recover any funds returned or charged back.
Ensuring your internal accounting reflects any reversals from DataPath.
Responding promptly to return/chargeback notifications sent by our Financial Operations team.
5. Timing of Fund Movements
Event Timing
Participant submits payment Day 0 (payment received)
Funds sent to TPA (or Carrier) Next business day
Payment is returned or charged back As determined by participant’s bank
Debit to TPA (for returned funds) Next business day after return
TPA notified Same or following business day
6. Communication Process
ACH Returns: Emailed with return code and participant details.
Chargebacks: Emailed individually upon report from Speedpay.
7. Compliance and Limitations
     This policy is based on:
NACHA Rules for ACH payments
Fair Credit Billing Act (FCBA) for credit card disputes

chunks.title: PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
chunks.content:
Card network guidelines for debit/credit card processing
ACI Speedpay Terms of Service
These frameworks strictly define what DataPath can and cannot do. DataPath facilitates the flow of funds and provides notifications. DataPath has no legal authority to contest or reverse disputes.
8. DataPath ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Policy Summary
As a TPA, you are a key partner in helping ensure premium payments are managed efficiently and correctly. While DataPath acts as the payment processor, we do not have authority to challenge returns or chargebacks. Your cooperation in recovering funds from participants or employers is essential.
For any questions or support, please contact your DataPath representative or our Financial Operations team at 501-296-9990 or FiOps@dpath.com.
Managing Credit/Debit Card Chargebacks
When ACI Speedpay notifies DataPath’s Financial Operations (FiOps) of a premium payment chargeback, FiOps sends the TPA an email with payment information. The TPA should communicate the chargeback information sent by FiOps to the remittance receiving entity (employer or carrier.) 
The TPA’s customer support should contact the participant to discuss the chargeback. If the participant claims that the chargeback was due to the amount paid being incorrect, be prepared to provide billing information to the participant and employer (or carrier) if the amount paid was correct.
If the chargeback cannot be resolved after contacting the participant, the TPA should request reimbursement from the receiving entity (employer or carrier) or inform the receiving entity of the intent to offset future remittances.
Figure 1 – Summit Premium Billing Return Card Chargeback Email
Change Chargeback Receipt Status to NSF

chunks.title: PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
chunks.content:
To send the participant an NSF notice for a payment chargeback, go to Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications and change the NSF Notice event to Approval Required before changing the receipt’s status to NSF to prevent the NSF notice from being automatically approved and to allow time to review the notice.
Select the chargeback premium payment on the Participant Central Receipts tab to open the Edit/Reassign user-interface. Change the receipt’s status to NSF. (Do not enter an NSF amount for a chargeback.)
The NSF status will unapply the charged back premium payment, and billing will be adjusted to reflect the unapplied payment.
*Note: For complete details for changing an event’s setting can be found in the Premium Billing User Guide. (https://summitguide.dpath.net/participant-participant-central-receipts/#htoc-edit-receipts)
Figure 2- NSF Notice Event Settings
Note: Unapplying the charged back receipt may result in one or more coverage terminations for failure to pay if the billing period amount is still outstanding after the billing period grace date. Triggered events can be viewed in Process Approvals.
Figure 3 – Participant Central Edit/Reassign Receipt UI
Figure 4 – Receipts Tab (Unapplied Receipt and Updated Receipt Status
Create a Chargeback Receipt Custom Notice
To send a custom chargeback notice to the participant instead of the NSF notice, a custom notice and event must be created. The custom event can be run on demand to mail and/or email the notice to the participant. The chargeback custom event can be added to a participant’s event history, to note that a chargeback has been made to a participant’s receipt.
Download and save a copy of the ACH Notification notice to a local drive.
Save the custom template as “Receipt Chargeback – Custom” or a title of choice.
Figure 5- Receipt Chargeback
Modify the custom notice to contain verbiage of your choice.

chunks.title: PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
chunks.content:
Note: DataPath recommends that you consult with your qualified benefits counsel before finalizing changes to the Receipt Chargeback Custom notice.
Note: Currently, the receipt’s information cannot be added to the custom notice.
Figure 6 – Receipt Chargeback Custom Notice
Upload the notice to Premium Billing Document Templates in Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications.
Figure 7 – Notifications & Communications Document Templates
Create a custom Receipt Chargeback – Custom event.
Figure 8  Receipt Chargeback Event
Select “Approval Required,” when adding the event to require the event’s approval.   This will allow time to review the notification before it is sent to fulfillment.
Select “Display in Participant History” to allow the participant to view the event in their participant’s events history on the Participant Portal and the mobile app.
Run the Receipt Chargeback -Custom event on Demand.
Figure 9 – On Demand Receipt Chargeback Event
Approve or decline the Receipt Chargeback event in Process Approvals.
Figure 10 – Process Approvals Receipt Chargeback Event
Managing ACH Returns
When a financial institution notifies DataPath’s Financial Operations of an ACH return, DataPath’s Financial Operations sends the TPA an email that includes the amount, return code, and the participant’s details.
Figure 11 – Summit Premium Billing Return (ACH) Email
An entry on the Pending Process Approval Alerts (alarm clock icon) alerts the TPA of auto-drafted ACH returns, and an automated process changes the receipt’s status to NSF, provided that the TPA has neither marked the item as “Resolved” in Process Approvals nor manually changed to receipt’s status to “NSF.”
The TPA should communicate the ACH return information that is sent by DataPath’s Financial Operations to the remittance receiving entity.

chunks.title: PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices
chunks.content:
The TPA’s customer support should contact the participant to discuss the return. If the participant claims an auto-drafted or payment amount was incorrect, be prepared to provide billing information to the participant and employer (or carrier) if the amount paid or auto-draft amount was correct.
If the ACH return cannot be resolved after contacting the participant, the TPA should request reimbursement from the receiving entity (employer or carrier) or inform the receiving entity of the intent to offset future remittances.
Figure 12 – ACH Returns
Remittance Offsets
If a receipt has been remitted prior to the return/chargeback, funds can be recouped from the remittance receiving entity (employer or carrier) by the TPA via remittance offset during a subsequent remittance process.
Figure 13 – Employer Remittance Offset

chunks.content:
Administrator Settings | Administrator Central | Bank Accounts
TPA banking details are recorded on the Bank Accounts tab of Administrator Central. These details are used for cash management purposes to track and facilitate the movement of money between Summit and TPAs’ operating accounts.
Table of Contents
Add a Bank Account
Edit a Bank Account
Terminate a Bank Account
 * Required fields appear in Red
To Access the Bank Accounts tab:
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Administrator Settings.
Click on the Administrator Central menu.
Figure 1. Navigation
Now open the Bank Accounts tab.
Figure 1. TPA Demographics – Bank Accounts Tab
TPA users can view all the associated Bank Accounts on this tab and print or export the list.
The “Refresh” link refreshes the list of accounts displaying on the tab if new filter criteria have been applied.
The “Excel” link exports the list of accounts as an Excel worksheet.
The “Print” link opens the user’s default print dialog box and allows the user to print the list of accounts.
The list of accounts may be filtered with the following options:
Include Terminated Accounts – By default, terminated bank accounts will not be listed in the display on this tab. If this checkbox is selected, terminated accounts will be included in the results.
Account Purpose – TPAs may have multiple bank accounts with different purposes or bank accounts with multiple purposes each. This dropdown allows users to filter accounts that display by the purpose assigned to the account. Those purposes include:
Debit Card Settlement
Reimbursement
General Operating
Remittance
Fees
ACH Remittance
Add a Bank Account
To add a bank account from the Bank Accounts tab:
Click the “Add Account” link (Fig 2.). The Add Account modal will open (Fig. 3).
Figure 2. Add Account
Figure 3. Add Account Modal Window

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Administrator Central | Bank Accounts
chunks.content:
Select a Bank Name using the dropdown menu. The user may type the name in this field to narrow available selections. If your bank is not available in the list of banks, select “Other”; a text field will appear and allow the user to enter the bank name.
Choose a Routing Number using the dropdown menu.
If the bank selected has only one Routing Number associated with it, that number will automatically populate and no action is needed. If the selected bank has multiple routing number associated with it, those routing numbers will display in the dropdown selector list—select the appropriate routing number for the account OR type the routing number in this field.
Enter the Account Name in the text field.
Enter the Account Number in the text field.
Select Checking or Savings using the Account Type dropdown menu.
Choose how the account will be used with the Account Usage dropdown menu. You may check one or multiple purposes.
Debit Card Settlement
Reimbursement
General Operating
Remittance
Fees
ACH Remittance
Let System Generate Check Numbers checkbox is selected by default. When this option is checked, Summit’s cash management system will auto generate check numbers in sequence as payments are issued.
Enter a value in the Next Check Number field to calculate the subsequent check numbers in Cash Management. This field will remain hidden unless the option “Let System Generate Check Numbers” option is enabled.
Click the Alert when Balance is below $0.00 checkbox, if desired. When checked, Summit will issue a communication if the account’s balance is ever placed below $0.00 due to transactions.
Click Save.
Edit a Bank Account
To edit a Bank Account on the Bank Accounts tab:
Click the “Bank Name” hyperlink (Fig. 4).
Figure 4. Edit Bank Account
The Edit Account modal will display (Fig. 5).
Figure 5. Edit Account Window
NOTE: Only certain elements may be edited. Once a bank account has been added to Summit, most fields will be locked.
Edit the details and Press Save when done.
Terminate a Bank Account

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Administrator Central | Bank Accounts
chunks.content:
TPA Bank Accounts can be terminated from the Bank Accounts tab. To terminate a TPA Bank Account:
Click the “Terminate” link in the Actions column of the Bank Account grid (Fig. 6). A Terminate Account popup window will appear (Fig. 7).
Figure 6. Terminate a Bank Account
Press the Continue button to confirm the termination.
Figure 8. Terminate Account Window
The Account will be flagged as Terminated in Summit and removed from the grid unless the “Include Terminated Accounts” option is selected in the filter settings.
If you are looking for further information, please refer to the Bank Accounts section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Administrator Central | Technical Settings
chunks.content:
Administrator Settings | Administrator Central | Technical Settings
The Technical Settings tab in Administrator Central allows TPAs to view and configure certain technical settings within Summit, including:
Summit Instance URLs
ZipLine
Single Sign-On
Provider Pay
Password Requirements
Table of Contents
Accessing Technical Settings
System URLs
Zip-Line EDM Settings
Single Sign-On
Provider Pay
Password Complexity
Accessing Technical Settings
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Administrator Settings.
Click on the Administrator Central menu.
Figure 1. Navigation
Open the Technical Settings tab (Fig 2).
Figure 2. Technical Setting Tab
System URLs
Each TPA has its own unique URLs for its Summit portals.
Summit URL – This is the unique URL for the TPA’s Summit Admin site. Administrator users will login to Summit using this URL. This is the Summit site which contains the administrative back-end for your TPA business.
Portal URL – This is the unique URL for the TPA’s Participant Portal site. Participant users will login to Summit using this URL. This is the Summit site which contains the individual benefit and account information for participants of groups administered by the TPA in Summit.
Figure 3. System URLs
Zip-Line EDM Settings
Summit offers Claim Fax imaging functionality via the Zip-Line utility. Participants are able to fax receipts to substantiate claims as images via a fax service. The images can then be assigned to claims in Summit.
The Fax Number field contains the TPA’s unique DataPath-assigned fax number associated with this functionality. Fax images sent to this number will be imported directly into Summit via the Zip-Line utility.
Figure 4. Zip-Line EDM Settings
Single Sign-On
Summit offers integrated Single Sign-on capabilities to DataPath clients. To enable Single Sign-on capabilities, an SSO Digital Certificate must be uploaded (Fig. 5).
Figure 5. Single Sign-on
For more details on Summit’s Single Sign-On capabilities, click here.
Provider Pay

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Administrator Central | Technical Settings
chunks.content:
RSCTPA Key – This is the TPA’s unique myRSC identifier, used for matching purposes to identify the TPA in regards to DataPath’s Provider Payment services.
Include $0.00 Payments –The option will be selected by default and as a result, will include all claims that are calculated to pay $0.00. These claims include those applied to a deductible and/or Participant coinsurance responsibility. They could also include claims that were denied in full for which the Payment Method is Provider Pay and the Destination Plan is NOT an HSA Benefit.
Figure 6. Provider Pay RSCTPA Key & $0.00 Payment
Password Complexity
Summit allows TPAs to control the strictness of password parameters. The default password standard implemented for all user types is:
Password Length – Passwords must be at least 8 characters long
Case – Passwords must contain at least one upper case and one lowercase letter
Special Characters – Passwords must contain at least one special character or number.
Expiration Timing – User Passwords will expire after a set number of days. 365 days is the default.
TPAs are able to implement password complexity requirements that vary from the default section of the Technical Settings tab.
Figure 7. Password Complexity
Minimum Length –the minimum number of characters allowed in a password
Maximum Length – the maximum number of characters allowed in a password
Days Until Password Expires – Summit user account passwords are set to expire after a fixed number of days, at which point the user will be prompted to create a new password.
Character Sets Required – The “Character Sets Required” drop-down specifies the number of character sets that must be included in the password.

If no boxes are checked in the “Required” column, the user may include any combination of characters so long as it contains the number of required character sets.

If a box in the “Required” column is selected, then a user MUST include characters from that character set when meeting the required character combination.

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Administrator Central | Technical Settings
chunks.content:
Press the Save button after entering the mandatory fields.

chunks.title: Administrator Settings
chunks.content:
Administrator Settings
Summit’s Administrator Settings is a top-level Settings category that covers many of the things which Third-Party Administrators (TPAs) must configure to administer benefits within Summit.
Table of Contents
Roles
Users
Administrator Central
Participant Portal Settings
Employer Invoicing
Online Enrollment
Annual Rates & Limits
Alerts/News
Administrator Settings and its various sub-pages may be accessed through the Settings menu at the top right.
Summit’s Administrator Settings include the following sub-pages:
Roles
The Roles page is used to create and modify various user roles in Summit. These roles grant specific feature access to various parts of Summit based on the type of user. These different roles, once created, may be associated with users, granting them specific levels of access per the assigned role.
Figure 2. Roles
Users
The Users page allows you to add new Summit user accounts, view existing accounts, and make modifications to those accounts.
Figure 3. Users
Administrator Central
The Administrator Central page contains many of the settings and information specific to your TPA, such as your demographic information, entities associated with your business, associated bank accounts, and technical settings pertaining to your set up of Summit.
Figure 4. Administrator Central
Participant Portal Settings
One of Summit’s features is a unique Participant Portal view that allows participants to access their Summit information, including plan details, account information, documents, and more. The Participant Portal Settings page allows you to configure and customize the available tools, appearance, and participant user experience of the Summit Participant Portal.
Figure 5. Participant Portal Settings
Employer Invoicing
The Employer Invoicing page allows TPAs to configure how Summit generates invoices to employer groups. These settings are configured at a global TPA level but may also be customized for specific groups at the employer level.
Figure 6. Employer Invoicing

chunks.title: Administrator Settings
chunks.content:
Online Enrollment
Summit allows TPAs to offer online enrollment for participants. The Online Enrollment page of Administrator settings allows TPAs to configure settings pertaining to Online Enrollment and Election Changes.
Figure 7. Online Enrollment
Annual Rates & Limits
The Annual Rates & Limits page of Summit includes informational tables of IRS-published limits and PCOR fee rates, with breakdowns by-year. This information is published on this page by DataPath and updated in accordance with IRS guidelines. The information displayed here is read-only.
Alerts/News
Summit allows TPAs to issue pop-up alerts and news to other Summit users. The Alerts/News page allows users to create and view these messages and designate the user types who will receive them when logging into Summit.
Figure 8. Alerts/News
If you are looking for further information, please refer to the Administrator Settings section in FAQs.

Advanced Plan Designs | Claim Calculation Formulas
Carrier claim files for import and carrier EOBs that TPAs receive and use to enter claims in Summit often contain amount fields that do not correlate to what Summit uses for total Claim Amount, Ineligible Amount, and Approved Amount.
To allow for TPAs to account for these discrepancies, users may define formulas for calculating the amounts from the claim files and/or EOBs to enter into claim forms. These formulas are configured at an administrator level from Advanced Plan Designs.
Table of Contents
Add Formula
Editing Claim Calculation
Add Period
Delete Formula
Delete Individual Detail Records
* Required fields appear in Red
To access Advanced Plan Designs | Claim Calculation Formulas,
Go to the Settings drop-down menu.
Mouse-over Advanced Plan Designs.
Click Claim Calculation Formulas.
Figure 1. Accessing Claim Calculation Formulas
This will open the Claim Calculation Formulas user interface.
Figure 2. Claim Calculation Formulas
The page lists any formulas that have been created. You may add, edit, or delete Claim Calculation Formulas from this page. Each Formula Header will display as a line item in the Claim Calculation Formulas list grid.
Clicking the blue arrow icon by the Formula Name will expand the formula header to show detailed records. Every formula header record includes at least one detail record when expanded. The detailed records include the effective date for that formula record.
Figure 3. Formula Details
The Refresh link will refresh the list of formulas if another user has added or modified formulas in the list.
The Excel link will export the list of formulas as an Excel worksheet.
The Print link will open the user’s default print dialogue box and allow the user to print the list of formulas.
Add Formula
To add a new formula:
Click the +Add Formula link. The Add Claim Calculation Formula modal displays (Fig. 4).
Figure 4. Add Claim Calculation Formula
2. Enter a Formula Name in the text box.

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Claim Calculation Formulas
chunks.content:
NOTE: Summit will automatically generate the System ID after the new formula is saved. This field is not editable.
3. Enter the Effective Date. Summit will use this date for claim calculation to determine for which claims the formula should apply.
Under the Total Denied Amount column, you can customize how the value of the Denied Amount will be calculated by denoting that the system should add or subtract the following values:
Total Charged Amount
Discount Amount
Allowable Amount
Carrier Coinsurance Amount
Carrier Deductible
Carrier Copay Amount
Carrier Ineligible Amount
Carrier Paid Amount
The fields for the corresponding values used to calculate the Denied Amount must be included on the Claim Entry Form. These fields may be added from Plan Default Settings | Reimbursement Settings | Claim Entry Preferences.
Editing Claim Calculation
To edit a claim calculation:
1. Click the Edit icon (pencil) by the listed formula detail record.
Figure 5. Edit Claim Calculation
This will open the Edit Claim Calculation modal (Fig. 6).
Figure 6. Edit Claim Calculation Formula Modal
2. Edit formula selections, Effective Date, and Formula Name as needed.
3. Click Save.
Add Period
You may make modifications to a formula that will take place on a specified Effective Date.
Click the Add + icon by a formula header.
Figure 7. Add Period
A pop-up will ask you to confirm that you want to add a new period for the formula. Click Continue.
Figure 8. Add Period Confirmation
The Add Claim Calculation Formula modal (Fig. 6) will open and a new formula may be configured.
2. Enter a new Effective Date.
NOTE: The new Effective Date must be later than the most recent Effective Date in the formula details. [For example, if the current formula’s most recent Effective Date is 01/01/2020, you would be able to enter 06/01/2020 but not 06/01/2019. If an earlier Effective Date is entered, the Save button will be unavailable.]

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Claim Calculation Formulas
chunks.content:
This allows for the creation of distinct periods under a single formula header. These periods do not overlap, and Summit will apply the formula based on matching a claim’s Service Begin Date with the distinct periods between the Effective Dates of the formula.
For instance, a formula is created with an effective date of 1/1/2019, then an additional period for that formula is created effective 1/1/2020. Under these effective dates, a claim with a 12/1/2019 Service Begin Date would be calculated using the formula for the period with the 1/1/2019 Effective Date; a claim with a 2/1/2020 Service Begin Date would be calculated using the formula for the period with 1/1/2020 Effective Date.
3. Click Save.
Delete Formula
Formulas and their associated periods may be deleted.
NOTE: A formula may not be deleted if there are claims associated with any of its periods.
1. Click the Delete (trash can) icon in the Actions column of the formula header.
Figure 9. Delete Formula
A confirmation pop-up will display.
2. Click Continue to confirm that you wish to delete the formula and all associated effective dates.
Figure 10. Delete Formula Pop-up Window
If the formula header is deleted, all associated formula period records will be removed as well.

Individual detail records may also be deleted.
NOTE: A formula’s period may not be deleted if there are claims associated with it.
Click the Edit icon (pencil) for the Effective Date detail record (Fig. 11).
Figure 11. Delete Individual Detail Records
The Edit Claim Calculation Formula modal displays.
2. Click the Delete link on the edit modal.
A pop-up will confirm that you wish to proceed and delete the formula period.
For further information, please refer to the FAQs page.

Advanced Plan Designs | Provider Networks
Summit allows TPAs to configure providers and provider networks for reporting and reimbursement purposes for CDH plans. In the case of HRA plans, for instance, Employers and TPAs often limit the reimbursement of expenses to services provided by “In-network” providers or they may reimburse the expense at a reduced rate for a service performed “out-of-network”.
Providers and Provider Networks can be linked to plans of any type, and Summit allows for providers to be associated with any plan type, however, most typically they will be linked to HRA plans.
The Advanced Plan Designs | Provider Networks page allows you to set up providers and configure provider networks that may be linked to plans.

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Service Categories/Codes
chunks.content:
Advanced Plan Designs | Service Categories/Codes
Service Codes correspond to different types of treatments or services a Participant may receive from a provider. These codes are utilized during claims processing to determine reimbursement eligibility and copays based on plan designs and the service code attributes.
When Service Codes are entered for a claim, it identifies the type of treatment that was received. Different treatments may be reimbursable only from specific plans; they may also be subject to reimbursements at a specific percentage and/or subject to reimbursement limits.
Service codes are grouped together with other “like” codes into Service Categories, eg. “Medical”, “Dental”, “Vision”, and “Pharmacy”. Codes grouped in the Medical category will typically include treatments at doctors’ offices or hospitals, while Codes included in Dental would typically be associated with teeth cleaning, fillings, etc.
Summit allows TPAs to manage and configure Service Categories and Service Codes from Advanced Plan Designs. Service Codes/Categories configured in Advanced Plan Designs | Service Category/Codes are used as the TPA default.

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Service Categories/Codes
chunks.content:
If there are multiple plans in a Benefit Order for a category and the Covered Expense is not enable on a given plan, then claim calculation will skip that plan on the Destination Plan field of the claim. If no plans have the service marked with Covered Expense, then the claim for this service cannot be approved.
Bypass Deductible – There may be circumstances whereby a plan (typically an HRA) is setup to have a deductible but may be able to pay out for certain eligible expenses prior to the deductible having been met. The Bypass Deductible flag indicates that claims associated with the service should create reimbursements regardless of whether the deductible has been met.
Copay Amount – Service Codes may be associated with Copay amounts by entering an amount in this field. This will be used in calculating the reimbursable amount of a claim that has been entered for the service. Claims that have a copay amount will calculate a reimbursable amount that the Approved amount less the Copay amount. Calculation of reimbursable amounts are based on individual claims unless otherwise specified by plan design. Note that while this value is used to calculate claim reimbursements, it is NOT used for autosubstantiation via copay matching for debit card claims. The copay values entered at the Employer Health Plan level are used for that purpose.
Max Reimbursement – This setting defines the maximum that can be paid for the Service Code. Reimbursement is calculated after any deductible, copay, and or coinsurance is applied.
Min Age – If the service has a minimum age requirement, the claimant (participant or covered dependent) must be at least the age entered in this field for claims for the service with this attribute to create reimbursements.
Max Age – If the service has a maximum age requirement, the claimant (participant or covered dependent) must be no older than the age entered in this field for claims for the service with this attribute to create reimbursements.

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Service Categories/Codes
chunks.content:
NOTE: The birthdate of the claimant must be present in order to determine if the claim is valid. If the birthdate is not present, Summit will deny the claim or calculate a $0.00 reimbursement amount.
Office Visit Options
This section and the Max Visits field allow you to set a maximum number of office visits for a particular service code. If the Max Visits field is blank, then there is no maximum visit limit associated with the code.
Figure 19. Office Visit Options
Enter an amount in the Max Visits field
Entering a value in the Max Visits field will enable both the Frequency and the Family/Individual dropdown selectors. These allow you to specify exactly how Summit’s claim entry and processing logic should handle claims entered with associated service codes that limit the number of visits that may be reimbursed under a plan.
Figure 20. Office Visit Options Drop-Downs
Select the desired Frequency amount
When an individual submits claims associated with a service code with a Max Visits value entered, Summit will check against any previous claims with the same Service Code to determine whether the participant has exceeded the allowable visits.
If the Frequency dropdown is set to Annual, the limit on visits will apply on an annual basis; Summit will check the number of claims entered against the service code for the entire year. If the Frequency dropdown is set to Monthly, Summit will check the number of claims entered against the service code for the month in which this claim’s Service Begin Date occurs.
Note: For Annual Renewal Plans, the Frequency ‘Annual’ refers to Plan Year. For Open-Ended Plans, the Frequency ‘Annual’ refers to the calendar year.
Choose Family/Individual using the dropdown
Family/Individual determines whether the Max Visits total during the Frequency period applies to each covered individual [Individual is selected] or to all covered individuals in aggregate [Family is selected].

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Service Categories/Codes
chunks.content:
If the number of claims entered for a participant with this service code exceeds the value of Max Visits entered for the selected Frequency and Family/Individual value, the claim will not be approved for reimbursement.

The value entered in this field is a percentage based amount that is used to determine the employer plan responsibility when calculating reimbursement.
Figure 22. Coinsurance Options – Service Code

The Edit Service Code modal will display.

Click Save

Advanced Plan Designs | Tier Groups/Definitions
Table of Contents
Tier Groups
Add a Tier Group
Edit a Tier Group
Delete a Tier Group
Tier Definitions
Add a Tier Definition
Edit a Tier Definition
Delete a Tier Definition
* Required fields appear in Red
Many plans, particularly HRAs, have different levels of coverage and other limits. One of the mechanisms of designing such plans and benefits is the use of funding tiers. Funding Tiers may be custom built by administrators based upon specific plan designs. These tiers may be created at the TPA level as default tiers as well as custom tiers per Employer Plan.
Funding tiers determine how much employer money is contributed to a plan based on the tier that is associated with a participant. These tiers are most often established to reflect a participant’s family situation. Such tiers might include:
Single – A flat dollar amount allocated to a single participant
Participant Plus Spouse – A dollar amount allocated to those participants that will cover themselves and a spouse, typically greater than for “Single” participant.
Participant Plus Family – A dollar amount allocated to those participants that wish to cover their entire family, spouse + children.
Additionally, Premium Billing Benefits are typically elected and priced based on a similar tier structure.
The Advanced Plan Designs page allows for the configuration of TPA-level default funding tiers for both CDH and Premium Billing benefits. Tier Groups are available to assign to plans that are Tier Funded/Premium Billing at both the TPA Level and the Employer Level.
The Tier Groups configured here are templates only for quickly building Tier Tables for Tier Funded/Premium Billing benefits. Tiers may be added or removed from those tables at any time during the benefit setup process.

Click on Settings

The Available For: CDH checkbox determines whether the tier group can be selected for completing tier tables for Tier Funded plans on the CDH tab of plan setup.
The Available For: Premium Billing checkbox determines whether the tier group can be selected for completing tier tables for Premium Billing plans on Premium Billing tab of plan setup.
Associated Tiers

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Tier Groups/Definitions
chunks.content:
The Associated Tier Definitions section allows you to associate/dissociate tiers from the Tier Group. Individual tiers that have been configured in the Tier Definitions section of Advanced Plan Designs | Tier Groups/Definitions will appear listed in the All Tiers list.
To move an Individual Tier to the Assigned Tiers list:
Select one or multiple [holding CTRL + click] tiers
Click add [>] or click add all [>>]
The selected tiers will appear in the Assigned Tiers column.
Tiers may be dissociated from the Tier Group by selecting one or multiple from the Assigned Tiers list and clicking remove [<] or all may be dissociated by clicking remove all [<<].
Click the green Save button when done.
The newly created Tier Group will display in the Tier Group list grid.
NOTE: The information on this screen may be printed using the Print button in the upper right corner.
Edit a Tier Group
Click on the edit icon (pencil) for the desired group.
Figure 6. Edit Tier Group
This will open the Tier Group modal (Fig. 5), where the attributes and the tier associations may be modified.
Delete a Tier Group
Click the delete icon (trash can) for the desired group.

Figure 7. Delete Tier Group
Note: Tier Groups are only used as templates for the quick setup of Tier Tables when designing individual benefits. Removing a Tier Group will not affect any plans previously set up using the Tier Group, however, a removed Tier Group will not be available for selection in the future when setting up a Tier Table for a Tier Funded or Premium Billing benefit.
A Tier Group Deletion Confirmation popup will appear (Fig. 8) to confirm that you wish to delete the Tier Group.
Figure 8. Tier Group Deletion Confirmation
2. Click the green Delete Tier Group button to proceed
Tier Definitions

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Tier Groups/Definitions
chunks.content:
The Tier Definitions section contains a list of all tiers and allows for the management of these tiers. The Tier Definitions table displays the Tier ID, Tier Name, and Tier Level of each Tier. These tiers are available to assign to Tier Groups for purposes of defining funding tiers for CDH plans and election tiers for Premium Billing plans.
NOTE: These global tier definitions are structural only. Attributes of the tier pertaining to pricing, coverage, etc. are defined in the Tier Table when building the benefit plans at the TPA or Employer levels.
Figure 9. Tier Definitions
Add a Tier Definition
To add a new Tier Definition:
Click the +Add Tier Definition link.
Figure 10. Add Tier Definition
This will open the Tier Definition modal.
Figure 11. Add Tier Definition Modal
2. Enter a Tier Name and Tier ID.
The Tier Name and Tier ID should be completed in a manner that reflects the tier of funding or coverage, indicating the covered individual(s), such as a Tier Name of “Employee + Spouse” or “Participant + Spouse” and a Tier ID of “EE/SP” or “PP/SP”.
3. Select a Tier Level using the drop-down.
The Tier Level indicates where the tier should be placed in the funding/election structure. When a qualifying event occurs for a participant, Summit identifies the original Tier Level of the participant’s plan, and only permits the election of Tiers with the same or lower Tier Level Value.  In the above structure, a participant who had been enrolled in Employee + Children (Tier Level 3) and had a Qualifying Event would not be permitted to elect Employee + Family (Tier Level 4).
A typical tier structure might look like this:
Employee Only – 1
Employee + Spouse – 2
Employee + Children – 3
Employee + Family – 4
Summit offers up to 8 levels for Tier Definitions to allow for more complex structures, such as those which may include “EE + 1CH”, “EE + 2CH”, “EE + FAM”, etc.
Relationship Validation

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Tier Groups/Definitions
chunks.content:
Summit will perform tier validation against the selected tier when the tier Relationship Validation option is enabled on the Tier Definition.
NOTE: Tier validation options are only applied to new benefits. These tier validations are performed as the coverages are added to participants.
Maximum QBs allowed – This checkbox will enable validation of the number of selected qualified beneficiaries on coverage. When enabled, the user will select a number of maximum qualified beneficiaries allowed for the tier. Summit will validate the election of coverage for this tier against the number selected here. If the number of selected qualified beneficiaries exceeds the Maximum QBs allowed value, Summit will display a warning message, informing the participant of the maximum allowed dependents for the selected tier.
Figure 12. Maximum QBs allowed
Tier-allowed relationships – This checkbox will enable validation of the tier by dependent/qualified beneficiary relationships. The user will be able to select the allowable dependent relationships for the tier by checking the checkbox by each dependent type. Summit will validate the participant’s election of the tier based on the dependent/qualified beneficiaries’ relationships.
Figure 13. Tier-allowed relationships
4. Click the green Save button
Edit a Tier Definition
To make changes to an existing Tier Definition
Click on the edit icon (pencil) beside the desired Tier Definition.
Figure 14. Edit Tier Definition
This will open the Tier Definition modal (Fig. 11), where you may change the Tier Name, Tier ID, and/or Level.
Delete a Tier Definition
To delete a Tier Definition:
1. Click the delete icon (trash can) for the desired Tier Definition.
Figure 15. Delete Tier Definition

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs | Tier Groups/Definitions
chunks.content:
Note: Deleting a Tier Definition will remove it from any Tier Groups it is associated with. These Tier Definitions and the Tier Groups configured on this page, are used as a template only for quickly setting up Tier tables for benefits and are not linked to Premium Billing or benefit plans that are setup with Tiered Funding. Deleting a Tier Definition will not affect any existing plans that may have used the Tier Definition in the Tier table. However, when new plans are added, tiers that have been deleted and/or removed from a Tier Group will not appear in the tier structure table when the Tier Group is selected. Tiers may always be added or removed manually when configuring the Tier table for a benefit.
A Tier Deletion Confirmation pop-up will appear confirming you wish to delete the Tier Definition.
Figure 16. Tier Deletion Confirmation
2. Click the green Delete Tier button to confirm.

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs
chunks.content:
Advanced Plan Designs
Advanced Plan Designs allows you to configure a number of settings that have bearing on Administrator-level plan design defaults at a global level without necessarily having to put these settings in place while creating the plans themselves.
Table of Contents
Provider Networks
Service Categories/Codes
Tier Groups/Definitions
Claim Calculation Formulas
The Advanced Plan Designs module of Summit includes set up sections for the following (for more in-depth information, click the hyperlink):
Provider Networks
This screen allows for the setup of Providers and Provider Networks, which are used for reporting and reimbursement purposes for CDH plans. From this screen, you are able to create custom networks of providers which may be associated with specific plans.
Service Categories/Codes
This screen allows for the setup of Service Categories of Service Codes administrator defaults in Summit. Service Categories and Service Codes may be used at the claim level to identify the service provided; decide if and how the plan should reimburse the claim; and determine claim eligibility and reimbursable amounts based on service code attributes, including office visit limits, age limits, whether claims associated with the service should bypass deductibles, and more.
Tier Groups/Definitions
This screen allows for the setup of default tier structure templates. For Tier Funded plans and Premium Billing elections, benefits require a tier table to be completed to denote levels of coverage and pricing. An example of a common tier structure would be:
Employee Only
Employee + Spouse
Employee + Children
Employee + Family
To quickly create these tables, global default structures may be created here and applied at the plan level, to be used as-is or modified as necessary by adding or removing tier rows.
Claim Calculation Formulas

chunks.title: Advanced Plan Designs
chunks.content:
This screen allows users to create claim calculation formulas. When applied, the formulas can account for discrepancies between how values are calculated on carrier feeds/EOBs and how Summit calculates certain values by default. TPAs can define formulas for calculating the amounts from the claim files and/or EOBs to enter into claim forms.

chunks.title: Communications | Entity Comm
chunks.content:
Communications | Entity Comm
The Entity Comm page allows users to indicate whether or not to send Report Repository file completion notices to individuals of selected entities.
This page includes a radio button toggle that controls whether the communications rules being applied are TPA-level or for a specific Employer. If Employer is selected, a single-select employer dropdown will appear, allowing the user to select which Employer group the settings will apply to.
The Entity Comm page contains a grid with the following columns:
Communication Type – This is a static field displaying the type of communication for which the notification settings will apply.
General Settings – All available records listed on the General Settings page of Communication will be available for selection in this field. “Summit Default” will be selected by default.
Send Email – This field contains a dropdown selector with the following options: 
Everyone 
To Selected 
Except to Selected 
Nobody 
Selected Users – If a user has changed the Receive an Email option settings from “Everyone” to “Except to Selected” or vice-versa, users who are eligible to opt-in/opt-out will be displayed in this field. If a user changes the Receive an Email option to either “To Selected” or “Except to Selected,” any usernames displaying here will be cleared.

chunks.content:
Communications | General Settings
The Communications | General Settings acts as a centralized location in Summit for users to configure the general settings for email communications.
These settings may be configured generally for all employers linked to the TPA defaults or for a single employer by selecting that employer from the Employer selector.
This page contains a grid with the following columns:
Name – This value will be validated for uniqueness within the organization, either TPA or employer. [Required]
TPA Default
From Email – This is a read-only field, and the default value will be communications@summitwith.us.  To change this value, contact DataPath Support.
CC Email
BCC Email
Image Location – Image position radio buttons [Left (default), Center, Right]
Image – Allows user to select and upload an image.
Actions – Edit (Pencil icon), Delete (Trashcan icon) [Only available if the user has Read/Update role permissions]
The grid has a default read-only “Summit Default” record with the following values which cannot be changed or deleted:
From Email: communications @summitwith.us
Users with read/update access may add a new record to the Settings grid by clicking the +Add Setting link. If an employer has been selected, the setting will apply only to the selected employer. If no employer has been selected, this new record will be used as a global default setting.

The communications tab contains the settings for the default email, communication notices list, and security email block history. Here the user is allowed to modify the content and format of these communications. A user can view and configure both TPA level and Employer level Communications settings.
Table of Contents
Default Email Settings
Communications Table
Security Email Block History
To access User Communications,
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Communications.
Select the User Communications menu from the dropdown list.
On this page, users are able to configure both TPA level and Employer level Communications settings. The settings configured at the TPA level will be automatically applied to new Employers who are added to Summit as still associated with the TPA Default Settings.
It includes the following fields:
Employer – This dropdown auto-populates all the employers present in the TPA.
Assigned to Administrator Defaults – To configure Communications Settings at the Employer level, select an Employer from the dropdown list and uncheck the checkbox that links the Employer to the Administrator Defaults. Only by de-selecting this checkbox, the user can customize Communications Settings for the selected Employer. As long as this box remains checked, changes updated at the TPA level will reflect at the Employer level too.
While unchecking this checkbox, a pop-up will display as shown below. Click “OK” to proceed with de-linking.
Now a message will display confirming the employer has been unassigned from the Administrator defaults:
To re-assign the Employer to Administrator Defaults, check the checkbox and click “OK” in the pop-up that appears.
Now a notification about the same will display as shown below.
Default Email Settings
In this section, the user can configure various settings related to the default communication email.
It includes the following fields and settings:

chunks.title: Communications | User Communications
chunks.content:
From – This is a mandatory alphanumeric text field where the user can set the address from which communication emails should be sent. By default, this field will auto-populate with the email address “communications@summitwith.us. In addition, TPAs will no longer be able to make changes to their From email address within Summit to avoid the possibility that communications sent from the new address will be seen as email spoofing. This is a function performed by DataPath personnel at the request of TPA-authorized personnel.
CC Recipients – In this text field, the user can enter up to 10 email addresses of users who want to receive a carbon copy of the communication email by separating them with a semicolon.
BCC Recipients – This is another text field to add email addresses of 10 users who want to receive a blind carbon copy of the communication email. The recipients specified in this field do not appear in the received mail header and they remain unknown for other recipients given in the “To” and “CC” fields.
Image – In this section, the user can configure an image or logo that should appear in the communication. Clicking the Edit icon will open a dialog box that will allow the user to browse and upload an image file. After uploading the image, the user can select the “Left”, “Center” or “Right” position to indicate where the uploaded image should appear on the top of the email. If needed, the user can delete the uploaded image by clicking the Delete icon given at the image’s top right side.
Communications Table
This table will list all the default communication notices sent by Summit via Email/Portal.
At the Employer level, if the selected Employer remains linked to Administrator Defaults, then the user can see a Link icon in the Name column of Communications table as shown below.
Name – Here the name of the communication email will be displayed.

chunks.title: Communications | User Communications
chunks.content:
Email – This is a link that opens the Email Communication Template where the user can view and customize the email communication by adding some additional fields and editing the content. An option to print the template is also available here.
Portal – This link opens the Portal Communication template where the user can view and customize the Participant Portal communication by adding some additional fields and editing the content. Here also a print option is available.
After completing the settings on this page, click “Save” to save the configuration.
Security Email Block History
In this section, the user can have a history of temporary security email blocks the system generates on Participant Demographics changes. It includes read-only fields such as Start Date, End Date, Status, and CreatedDate.
For further information, please refer to the Communications section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Creating Roles
chunks.content:
Creating Roles
Table of Contents
Adding a Role
Editing a Role
Deleting a Role
  * Required fields appear in Red
Summit has been designed to provide TPA the ability to create, delete and maintain user roles with fully customizable feature access associated with each role. Users may be given Read Only or Read/Write access to any combination of features within Summit.
TPAs may configure as many roles as they wish, but they must create at least one role. TPAs may set up the following types of roles:
Administrators – Administrator user roles have access to features specific to job responsibilities, with either Read-Only or Read/Write access to any combination of features.
Brokers – Different broker users have different user roles.  These roles only allow access to the employers associated with the specific broker.
Employers – Different employer users have different user roles. These roles only allow them access to their employer data.
Participants – This role grants users access to the Participant Portal.
Adding a Role
Go to Settings >> Administrator Settings >> Roles.
The Roles page displays.
Select the Administrators, Brokers, Employers, or Participants tab from the Roles Page depending on the type of role you wish to create.
Press the green Add Role button. The Role setup screen will display.
Enter a name for the role in the Role Name field.
A new role may be based on an existing role and can be created by selecting the Copy Role checkbox.

This will enable a Select Role dropdown. The new role will use the access settings of the selected role. The user may make changes to these settings for the new role.
The Status “ON/OFF” toggle determines whether the role is an active role that may be assigned to users. For the role to be active and assigned to users, the Status should be set to “ON”.

chunks.title: Creating Roles
chunks.content:
The “Default” checkbox indicates that new users created for the entity will be assigned this role by default. However, other roles may still be assigned. Only one role may be selected as the default selection for any given entity.
Click “Show” on the Permissions modal to display the list of all modules in the grid.
Each module has corresponding “Read” and “Read/Update” checkboxes on the grid.

For the user to view the module, the “Read” checkbox must be selected. To be able to update data within the module, both the “Read” and “Read/Update” checkboxes must be selected.
NOTE: Modules are listed hierarchically, and certain modules will require a role to have access to a top-level module, to have access to sub-modules. For instance, a role must have “Read” access to TPA Central to be given access to the TPA Demographics sub-module.
Click “Show” on the Assign Users modal to display the User assignment tool.

Once access has been assigned to the role, users may be assigned to the role from the Assign Users modal by moving users from the “All Users” list to the “Assigned Users” list.
Click “Show” on the Report Access modal. The Report Permissions role access displays a grid interface with checkboxes controlling access to reports. It also includes the ability to control users’ access to output types, allowing access to formatted report outputs only or both formatted and raw-data outputs. Note that users granted Raw Data Output access will also have access to Formatted Output.
Additionally, there are checkboxes on the Raw data output and Formatted output columns that will select all reports as available to the role. If this is checked, individual reports may still be disabled for a role by unchecking the respective checkbox for that report.
When a user runs a report, only the output options defined by their user role will be available to them on the report parameters screen.
Formatted
In Browser
PDF (Default)
Email
Docx
RTF
Raw Data Output
CSV (default)
JSON
Click Save when done.

chunks.title: Creating Roles
chunks.content:
The Role Table contains the following columns:
Role Name – By clicking on the role name, the user can View/Edit details that were described in the Edit Role section below.
Role Status – The Role status will be displayed in this column whether it is Active or Inactive.
Administrative Rights – If the Role would grant the user access to create/edit a User or a Role, this column will reflect an icon or icons.
Global Role – This column indicates whether the role is a global role or not with a green check mark symbol.
Date Created – The date created will be displayed in this column.
Assigned Users – The users assigned to the corresponding role will be displayed here.
Action – In this column, a delete icon will be displayed for unused user roles (Global roles cannot be deleted).
Editing a Role
To edit a Summit Role:
Go to Settings >> Administrator Settings >> Roles.
Select either Administrators, Brokers, Employers, or Participants tab depending on the role you wish to edit.
Click the “Role Name” hyperlink to select the role from the grid. The Role setup screen will display, where changes to the role can be made.
Click Save, once changes were made.
Deleting a Role
Admin users can delete unused User Roles in Summit. If there are no users assigned to a custom Role, a delete icon will appear beside it in the Action Column. Note that Global Roles cannot be deleted and will not have a delete icon even if no users are assigned to them.
If you are looking for further information, please refer to the Administrator Settings section in FAQs.
