Default Card Package
The Default Card Package section contains details about the card package.
Some of the fields on this screen contain default values while others do not.  The User can, but is not required to, configure these settings or add data to the fields that are not populated by default at the TPA level.
If a TPA has been granted access to card processing capabilities, they will have the option to enable an Employer for card issuance and processing and to associate the Employer to card settings and a Card Package.
This section contains the following fields:
Name – This is a dropdown list.  The default value is “Select Card Package”.  The TPA will select from all of the Card Packages that have been made available to them, all “default” Card Packages as well as all Card Packages that have been specifically linked to them.  The Card Packages available will be those in an “Active”, “Setup Pending,” or “Temporarily Disabled” status.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
The Card Package Name will have the status of the Card Package appended to the end in brackets (eg. [Active], [Setup Pending], or [Temporarily Disabled]). Card Packages that are in a “Setup Pending” or “Temporarily Disabled” status are selectable by the TPA, but when selected, the TPA will receive a pop-up warning indicating that the status is currently inactive.
All card orders based on that package will be held until such time as the package is activated.  Card Packages that are “Inactive” will not be available to the TPA to select from the point it is marked as Inactive.
When the User makes the selection of what will be their default card package, the system will auto-populate the values below associated with the package (if they have been associated).  Only one Card Package can be associated with a TPA as a default at a time.
Package ID – This is a read-only field indicating the ID of the selected Card Package. This ID cannot be a duplicate of any other Card Package ID.
Description – This field will display a description of the associated Card Package by default. If no description was provided at the Card Package level, this field will remain blank.
Card Network – The card network associated with the selected Card package will be displayed here by default. It may be either MasterCard or VISA based on the value entered in the BIN number field at the Card Package level. If the BIN number begins with “4”, this field will auto-populate “VISA” and if it begins with “5”, “MasterCard” will be auto-populated.
Card Expiration – Every Card Package will have a Time Frame that indicates the period up to which the card is valid. This field will display an auto-populated value in months associated with the selected Card Package. For example, if the value is 60, it means that the card will expire after 60 months from the date of issue.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
Card Re-Issue – This field will display the Card Re-Issue details provided at the Card Package level. It indicates the time in days prior to a card’s expiration date when the system should automatically re-issue cards. A card can be re-issued only when the card is damaged, but still valid. If a request for a card re-issue is sent, a new card with a new card number and CVV code with a new expiration date will be issued.
Card Design Details
This section allows TPA users to customize design details for Summit debit cards.
Front Logo Left– This will only show on the page if the card package has been set for customization.  If the value for customization is pre-defined by DataPath, this will reflect the logo ID selected and display the image, and this will not be editable by the TPA.  If the customization value was set such that the TPA can edit the value, this will be a dropdown list with a default value of “Select One”.  The TPA will have the option to select a logo from the list of Logos that have been tagged as Top Left Logos and have been marked as” Default” Logos as well as those Logos specifically associated with the TPA.
Front Logo Right – This dropdown list will allow for the selection of a logo image that has been added to the card package by DataPath. This list contains Image IDs stored in Summit and enabled for Front-Right Logo printing. The user can select any one of them as a Front-Right Logo to be printed on the card.
Front Logo Bottom – This option will display on the page only if the card has been enabled for customization.
Rear Logo – The Rear Logo option will display on the page only when the card has been set for customization

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
Carrier Logo – If the Card Package the user selects is enabled for the Carrier Logo, Summit will display the carrier logo pre-defined by the DataPath, or if it is enabled for customization, the user will have an option to select a logo from the list of Logos that have been tagged as Carrier Logos and have been marked as” Default” Logos as well as those Logos specifically associated with the TPA.
Insert – Card packages that allow for customization may include an insert. The Insert will be either a default set by DataPath or if the Card Package allows, a user may select from options to choose an insert to use.
Insert Logo – The Insert Logo option is visible only when the card has been set for customization. By default, values set by DataPath will be displayed here. If it is editable by the user, the Insert Logo option will display as a dropdown list from which the user may select a logo.
Card Sticker – If DataPath has set up a Card Sticker for the Card Package, it will be displayed here. If DataPath has enabled TPA customization, then the user can customize this card sticker field.
Fourth Line – This is an alphanumeric text field.  If the Card Package selected is of the type “MasterCard”, the system will allow a user to input up to 26 characters; if the package is of the type “VISA”, the User will have the ability to update up to 19 characters.  If a value has been entered at the Card Package level, it will display here, if not, it will be blank by default.
Carrier (Mailer)– This option will only be available if the card is set up by DataPath for customization. Carrier (Mailer) field may have default values set by Datapath. Otherwise, the user can set the value for the carrier by selecting a value from the dropdown.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
Support Phone & URL – The Support Phone & URL is a mandatory field. This field is available only when the selected Card Package has been enabled for Thermal Text. This is an alphanumeric field that allows the user to enter the customer service phone number and website to be printed on the backside of the card. If a value has been entered at the DataPath level, it will be displayed here. If not, it will be blank by default.
Employer Selection Box – The First list box will show all of the Employers. To link the employers to package and design defaults, select the name and click on the right arrow So that the employers will link to the Associated Employers list.
Card Shipping Details
This section allows for the configuration of debit card shipping details.
This section contains the following fields:
Activation Methods – This will be represented as checkboxes.  The TPA will have a check box available to them associated with each activation option for the selected card package.  The TPA can select any or all of the available options. The options are: “Issue Active”, “Manually Activate”, “Web Activation” and Summit IVR”. The options available at the Card Package level will be selected here by default.
Issue Active – If this is selected, cards will be sent to Participants in an Active status and no additional action from Participant’s side is required.
Manually Activate – If this option is selected, a participant has to call the TPA for the activation of the card. TPA will then access Summit to manually activate the card on behalf of the participant or offers their own IVR or web portal to activate the card. TPAs will need to send a message via file (and later, web service) to activate the card status.
Web Activation – If this option is selected, Participants may activate their card via the Participant Portal.
Summit IVR – If this option is selected, Participants may call the Summit IVR line to activate their cards.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
If the Summit IVR Activation Method is selected, it is required to provide a secondary ID for validation.
IVR ID– This is a dropdown list with available options. The options are Employer Custom ID, Employer System ID, Participant Custom ID, Participant System ID, SSN, TPA ID.
Default To Address – This is a dropdown list. 
The options to select are:
Cardholder Address – This is the address of the cardholder, whether the primary Participant or Dependent.  If a card is being issued to a Dependent, the card would be mailed to the Dependent’s address, which may be different than the address on file for the primary participant.
Employer Address – This option would send all cards for all cardholders to the mailing address of the Employer.
Participant Address – If this option is selected, all cards issued to members of a family, the primary Participant and all Dependents will be mailed to the address of the primary Participant.
TPA address – This option would send all cards for all cardholders to the address of the TPA.  If this is selected, the system will show the mailing address of the TPA as set on Administrator Central by default as well as a check box “Use Mailing Address”.  As long as this box is selected, anytime the TPA updates their mailing address on Administrator Central, this address will also be updated automatically.  If the TPA de-selects this box, updates to their mailing address will not update this address.  If the TPA manually changes the address here, the box will automatically be de-selected.
Shipping Methods – This is a dropdown list. The selection made in this list will determine the method used to deliver cards. The options are:
Standard USPS – This is the default selection

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
Overnight Shipping – If the TPA chooses this option, the system will produce a pop-up window with a disclaimer regarding the cost.  The window will require the User to check a box indicating they have read the disclaimer and agree to the additional costs.  They can then click “Continue” or “Cancel”.  Selecting Cancel will not complete the action and leave Standard USPS as the selected option.  If this method is selected, the system will retain the fact that the method was selected in the database along with the User name and ID of the User making that selection along with the date.
Employer Selection Box – This list box will show all the Employers currently associated with the defaults of the Card shipping Detail section and all Employers not associated.
Return Address
Use Mailing Address (from TPA Central) – By default, this will show the TPA’s Mailing Address as well as a check box “Use Mailing Address”.  As long as this box is selected, anytime the TPA updates their mailing address on Administrator Central, this address will also be updated automatically.  If the TPA de-selects this box, updates to their mailing address will not update this address.  If the TPA manually changes the address here, the box will automatically be de-selected.  The TPA must include an address here.
Include Name – This is a check box option that the TPA can select to include their TPA name in the return address included on the envelope.  This will be selected by default.
Card Issuance Details
Default Participant Issuance Settings – This is a dropdown list.  The options are: “Issue to All” and “Issue to None”.  This is an indicator that will either auto select all Participants for card issuance during Participant setup or will not select to have any Participants receive the card by default.  The default value is “Issue to All”.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
Default Dependent Issuance Settings – This is a dropdown list.  The options are “Spouse”, “All Dependents” and “None”. There will be a help icon next to this feature that the User can click to receive additional information. While clicking on icon a message will show as “Select spouse to automatically issue a debit card to all dependents identified as a spouse when assigned to card enabled plan. Select all dependents to automatically issue a debit card to all dependents, regardless of the identified relationship, when assigned to a card plan”.
Selection of fee from benefit account types – This is a radio button option and the options are “Notional” and “Custodial”.
Notional Account Card Issuance Fee – This checkbox enables a Card Issuance fee for debit cards linked to a notional employer-owned Summit plan account, such as an FSA, an HRA, DCAP, LFSA, Parking, or Transit plan. The Initial and Re-Issue fields allow you to enter a dollar amount that will be charged to the notional accounts as described above when a card is first issued and when a card is re-issued.
Custodial Account Card Issuance Fee – This checkbox enables a Card Issuance fee for debit cards linked to custodial accounts, such as individually owned HSAs. The Initial and Re-Issue fields allow you to enter a dollar amount that will be charged to the notional accounts as described above when a card is first issued and when a card is re-issued.
Issue Only When Linked to Card Enabled Plans – This is a setting to issue cards to Participants only when they have been linked to “card enabled” Plans.  This is a check box option, it is selected by default.  There will be a help icon next to this feature that the User can click to receive additional information.
Issue Only When Participant has an Email Address – This is a setting to issue cards to Participants only when they have an Email Address.  This is a check box option, it is selected by default.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Card Issuance Default
chunks.content:
Issue Date – This setting allows you to configure the default issue date for participant card issuance.
Two Weeks Prior to Plan Start – Summit will use the Plan Start Date of the card-enabled plan to determine when the card should be issued.
Upon Enrollment – Summit will issue the card at the time the participant enrolls in the plan.
Location Usage
In this section, the TPA user can view or edit the location usage settings of cards.
This section contains the following fields:
Location Usage – This mandatory dropdown allows you to restrict card usage to within the United States by selecting “US Only” or allow card usage abroad by selecting “Global”.
Daily Transaction Limit –This checkbox enables a limit on the maximum number of transactions the card may be used for in a single day. When checked, a numeric field will be available to enter the number of maximum daily transactions. Swipes beyond those allowed in a single day will be declined. This is not selected by default.
Per Transaction Limit – This checkbox enables a limit on the dollar amount per transaction. When checked, a dollar amount field will be available to enter the maximum transaction value. The portions of swipes exceeding this amount will be declined.
Annual Spending Limit – This checkbox enables a limit on total annual spending. When checked, a dollar amount field will be available to enter a maximum annual spending limit. The portions of swipes exceeding this amount will be declined.
Employer Selection Box – This list box will show all of the Employers associated with the defaults of the Location Usage section and those Employers that are not.
After selecting all the required fields, click “Save”.
For further information, please refer to the Cards section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Default MCCs
chunks.content:
Default Card Settings | Default MCCs
To ensure benefit-linked cards properly adhere to regulatory guidelines, the IRS mandates that cards be restricted to specific MCC Codes (Merchant Category Code), the codes Master Card assigns to merchants to identify the type of merchant they are in an authorization message. On this Default Card Settings page, the user will be allowed to configure various MCCs settings for TPAs through different tabs of Default MCC page.
Table of Contents
Plan MCCs
MCC Categories
Auto-Substantiation
To access Default MCCs,
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Default Card Settings.
Select Default MCCs menu.
Now the Default MCCs page with a row of tabs will appear as shown below. To access these tabs, the user has to select a TPA from the given dropdown list.
The tabs present in the Default MCCs page are:
Plan MCCs
In order to ensure cards are used for their intended purposes, the IRS mandates that cards be restricted to specific MCC Codes (Merchant Category Code), the codes Master Card assigns to merchants to identify the type of merchant they are in an authorization message. In this tab, users are able to associate or customize MCC Codes to specific Plan Types and Plan Templates.
MCC Categories
To ensure benefit-linked cards properly adhere to regulatory guidelines, the IRS mandates that cards be restricted to specific MCC Codes (Merchant Category Code), the codes Master Card assigns to merchants to identify the type of merchant they are in an authorization message. In this tab, the user can view, add and edit MCC Categories with an option to delete the same.
Auto-Substantiation

chunks.title: Default Card Settings | Default MCCs
chunks.content:
To ensure benefit-linked cards properly adhere to regulatory guidelines, the IRS mandates all cards to be restricted to some specific MCC Codes (Merchant Category Code), the codes Master Card assigns to merchants to identify the type of merchant they are in an authorization message. The IRS also requires the review of every transaction to determine its eligibility under IRS rules. This review of transaction can be performed electronically and if verified, can be “auto-substantiated” by the system.
For further information, please refer to the Cards section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Default Card Settings
chunks.content:
Default Card Settings
The user will be presented with default card related settings for that TPA in the Default Card Settings section. The user can view or edit the debit card settings here. There are three sections associated with Debit Card Settings. They are Card Issuance Default, Receipt Management, and Default MCCs.

Go to Settings.
Select Default Card Settings.
Choose a sub-menu.
The following sub-menus are available for Default Card Settings.
Card Issuance Default
Receipt Management
Default MCCs

chunks.title: Document Manager
chunks.content:
Document Manager
The Document Manager page allows TPA users to upload documents, organize those documents into categories, and assign them to Employers and Participants.
Table of Contents
Document Manager
Documents
Add Document
Categories
Add Category
Edit Category
* Required fields appear in Red
To access Document Manager,
Go to Settings.
Then to Communications.
Select Document Manager.
The Document Manager page will display on the screen as shown below.
Document Manager
Audience Type – When a TPA user accesses the page, the page will include an “Audience” dropdown; the options in the dropdown are “All”, “TPA”, “Employer”, or “Participant”.  The default value in this dropdown is “All”.
Documents
The Document table will list all of the documents that have been uploaded to the system.  If “All” is selected in the dropdown, the system will list all the documents uploaded. If a specific audience is chosen, the table will list only those documents that were uploaded and made available to the specific audience. The Document Table will display according to the audience type selected.
The table will display columns for:
Document Icon – This is an icon in the shape of a document. When the user clicks the icon, the system will allow the user to download and save the document locally.
Name – This column will display the name given to the document. It will be a hyperlink that will take the user to the Edit Document page. The parameters of the Edit Document are the same as mentioned in the Add Document page below.
Description – This column will display the document description.
Author – This column will display: “DataPath or “TPA” based on the user type uploading the document; if the user uploading the document is a TPA, this will reflect “TPA”.
Audience – This column will display “TPA”, “Employer”, or “Participant”. Documents can be associated with more than one audience type, and this column therefore, could show multiple audience types.

chunks.title: Document Manager
chunks.content:
Globally Available – If the document has been made “Globally Available”, this column will display a check mark here.
Action – By clicking on the trash icon, the document can be deleted.
Delete Selected Document – Preceding each document, there will be a checkbox.  The user will be able to check the box and will then have a link named “Delete Selected Document” that they can click to remove the documents from the table. By clicking on it, a confirmation message will appear as shown below.
Restore DataPath Documents – If this link is selected, the page will then re-display any DP level documents that had been hidden. By clicking on it, the Restore Default message will appear as shown below. Click “Restore” to proceed.
Add Document
By clicking on the Add Document button, a pop-up will display as shown below.
The Add Document modal contains the following fields:
Upload File – The user will be presented with an upload button; when this button is selected, they can browse a file on their network and click the file to retrieve it.
Document Name – This mandatory field represents the name of the document.
Document Description –The user can add a description of the document here.
Document Type – The Document Type dropdown includes the following documents:
User Guide
Form
Plan Docs
Agreements
General Document
Release Notes
Globally Available – This is a checkbox.  If this box is selected, the audience type will be greyed out. The document will be available to all Employers and their participants who have been given Role access to the Document Manager page.
Audience Type – Here, the user can select one or both audience types by selecting the checkboxes. The audience type includes:
Employer
Participant
If the audience type selected was “Employer”, the system will list all Employers under that TPA in one box, and the other will be the “Associated Employers” box.  The user can move Employers from the Employers box to the “Associated Employers” box.

chunks.title: Document Manager
chunks.content:
If “Participant” was selected, the user will be presented with the same option to associate the document with all or selected Employers.
A user can upload a document, but is not required to associate it with any Employers or Participants to save it.
Category – The system will include a list box with all the categories in the system. The user can associate the document with one or many/all of the categories they have created.
Once the document and its attributes have been uploaded and completed, the user will have the option to “Save” the upload or “Cancel” the upload.  After selecting either the Save or Cancel option, the system will close the pop-up and leave the user on the main Document Manager page.
Categories
The Document Manager page will also include a table listing all of the document categories in the system created by the TPA.
The table will include columns for:
Name – This field will reflect the name given to the Category. It will be a hyperlink that will take the user to the Edit Category page.
Description – This field will display the description given to the Category.
By clicking the arrow icon on the left end of the grid, the associated documents with the fields, Name and Description, will be shown.
Add Category
By clicking the Add Category button, the user can add a new category.
The Add Category contains the following fields:
Category Name – The user can enter the category name here. The value in this field must be unique across all Category names under the TPA.
Category Description – This field represents the description of the category.

chunks.title: Document Manager
chunks.content:
Associated Document – This is a list box that will list all the documents that are associated with the Category.  One side of the list box will list all of the documents in the system, and the other will list all of the documents that have been associated with the Category.  The user may add or remove documents from the “Associated Document” box as necessary.  The “All Document” box will show all DataPath documents made available to that TPA (which the TPA did not delete) and all documents uploaded by the TPA.
The user can then “Cancel”, “Delete”, or “Save” the Category.
Edit Category
The user can edit/delete a category by clicking on the Category Name in the Categories table. The user can also edit the Category Name, Description, or associated documents at any time. 
After editing the fields, the user can then “Save”, “Cancel”, or “Delete” the Category.
If you are looking for further information, please refer to the Document Manager section in FAQs.
Categories

chunks.title: Employer | Bank Accounts
chunks.content:
Employer | Bank Accounts
Bank Accounts details are necessary at the Employer level for the system to function properly on claim reimbursement, settlement of debit card transactions, etc. A user can create, edit, and view Employer-level Bank Accounts. If needed, users can also terminate accounts from the Employer Bank Accounts tab.
Table of Contents
Adding a New Employer Bank Account
Editing an Employer Bank Account
Terminating an Employer Bank Account
  * Required fields appear in Red
To access Employer Bank Accounts,
Go to Employer dropdown in the main navigation bar.
Select Bank Accounts from the drop-down menu.
Select a TPA and its Employer from the drop-down list.
On this page, the user can view all the Bank Accounts that belong to the selected Employer. Options to add new accounts, edit and terminate existing accounts are also available here. 
Include Terminated Accounts – This checkbox option is unchecked by default. By checking this box, a user can view all the bank accounts including both terminated and non-terminated accounts of the selected Employer.
Account Purpose – This is an advanced filter by which the user can filter the accounts on the basis of the purpose assigned to the account. An Employer can have multiple bank accounts with different purposes or bank accounts with multiple purposes. The account purposes include Debit Card Settlement, Reimbursement, General Operating, Remittance, and Fees.
Refresh – By clicking the Refresh link, the list of accounts displayed will be refreshed based on the filters applied.
Excel – By clicking the Excel link, the user can export the list of accounts to an Excel worksheet.
Print – Print link will open the default print dialog box, allowing the user to print the accounts list.
Adding a New Employer Bank Account
This page displays a list of existing Bank Accounts for the selected Employer and a link to add new Employer Bank Accounts. The user can also edit details of existing Bank Accounts if required.

chunks.title: Employer | Bank Accounts
chunks.content:
By clicking the link “Add Account”, a pop-up will be produced as shown below where the user can enter bank details to create a new Employer Bank Account.
The pop-up will have the following fields:
Bank Name – This is a dropdown list showing the names of included Banks. The user can select the bank name from the list or type to narrow the available selections.
If the user’s bank name is not included in the list, then select the entry “Other” from the list.
This will produce a new text field to enter the user’s bank name into the drop-down list.
Routing Number – This is a mandatory field. If the selected bank has only one associated Routing Number, then it will be populated automatically in this field. But if it has multiple Routing Numbers, the user needs to select a Routing Number from the available drop-down list. Also, it needs to be typed when the user’s bank is not included in the Bank Name list.
Account Number – Enter the Account Number associated with the Bank Account here.
Account Type – The user has to select the type of account being created by choosing either “Checking” or “Savings” from the drop-down list. By default, it is set as Checking.
Account Owner – This is a radio button with two options, TPA and Employer. The user can select either TPA or Employer as Account Owner. By default, this is set as Employer.
Account Purpose – This is a dropdown list with multiple checkboxes. The user can either check one or multiple purposes for the account. The list includes Debit Card Settlement, Reimbursement, General Operating, Remittance, Fees, and ACH Remittance.
Let System Generate Check Numbers – This is a checkbox that is checked by default. If this option is checked, Summit’s cash management system will auto generate check numbers in sequence as payments are issued.

chunks.title: Employer | Bank Accounts
chunks.content:
Next Check Number – This field will remain hidden unless the option “Let System Generate Check Numbers” option is enabled. In this field, the user has to enter the value of the next check number to calculate the subsequent check numbers in cash management.
Alert when Balance is below $0.00 – If the user wants to get notified whenever the account balance is below $0.00 due to transactions, this checkbox must be made checked.
After entering all the required information, click ‘Save’.
Editing an Employer Bank Account
The user can view a list of all the created Employer Bank Accounts with an option to edit the same.
To edit a Bank Account,
Click on the Bank Name that you want to edit. The Bank Account Names in the list are links that produce a pop-up showing respective bank account details.
A pop-up window with the details of the selected bank account will be then displayed as follows.
Edit the unlocked fields, if required.
NOTE: Once a Bank Account is created in Summit, most of the fields will get locked. Users may only edit unlocked fields.
Click ‘Save’ when changes are done.
Terminating an Employer Bank Account
Employer Bank Accounts can be terminated from the Employer Bank Accounts tab by the user.
To terminate an Employer Bank Account,
Click the “Terminate” link on the Actions column of the bank account that you want to terminate.
A new pop-up asking for confirmation to terminate the bank account will be produced as follows:
Click button “Continue” to proceed with the termination.
Now the Bank Account will be flagged as Terminated and removed from the list unless the “Include Terminated Accounts” filter is checked.
If you are looking for further information, please refer to the Bank Accounts section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Employer | Benefit Orders
chunks.content:
Employer | Benefit Orders
Benefit Orders are arrangements created by the TPA to arrange the Employer Plans associated with specific Service Categories and Codes created by the TPA and to enhance the claim entry process for auto-selecting the appropriate Plan during claim entry. Benefit Order determines the priority logic by which plans will attempt to reimburse participants for the submitted claims. Employer Benefit Order page can be accessed from the “Benefit Orders” link on the Employer dropdown menu on the navigation bar. On this page, a user can add, edit, view, and delete Benefit Orders at the Employer level.
Table of Contents
Add Employer Benefit Order
Edit Employer Benefit Order
Deleting Employer Benefit Order
Effective Date
To access Employer Benefit Orders
Go to the Employer tab in the main navigation bar.
Select Benefit Orders from the dropdown.
Select TPA and Employer from the drop-down list.
On this page, the user can view default Benefit Orders created at the TPA level for both debit cards and manual claims. By this default benefit order, the system will associate the Employer Plans with the default category based on their plan type.
The Employer-level Benefit Order will list only those Employer Plan Types in the default Benefit Order that actually exist at the Employer level. It will not list any other Employer Plan Types until the Employer adds them later. If no Benefit Orders are created at the TPA level, the TPA can use the default Benefit Orders created by the DataPath. The user may add, edit, and rearrange Employer Plans in the Benefit Order to prioritize Plans.

chunks.title: Employer | Benefit Orders
chunks.content:
Benefit Orders and their assigned services have effective dates, which provides the option to change Benefit Orders and their allowable services with a current or future effective date. This will allow administrators to change Benefit Orders for upcoming plan years ahead of the first day of the new plan year. Claims will be processed using the appropriate Benefit Order based on the claim’s service dates.
Add Employer Benefit Order
This page displays default Benefit Orders created at the TPA level. If an employer is created and no plans for the employer have been created yet, then this page will be blank.
To create a new Employer Benefit Order,
Click the “New Benefit Order” button on the right side.
A pop-up window will be displayed as shown below.
Enter the name for the Benefit Order. This is an alphanumeric field including the space. The Benefit Order name must be unique within the Employer and cannot be the same as the name of any TPA level Benefit Order.
Select Service Categories to associate with the Benefit Order. The user can select multiple Service Categories by checking respective check boxes in the list. Note that a Service Category can be associated with only one Benefit Order. When a claim is entered with a Service Category of the selected type(s), Summit will attempt to run the claim through the Benefit Order associated with that Service Category.
Select Plan Types from the given list to be included in the Benefit Order by checking the respective checkboxes. The list will include all the system standard Plan types and TPA custom types. Plan types can be associated with multiple Benefit Orders.
Arrange the list using Up and Down arrows to prioritize Plan types in the Benefit Order. Based on this ordering, plans will attempt to reimburse participants for the submitted claims.
After selecting Service Categories and Employer Plans, Service Codes will be displayed with an option to edit Service Code Characteristics.

chunks.title: Employer | Benefit Orders
chunks.content:
Click the Service Code icon to produce a pop-up for adding Service Code characteristics. After adding required details, click ‘OK’ to save.
Click ‘Save’ once you have completed creating the Benefit Order.  
Edit Employer Benefit Order
The page will display all the Benefit Orders that have been created at the TPA and Employer levels. You can use TPA level Benefit Order as it is or can edit it to have Employer level Benefit Orders. Next to each Plan in the Benefit Order, there will be a number indicating its priority. If needed, you can edit each Benefit Order and associated Service Categories and Plans.
To edit a Benefit Order,
Click the button ‘Edit’ next to the Benefit Order that you want to edit.
If the user clicks the edit button of Card Purse Order, then a pop-up window will be displayed as follows.
Edit name of the Benefit Order and rearrange associated plans if needed. The text in the square bracket along with the Benefit Order name shows at which level the respective Benefit Order was created. For example: Medical ER [TPA] shows that the Benefit Order Medical ER was created at the TPA level.
If the user clicks an edit button corresponding to a manual Benefit Order, then a pop-up window will be displayed as follows.
On this page, the user can edit the Benefit Order name, effective date, add or remove associated Categories and Plans by checking and unchecking the boxes.
Rearrange the order using Up and Down arrows if needed.
Edit Service Code characteristics by clicking the icon of the respective Service Code which you want to edit. After editing, click ‘OK’ to save.
Click Save to update changes.
Deleting Employer Benefit Order
Users may delete Employer Benefit orders so long as there are no claims associated with it.
Effective Date

chunks.content:
For each Employer Benefit Order record, Summit users with Read/Update access will be able to see the Effective Date. The Effective Date displayed is the latest date associated with the specific Employer Benefit Order record. The default Effective Date will be 1/1/1900.

chunks.title: Employer | Employer Central
chunks.content:
Employer | Employer Central
Employer Central is where Employer related information, such as Demographics, Benefit Plans, Health Plans, etc., is entered, displayed, and may be viewed or modified in Summit. Here, users can add or view and edit employer information.
Table of Contents
Add Employer
Demographics
Division
Benefit Plans
Schedules
Cards
Health Plans
Premium Billing
Notes
* Required fields appear in Red
To access Employer Central,
Go to Employer.
Click the menu “Employer Central” from the dropdown.
Select an Employer from the dropdown list either by Employer Name or Employer ID.
Add Employer
If the user wants to create a new Employer, then click the “Add Employer” button on the right side of the Employer Central landing page. An Employer can be created either via a setup wizard or manually.

The CDH and Premium Billing checkboxes will indicate which lines of service the Employer will have access to.
If the user selects Employer creation via the Wizard, they will be taken to the New Employer Setup Wizard page as shown below.
For more information, see the Employer | Employer Central | Wizard page.
Clicking the Manual button will take you to the Employer | Employer Central | Employer Demographics screen, where you will be able to manually setup the employer group tab-by-tab on the Employer Central interface.
Employer Central page has many sub tabs. The location of these tabs may vary from Employer to Employer based on feature access settings.
Demographics
This is the default tab that opens when a user accesses the Employer Central Employer page. The demographics tab represents all the information entered in step 1 of the Employer Set up Wizard. The user will have the option to edit any of this information at any time after the initial creation. If needed, the user can add any number of user-defined fields and assign Agencies to the Employer. An option to add a new Agency is also present. For more information, refer to the Employer Central Demographics page.
Division

chunks.title: Employer | Employer Central
chunks.content:
This is a tab containing all the Division, Location, and Union information for the employer. The user can create new Divisions, Locations, and Unions at any time or edit the existing ones. By clicking the Division/Location/Union Name, details associated with them will be open in a new tab for editing. For more information about the Division tab, see the Employer Central Division page.
Benefit Plans
On this tab, Summit users are able to view, add, and edit Employer benefit plans. Employer CDH Plan setup is described on the Employer CDH Plan page, and Employer PB Plan setup is described on the Employer PB Plan page.
Schedules
Schedules are pre-defined processes that are used to generate or post the Contributions or Remittances in batches. There are two types of schedules; Contribution Schedule and Remittance Schedule. A user can add, edit, and view created schedules in the Schedule tab of Employer Central Page. Also, users have the option to create on-demand remittances. Refer to Employer Central Schedules for information about schedule creation and modification.
Cards
Summit allows debit card feature. Debit Card is a way of electronic access to funds. TPAs issue debit cards to Participants, which would be linked to their benefit plans. Debit cards allow Participants to pay for the medical service or prescription or eligible purchase. If the Participant is at an eligible type of merchant, the system will allow for a deduction of funds in real time to pay for the expense. This new method results in the automation of fund access and reduced expenses for the TPA.
In the Employer Central Cards tab, a user can enable an Employer for card issuance and processing and also associate them with card settings and a Card Package. For additional information about Card Packages, see the Employer Central Cards page.
Health Plans

chunks.title: Employer | Employer Central
chunks.content:
Summit allows the user to manage Health Plans. A Health Plan is a type of insurance by which participants are reimbursed for medical expenses. The user can create, edit, and view Employer Health Plans and link participants with the created health plans. For detailed steps about the same, refer to the Employer Central Health Plans page.
Premium Billing
Premium Billing system is used to administer the collection of premiums from employees or former employees. Users have the ability to select Participant benefit plans, elect benefit rate tiers, and change the Participant’s benefit coverage status. Summit can bill the participant, handle the collection of remittances, and generate events and notifications for the elected coverages for COBRA, Retiree, and Direct Bill benefits. For more detailed information, please visit Employer Central Premium Billing.
Notes
This tab allows users to view notes and included attachments entered by DataPath and the TPA that are specific to the Employer. From this page, the user can view an existing note or delete a note or add a new note. Modification and deletion of notes is possible only when it has not been locked by another user. Employer users will not have the ability to add, edit or delete a note, but may have an ability to read a note. By default, notes that are marked as HIPAA will not be displayed when the notes section is accessed. For more detailed information, refer to Employer Central Notes.

chunks.title: Employer | Receipt Management | Settings
chunks.content:
Employer | Receipt Management | Settings
Receipts are documents used to verify the eligibility of expenses in a transaction. When a transaction cannot be auto-substantiated, the system will automatically generate letters/emails based on these Receipt Management templates to Participants asking them to send receipts or other documentation verifying the eligibility of the transaction. Once this notice is sent, the Receipt Management process will be turned off for that transaction and no additional steps will be taken by the system. Settings is the default tab that opens up when a user access Employer Receipt Management. A user can view and edit Employer Receipt Management Settings that are linked to TPA Default Receipt Management Settings. In this tab, the user is allowed to implement some of the basic settings that will apply to the overall Receipt Management process.
Table of Contents
Email Settings
Image settings
* Required fields appear in Red
To access Employer Receipt Management Settings,
Go to Employer.
Select “Receipt Management” menu from the dropdown.
Open the tab named “Settings”.
Select an Employer from the given dropdown list.
Assigned to Administrator Defaults – When this checkbox is checked, the Employer Receipt Management settings are linked to the TPA default settings. As long as this box remains checked, changes made at the TPA level will be reflected at the Employer level. If the user wishes to customize these settings at the Employer level, then de-select the checkbox. A pop-up warning will display when this checkbox is unchecked confirming that you wish to delink the employer from the TPA default settings.

chunks.title: Employer | Receipt Management | Settings
chunks.content:
Begin sending communications for transactions that were settled by the merchant after – This date field determines when Summit should send receipt request communications based on the settlement date for transactions. The default date is the TPA creation date [when the TPA account was first added to Summit]. The user can edit this date to a date in the past or the future by selecting a date from the calendar selector. The system will generate communications for all transactions that were settled after this specified date. If a past date is specified, all transactions in Receipt Requested status with a posted date on or after the specified date will trigger the Receipt Request process. No transactions before the specified date, nor transactions on or after the date in any other status, will trigger Receipt Request communications.
Initiate a Receipt Request _ days after the transaction settlement date if the transaction is still pending substantiation – This field determines the number of days after the transaction settlement date initiates a Receipt Request if the transaction is still pending substantiation. The user can enter a numeric value greater than or equal to 0 in the provided space. The default value is zero.
Only show the last four digits of the Participant ID on communications – This checkbox is unchecked by default. By checking this box, the communications produced will show only the last 4 digits of the primary Participant ID that is entered by the TPA or the default ID.

chunks.title: Employer | Receipt Management | Settings
chunks.content:
Suspend templates – This checkbox is unchecked by default. When this is checked, the processing of e-mails/letters based on the template will be suspended and an icon will appear right to the check box. The TPA level template will be considered to be “Active” at all times unless this is selected. Transactions that will be included on communications will queue until this is de-selected. If a processing date was missed while this was selected, when the check is removed, the process will run that day.
Post processing alerts – This is an e-mail alert configured by the user to be sent once the communication process had completed its run based on the template. The completion of communication file creation/ e-mail generation should trigger this e-mail.
The user must check the Post processing alerts checkbox and add recipients of this email alert by clicking the “Assign Users” link. The link will produce a pop-up containing the list of all existing TPA users with checkboxes. The user can select up to 10 users to receive this alert.
When the selection is saved, the page will list all the e-mail addresses associated with the selected users in a box on the page. If needed, the user can add additional e-mail addresses manually as long as the total number of addresses does not exceed 10.
Email Settings
In this section, the user can configure various settings related to receipt request e-mails. The fields in this section include:

chunks.title: Employer | Receipt Management | Settings
chunks.content:
Set From address as – This is a mandatory alphanumeric text field that sets the address from which receipt request e-mails should be sent. By default, this field will auto-populate with the email address “communications@summitwith.us. In addition, TPAs will no longer be able to make changes to their From email address within Summit to avoid the possibility that communications sent from the new address will be seen as email spoofing. This is a function performed by DataPath personnel at the request of TPA-authorized personnel. In order to customize the From email address in Summit, you will need to work with your IT personnel or hosting provider to update the DNS settings for your custom domain; once the DNS settings have been updated, you may contact your Client Services representative to assist you with changing your Summit “From” address.
Auto–forward a copy of all cardholder communications – This checkbox is unchecked by default. When this box is selected, the user can enter an e-mail address in the “Forward to” field.
Forward to – This field will be mandatory if the user checks the “Auto-forward a copy of all cardholder e-mail communications” checkbox. Here the user must enter an e-mail address to which all cardholder communications via the template will be forwarded.
Image settings
This section allows the user to configure various image settings. The minimum size of the image should be 300X100 pixels and must be saved as .gif, .jpg, or .png.
Change Photo – When the user clicks “Change Photo”, an option to browse files will be made available. Thus, the user can choose and upload an image there.
Image Location – After uploading an image, the user can select the location where they want the image to appear in their communications. There are three options. They are, “Left”, “Center,” and “Right”. These positions indicate where the image will appear on the top of the letter/e-mail.
Click ‘Save’ after entering all the required information to save the settings.

chunks.title: Employer | Reimbursement Settings
chunks.content:
Employer | Reimbursement Settings
Reimbursement is a process of paying money to Participants for the out-of-pocket expenses for an eligible service or product. The purpose of the Employer Reimbursement Settings page is to configure default values at the Employer level that will drive the reimbursement process. A user can view and edit Reimbursement Settings for specific employers on this page. These settings may be linked to the TPA Default Reimbursement Settings or they may be tailored for the specific employer.
Table of Contents
Reimbursement Settings
General Settings
Duplicate Claims
Banking/Checking
Schedules
Communications
To access Employer Reimbursement Settings,
Go to Employer.
Select “Reimbursement Settings” menu from the dropdown.
Select the Employer.
NOTE: The Employer dropdown does not have a default “Select Employer” option. The page will show data for the last selected Employer. If no Employer is selected, no data will be displayed until one is chosen.
Reimbursement Settings
There are five tabs on the Reimbursement Settings page: “General Settings”, “Duplicate Claims”, “Banking/Checking”, “Schedules”, and “Communications”.
The settings in each of these tabs will correspond to the employer group selected in the employer dropdown on this page and to that employer only.
Assigned to Administrator Defaults – This checkbox indicates that Employer’s Reimbursement Settings are the same as the TPA default settings. As long as this box remains checked, changes updated at the TPA level will reflect at the Employer level also. If the user wishes to customize these settings for the selected employer, they must first de-select this checkbox. This box is checked by default for all new employer groups.
General Settings

chunks.title: Employer | Reimbursement Settings
chunks.content:
General Settings is the default tab that opens up when a user accesses Employer Reimbursement Settings. It is the leftmost tab of the Reimbursement Settings page. This tab contains run-out/timeout logic settings as well as an option to include or exclude the system-generated claim number on participant communications and the Participant Portal. To know more about each field on the General Settings page, refer Employer | Reimbursement Settings | General Settings.
Duplicate Claims
In this tab, the user can configure Employer-level Duplicate Claim detection logic to identify and prevent the creation of duplicate claims. For a detailed explanation of the Duplicate Claims detection logic settings in this tab see the Employer | Reimbursement Settings | Duplicate Claims page.
Banking/Checking
In this tab, the user can set up the necessary settings for the Employer Reimbursement Account from which reimbursements will be issued, as well as configure the Debit Card Settlement account and other Employer level banking settings used by the Summit for the purpose of creating payments. Refer Employer | Reimbursement Settings | Banking/Checking page to get detailed information about various Employer level banking settings.
Schedules
This tab allows the user to set up and configure batch processes for the creation of reimbursements. A user can add, edit and view schedules at the Employer level in the Schedules tab of the Employer Reimbursement Settings Page. See the Employer | Reimbursement Settings | Schedules page for a detailed look at Employer-level reimbursement schedule creation.
Communications
This tab contains the settings for how Summit will handle communications related to claims, including Approval, Denial, and Request letters, and allows the text of these communications to be modified globally for both emails and physical letters. To learn more, refer Employer | Reimbursement Settings | Communications.

chunks.title: Employer | Reimbursement Settings
chunks.content:
For further information, see the pages for the respective tab or refer to the Reimbursement Settings section in FAQs.

Employer
Summit is primarily a tool for administering group benefits. As such, it offers extensive employer management capabilities to administrators.

Reimbursement Settings
The Employer page serves as an umbrella for accessing the demographics and settings particular to your employer clients as well as allowing you to manually add and configure new employer groups.
The Employer page and its sub-pages may be accessed from the ribbon.
Employer Central
Employer Central and its subtabs are where you will be able to add, view, and edit employers’ information and configure administrative settings at an employer-level.
When first accessing Employer Central, you will be presented with a Search page that will allow you to search for and select the employer you wish to manage.
Employer Search Page

Receipt Management
Receipts are documents used to verify the eligibility of expenses in a transaction. When a transaction cannot be auto-substantiated, the Summit will automatically generate letters/ emails to Participants requesting them to submit receipts or other documentations for expenses that cannot be auto-substantiated. Once this notice is sent, the Receipt Management process will be turned off for that transaction and no additional steps will be taken by the system.
The logic and settings for communications pertaining to these receipts may be configured at the employer level from the Receipts Management module.
Receipt Management will open to the Receipt Management | Settings page by default.
In addition to the Settings page, Receipt Management also has a Request page and a Processing page.
Benefit Orders

chunks.title: Employer
chunks.content:
Summit allows for the administration of multiple plans and benefits offered by employers and elected by participants. In order to handle the logic of how claims submitted against myriad employer-offered plans should reimburse, a Benefit Order must be established.
The Benefit Order is used by Summit to determine which plans should pay out and in what order based on the plan designs and the types of claims submitted by the participants.
These Benefit Orders are configured on a by-Employer basis.
Employer MCCs
Summit allows plan reimbursement logic to be tied to Merchant Category Codes at point of sale by associating MCCs and MCC Categories to benefit plans. MCC and Auto-Substantiation logic as it pertains to card claims may be configured on this page and its tabs on a by-employer basis, overriding the TPA default settings configured in your administrator-level Default Card Settings.
Bank Accounts
Summit allows for the addition and management of multiple bank accounts for assignment to Employers. These accounts may be used for claim reimbursement, debit card settlement, ACH remittance, fee payments, etc.
Reimbursement Settings
Summit creates reimbursement payments based on several logic settings that can be configured at the Administrator default level, or on a by-employer basis. The Employer | Reimbursement Settings page allows for creating customized variations from Administrator default that may be assigned to individual employer groups.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Account Detail
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Account Detail
The Account Detail Page displays all the relevant information regarding the selected Benefit of the user.
Table of Contents
Account Detail Page
Account Detail for Annual Renewal plans
FSA with carryover
FSA without carryover
HRA with carryover
HRA without carryover
Account Detail for Open-Ended plans
To navigate to the Account Detail page,
Go to the Home page of the Summit Mobile App.
Tap on the benefit listed under the Benefits section:
Account Detail Page
All relevant details of the selected benefit will display on this page. The details that the participant will see on this page are determined by the selected plan and may differ based on the plan type and whether the plan is Open-Ended or Annual Renewal. The user can swipe left or right between records when viewing benefit details rather than tapping “back” and selecting a new record.
When a record is displaying and the user touches their screen, an indicator that they may swipe between the records will display. On iPhone devices, a swipe icon will display whereas dots will indicate the selected record in sequence on Android devices.
Account Detail for Annual Renewal plans
FSA with carryover
An FSA account will display the same detail as the Dependent Care or any other Annual Renewal plans, but the balance will be based on the Annual Election rather than the contributions.
Plan Detail – This will display the name of the plan.
Carryover Balance – This is the carryover balance of the selected FSA, if there is any.
Annual Election – The annual election amount will display here.
Contributions YTD – The total amount of contributions made during the plan year-to-date will be shown here.
Reimbursements YTD – This will display the total amount of reimbursements made during the plan year-to-date.
Pending Debits – The total amount of any pending debits for the selected plan will be displayed here.
Balance – This will show the disbursable balance of the selected plan.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Account Detail
chunks.content:
Explanatory Text – Explanatory Text accompanies the Available Balance field based on the plan type and whether the plan has a carryover balance. For FSA Plans with carryover: “Balance equals Carryover Balance plus Annual Election less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits”
Contribution Per Pay Period – The dollar amount of the contribution made each pay period. This will typically be the Annual Election divided by the total number of pay periods throughout the plan year.
Recent Transactions – Pressing this button will take the user to the Recent Transactions page which lists all the recent transactions for the selected plan.
Linked Dependents – This section will display all the linked dependents of the participant under the selected plan.
FSA without carryover
When the carryover balance is zero, the line item for the carryover balance will not be displayed, and the balance explanation text will be as shown below.
“Balance equals Annual Election less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits.”
HRA with carryover
An HRA account will display the same detail as any other Annual Renewal plans, but the balance will be based on Contributions, rather than the Annual Election.
Funding Method – Contribution Schedule
The Balance Explanatory text will be “Balance equals Benefit Value (YTD Employer Contributions) plus Carryover Balance less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits.”
Funding Method – Single Fund
The Balance Explanatory text will be “Balance equals Benefit Value plus Carryover Balance less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits.”
HRA without carryover
When the carryover balance is zero, the line item for the carryover balance will not be displayed.
Funding Method – Contribution Schedule
The Balance Explanatory text will be “Balance equals Benefit Value (YTD Employer Contributions) less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits.”
Funding Method – Single Fund
The Balance Explanatory text will be “Balance equals Benefit Value less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits.”

chunks.title: Mobile App | Account Detail
chunks.content:
Other Annual Election Plans with Carryover
The balance explanatory text will be “Balance equals Carryover Balance plus Contributions YTD less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits.”
Other Annual Election Plans without Carryover
The balance explanatory text will be “Balance equals Contributions YTD less Reimbursements YTD less Pending Debits.”
Account Detail for Open-Ended plans
Open-ended plans, such as HSAs, will have a different page layout for Account Detail.
Account Detail – The name of the plan will display here.
Total Accounts Value – The total value of all accounts in the selected plan.
Investment – The total investment amount if the user has made any investments using his/her HSA. This item will only be displayed if the selected HSA plan is investment-enabled and the user has enrolled for investments.
Pending Debits – The total amount of any pending debits for the selected plan.
Balance – The disbursable balance of the selected plan.
Contribution Per Pay Period – The dollar amount of the contribution made per pay period. This will typically be the Annual Election divided by the total number of pay periods throughout the plan year.
Reimbursements To Date – The total reimbursement amount to date.
Contributions To Date – The total amount of contributions made to date.
Recent Transactions – Pressing this button will take the user to the Recent Transactions page which lists all the recent transactions for the selected plan.
View Investments – This button will only be displayed if the selected plan is investment-enabled and the participant has enrolled in investments. Clicking on this button will redirect the user to the Investments page which displays all the details regarding the participant’s investments.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Account Detail
chunks.content:
Account Statements – Participant users can access their available HSA tax forms and account statements (both monthly and annual statements) via the Account Statements button. Clicking on this button will redirect the user to the following page where they can select the statement type and tax form using the radio button.
For monthly statements, both year and month dropdowns will appear whereas, for annual statements and tax forms, only a year dropdown will appear.
Once the user has selected the forms, click the “Get Tax Statement” button. The account statements can be downloaded to the user’s device as PDFs. Downloaded statements will be available in the “Downloads” folder of Android devices and in the “Summit” folder of iOS devices.
If no option is selected, an alert saying “Please select an option” will display.
Examples of:
Monthly Statement
Annual Statement
Tax Form
If no statement is available for the participant, an alert will display that there is no statement details available.
Linked Dependents – This section will display all the linked dependents of the participant under the selected plan.

Mobile App | Banking

Table of Contents
Banking Page
Adding a Bank Account
TPA-Initiated Auto Draft
Participants with No Bank Accounts
To navigate to the Banking Page:
Go to the Profile page of the Summit Mobile App.
Press the Banking button:
Banking Page
The details of each bank account will be displayed inside a card layout on the Banking page. A participant can have a maximum of two bank accounts added to his or her profile and assign one account as the default bank account. The default bank account will be displayed first in the list.
The bank details are displayed in read-only format inside the card layout as shown here:
Bank Name – The name of the bank as entered into the system.
Account Number – The account number will be masked, showing only the last 4 digits.
Routing Number – The routing number of the bank as entered into the system.
Account Type – The account type denotes whether it is a savings account or a checking account.
Default – The card layout for the default account will have a text denoting it is the default account.
Pencil (Edit) Icon – Tapping on the Pencil icon displayed inside the card layout will take the user to the Edit Banking page. Only those participants with “Allow updates to participant bank details” option enabled will have this Pencil icon.
If the “Allow updates to participant bank details” option is not enabled for a participant, then the Pencil icon will not be displayed and the page will display a note below the bank account(s) that says “Please contact your administrator to make changes to your bank account.” Clicking on the note with the “contact” hyperlink will take the user to the TPA Contact page.
Adding a Bank Account
Summit Mobile app restricts the number of bank accounts linked to a profile to two.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Banking
chunks.content:
If a participant has not added a bank account or has only added one bank account, and the “Allow updates to participant bank details” option is enabled for the participant, then the banking page will display a button to Add a Bank Account as shown below.
Pressing the button will take the user to the Add Banking page. If the option “Allow updates to participant bank details” is disabled for the participant, then the Add A Bank Account button will not be displayed.
Bank Name – In this searchable dropdown list, all the bank names from Summit’s database will be populated. The user can select the desired bank name from the list or by typing in the bank name. The user can also add a new bank which is not already listed in the dropdown by selecting the “Other” option from the bank name dropdown. When “Other” is selected, a new text field to enter the bank name will display.
Routing Number – Routing numbers for the selected bank will auto populate in the routing number dropdown list. This dropdown will be enabled only if the user has selected a bank account. Here also, the user can add a new routing number which is not already listed in the dropdown by selecting the “Other” option from the routing number dropdown. When “Other” is selected, a new text field to enter the routing number will display.
Account Number – Enter the Account Number associated with the bank account here.
Account Type – Here the user must select the type of account by choosing either “Checking” or “Savings”.
Default Account – By selecting/unselecting this box, the user can specify whether the entered bank account will be used as the default account or not.
Once the user has entered and selected details for the account, they may press the Add button to add the new bank details to Summit.
TPA-Initiated Auto Draft

chunks.title: Mobile App | Banking
chunks.content:
If the user selects ‘Default Account’ in the Add/Edit Banking page and the ‘Allow Premium Payment Auto Draft Opt-in’ option is enabled for the participant, then the page will display a checkbox for the TPA-Initiated auto draft option as shown below.
Participant will only be able to opt into Auto Draft if recurring payments have not been scheduled. Enabling this option will cancel all the scheduled payments.
Participants with No Bank Accounts
If a participant has no bank account added, the Banking page will display a note depending on whether the “Allow updates to participant bank details” option is enabled or disabled. If “Allow updates to participant bank details” is enabled for the participant, the Banking page will display a note that says “You do not have a bank account set up. Set one up now.” Clicking on the “Set one up now” text link will open the Add Banking page.
If the “Allow updates to participant bank details” option is not enabled for the participant, the Banking page will display a note that says: “You do not have a bank account set up. Please contact your administrator to add your bank account”. Clicking on the note with the “Contact” hyperlink will take the user to the TPA Contact page.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Cards
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Cards
The Cards page displays the details of the card(s) issued to a participant and any dependents. The user can also report the card Lost/Stolen and can request a PIN change from the Cards page.
Table of Contents
Cards Page
Dependent Page
Report Lost/Stolen
Request PIN Change
TPA/Employer Level Card Block
To navigate to the Cards page,
Go to the Home page of the Summit Mobile App.
Press the View My Cards button on the home page.
OR
Tap on the three-line menu and select Cards.
Cards Page
All the relevant details of cards allocated to a participant and their dependent (if any) will display on this page. The user will have the option to request a PIN change and report the card as Lost/Stolen on this page.
The following details are displayed inside the card layout that resembles an actual debit card.
Card Number – The last four digits of the card number will be displayed here.
Effective Date – The date on which the card became effective will be displayed here.
Expiration Date –The expiration date of the card will be displayed here.
Name on Card – The name of the card holder will be displayed here.
Status – The status of the card will be displayed here.
The Details section contains the following information:
Mailed Date – The date on which the card was mailed will be displayed here.
Mailed To – The address of the participant to where the card was mailed. This will be a text link. Clicking on the link will display the mailed address as a pop-up.
Shipping Method – The method used to ship the card will be displayed here.
Tracking Number – The tracking number of the shipment will be displayed here.
Dependent Card Section – The Dependents with Card section will list the dependents of the participant with a card issued for them. Clicking on the dependent item will redirect the user to the Dependents card page where they can view the card details for the selected dependent.
Dependent Page

chunks.title: Mobile App | Cards
chunks.content:
The Dependents page displays all card details for a dependent. The user can navigate to this page by clicking on the Dependent item in the “Dependents with card” section on the cards page. Dependents have the options to report the card as lost or stolen and to request a PIN change.
Report Lost/Stolen
Participants and their dependents with active cards have the option to report their card as lost or stolen. If the “Allow Lost/Stolen Replacements” setting is turned off by the TPA or Employer, then the existing card will be marked as Lost/Stolen, and a confirmation message that says “You have reported your card as Lost/Stolen” will display when the user presses on the Report Lost/Stolen button on the Cards page.
If the “Allow Lost/Stolen Replacements” setting is turned on, the user will be redirected to the Report Lost/Stolen page, where they can view and edit their mailing address and proceed with the request for a new card. The card replacement fee will be displayed as a note above the address. The replacement fee is the same as the card issuance fee set by the TPA for the employer.
Request PIN Change
Users have the option to change the card PIN from the mobile application. Pressing the Request PIN button on the Cards page will redirect the user to the Request PIN page. The user can change their card PIN on this page by answering the security question they set during the time of initial registration. Upon validation, the PIN will be changed to the new one entered by the user. A “PIN saved successfully” confirmation message will display after the user presses the Save button.
TPA/Employer Level Card Block
When a TPA/Employer Card Block is in place for an Employer, a message will display for all participant users associated with the blocked employer.
When an Employer block is in place, the following message will display on the Cards Page.
“There is currently an Employer Level Block applied. Card activity is suspended.”

Mobile App | Contact
The Contact Page of Summit Mobile App displays the contact information of the user’s Third-Party Administrator (TPA).
Table of Contents
Contact Page
Contact Page
By selecting the “Contact” option from the three-line menu, the user can navigate to the Contact page.
The Contact screen will display the TPA’s contact details in a card layout as shown below:
TPA – The first line of contact information will be the name of TPA.
Address – Here, the TPA mailing address will be shown.
Phone – The contact number of the TPA will display here. When the user clicks on the text link, the phone dialer of the mobile phone opens with this phone number.
Fax – This field shows the fax number of the TPA as a text link.
Email– The Email address of the TPA will display here. When the user clicks on the text link, the default email client in the mobile phone will open with this email address in the recipient list.
Website – If available, the TPA website URL will be displayed here.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Coverage Details
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Coverage Details
The Coverage Details page displays all the relevant information regarding a selected coverage. Users with at least one PB coverage will have a “Billing” section on their Home Page. The billing section will list the Premium Billing coverages of the participant along with other details. Tapping on any of the PB coverage items from the list will take the user to the Coverage Details page.
Table of Contents
Coverage Details Page
Events
Premium Amount Due Label
To navigate to the Coverage Details page,
Go to the Home page of the Summit Mobile App.
Tap on the PB coverage under the Billing section.
Coverage Details Page
All the relevant details of the selected coverage will be displayed on this page. When the user selects a particular PB coverage item from the billing list to view its details, the user will be directed to the Coverage Details page.
The user can swipe left or right between records when viewing coverage details rather than tapping “back” and selecting a new record. When a record is displaying and the user touches their screen, an indicator that they may swipe between the records will display. On iPhone devices, a swipe icon will display whereas dots will indicate the selected record in sequence on Android devices.
Coverage Plan Type – The Coverage plan type populates in the Coverage field.
Coverage Name – The Coverage Name displays in the Coverage Name field next to the Coverage plan type. 
Coverage Status – The Coverage Status displays under the Coverage Name. 
Tier/Level – The coverage Tier/Level values display in the Tier/Level field next to the Coverage Status.
Premium Amount Due Label – The Total Amount Due On label will be displayed based on whether or not a custom billing schedule is in use.
Start Date – The coverage’s start date displays in the Start Date field. 
Expiration Date – The coverage’s end date or Expiration Date displays in the Expiration Date field.
Current Due Date – The Due Date of the current billing period.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Coverage Details
chunks.content:
Current Amount Due – The Current Amount Due as of today’s date.
Next Due Date – The Due Date of the next unpaid billing period displays here. If no future billing periods exist, the field will be left blank.
Next Amount Due – The Amount Due for the next unpaid billing period displays here. If no future billing periods exist, this field will display $0.00.
Paid Through Date – The coverage’s Paid Through Date will be displayed.
View Fullfilled Notification Events – The user will be taken to the Events page, when this link is clicked.
Events
The events page displays fulfilled premium billing notification events when the participant selects a coverage from the Billing section. If “Display in Participant History” (in event settings) is enabled for a particular event, that event will display on the Events page. The Events page is only available to participants with Premium Billing coverages.
All events with an event date for the selected coverage will display in this section. Events that do not have a Sent Date will not display on this screen. Any event that has an associated attachment will display as a link. A participant may click the linked event to view the associated notification details and they may click the notification details to download and view the notification itself.
Premium Amount Due Label
The Total Amount Due On label will display based on whether or not a custom billing schedule is in use.
If a participant’s coverage is not associated with a custom billing schedule, the “Total Amount Due On” label will instead read “Amount billed every month on the 1st.”
If a participant’s coverage is associated with a custom billing frequency, the “Total Amount Due On” label will instead read “Amount billed every [frequency occurrence] on [days/day of month]” based on the custom billing frequency’s settings.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Coverage Details
chunks.content:
In cases when a date is added to the custom billing schedule or if a day is skipped, an exception note will display informing the participant to “Contact your administrator for billing frequency exceptions.”

chunks.content:
Mobile App | Forgot Password
The Forgot Password page is used to retrieve the user account by resetting the forgotten password.
Table of Contents
Forgot Password Page
Password Change Page
To navigate to the Forgot Password Page:
Go to the Login Page of the Summit Mobile App.
Press the Forgot Password button:
Forgot Password Page
The Forgot Password page will appear as shown below:
To reset the forgotten password:
Enter the TPA ID/URL of the user.
Enter the Email/Username.
Now, press the Reset Password button to proceed.
If the entered values are valid, then a success alert will be shown as seen below:
If the user has entered an invalid TPA ID or Username/Email, then an error alert will be shown:
