chunks.title: Mobile App | Home
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Home
Table of Contents
CDH Only Participant
PB Only Participant
Participant with CDH and PB
The layout of the home page is based on the type of participant. The home page contents will be different for each participant depending on which category they are in. Icons and sections will be displayed differently according to the following categories:
CDH only participant
PB only participant
Participant with CDH and PB
CDH Only Participant
A participant with CDH only benefits will have a Benefits section and an “I Want To” section on the Home Page. The Benefits section will display a list of user CDH benefits.
PB Only Participant
A participant with PB only benefits will have no features such as Enter A Claim, Withdrawal, or Cards. Therefore, the home page for a PB only participant will have the Billing section and an “I Want To” section with options ‘View Recent Transactions’, ‘View My Alerts’, and ‘Update My Profile’.
Participant with CDH and PB
The home page of a participant with both PB and CDH benefits will have three sections; Billing, Benefits, and I Want To.
Hamburger Menu – The top left corner of the Home page will have a Hamburger menu, which will list options to navigate to all the available pages in the Summit Mobile app. The Hamburger menu will be displayed on all the main pages in the app except the subpages.
Billing Section – The Billing section will be displayed for those participants who have at least one Premium Billing coverage.
Pay Now link – By clicking on the Pay Now link, the user will be navigated to the Make A Payment page. The “Pay Now” link will only be displayed in the Billing Section if the participant has PB coverage and has a premium due.
Total Amount Due – The sum of the current amount due for all the Premium Billing coverages will be displayed at the top left corner of the Billing section along with the due date.
Last Payment Received – Here the amount of the last payment received will be displayed with the received date.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Home
chunks.content:
Last Check Number – The check number of the last payment received.
Recurring Payments – By clicking this link, the user can set up recurring payments. The participant will only be able to set up recurring payments if the TPA-Initiated Auto Draft option has not been selected.
View Scheduled Payments – Here the user can review scheduled payments.
Clicking the “Pay Now” link on the billing section will open the Make A Payment screen. The Make A Payment screen allows the user to make a scheduled one-time payment. The current system date will default as the payment date, however, the participant may select a different date by clicking on the display. Payment will be for the amount due.
Benefits List – Here, the list of all active PB benefits and their premiums will display. Clicking on this will navigate the user to the Coverage Details page.
Benefits Section – The Benefits section will display all the active and prior year benefits and their balances on the Home page for those participants with CDH benefits. Benefit cards linked to plans with an Annual Renewal type Plan Structure will be displayed with the Plan Year’s range and cards linked to plans with an Open Ended type Plan Structure will be displayed with the Plan Effective Date. By clicking on a particular benefit from the benefits list, the user will be navigated to the Account Detail page of the respective benefit.
I Want To section – The user can navigate to the inner pages using this quick access menu.
Enter A Claim – Navigates the user to the Enter A Claim/Withdrawal page.
Request A Withdrawal – Navigates the user to the Make A Withdrawal page.
Make A Deposit – Navigates the user to the Make A Deposit page.
Claims Vault – Navigates the user to the Claims Vault page.
View Recent Transactions – Navigates the user to the Transactions page.
View My Expenses By Category – Navigates the user to the Expense Pie Chart page.
View My Cards – Navigates the user to the Cards page.

chunks.content:
View My Alerts – Navigates the user to the Alerts page. The Alerts icon will display a red dot when there is an unread alert for the participant.
Update My Profile – Navigates the user to the Profile page.
For a PB only user, the I Want To section will have the following options:
View Recent Transactions – Same as described above.
View My Alerts – Same as described above.
Update My Profile – Same as described above.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Investments
Summit allows for individually-owned HSAs to be investment-enabled, meaning that participants who own those accounts may invest their account funds, over $1000.00, using Summit’s Investments platform on the Mobile. If a participant has an investment-enabled benefit and has set up an investment on the Participant portal, then the user will see the View Investments option on the Mobile app.
Table of Contents
Investments Page
Investments Section
I Want To Section
View Contributions Breakdown
View My Portfolio
View Market Value Breakdown
View Shares Breakdown
Rebalance Investment
Pending Transactions
Transfer Fund-to-Fund
View Detail Trade History
Liquidate To Savings
View Statement of Investment
View Investment Disclaimer
View Privacy Policy
To navigate to the Investments Page,
Go to the Benefits section of the Home page on the Summit Mobile App.
Click on the HSA Benefit.
In the Account Detail screen, click on the “View Investments” button.
Investments Page
The Investments page will appear as shown below. The users who have not made investments will only have the “View Contributions Breakdown” menu in the I Want To section.
Investments Section
Investment – The Investment balance the participant has will be displayed here.
Investment Description – A description with the fund evaluation date will be displayed here. An example would be “Investment balance based on the fund evaluation as of 09/10/2023 23:08:50 PM”.
Investment Model – The Investment Model the participant selected will be displayed here.
Investment Allocation – This will be the Investment Allocation percentage selected by the participant.
Investment Allocation Description – A description about the Investment Allocation percentage that says “Percentage of future contributions to invest” will be displayed under the Investment Allocation.
Edit Icon – A Pencil icon for editing the investment details appears at the top right corner. Clicking on this icon will take the user to the Edit Investment screen.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
The Edit Investment modal displays the following fields:
Balance – The current account balance the participant has displays here.
Investment –The investment balance of the participant displays here.
Investment balance description – A description with the fund evaluation date displays here. An example would be “Investment balance based on the fund evaluation as of 03/22/2023 23:05:09 PM”.
Total Accounts Value – The total accounts value displays here.
Invest Future Contributions Info Icon – An info icon that opens a popup that says “The default is 0% which means every dollar deposited will remain in savings. If you set the percentage to 100%, then every dollar over the $1,000 threshold will be invested. An entry of 25% means that 25 cents of every dollar will be invested into your chosen allocation model and 75 cents will be directed to savings”.
Invest Future Contributions – This text field allows the user to set an investment allocation for future contributions. Here the participant can enter what percentage of contributions will be invested in the selected Investment Model. Only contributions made after the percentage is defined and saved will be subject to investment. For example, if the percentage is 50% and the contribution amount is $100.00 then $50.00 will go to the cash account and $50.00 will be invested in the selected Investment Model. Also, note that the participant must have more than $1000 in cash to invest initially.
Invest Available Cash Info Icon – This info icon opens a popup that says “You can invest every dollar in your balance over $1,000 into your chosen allocation model”.
You can invest up to – The participant’s maximum investment limit displays here. This limit is calculated by the participant’s available uninvested account balance less the minimum $1,000 reserve balance.
Invest Available Cash – Here, the user can enter the amount to be invested.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
Choose Investment Model – These radio buttons allow the user to select an investment model. The user is able to select from Conservative, Moderately Conservative, Balanced, Moderately Aggressive, Aggressive, and Custom investment models. Each item has a description and a link to view the detailed breakdown of the model that will be displayed when the radio button is clicked. For the custom investment model, no breakdown is provided. Given below are the detailed pie charts for the conservative and aggressive investment models.
Conservative Growth Portfolio – This selection is recommended for an investor who seeks to allocate a large percentage of their portfolio to lower-risk securities such as fixed-income securities. The main goal of a conservative portfolio is to protect the principal value of your portfolio. That is why these models are often called “capital preservation portfolios.” Even if you are very conservative and are tempted to avoid the stock market entirely, some risk exposure in selected funds can help offset inflation. The suggested time frame for this risk allocation is at least 5 years.
Moderately Conservative Growth Portfolio – This selection is recommended for an investor who seeks to preserve most of the portfolio’s total value but is willing to take on some risk for inflation protection. A common strategy within this risk level is called “current income.” This includes securities that pay a higher level of dividends. The suggested investor’s time frame for this model is at least 5 to 8 years. 
Balanced Growth Portfolio – This selection is for an investor who seeks a balance between the preservation of account value and the portfolio risk. The goal is a near even split between low risk fix-income securities and higher-risk growth securities. This strategy also includes securities that pay a higher level of dividends. The investor’s time frame for investing in this model should be medium term or greater than 8 years.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
Moderately Aggressive Growth Portfolio – This selection is for an investor who has a longer-term strategy, of greater than 10 years. This investor is willing to take a medium to higher level of risk to achieve portfolio growth, while still diversifying the portfolio by including fixed-income securities. The strategy is often called the “capital growth” strategy. To provide diversification, the portfolio includes fix-income securities.
Aggressive Growth Portfolio – This selection is for an investor with a long-term investment strategy of greater than 12 to 15 years. This investor is willing to accept that their portfolio value can fluctuate widely from day to day. The main goal of this model is to achieve long-term growth of capital. The strategy of an aggressive portfolio is considered a “capital growth” strategy. To provide diversification, investors with aggressive portfolios usually add some fixed-income securities.
Custom – This selection is recommended for an investor who wishes to have a customized portfolio rather than choosing a pre-defined investment model. If this is the selected investment model, the user can choose from the list of available funds to allocate their investments.
Clicking the “Next” button will take the user to the Changing your Investment Direction page. For the custom investment model, the user can enter % based custom allotments for each fund. When editing a Custom Model, the Current% column will display the current percentages and the New% column will be set to 0 as default which can be updated.
For other investment models, the New% column will be read-only and pre-populated with default values.
The total percentage must be equal to 100. If a user presses “Submit” and the totals do not equal 100%, a warning text will display informing the user that amounts must equal 100% to proceed.
Once percentages have been allocated to available funds, press “Submit” to confirm participant choices.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
The user will be then navigated to an Investment Confirmation Screen where they can view the investment details along with the chosen funds and their allocated percentages.
I Want To Section
The I want to section of the Investments screen has the following options:
View Contributions Breakdown
View My Portfolio
View Market Value Breakdown
View Shares Breakdown
Rebalance Investment
Pending Transactions
Transfer Fund-to-Fund
View Detail Trade History
Liquidate To Savings
View Statement of Investment
View Contributions Breakdown
By clicking on this menu, the participant will be able to view the amount of each per pay period contribution that is invested in each fund, based on the selected model as shown below. Also, the total contribution per pay period and the total investment amount in dollars will be displayed here.
View Breakdown of Prior Contribution – Here, the user can view per pay period contributions’ breakdown in each fund for prior pay periods. This link will display only if there are any prior contributions.
View My Portfolio
Here a table showing portfolio details of the participant such as Fund, Number of Shares, and Market Value will be displayed. The portfolio balance of the participant will be displayed below the Portfolio details table.
View Market Value Breakdown
By clicking on this menu, the participant can view a pie chart for the selected investment model that shows the market value of each fund. The savings and investments market value in dollars will be displayed here.
View Shares Breakdown
Clicking on this menu will take the user to their Shares Breakdown graph. The savings and investments share in percentage can also be viewed here.
Rebalance Investment

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
Participants can rebalance their HSA investment balances through the Summit Mobile App. Clicking on this menu will take the user to the Rebalance Portfolio page. The Rebalance Investment Model page will include options to confirm whether the user wishes to proceed with the rebalance along with static text explaining what the rebalance is and how it will affect their investments.
After confirming the rebalance, users will be redirected to a confirmation page.
The user may cancel the Rebalance Request before the request has been processed. If the request has not been processed and the user clicks the Rebalance Investment, a screen will open informing the user that a rebalance order exists and allowing the user to cancel the order.
Pending Transactions
The Rebalance Investment action will be listed in the Pending Transactions queue. The Rebalance request may be cancelled from the Pending Transactions queue if it has not yet been processed.
Transfer Fund-to-Fund
The Transfer Fund to Fund option will allow users to initiate the sale of shares from one fund to buy shares for another.
Note that this will only be available if the account owner is using a custom investment model. If the user selects this option but does not have custom investments selected, the following message will display:
When the user selects the Transfer Fund to Fund option and has custom allocations enabled, they will be taken to the Fund-to-Fund Transfer screen, where they must select the fund from which they wish to transfer funds to. Only one fund may be selected.
Once the fund has been selected, users will be prompted to enter a dollar amount or a percentage amount based on the selected Transfer Type.
Dollar Amount Transfer Type
Percentage Amount Transfer Type
The App will validate that an appropriate value has been entered before allowing the participant to continue to the next screen.
The user will then be taken to a screen listing all available funds.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
Users will be able to select one or multiple funds to transfer the funds to. If selecting multiple funds, the user must enter a percentage amount to specify the allocation of funds. Percentages must add up to 100%.
Once the user has selected the fund(s), they may click Submit to complete the Transfer.
The user will then be taken to a confirmation page, which will list details of the investment action taken.
The user will be sent the Investment Fund-to-Fund Transfer notice.
View Detail Trade History
When this option is clicked, the user will be taken to the Detail Trade History page for invested HSA funds.
The Detail Trade History page will include a dropdown of all funds in which the user has ever invested which will allow the user to select one, multiple, or all funds to include in the Detail Trade History results. All funds will be selected by default.
Additionally, date selectors will be present allowing the user to enter from and to dates to define a date range for trade history.
Clicking the View Trades button will load the trade history for the selected funds within the selected date range.
Detail Trade History With All Funds Selected
The results will include the following information:
Reference #
Trade Date
Fund Name
Security Type
Transaction Type
Transaction
Dollar Value
Shares
Share Price
Users may download the trade history as a PDF.
Liquidate To Savings
By selecting this option, participants with investment-enabled accounts can process liquidations of funds.
When this option is clicked, the user will be taken to the Liquidate to Savings screen. Here, they will be informed of their invested amount and be able to enter an amount to be liquidated up to that invested amount.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Investments
chunks.content:
Liquidated investment shares will be prorated based on the percentage of the corresponding market values in the account owner’s portfolio. Example: Fund A has $10,000, Fund B has $10,000, and Fund C has $20,000; the account owner chooses to liquidate $400 to savings; $100 from Fund A, $100 from Fund B, and $200 from Fund C will be liquidated to the participant’s cash account.
The user may tap Cancel to back out or Save Investment Order to proceed.
If the user tapped Save Investment Order, they will be taken to a Liquidate To Savings Confirmation screen with the details of the transaction. From this screen, they may download the confirmation as a pdf by clicking the Download Confirmation link.
The liquidate to savings request will be listed in the Pending transactions list until the HSA Investment process is completed in HSAToday. Once it is completed, the investment balance will be reduced accordingly. 
View Statement of Investment
This will initiate a download of the Statement of Investment Policy on the user’s device.
Investment Policy Statement
View Investment Disclaimer
This will initiate a download of the Investment Disclaimer on the user’s device.
View Privacy Policy
This will initiate a download of the Privacy Policy on the user’s device.
Privacy Protection Notice

chunks.title: Mobile App | Make A Deposit
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Make A Deposit
HSA Account Owners can make post-tax deposits into their HSA account from their personal bank account through the Summit Mobile App. Make a Deposit option is available only for those having a benefit that allows participant-initiated contributions, i.e. an HSA.
Table of Contents
Make A Deposit Page
The Deposit Confirmation Page
To navigate to the Make A Deposit Page,
Click on the “Make A Deposit” option from the three-line menu:
OR
Tap the “Make A Deposit” option from the I Want To section on the Home page:
Make A Deposit Page
The Deposit Transaction page will appear as shown below:
To make a deposit, follow the steps given below:
Select the HSA Account from the “Deposit To” dropdown.
Now the Balance will display.
Select the tax year (the tax year the deposit or return applies) from the “For Tax Year” dropdown.
Choose the radio button, “Normal Contribution, Post-tax”.
Enter the amount of deposit in the “Amount” field.
Add Notes if needed.
Select an available Personal Bank Account from the “Bank Account” dropdown. This dropdown will contain a list of all the Personal Bank Accounts the participant has setup on the Summit. The user may click the Edit icon to setup a new bank account or make changes to the account details.
Then click the checkbox acknowledging and authorizing the drafting of funds from the account.
Finally click on “Submit”.
The Deposit Confirmation Page
After submitting the payment, the Mobile App will display a Deposit Confirmation with the following information:
Request Date
Account Owner
Amount
Deposit To [the HSA benefit]
Banking Details [Bank Account Name and last 4 digits of the account number]
Processing time and NSF service fee disclaimer

chunks.title: Mobile App | Make A Payment
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Make A Payment
Users can make premium payments through the Make A Payment page of the Summit Mobile app. The “Pay Now” link is displayed in the Billing Section of the Home Page for participants with PB coverage and has a premium due. Clicking on the link will take the user to the Make A Payment UI.
Table of Contents
Make A Payment Page
Participants with No Bank Account – ACH
If “allow updates to banking info” option is turned OFF:
If “allow updates to banking info” option is turned ON:
Premium Billing Card Payment
PB Post-Grace Date Warning
To navigate to the Make A Payment Page,
Go to the Billing section of the Home page.
Click on the “Pay Now” link:
Make A Payment Page
The Make A Payment page will appear as shown below:
The Make A Payment screen has the following fields:
Transaction Type – Displays “Premium Payment” as the Transaction Type.
Payment Method – This dropdown menu has options, “ACH” and “Credit/Debit Card” only if the ‘Allow Participant Portal and Mobile App ACH Payments’ and/or ‘Allow Participant Portal and Mobile App Card Payments’ is enabled. If these options were not enabled, the “Pay Now” link will not appear in the Billing section.
Bank Account – The Bank Account field is a list that contains participant bank accounts. Here the app auto-populates the default bank account. If the user has multiple accounts, they can select the desired bank account from the list. This field is applicable only for ACH payments.
Edit Bank Account – This is applicable only for ACH payments. Clicking on this icon will take the user to the Edit Banking page. The edit icon will be displayed only if the “Allow updates to banking info” option is turned ON in Summit.
Total Amount Due – The app will auto-populate the total premium due in the Total Amount Due field.
Payment Date – The current system date will default as the payment date, however the user may select a different date by clicking on the calendar icon.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Make A Payment
chunks.content:
Payment Amount – The system will auto-populate the total amount in the Payment Amount field.  The user can enter any dollar amount here. This is a mandatory field for submitting the payment.
Service Fee – Here, the variable ACH fee amount ($2.00 to $100.00 per transaction) designated by the TPA in the Participant Portal Settings UI will display as Service Fee when the participant is the ACH fee payor.
Total Payment – This is a read-only field that shows the sum of the payment amount and any applicable service fee.
Note – Note field will show processing time and applicable fee for the payment via mobile app. A note will be displayed here when a participant makes a mobile premium payment.
Authorization – The system will require the user to select the Authorization message checkbox before submitting the payment request, for mobile application premium payments.
Cancel – Press the Cancel button to close the Make A Payment screen and return to the previous screen.
Submit – The user must press the Submit button to complete the payment transaction. 
Confirmation – After a payment has been successfully made, the app will display a confirmation message for the ACH payment.
NOTE: When the Total Amount Due is zero, the “Pay Now” option will not be displayed.
Participants with No Bank Account – ACH
If the payment method selected is ACH and there is no bank account on the participant’s record, the participant will not be able to make a payment from the mobile app.
If “allow updates to banking info” option is turned OFF:
If this option is not turned on and the participant does not have a bank account setup, a note will display in the Make A Payment UI that says “You do not have a bank account set up. Please contact your administrator to add your bank account.”
If “allow updates to banking info” option is turned ON:

chunks.title: Mobile App | Make A Payment
chunks.content:
If this option is turned on and the participant does not have a bank account setup, a note will display in the Make A Payment UI that says “You do not have a bank account set up. Set one up now”. Clicking the “Set one up now” link will take the user to the Add Banking Page. The user can add a bank account from there.
Premium Billing Card Payment
The Make A Payment UI on the Summit Mobile App is able to accept one-time card payments if the “Allow Participant Portal and Mobile App Card Payments” option is enabled. Participants may make either debit or credit card payments on the Summit Mobile App via ACI Speedpay integration. The Payment Method includes an option for Credit/Debit Card based on the Online Payment settings.
Upon accepting the terms and clicking Submit, the user will be taken to the ACI Speedpay Pay Bill site with the personal and payment information populated in the same manner as if the selected Payment Method was ACH.
After clicking “NEXT STEP,” the participant will be taken to the Payment Method section where they will be able to enter their Credit/Debit card information.
The user may store the payment information with ACI Speedpay by clicking the “Save this payment method to my wallet” checkbox. [Note: This information will be stored by the payment processor and is not stored by Summit.]
Clicking “NEXT STEP” will take the user to the Payment Amount section.
Here the payment amount selected on the Summit Mobile App will populate. The user will have an opportunity to adjust the payment amount before proceeding.
The user may proceed to review the payment by clicking the REVIEW button.
Here, the user must acknowledge that the information is correct and they have read and agree to the terms and conditions.
After authorization, the user will be redirected to the Receipt page where the receipt can be either saved or printed.
PB Post-Grace Date Warning

chunks.title: Mobile App | Make A Payment
chunks.content:
When the participant attempts to make a payment for a billing period that is due on the Make A Payment UI of the Summit Mobile App that is after the billing period’s grace date, the following Post-Grace Date warning message will display. Participants will be unable to make premium payments on the mobile app after the grace date.
Summit will use the system date as the postmark date for payments made via the Summit Mobile App.
For information about handling chargebacks for Premium Billing payments, see our PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices guide.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Make A Repayment
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Make A Repayment
Users can repay benefit plans that have a Balance Due through the Make A Repayment page of the Summit Mobile app. The “Repay Now” link is displayed in the Alert detail page and in the Transaction details page for the participants with the balance due. Tapping on the link will take the user to the Make a Repayment page.
Table of Contents
Make A Repayment Page
Participants with No Bank Account
If the “allow updates to banking info” option is turned OFF:
If the “allow updates to banking info” option is turned ON:
To navigate to the Make A Repayment Page:
Click on the Alerts option from the three-line menu.
Click on the “Ineligible Expense – Repayment Required” alert.
Press the Repay Now button in the Alert: Details page.
OR
Click on the Transactions option from the three-line menu.
Click on the transaction requiring repayment.
Press the Repay Now button in the Transaction Detail page.
Make A Repayment Page
The Make A Repayment page will appear as shown below:
The Make A Repayment screen has the following fields:
Transaction Type – This field displays “Repay ineligible Trxn” as the Transaction Type.
Account Owner – The participant name will be displayed here.
Bank Account – The Bank Account field is a dropdown list that contains the participant’s bank accounts. The app auto-populates the default bank account in this field.  If the participant has multiple bank accounts, the user can select the desired bank account from the dropdown.
Ineligible Transaction – This section will display the details of the ineligible transaction.
Notes – The user can add notes in this text field.
Repayment Amount – The system will auto-populate the Total Amount Due in the Repayment Amount field. However, the user can enter any dollar amount in the Repayment Amount field. This is a mandatory field for submitting the payment.
Signature Fields – It includes a note along with fields for users to enter their name and initials along with an auto populated date field.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Make A Repayment
chunks.content:
Disclaimer Policy Text and Checkbox – The user has to accept the disclaimer policy in order to proceed.
Cancel – Press Cancel to close the Make a Payment screen and return to the previous screen.
Submit – The user must press Submit to complete the payment transaction.
Confirmation – The app will display a confirmation message, on the Make a Payment UI, after the payment has been successfully made.
Note: When the Balance due is zero, the “Repay Now” option will not be displayed in the App.
Participants with No Bank Account
If there is no bank account on the participant’s record, the participant will not be able to make a payment from the mobile app. The Pay Now button will not be displayed.
If the “allow updates to banking info” option is turned OFF:
If this option is not turned on and the participant does not have a bank account setup, a note that says “You do not have a bank account set up. Please contact your administrator to add your bank account.” will be displayed in the billing section. The user cannot add banking information in this case.
If the “allow updates to banking info” option is turned ON:
If this option is turned on and the participant does not have a bank account setup, a note that says “You do not have a bank account set up. Set one up now” will be displayed in the billing section. Clicking the “Set one up now” link will take the user to the Add Banking Page and the user can add a bank account from there.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Profile
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Profile
The Profile page contains the relevant contact information of the participant as saved in the Summit database. It also contains some settings related to the app login, banking, and the user’s alert subscription. The user can edit their profile information and change the notification settings if needed.
Table of Contents
Edit Profile Page
To navigate to the Profile page,
Click on the “Profile” option from the three-line menu:
OR
Tap the “Update My Profile” option from the I Want To section of the Home page:
The Profile page also displays an “Edit” option which allows the user to edit the existing details and modify the settings.
Edit Icon – Clicking on the Pencil icon next to the profile page title will take the user to the “Edit Profile” page.
Contact Section – Here, the contact details of the participant user will display as a card layout below the Profile title. It includes:
Participant Name
Address (Address Line1, Address Line2, City, State and Zip Code)
Mobile Number
Home Phone Number – Denoted by (H)
Work Phone Number – Denoted by (W)
Email Address
Banking Button – Pressing the Banking button will open the Banking page in the mobile app.
Debit Card Alerts Subscription Settings – This section contains the setting statuses for displaying alerts in the Mobile app and in the Participant Portal for Debit Card Declines and Authorization events. The subscription selections made here will apply to all mobile devices associated with your account.
Declines – This shows whether the alerts for Debit Card Declines are turned ON or OFF for the Mobile app and Participant Portal. If it is turned ON for any, it will be indicated by a green bell icon and if the alert is turned OFF, it will be indicated by a red, crossed-out bell icon.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Profile
chunks.content:
Authorizations – This shows whether the alerts for Debit Card Authorizations are turned ON or OFF for the Mobile app and Participant Portal. If it is turned ON for any, it will be denoted by a green bell icon and if the alert is turned OFF, it will be denoted by a red, crossed-out bell icon.
Face ID/ Touch ID – This shows whether the Face ID or Touch ID for login is enabled.
All of the above settings can be changed from the Edit Profile page.
Edit Profile Page
The Edit Profile page is where the user can make changes to his/her contact details or notification settings. When the user clicks on the Pencil icon to go to the Edit Profile page, the page loads with all the existing details pre-populated. The user may choose to edit any information in these fields or navigate back to the previous page.
The Edit Profile page includes the following fields:
Name –The Name section includes fields for First Name, Middle Initial, and Last Name.
Address – The Address section includes fields for Address Line 1, Address Line 2, City, State, and ZIP Code. The State field is a dropdown list of all states.
Phone numbers – Shows three fields respectively for Mobile, Home, and Work Phone numbers.
Email – Contains the Email address of the participant user.
Login – This section includes a switch control to turn the Touch ID ON or OFF for login. Touch ID can be enabled by the user at the login page.
Debit Card Alerts Subscriptions
Declines – There are two toggle switches to turn alerts ON or OFF for Debit Card Declines in Mobile app and Participant Portal respectively.
Authorizations – There are two toggle switches to turn alerts ON or OFF for Debit Card Authorizations in the Mobile app and Participant Portal respectively.
Save Button – Pressing the Save button will validate all the fields and save the changes in the Summit database.
Cancel Button – Pressing the Cancel button will navigate back to the Profile page.
Categories

chunks.title: Mobile App | Request A Withdrawal
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Request A Withdrawal
The Withdrawal page allows the user to submit a withdrawal request if the participant has at least one withdrawal-enabled plan.
Table of Contents
Withdrawal Page
Withdrawal Confirmation Page
To navigate to the Withdrawal Page,
Click on the “Request A Withdrawal” option from the three-line menu:
OR
Tap the “Request A Withdrawal” option from the I Want To section on the Home page if the participant has at least one withdrawal enabled plan:
Withdrawal Page
The Make A Withdrawal page will include the following details:      
Withdraw From – This dropdown includes all available plans that have the “Allow Withdrawals” option enabled for the participant.
Balance – After selecting a plan from the “Withdraw From” dropdown, this field will display the current balance of the selected account.
Qualified/Non-Qualified radio buttons – This is applicable only for custodian-enabled benefits. The user will choose whether the transaction is qualified or not.
Non-Qualified Disclaimer Checkbox – In order to continue with the transaction, the user must accept the Non-Qualified Disclaimer policy by selecting this checkbox. The user may click the “Non-Qualified Disclaimer” text link displayed here to read the policy.
Distribution Method – This dropdown list allows the participant to select a distribution method. The dropdown list will only appear if the TPA/Employer allows the participant to change the distribution/reimbursement method. The options are Direct deposit and Check. The dropdown will default based on the TPA/Employer’s default reimbursement settings.
Amount – This text field is where the user will enter the transaction amount to withdraw.
Notes – This text field allows the user to enter notes.
Terms and Conditions Checkbox –In order to continue with the transaction, the user must accept the Terms and Conditions by selecting this checkbox. Clicking on the linked text will open a display containing the terms and conditions.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Request A Withdrawal
chunks.content:
Cancel – The Cancel button takes the user back to the previous page.
Submit – The Submit button will validate all the mandatory fields, including the Terms and Conditions checkbox, and ensures the entered amount is greater than zero, but less than the available balance. If the request passes validation, it will be transmitted to Summit to initiate the withdrawal.
If the distribution method is selected as Direct deposit and the banking details are not available for the participant, what happens next will depend on whether the “Allow updates to participant bank details” setting is enabled for the participant.
If the “Allow updates to participant bank details” setting is enabled and the participant doesn’t have a bank account added, the app will display an “Add Bank Account” text link below the Distribution Method dropdown, when the participant chooses the option Direct Deposit. Clicking on the link will take the user to the Add Banking page where they can add the bank account and then proceed with submitting the Withdrawal request.
If the “Allow updates to participant bank details” setting is not enabled and the participant doesn’t have a bank account added, the app will display a note that says “You have selected Direct deposit as the Distribution Method, but the details of your bank account are missing. You cannot proceed with this claim with the selected Distribution Method. Please contact your administrator.” The Submit button will be disabled in this scenario and it can be re-enabled only when the Distribution Method is changed to Check.
In either case, the Submit button will be disabled if the participant has no Bank Account and has selected the Direct deposit as the Distribution Method, preventing the participant from submitting the withdrawal request. The Submit button can be re-enabled only when the Distribution Method is changed from Direct deposit to Check, or the participant has added at least one Bank Account.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Request A Withdrawal
chunks.content:
If the withdrawal request is submitted successfully, the user will be taken to a confirmation page. Otherwise, a failure alert will be shown as below:
Withdrawal Confirmation Page
The Withdrawal Confirmation page will display the following data:
Claim Number – This is a unique number assigned by Summit to the transaction.
Withdraw From – This shows the plan from which the withdrawal is initiated.
Is Qualified – This additional field shows when the benefit selected for withdrawal is a custodian-enabled benefit. It denotes if the withdrawal was requested for a qualified medical expense.
Balance – This displays the current balance of the selected account.
Amount – This displays the amount of the requested withdrawal.
Distribution Method – The selected distribution method will be shown here.
Notes – This displays the notes entered by the user during the transaction, if available.
If the selected benefit for withdrawal is not a custodian-enabled benefit, then the confirmation page will appear as shown below:

chunks.title: Mobile App | Enter A Claim
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Enter A Claim
Users can enter claims through the Enter a Claim page on the Summit Mobile app.
Table of Contents
Enter A Claim Page
To navigate to the Enter a Claim page,
Click on the “Enter A Claim” option from the three-line menu.
OR
Tap the “Enter A Claim” option from the I Want To section on the Home page:
Enter A Claim Page
The Enter A Claim page will appear as shown below:
Unfinished Claims – This will open the Unfinished Claims screen that will list all unfinished claims that have been saved but not yet submitted. Tapping one of the claims on this screen will open the claim form, allowing the user to complete and submit the claim form. Note that unfinished claims may only be saved and edited once; they cannot be saved again once opened from the Unfinished Claims list.
The user may delete an unfinished claim if it is no longer needed by tapping the Delete button.
Add or View Receipt/EOB button – Clicking on this button will take the user to a new page where they can select images from the phone’s gallery or take pictures using the phone’s camera. Users can add multiple images from this page. All selected images will display in a grid view as thumbnails. Pressing the Done button on this page will take the user back to the Enter A Claim page.
Camera Button – Pressing this button will open up the device’s camera. The user can take a picture of the receipt they wish to attach to the claim.
Gallery Button – Pressing this button will open up the device’s photo gallery from which the user can select single or multiple images to attach to the claim.
Files Button – Pressing the Files button will open the device file picker interface, allowing the user to select one or more .pdf files to attach to the claim. The file picker control restricts the user to select only .pdf files.
Done Button – Upon pressing the Done button, the user will be taken back to the Enter A Claim page, where they can enter the other claim information and proceed with submitting the claim.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Enter A Claim
chunks.content:
Claimant – This dropdown list allows the user to select the claimant for the manual transaction. The claimant list includes the participant and his/her dependents.
Service Date(s) – This date range picker allows the user to select the service start date and end date. If the user selects only a single date, the end date will be the same as the start date.
Service Category – This dropdown allows the user to select the service category.
Service Code – Here, the user can select service codes. If the user has first selected a service category, only those codes associated with that selected category will display here.
Requested Plan – This dropdown list allows the user to select the plan. The list contains all active and open-ended plans for the claimant between the selected service start date and end date.
Reimbursement Method – This dropdown list allows the user to select a reimbursement method. The dropdown list will be enabled only if the TPA/Employer allows the participant to change the reimbursement method. The default reimbursement method selected by the TPA/Employer will be selected in the dropdown by default. The options are Direct deposit and Check.
Amount – The user must enter the transaction amount in this field.
Provider/Merchant – This text field allows the user to enter the Provider/Merchant name.
Description of Service – This text field allows the user to enter a description of the service provided.
Notes – This is a text field to enter notes.
Terms and Conditions link with Checkbox – The user must check the checkbox to acknowledge that they accept the terms and conditions. The terms and conditions may be viewed by clicking the hyperlinked text.
Cancel – Pressing the Cancel button will navigate back to the previous page.
Finish Later – When the user taps this link, the completed fields of the claim will be saved, though the claim will not be submitted. The claim will be placed under Unfinished Claims, where it may be completed later.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Enter A Claim
chunks.content:
Submit Claim – When the Submit Claim button is pressed, the system validates whether all the mandatory items like the receipt image, Service Start Date, Service End Date, Amount, Provider/Merchant, Service Description, and Requested Plan are provided. Also, the terms and conditions check box must be checked.
If the reimbursement method is selected as Direct deposit and the banking details are not available for the participant, the following will happen depending on whether the “Allow updates to Banking info” setting is enabled by the TPA for the Employer of the participant.
If the “Allow updates to banking info” setting is enabled and the participant doesn’t have a bank account added, then the app will display a note “You do not have a bank account set up. Set one up now” below the Distribution Method dropdown list when the participant chooses “Direct Deposit” as the reimbursement option. Clicking on the “Set one up now” link will take the user to the Add Banking Page. The participant can then add the bank account and proceed with submitting the Claim.
If the “Allow updates to banking info” setting is disabled and the participant doesn’t have a bank account added, then the app will display a note that says “You have selected Direct Deposit as the Distribution Method, but the details of your bank account are missing. You cannot proceed with this claim with the selected Distribution Method. Please contact your administrator.” The Submit button will be disabled in this scenario. The button will be re-enabled if the Distribution Method is changed to Check.
After the successful claim submission, a confirmation page will display the details of the entered claim. Press “OK” to confirm.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Transactions
chunks.content:
Mobile App | Transactions
The Transactions page lists all the transactions made by the participant in the last calendar year until the current date.
Table of Contents
Transaction Detail Page
To navigate to the Transactions Page,       
Click on the “Transactions” option from the three-line menu:
OR
Tap the “View Recent Transactions” option from the I Want To section on the Home page:
Now the transactions page will appear as shown below:
The user can change the date range using the date selector inside the filter menu to see more transactions from the previous year(s). A note will be displayed under the search bar saying “Displaying transactions from *start date* to *end date*. To see more, choose a different date range from filter options”.
A Transactions page will include:
Sort Icon – Clicking on this icon at the right side of the transactions page title will display pop-up showing options to sort the list of transactions. The user can sort the transactions either by the Transaction Amount or the Transaction Date.
Sort Amount smallest to largest – This option will sort all the transactions based on the transaction amount in ascending order.
Sort Amount largest to smallest – This option will sort all the transactions based on the transaction amount in descending order.
Sort Date newest to oldest – This option will sort all the transactions based on the transaction date in ascending order.
Sort Date oldest to newest – This option will sort all the transactions based on the transaction date in descending order.
Filter Icon – A Filter icon will be shown at the top right corner, near the Transactions title. Clicking on this icon will display a pop-up from which the user can select any of the filter options to filter the transactions list. The transactions can be filtered by Date, Transaction type, Plan type, Amount, Claimant, Status, and Reimbursement method. The user can select any or all of these filter options to filter the transaction list upon their choice.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Transactions
chunks.content:
For Premium Payment transaction type:
Search bar – This search bar at the top section of the Transactions page below the page title row will allow the user to search for any value that is entered in the transactions list.
Transaction Item – Each transaction item will be displayed as a card layout in the list. Clicking on any item will take the user to the Transaction Detail page where the selected individual transaction’s details are displayed. If any transaction requires user action, such as uploading a receipt or repaying a plan, the required action will be listed as a text link right below the transaction amount in each transaction item. Following are the details included in a transaction item:
Transaction date
Transaction amount
Plan name
Transaction type followed by Transaction status
Receipt Required Text– This text alerts the user that a receipt must be uploaded to substantiate the claim. It will be visible for online claims transactions that do not have an attached receipt.
Repayment Required Text– This text alerts the user that they must repay the plan, and it will only be visible for transactions with a balance due amount.
Transaction Detail Page
The Transaction Detail page displays all the details of the selected transaction as explained below. The user can swipe left or right between records rather than tapping “back” and selecting a new record. Swiping left will take the user to the next older transaction after the one currently viewed while swiping right will take the user to the next newer transaction before the one currently viewed.
When a record is displaying and the user touches their screen, an indicator that they may swipe between the records will display as shown below.
On iPhone devices, a swipe icon will display.
On Android devices, dots will indicate the selected record in sequence.
Plan Type (Account Type for HSA) – The type of the plan (account) used for this transaction.

chunks.title: Mobile App | Transactions
chunks.content:
Plan Name (Account Name for HSA) – The name of the plan (account) associated with the transaction.
Claimant – Name of the participant/dependent who is the claimant on the transaction.
Transaction Type – Shows the type of the selected transaction.
Status – Current status of the transaction.
Is Qualified – Shows whether or not the transaction is Qualified (applicable only for withdrawal transactions from HSA accounts).
Service Date(s) – Shows the date of the transaction.
Service Category – Shows the selected service category. (Display only for open-ended plans)
Service Code – Shows the selected service code. (Display only for open-ended plans)
Provider/Merchant – Displays the name of the Provider/Merchant.
Total Amount – Shows the total amount of transaction.
Below are the transaction detail pages with different action buttons, including:
Upload Receipt Button
Repay Now Button
Like the Transactions page, the Transaction Detail page has Upload Receipt and Repay Now buttons for the corresponding transactions.
HSA Withdrawal
Premium Billing Transaction Detail
Clicking the link View Premium Payment Breakdown will allow the user to view the PB Premium Payment pie chart displaying the breakdown of participant’s Premium Payments to each PB plan for which they are enrolled.
The user is able to select any premium payment made within the past 12 months to see the payment breakdown charts for any given premium payment transactions applied within the selected time period.
This chart only includes the coverages to which the premium was applied if the participant had multiple coverages and payment was not applied to all coverages. The chart shows 100% of the premium applied to a coverage if the payment was a short payment that applied to a single coverage.
If the premium payment remitted by the participant was greater than the amount due, the percentage of the amount which was unapplied will be displayed in the chart.

chunks.title: Mobile App
chunks.content:
Mobile App
In addition to the Participant Portal, Summit offers a mobile app which will allow participants to access their account information, submit claims, make payments, and more. Many of the screens and processes on the mobile app mirror the functionality and processes of the Summit Participant Portal, allowing employee and dependent users to access their Summit account info on the go.
Login Page and User Registration
Users accessing the Mobile App will first be presented with a login page. From here, they may login to the app or register their account.
Forgot Password – If a user has forgotten their password, they may click the Forgot Password button to reset their account’s password.
Home
After logging in, users will be taken to the Home page of the Mobile App. From here, they may access other portions of the app via the menu, the I Would Like To list, and other links.
Investments – If the participant has investment-enabled benefits, they may go to the Benefits section of the Home Page to access the benefit and make and view their investments.
Make a Payment – This link on the homepage allows the participant to pay premium billing benefit premiums through the Mobile App.
Add Bank Account – If no bank account is setup for the participant, they may add a bank account during the Make a Payment process.
Coverage Details – Users can view the coverage details of their Premium Billing coverages by clicking the plan listed in the Billing section of the homepage.
Account Detail – User can view the details of the CDH coverages by clicking the respective benefit listed in the Benefits section of the homepage.
Transactions
The Transactions screen allows users to view recent transactions and their details.
Make a Repayment – The User may make a repayment for a plan with a balance due transaction.
Alerts
Users may see any alerts requiring attention by either clicking the Alerts menu item or clicking “View My Alerts” from the “I Want To” menu.

chunks.title: Mobile App
chunks.content:
Make a Repayment – The User may make a repayment for a plan with a balance due transaction.
Enter A Claim
The Enter A Claim menu option will allow the user to enter and submit claim details for reimbursement against benefit plans.
Request A Withdrawal
The Request a Withdrawal menu option will take the user to the Make a Withdrawal screen, where users with withdrawal-enabled accounts may request direct distribution from their accounts.
Make a Deposit
The Make a Deposit option allows HSA Account Owners to make post-tax deposits directly into their HSA from their personal bank account.
Cards
Participants are able to view and manage their Summit Debit Cards from the Card screen by either clicking the Cards menu option or the View My Cards option from the “I Want To” menu.
Profile / Update My Profile
Participant users may view and update their user profile by clicking the Profile menu option or clicking the Update My Profile option from the “I Want To” menu.
Banking – Participant view and update their banking information from their Profile page.
Contact
The user may access the TPA’s contact information from this menu link on the app.
Categories

chunks.title: Communications | Participant Communications
chunks.content:
Communications | Participant Communications
Summit sends email/letter communications to Participants once they are established in the system. On the Participant Communications page, the user will configure the communication settings for Welcome Notices and Card Issuance Communications. The purpose of the Welcome Notice is to inform participants that they have been added to the system and enrolled in benefits/plans and instructions on how to access the participant portal. Card Issuance Communications will be sent upon the issuance of a debit card to the Participant.
Table of Contents
Email Settings
Image Settings
Welcome Notice
Communication Methods
Card Issuance Communication
Communication Methods
  * Required fields appear in Red
To access Participant Communications,
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Communications.
Select the menu “Participant Communications” from the dropdown.
The Participant Communication page will display on the screen as shown below.
The Communications fields are:
Email Settings
In this section, the user can configure various settings related to communication e-mails. The fields in this section include:
Set From address as – This is a mandatory alphanumeric text field that sets the address from which communication e-mails should be sent. By default, this field will auto-populate with the email address “communications@summitwith.us. In addition, TPAs will no longer be able to make changes to their From email address within Summit to avoid the possibility that communications sent from the new address will be seen as email spoofing. This will now be a function performed by DataPath personnel at the request of TPA-authorized personnel.
Auto – forward a copy of all card holder communications –When this checkbox is selected, the user must enter an e-mail address in the “Forward to” field.

chunks.title: Communications | Participant Communications
chunks.content:
Forward to – This field will be mandatory if the user checks the box for “Auto-forward a copy of all cardholder e-mail communications”. Here the user must enter an e-mail address to which all communications will be forwarded.
Image Settings
In this section, the user can upload an image to be included in the communications. The minimum size of the logo image should be 300X100 pixels and must be saved as .gif, .jpg, or .png.
Change Photo – When the user clicks “Change Photo”, an option to browse files from the machine will be made available. Thus, the user can choose and upload an image there.
Image Location – After uploading an image, the user can select at which location they want the logo image to appear in their communications. There are three options available. They are, “Left”, “Center” and “Right”. These positions indicate where the uploaded image should appear on the top of the letter/email.
Welcome Notice
In this section, the user can enable the communication settings to send a Welcome Notice.
Enable Communication – The “Enable” checkbox indicates the TPA would like to enable the communication. If Enable checkbox is selected it will auto-populate the Communication methods.
Include Participants Enrolled Online – This checkbox option will be visible only when the ‘Enable’ checkbox is selected. This will include communications to participants enrolled online.
Include Participants that are Premium Billing Only – This checkbox option will be visible only when the ‘Enable’ checkbox is selected. This will include communications to participants that have Premium Billing only.

chunks.title: Communications | Participant Communications
chunks.content:
Effective Date –In this field, the user can enter the effective date by picking it from the calendar or typing a value. The default date in the field will be the TPA creation date. If the Welcome Notice is enabled, this date must be populated.  The user may update the date to a date in the past or the future.  The system will use this date to determine which participants should receive the welcome notice.  The system will send a Welcome Notice to all participants created in the system on or after the Effective Date. For example, a participant is fully set up in the system (to the extent that triggers the notice) on 5/1/15; the TPA has the Effective Date set at 4/1/15; in this case, since the participant was created after the Effective Date, they will receive a Welcome Notice.  Participants created before 4/1 will not receive a notice.
Communication Methods
Methods – These settings determine the means by which the welcome notice will be sent. The two options available here are:
Email – Selecting “Email” indicates that the system should send participants communications via email.
Mailed Letter – Selecting “Letter” indicates the system should produce a file of letters to be downloaded from the system, printed, and mailed. By selecting ‘Mailed Letter’ the Fulfillment field will appear as shown below.
The User can select one of two Fulfillment types:
Manual – Documents will be created in a batch file which may be downloaded by the TPA and sent to a 3rd party fulfillment service.
Datapath – Documents will be created in a batch file which will be sent to DataPath’s Fulfillment Service partner for fulfillment.
Format – These links will open a popup modal for the respective communication method whereby the TPA user may customize the communications.
Email | Letter – By clicking one of the communication methods, a pop-up will be displayed as follows for the respective method. Here the user can customize the format by adding additional fields and editing the content.

chunks.title: Communications | Participant Communications
chunks.content:
Send Letter if there is no email address on file – If this box is checked, then the system will default the communication method to letter when the participant’s email address is not present in the system.
Card Issuance Communication
This notice will be created for each card issued by the system.
Enable Communication – The “Enable” checkbox indicates the system should enable the communication. If the Enable checkbox is selected it will auto-populate the Communication methods.
Communication Methods
Methods – These checkbox settings determine the means by which the Card Issuance communication will be sent. The options available here are:
Email – Selecting “E-mail” indicates that the User would like the system to send communications via e-mail.
Mailed Letter – Selecting “Letter” indicates the system should produce a file of letters that would be downloaded from the system, printed, and mailed. When ‘Mailed Letter’ is selected, the Fulfillment field will be available for selection.
Participant Portal – The communications will be made available for the participant users to view on the Participant Portal.
If “Mailed Letter” is selected
The User can select one of two Fulfillment types:
Manual
Datapath
Format – These links will open a popup modal for the respective communication method whereby the TPA user may customize the communications.
Email | Letter | Portal – Here the user can set the format of Email and Letter which will be send as Card Issuance communication as well as text for an alert on the Participant Portal.
By clicking any one of the communication methods, a pop-up will be displayed as follows. Here the user can customize the format by adding additional fields and editing the content.
Send Letter if there is no email address on file – – If this box is checked, then the system will default the communication method to letter when the participant email address is not present in the system.
Click ‘Save’ after entering all the required information.

chunks.title: Participant | Participant Central
chunks.content:
Participant | Participant Central
Participant Central is the page that collects and configures various Participant related information such as Demographics, Dependent, Banking, Plans, Cards, etc. Here the user can add or view and edit participant information.
Table of Contents
Add a Participant Wizard
Manual Setup
Demographics 
Dependent
Banking
Plans
Cards
Transactions
Health Plans
Notes
Billing
Events
Receipts
To access Participant Central,
Go to Participant.
Select Participant Central from the dropdown menu.
Choose an Employer from the dropdown list. The user can type the name of the employer in this field to narrow available selections.
The Premium Billing Statuses dropdown will display when the employer is a Premium Billing Only or CDH + Premium Billing. The user can filter Premium Billing participants on Participant Central by their premium billing coverage statuses.
Now search or enter a participant by first name, last name, participant system ID, or participant custom ID. When hovering the mouse over a participant’s name in the result list, that participant’s employer name will display to the side.
Additionally, the employer’s name will be displayed on the search results popup as given below.
To create a new Participant, click the “Add Participant” button on the right side of the Participant Central landing page. A Participant can be created either via setup wizard or manually.
By default, the selection for this filter is “All Selected”. The options available are:
Active
COBRA
Direct Bill
No Coverage
Qualified Beneficiary
Qualified Direct Bill
Qualified Retiree
Rehire
Retiree
Terminated
Add a Participant Wizard
For information on how to Add a Participant Via the Wizard, click here.
Manual Setup

chunks.title: Participant | Participant Central
chunks.content:
The user can complete the Participant set up outside of the wizard by accessing the individual sub-tabs of the Participant Central page. A user can enter the wizard and add Participant’s Demographics and then “Save and Exit” the wizard without completion, can simply go to the Dependent tab under the Participant Central, and add a Dependent from there. Information added directly into the sub-tabs will still reflect on the Setup Status bar. The Participant Central page has many sub-tabs. The location and visibility of these tabs may vary from Participant to Participant by its feature access settings.
If the selected option in the Add Participant pop-up is “Manual”, then the system will redirect the user to the Demographics tab of the Participant Central page to enter the details of the Participant.
Demographics 
This will be the default tab that opens when the user accesses the Participant Central page. The demographics tab represents all the information entered in Step 1 of the Participant Set up Wizard. The user will have the option to edit any of this information at any time after the initial creation. For more information, please refer to Participant | Participant Central | Demographics.
Dependent
This tab will include all the same fields of Step 2 of the Wizard. A table showing the name and details of all entered Dependents can be seen here. By clicking the Dependent Name, which is a link to display Dependent Details, the user can edit the details of Dependent at any time. The user will also have an option to add a new Dependent by clicking the “Add Dependent” button. For more information, refer to the Participant | Participant Central | Dependent tab page.
Banking
Here the user can view/edit any of the Banking information that was entered by the user during the Wizard. For more information, please refer to the Participant | Participant Central | Banking tab page.
Plans

chunks.title: Participant | Participant Central
chunks.content:
In this section, Summit enables the user to enroll the Participant into CDH or PB plans offered by their Employer. The CDH and PB plans in which the participant was enrolled will display in separate tables. For more information, see the Participant | Participant Central | Plans tab page.
Cards
The Cards tab will display a table with issued card details. The user can issue cards to Participant/Dependent by clicking the Issue Card(s) button on the top of the page. For more information, see the Participant | Participant Central | Cards tab page.
Transactions
The Transactions tab will show recent transactions and declined card transactions that have been applied to any of the Participant plans. It will show transactions of all types including Manual Claims, Debit Card Claims, Repayments, Withdrawals, etc. Here the user can also add a claim by clicking the “Add Claim” button. For more information, see the Participant | Participant Central | Transactions tab page.
Health Plans
Health Plans are a type of insurance that reimburses the cost of medical treatment if the Participant/Dependent are ill or injured. Participants can be linked to the health plans via the Health Plans tab. See the Participant | Participant Central | Health Plans tab page for more information.
Notes
In the Notes tab, the user can view existing Notes or add a new Note.  The tab will show a listing of all existing notes with an option to delete them. For more information, see the Participant | Participant Central | Notes tab page.
Billing
This tab is only visible for participants of the employer who were enrolled in PB plans. Here, the user can view the premium billing details. This tab displays all the coverage billing periods for the participant. For more detailed information, see the Participant | Participant Central | Billing tab page.
Events

chunks.title: Participant | Participant Central
chunks.content:
In the Events tab, the Coverage Line table will contain the “Coverage”, “Type” and “Status” columns. Summit will trigger Premium Billing events and notifications when an event occurs and benefit coverage options are changed. Participants of the employer who were enrolled in PB plans can only view this tab. Refer to the Participant | Participant Central | Events page for more information.
Receipts
Here, Summit allows the user to add, edit, delete, or select one or more receipts to adjust, etc. These are the payments (receipts) received from the Participant for coverage premiums. This tab is only visible for participants of the employer who were enrolled in PB plans. For more information, see the Participant | Participant Central | Receipts tab page.
Watch this short video for a step-by-step guide to the above instructions

chunks.title: Participant | Participant Portal
chunks.content:
Participant | Participant Portal
The Participant Portal is a means by which participants can access, view, and manage their user profile, coverages, cards, transactions and benefit and investment accounts in Summit. Once they have been added to Summit and have a valid email address, a welcome notice will be sent with instructions on how to register for the portal, including the necessary Employer ID and Participant ID keys to associate their account with their information.
A description of the participant registration process can be found here.
TPA users also have the ability to view individual participants’ Participant Portal accounts from the admin side to assist in customer support.
Table of Contents
User Profile
TPA Contact
Documents
Home
Coverages
Transaction History
Claims Vault
Transactions
Add A Transaction
Cards
Investments
To access the TPA view of Participant Portal,
Go to Participant and select the Participant Central menu.
Choose an Employer from the dropdown list.
Click on the “Login to Portal” link of the participant.
OR
Click the “Login to Portal” link on the individual participants’ account page.
The “Login to Portal” link will display only for those participants who have created Participant Portal logins.
When the user clicks the “Login to Portal” link, they will be directed to the Participant Portal Home page.
NOTE: Participants logging into their accounts via the URL will be required to complete Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) to enhance the security of their login and access. After entering their credentials, participants must provide an additional verification code, which will be sent via SMS or email to the phone number or email address registered in Summit. If neither a phone number nor an email address is available in Summit, participants will need to contact the administrator for assistance.
User Profile

chunks.title: Participant | Participant Portal
chunks.content:
The TPA user can view the participant account information on the Participant Portal Profile page by clicking the User ID displayed at the top of the Participant Portal page.
TPA Contact
Clicking the Support icon at the top end will display the TPA contact information. The user can view the Address and Contact details as the participant would see them.
Documents
The user can view the documents by clicking the Documents menu in the top menu bar.
Home
Based on the employer’s benefit administration type: CDH-only, Premium Billing-only, or CDH and PB, the Participant Portal Home Page will display varying sections and widgets. The Participant Portal Home page is divided into different subsections:
Coverages
The Participant Portal Coverages page will display all the active plans in which a participant is currently enrolled. If the participant has enrolled in multiple plans, then the plan year will be listed on the page by Plan Type (alphabetically) and then Plan Year (oldest first).
Transaction History
The Participant Portal Transaction History page will display the participant’s transaction history across all plans, allow the user to search for specific transactions or those meeting certain criteria, and perform specified actions.
Claims Vault
The user can enter a claim, upload the associated receipt, and store it in the system via Participant Portal Claims VaultTM. Claims submitted via Claims VaultTM can be reimbursed at any later time and will not be visible to the TPA in the main application. The Claims VaultTM page will not display for PB-only participants and will not appear as a menu option.
Transactions
The user can initiate transactions like Online Claims, Withdrawals, Repayment of the Balance Due, Pay Premiums, and Vault Claims via the Participant Portal Transactions page.
Add A Transaction
The Add A Transaction menu takes the user directly to the Add A Transaction interface with no need to first access either Transactions or Claims Vault and click the Add Transaction button.

chunks.title: Participant | Participant Portal
chunks.content:
Cards
Debit Cards are a way of gaining electronic access to funds. TPAs issue debit cards to participants that are linked to their benefit plans. These debit cards allow participants to go to the pharmacy or doctor and pay for the prescription or medical service provided. If the participant is at an eligible type of merchant, the system will allow for a deduction of funds in real-time to pay for the expense. This results in the automation of fund access and reduced expenses for the TPA.  On the Participant Portal Cards page, the user can view details of all cards issued to participants and their dependents distinctly in separate sections. The Cards page will not display for PB-only participants and will not appear as a menu option.
Investments
Summit allows for individually-owned HSAs to be investment-enabled, meaning that participants who own those accounts may invest their account funds using Summit’s Investments platform on the Participant Portal.
If a participant has an investment-enabled benefit, they will see the Investments menu option on the Participant Portal.
A guide for the first-time investment process can be found here.
For further information, please refer to the Participant Portal section in FAQs.

chunks.content:
Participant
One of the core functionalities of Summit is the creation and management of individual participant members of employer groups.
This includes the entry of their basic demographic information, the entry and management of their dependent relations, the entry of participant banking information, and the assignment and management of benefits.
These actions and more are handled through Summit’s Participant Module.
Table of Contents
Participant Central
Participant Portal
Participant Central
Participant Central is your central management point for the creation and management of individual participants. From here, you are able to search for participants within Employer Groups and access their information or manually create new participants.
When a participant is selected from the search results, it will open the Participant Central demographic tabs for that individual. The information on these tabs contains all information and plan data pertaining to the individual participant.
For more information on each Participant Central tab, visit the following pages:
Demographics
Dependent
Banking
Plans
Transactions
Health Plans
Notes
Billing
Events
Receipts
Participant Portal
The Participant Portal is the primary way in which participants will interact with Summit. From this portal, they are able to view their health plan information, their account balances, enter transactions/file claims, pay premiums, manage their address and dependent information, and more.
For support purposes, TPA users are able to view and access an individual participant’s view of the Participant Portal.
Clicking the “Login to Portal” link on the participant list display and on the individual participants’ account page will direct the user to the individual participant portal page(s).
The “Login to Portal” link will display only for those participants who have created Participant Portal logins.
