chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Benefit Orders
chunks.content:
Plan Default Settings | Benefit Orders
Participants enrolled in benefit plans may have access to multiple purses with their plan dollars. Different benefit plans cover and pay out different amounts for different products/service based on the plan design. Because Summit allows for many different kinds of plans to be designed and assigned to participants and for those purse values to be loaded onto a single participant debit card, a Benefit Order is used to determine the priority logic by which plans will attempt to reimburse participants for the claims they have submitted.
Table of Contents
New Benefit Order
  * Required fields appear in Red
To access Benefit Order:
Go to Settings
Mouse-over Plan Default Settings
Click Benefit Order
Figure 1. Accessing Benefit Order
The DataPath Default Benefit Order for Card Purses is:
LFSA – Limited Purpose Medical FSA
FSA – Medical Flexible Spending Account
HRA – Health Reimbursement Arrangement
MERP – Medical Expense Reimbursement
HSA – Health Savings Account
DCA – Dependent Care Account
TRN – Transportation Plan
PRK – Parking Plan
LSA – Lifestyle Spending Account
Figure 2. Plan Default Settings | Benefit Orders
When a claim is submitted to Summit, it is run through the Benefit Order, checking each benefit to see if the claim is eligible to be reimbursed by that plan. Summit will attempt to reimburse a claim to its fullest eligible amount by each plan, then pass the claim to the next available benefit to attempt to complete reimbursement if eligible until either the claim has been fully reimbursed or the participant has no eligible plans/funds/purses remaining to complete reimbursement.
NOTE: A participant generally will not have all benefits listed in the default order. For instance, participants with HSAs may not have Medical Flexible Spending Accounts, but they may have Limited Purpose Medical FSAs for things such as vision and dental.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Benefit Orders
chunks.content:
Based on the Benefit Order shown above, if an individual with an LFSA and an HSA had a claim for a vision exam, Summit would first attempt to reimburse the participant from any LFSA funds they had available. If they had no LFSA funds available, the claim would be passed along the Benefit Order until it reached their HSA; provided their HSA had funds, the individual would be reimbursed for any amount not paid from their LFSA.
Figure 2.1 Plan Default Settings | Benefit Orders | FSA Store
Additionally, TPAs who have the DirectPay enabled will have a special default benefit order for DirectPay service categories that will allow the purchases from the store to be processed as claims within Summit.
For more information about DirectPay, see here.
New Benefit Order
You may wish to create a new Benefit Order in certain circumstances. For instance, if you administer a plan where an Employer offers an HRA that pays out first on certain kinds of claims before either an FSA or an HSA, you would want to create a Benefit Order in which the HRA was first.
To create a New Benefit Order:
Click the green New Benefit Order Button to open the Edit Benefit Order modal.
Figure 3. New Benefit Order
Enter a name for the new Benefit Order in the text box.
Figure 4. Edit Benefit Order
Select the Service Categories checkbox(es) that should be associated with the Benefit Order. When a claim is entered with a service category of the selected type(s), Summit will attempt to run the claim through the benefit order associated with the Service Category.
NOTE: You will only be able to associate a Service Category with one Benefit Order.
Figure 5. Service Category Selection
Select the Plan type check box(es) to include in the order.
Figure 6. Plan Type Selection
Highlighting the plans, arrange the order using the Up and Down arrow buttons.
Figure 7. Plan Order
Click Save when done.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Contribution Schedules
chunks.content:
Plan Default Settings | Contribution Schedules
Schedules are pre-defined processes that are used to generate or post Contributions in batches. Contribution Schedules are used to pull contributions for contribution-funded benefits. Summit will automatically calculate contributions from both employers and participants to plans based on Contribution Schedules. The TPA user can add, edit, and view schedules from the Contribution Schedule option in the Plan Default Settings menu.
Table of Contents
Add a Contribution Schedule
Edit a Contribution Schedule
Contribution Schedule Templates
  * Required fields appear in Red
To access the Contribution Schedule,
Go to Settings.
Click Plan Default Settings.
Select Contribution Schedules.
Add a Contribution Schedule
The user can add schedules by clicking the “+Add Schedule” link.
By clicking the “+Add Schedule” link, the Contribution Schedule Template modal will display.
Schedule Name – This is a mandatory alphanumeric field including spaces. Here the user has to enter a name for the schedule which is being created.
Process Type – From this dropdown list, the user can select any one of the entries to provide the type of process being carried out.
Automatic Processing – By selecting this option, the system will fully automate the process without any manual intervention.
Manual Processing – If this option is selected, the process needs user approval.
Status – All the created schedules will be in a status of “Active” by default. Only at the time of editing, a user can update the status to “Inactive” or “Suspended”.
Funding Source – This field indicates by which sources funding will be done. Two checkboxes with options “Employer” and “Participant” can be seen here. By default, both are checked.
Recurrence – This field indicates by which recurrence the created schedule should works. The options populated are:
Weekly
Bi-weekly
Semi-monthly
Monthly
Quarterly
Annual

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Contribution Schedules
chunks.content:
Day – This field will display values based on the selections made in the Recurrence field. The user has to select the required value from this dropdown list.
If “Weekly” was selected in the Recurrence field, then this section will display a dropdown list inclusive of every day of the week (Sunday to Saturday). The user needs to select a day from the dropdown or type the desired day to narrow the selections.
Bi-weekly selection indicates that the system will run the process every other week. (Or once every two weeks). If “Bi-weekly” was selected, the user has to type or select a day from the dropdown list.
If the entry in Recurrence field is “Semi–monthly” (twice a month), the system will display a calendar showing 31 days. The user needs to click and highlight two numbers on the calendar indicating these are the 2 days of every month they would like to run the process. If 29, 30 or 31 is selected, then the system will pop-up a warning informing while saving the template. This is to inform the user that the process will run on the selected day or the last day of the month, whichever is later.
If it is “Monthly”, the user can enter a numeric value in this field or can select a number from the calendar indicating the day of each month they would like to run the process. If the user selects 29, 30 or 31, the same logic described for “Semi–monthly” will apply here.
For “Quarterly”, once the date has been set, the system will then calculate exact dates with a time interval of 3 months from the first contribution date. Here the system will display an actual calendar instead of a grid of 31 days. The user has to click on a date or simply type the date indicating the first contribution date.
If it is “Annual” the same date field as that of “Quarterly” is provided. The user needs to click on a date or type the desired date to indicate the date of each year they would like the process to run.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Contribution Schedules
chunks.content:
Start Date – The Start Date indicates the date on which the contribution process begins to run. This is a standard date field where the default date is set as the current date. The user can update this date to a date in the past or the future.
Default Schedule – For each Funding Source, a user can mark one schedule as default by checking the given check box. If the user marks a single schedule with a Funding Source of both Employer and Participant as default, then no other schedule at the TPA level can be marked as the default schedule.
Account for US Banking Holidays – This is a checkbox that is checked by default. By checking this box, the system will avoid scheduling the contribution process on US Banking Holidays. The “show” link next to the checkbox will produce a small pop-up window showing the list of holidays.
Each holiday will have a checkbox that will be checked by default. If needed, the user can uncheck or recheck these checkboxes.
Another link named “Add Custom Holidays” can be seen next to the “show” link.
By clicking this link, a pop-up will be displayed as follows to add or remove Custom Holidays to the standard US Holidays.
Weekend/Holiday Processing – This is a read-only dropdown list with the default value “No Change”. A contribution schedule may have a number of dates that will fall on weekends or holidays. By this option, the user can update the process dates on the calendar to business days before or after weekends/holidays else keep the same. The options populated in the dropdown are:
Before
After
No Change

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Contribution Schedules
chunks.content:
Display Dates – This is a link that shows all of the calculated contribution dates on a calendar when clicked. The first month of the calendar will be the month of Start Date and then 11 additional months. When adding a schedule, the expected contribution dates will only be highlighted as green. In Edit mode, Contribution dates are well highlighted on the calendar with green for the dates that are not yet processed, and with yellow for that have already been processed. The user has the ability to manually update individual contribution dates. The user can click on a date to add it to the schedule in edit mode and can also click on a calculated date to remove it from the schedule. The additional dates will appear as blue and skipped dates will appear as red in the calendar.
Display Dates in Add Schedule mode will be as follow:
Display Dates in Edit Schedule mode will be as follow:
Pre-Processing Alert – This alert is configured to notify the user in advance that the contribution process will run at the scheduled time. The user has to check the check box of Pre-processing Alert and add recipients of this email alert by clicking the “Assign Users” link. The link will produce a pop-up containing the list of all existing users with checkboxes. The user can select up to 10 users to receive the alert.
When the selection is saved, the page will list all the e-mail addresses associated with the selected users in a box on the page. If needed, the user can also add additional e-mail addresses manually as long as the total number of addresses does not exceed 10.
Alert/Notify – From this dropdown list, the user can determine on which day they wish to receive this Pre-processing alert. The default option is Processing Minus 1. The options in the dropdown list are:
Same Day
Processing Minus 1
Processing Minus 2
Processing Alert – Processing Alerts are triggered when the process begins to run. Adding recipients for processing alert is the same as that described in the Pre-processing Alerts.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Contribution Schedules
chunks.content:
Post-processing Alert – Post-processing Alerts are configured to trigger once the process completes its run. Adding recipients for this alert is the same as that described in the Pre-processing Alerts.
Click the “Save” button after entering all required fields.
Edit a Contribution Schedule
The Contribution Schedules page will display the contribution schedules added in the schedule table with the Schedule Name, Processing Type, Employer Funding, Participant Funding, Recurrence, and Status details.
Schedule Name – In this field, the name of the schedule will display. The user can edit a schedule by clicking the Schedule Name, the Contribution Schedule Templates modal will display.
Processing Type – Here, the processing type of the schedule will be displayed.
Employer Funding – This field will indicate, whether the schedule is employer funding or not.
Participant Funding – This field will display, whether the schedule is participant funding or not.
Recurrence – The recurrence of the schedule will be shown in this field.
Status – Here, the status of the schedule is displayed.
Contribution Schedule Templates
Status – By default, all the created schedules will be in a status of “Active”. But a user can change the status into “Inactive” or “Suspended” by updating it.
Active – It is the default status of all created contribution schedules. When a schedule is in a status of “Active”, it means that the schedule is available for assignment to Employers.
Suspended – When this status is selected, the system will display an icon right to the dropdown. After saving this status, the system will suspend the process associated with the schedule and will not send alerts until the status is updated back to Active. If a date was missed between suspension and reactivation, the system will catch up and create a file for that missed date.
Inactive – When a schedule is in “Inactive” status, it means that the schedule is no longer available for assignment.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Contribution Schedules
chunks.content:
Last Date – This field will display the last date that the schedule has run.
Next Date – This field will display the very next date that the schedule will run. There available an option on the right side of the field to skip this date.
Assigned Employers – The employers assigned will display in the employer table with Employer, Funding Source, Pre-processing Alert, Processing Alert, Post-processing Alert, and Alert E-mail details.
Employer – Here, the employer name will display.
Funding Source – Here, there are two checkboxes (Employer and Participant) to indicate the funding source.
Pre-processing Alert – This checkbox will indicate whether the schedule has pre-processing alert.

  * Required fields appear in Red
The Denial Codes/Comments section of Plan Default Settings allows you to view and modify the Denial and Request codes for claims submitted for reimbursement through Summit. [Not to be confused with Premium Billing Denial Codes which are used for when an individual is denied coverage.]
When reviewing participants’ claims, if the claim is not approved for reimbursement, it may either be denied or held pending the fulfillment of a request for additional information. The denial and request code reasons allow you to record the reason for why a claim has been denied or why a request for additional information has been sent.
To access the Denial Codes/Comments screen:
Go to Settings
Mouse-over Plan Default Settings
Click Denial Codes/Comments
Denial Codes
The Denial Codes here are available to assign as the denial Reason when entering manual claims or reviewing claims that have been denied. The code number is available for importing/exporting purposes. The Description is the reason which will display to both the TPA and the Participant on the claim form and may be merged in claim denial communications.
The default denial codes in Summit include:
1 – Claim exceeds available funds
2 – Claim was received after the run-out date
3 – Claim denied because you do not participant in the 105 plan
4 – Claim denied because you do not participate in the 125 plan
5 – Claim denied because you do not participate in the 132 plan
6 – The expense submitted is not eligible for your plan
7 – Claim submitted does not fall within a valid plan year
8 – Claim submitted is a duplicate of a previous claim

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Denial Codes/Comments
chunks.content:
9 – Claim exceeds the annual election for your plan year
10 – Claim exceeds the allowable monthly limits of your plan
11 – Dependent not covered
12 – Electronically submitted claim was denied by insurer
These denial code reasons cover most reasons why you would deny a participant’s claim, however you may add your own custom Denial Codes.
Add a Denial Code
If you need to add an additional Denial code, click the green Add Code button.
A New Denial Code popup will appear, allowing you to add a new Code and a short Description.
Complete the fields and click Save to add the new denial code.
Note: The Code may consist of numbers and/or letters. If the Code or Description matches an existing code/description, a warning will appear, however, you will be allowed to save the duplicate code/description.
Edit a Denial Code
To edit a Denial Code, click the linked code in the Denial Codes grid.
The Edit Denial Code modal will appear and allow you to modify the Code and Description or Delete the code.
If you choose to delete the code, a Deletion Confirmation pop-up will verify that you wish to continue.
Delete One/Multiple Denial Code(s)
In addition to deleting Denial Codes from the Edit Denial Code screen, you may remove one or multiple codes by selecting the checkbox(es) on the Denial Code grid and clicking the green Delete Selected Code button.
You will be prompted by a Deletion Confirmation pop-up if you wish to continue.
Restore System Defaults
If for any reason you need to restore the Denial Codes list to the DataPath default, you may do so by clicking the Restore System Defaults link.
A pop-up will confirm that the Denial Code data has been restored to the DataPath defaults.
Note: This will not only remove any codes you have added and restore any codes you have deleted, but it will also revert any edits you have made to the default codes to their original values.
Request Codes

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Denial Codes/Comments
chunks.content:
In some cases, additional information may be required to determine whether a claim should be approved and reimbursed or denied.
The Request Codes here are available to assign as the request Reason when entering manual claims or reviewing claims that have been flagged as Request for additional information from the participant. The code number is available for importing/exporting purposes. The Description is the reason which will display to both the TPA and the Participant on the claim form and may be merged in claim request communications.
The default request codes in Summit include:
1 – The receipt submitted is not readable
2 – The amount of the claim submitted cannot be determined
3 – Need additional facts and circumstances of the claim
4 – Need the claimant
5 – Need to know the dates of service
6 – Need to know what service was performed
7 – Need to know what type of claim was submitted
8 – The claim form was not signed
9 – The claim is still pending adjudication by your health insurer
Add a Request Code
If you need to add an additional Request code, click the green Add Code button.
A New Request Code popup will appear, allowing you to add a new Code and a short Description.
Complete the fields and click Save to add the new request code.
Note: The Code may consist of numbers and/or letters. If the Code or Description matches an existing code/description, a warning will appear, however, you will be allowed to save the duplicate code/description.
Edit a Request Code
To edit a Request Code, click the linked code in the Request Codes grid.
The Edit Request Code modal will appear and allow you to modify the Code and Description or Delete the code.
If you choose to delete the code, a Deletion Confirmation pop-up will verify that you wish to continue.
Delete One/Multiple Request Code(s)

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Denial Codes/Comments
chunks.content:
In addition to deleting Request Codes from the Edit Request Code screen, you may remove one or multiple codes by selecting the checkbox(es) on the Request Codes grid and clicking the green “Delete Selected Code” button.
You will be prompted by a Deletion Confirmation pop-up if you wish to continue.
Restore System Defaults
If for any reason you need to restore the Request Codes list to the DataPath default, you may do so by clicking the Restore System Defaults link.
A pop-up will confirm that the Request Code data has been restored to the DataPath defaults.
Note: This will not only remove any codes you have added and restore any codes you have deleted, it will also revert any edits you have made to the default codes to their original values.
Claim Comments
In addition to Denial and Request codes, you may add any custom Claim Comments that have been set up here to claims. These comments will be available for selection from the Claim Comment dropdown of the claim entry form regardless of the claim’s status [Approve, Deny, Request, or Review].
Note: There is no default Claim Comments.
Add a Claim Comment
To add a Claim Comment, click the green “Add Comment” button.
The New Claim Comments pop-up will appear.
Enter a name and comment in the Name and Detail field and click Save.
Edit Claim Comments
To edit a Claim Comment, click the linked code in the Claim Comments grid.
Delete One/Multiple Claim Comment(s)
In addition to deleting Claim Comments from the Edit Claim Comment screen, you may remove one or multiple codes by selecting the checkbox(es) on the Claim Comments grid and clicking the green Delete Selected Comment button.
You will be prompted by a Deletion Confirmation pop-up if you wish to continue.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
DirectPay is a feature by which we are able to securely integrate payment information so that participants can use their plan dollars to shop at FSAStore.com, an online health products retailer. DirectPay allows Summit Participants to utilize their FSA dollars to make direct purchases of goods and automatically create claims in Summit for the corresponding purchases without providing their debit card information or post-purchase substantiation.
The DirectPay feature is a no-cost Add-On that must be enabled for your TPA in Summit for the settings described to be available to your users. Please contact your DataPath Account Manager if you would like this feature activated. Once activated, the guidance below regarding Plan Templates and Employer Plans will provide instructions to configure DirectPay in Summit, as desired.
Table of Contents
Plan Templates & Employer Plans
Benefit Order
Method of Payment: DirectPay – FSA Store
Providers
Service Categories & Codes
Participant Portal Links
Participant Consent Form
APIs
Reimbursement Process
Cash Management
Transaction Search
Participant Portal Settings – Optional Home Banner
Plan Templates & Employer Plans
FSA Plan Templates have an “FSA Store DirectPay” checkbox which, when checked, will enable the FSA Store DirectPay option for plans subsequently created using that template. If the FSA Store DirectPay feature is enabled for a TPA, new FSA Plan Templates will have the FSA Store DirectPay option selected by default.
The FSA Store DirectPay checkbox option located in the Claim Processing Rules section of the Plan Template.
This option will also display accordingly on FSA Employer Plans. If the Employer Plan was created using a Plan Template, the value from the plan template at the time of plan creation will populate for the Employer Plan.
Benefit Order

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
When the FSA Store DirectPay module is enabled, a TPA default Benefit Order specifically for DirectPay will be included on the Settings | Plan Default Settings | Benefit Orders screen. This Benefit Order is used for the FSA Store DirectPay feature that will allow the purchases from the store to be processed as claims within Summit. Claims with the FSA Store Service Category will pass through this Benefit Order for processing.
Method of Payment: DirectPay – FSA Store
The “DirectPay – FSA Store” Method of Payment will appear in the ClaimPaymentMethod table for claims created by purchases in the FSA. Claims with the MOP = “DirectPay – FSA Store” and Provider = “FSA Store” will be excluded from reimbursement schedules.
This Method of Payment may not be manually selected or associated with any other kinds of claim transaction. Claims imported with this Method of Payment will be rejected with an “Invalid Method of Payment” exception.
Payment Method displaying as “Direct Pay – FSA Store” in Claim Details
Providers
The FSA Store is included as a Provider in the list of providers in Settings | Advanced Plan Designs | Provider Networks. This allows Summit to process claims for DirectPay to the FSA Store. When a claim is received from the FSA Store, Summit will automatically select the FSA Store as the Provider for purposes of remitting payment via an automated EFT process.
Provider will appear as “FSA Store” in claim details.
Service Categories & Codes
Summit uses an “FSA Store” Service Category which is assigned to all claims resulting from purchases made in the FSA store.
An “FSA Store (health product)” default Service Code is assigned to the “FSA Store” Service Category.
Neither the FSA Store Service Category nor the FSA Store (health product) Service code may be modified or deleted by users.
Service Category displaying “FSA Store” and Service Code displaying “FSA Store – FSA Store (Health Product)” in Claim Details
Participant Portal Links

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
When DirectPay is enabled, the Participant Portal will include Single Sign-On (SSO) links to the FSA Store site, allowing participants who have been assigned FSA plans that are DirectPay enabled to make direct purchases of goods using their plan dollars within the current plan year or its Grace Period.
If the Participant has an FSA and the plan is FSA Store DirectPay-enabled, the link will take the user to the FSA Store.
Link to the FSA Store on the Participant Portal Homepage
The link will be present for the Participant on the Coverages page for each FSA coverage that is current or in the Grace Period.
Link to the FSA Store on the Participant Portal Coverages screen
The SSO authentication will pass along the following information to the store site:
TPA Unique ID
TPA Name
Employer Name
Participant Unique ID
First Name
Last Name
Email Address
Participant Portal URL
Participant Mailing Address 1
Participant Mailing Address 2
Participant City
Participant State
Participant ZIP
The participant will automatically be logged into the store site provided the Participant Consent form described in the following section has been completed and stored with an affirmative value. If the Consent form has not been completed or Consent has been revoked by the participant, the participant will be prompted to complete the Consent for before being passed to the FSA Store site.
Participant Consent Form
To access the FSA Store via the SSO integration, the participant must have an active consent to share their data with the FSA Store.
If the participant does not have an active Consent to Share Data status on their account when attempting to access the FSA Store through the Participant Portal, they will be prompted to acknowledge and approve enrollment in DirectPay.
A popup with the following consent language will display:

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
“By enrolling in DirectPay, you allow Health-e Commerce, parent brand of FSA Store, to use your personal information as provided by DataPath, in accordance with FSA Store’s Terms of Use and Privacy Notice. Your personal information may include, but is not limited to: your name, age, postal address, phone number, account balance, employer identification, participant identification, administrator identification, and other information used to populate your registration. This consent to share data with Health-e Commerce will expire in 365 days.  The expiration date will refresh every time you use one of the DirectPay links on the Participant Portal.  You may opt out of your enrollment at any time [by logging in to your portal, viewing your User Account (click your name at the top of the page), and following the prompts.
Please note that this authorization constitutes your written consent to enroll in FSA Store Inc.’s DirectPay service.”
If the participant agrees to continue, the Consent will be saved to their Summit Account.
The Consent will be saved for the participant for up to one full calendar year + 1 day unless revoked. If the Consent expires, the participant must complete the Active Consent form again to access the FSA Store.
APIs
The FSA Store DirectPay module uses a number of APIs that synchronize the data being exchanged between Summit and the FSA Stores, update balances, create claim records, etc.
Balances – Summit will receive and respond to balance calls from FSAStore.com for participants’ plan balances. Summit will only respond with the balance and identifying information if the participant has an active Consent status.
DirectPay Purchase – Whenever a participant initiates a DirectPay purchase on the FSA Store, the store site will send a DirectPay Purchase call with the participant’s ID and the Purchase Request amount. Summit will return the Authorized Payment Amount if applicable and will create a pending claim in Summit.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
Claim from Purchase Authorization – When a DirectPay Purchase results in an Authorized Payment Amount >0, a claim will be created for the participant in Summit.
The “CreatedBy” field for the claim record will be “FSA Store.”
The Created Date, Start/End Dates, and Received Date will use the system date on which the API call was received.
The Claimant will be “Participant”
The Total Claim Amount will be the Authorized Payment Amount from the API
The Total Denied Amount will be 0.
The Service Category will be “FSA Store”
The Service Code will be “FSA Store – FSA Store (health product)”
The Provider will be “FSA Store”
The Payee will be “Provider”
The Payment Method will be “DirectPay to FSA Store”
The Carrier Claim Number field will record a unique order/transaction identifier included in the Claim API
The Claim Status will be “Approved”
The claim will be calculated and applied to appropriate plan balances as determined by the Benefit Order and a payment record will be created for the claim with the Provider as the Payee and DirectPay to FSA Store as the method of payment. The participant’s plan balance will be debited by the appropriate amount [the Payment Authorization Amount included in the API call]. No reimbursements will be created by Summit via this claim [i.e. no Direct Deposits or Checks will be generated corresponding to the claim amount.]

DirectPay claims WILL NOT recalculate when other claims are edited. If the recalculation of an older claim results in a reimbursement amount that was different than what was previously paid and is more than the current plan balance, DirectPay claims will be excluded from the recalculation process and will never be placed in a Balance Due status.
Cancel Transaction – In the event that a transaction is cancelled, a Cancel Transaction API will be exchanged for the amount of the transaction and with an indication of the type of cancellation:

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
CustomerReturn – If a participant performs a return on the FSA Store, then the site will send a Cancel Transaction: CustomerReturn call to Summit, and Summit will apply the return transaction against the prior FSA Store Claim. The Return will be matched to the original purchase transaction via the unique identifier recorded in the Carrier Claim Number. The original claim’s Total Claim Amount, payment record, and reimbursement amount will be reduced by the Return amount sent by the FSA Store.
CustomerCancellation – In the event that a participant cancels a DirectPay purchase from the FSA Store before the product order is shipped, the site will send and Summit will receive a call that will reduce the original claim amount by the amount of the cancellation (up to the entire amount of the original purchase if the entire original purchase is cancelled). Note: Participants may need to directly contact FSA Store’s customer service to cancel orders currently in process.
VendorReversal – In the event that the transaction is reversed by the vendor, the site will send and Summit will receive a call that will reduce the original claim by the amount indicated by the vendor reversal.
The CancelTransaction will create a record in EFTLocal to reduce the daily net of funds to pull from the employer’s bank account.
Reimbursement Process
Claims with DirectPay to FSA Store as the payment method are not considered or processed when TPA-defined reimbursement schedules are run.
These claims are handled by an automated process which will run Monday through Friday just after midnight.
The process will aggregate all transactions with MOP = DirectPay to FSA that have not been captured, summing Payments less CancelTransactions by employer.
A Settlement file will be created and sent to EFTLocal for each employer for FSA Store claims when the calculated FSA Store transactions amount is greater than 0.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
The process will create a record in Cash Management with a “DirectPay to FSA Store Settlement” Transaction Type.
Cash Management
DirectPay money movements may be tracked in Summit’s Cash Management using the following Bank Transaction Types:
DirectPay – FSA Store Settlement
Post
CustomerReturn
CustomerCancelation
VendorReversal
The DirectPay – FSA Store Settlement will be available for selection from the Transaction Types filter in Cash Management. The other transaction types are subtypes which are contained within the Settlement transactions.
DirectPay – FSA Store Settlement contains the following details:
Date
Filtered Amount
Total Amount
Transaction Type (DirectPay – FSA Store)
Employer Name – This field will display the total # of sub transactions within the settlement transaction
Participant Name -This field will display the total # of participants for whom there were subtransactions within the settlement transaction
Payee (FSA Store)
DirectPay – FSA Store Settlement transactions are expandable to show all transactions included in the settlement calculation. Payment, Customer Return, Cancelation, and Reversal subtransaction types are aggregated within the Settlement Transaction on Cash Management.
The Transaction Types contained within the expanded settlement records include the following fields:
Date
Amount
Employer name
Participant Name
Coverage – This column will be blank as it does not apply to FSA Store subtransactions
Period – This column will be blank as it does not apply to FSA Store subtransations
Reference Number (Unique Order ID)
Type [Subtype]
These records in Cash Management are read-only and cannot be edited, voided, or deleted.
Transaction Search
The Provider multiselector on the Processing | Transaction Search and the Participant Central | Transactions tab Transaction Search allows users to search for transactions by Provider, particularly those transactions associated with DirectPay. [Note that all providers will be selected by default on these filters.]

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | DirectPay
chunks.content:
The “DirectPay – FSA Store” Transaction Type can be chosen from the Transaction Type selector to include or omit DirectPay transactions from the query results.
These filters will allow users to search for Summit Transactions by Provider as well as search for DirectPay transactions.
Processing | Transaction Search
Participant Central | Transactions tab | View Transaction History / Transaction Search History
Participant Portal Settings – Optional Home Banner
TPAs may enable or disable an optional FSA Store banner from the Participant Portal Settings’ page’s Recommendations section that will display on the Participant Portal Home Page. This banner will be selected to display by default. This banner is in addition to the banner links that will automatically display next to the participant’s FSA Coverages.

chunks.title: Plan Default Settings | Reimbursement Settings
chunks.content:
Plan Default Settings | Reimbursement Settings
The Plan Default Settings | Reimbursement Settings page is where you will customize the TPA-level business logic by which Summit will process claims and generate reimbursements for participants.
Table of Contents
General Settings
Duplicate Claims
Banking/Checking
Schedules
Communications
Claims Entry Preferences
To access Plan Default Settings | Reimbursement Settings:
Go to Settings
Mouse-over Plan Default Settings
Click on Reimbursement Settings
General Settings
This tab contains run-out/timeout logic settings as well as an option for whether Summit should include the system-generated claim numbers on participant communications and the Participant Portal.
Duplicate Claims
This tab contains the settings that will determine the logic used to match claims and determine which claims may be duplicates.
Banking/Checking
This tab contains the settings necessary for the setup of the TPA Reimbursement Account from which reimbursements will be issued, as well as the configuration of the Debit Card Settlement account and other TPA-level banking settings used by Summit for the purpose of creating payments.
Schedules
This tab allows for the setup and configuration of batch processes for the creation of reimbursements.
Communications
This tab contains the settings for how Summit will handle communications related to claims, including Approval, Denial, and Request letters, and allows the text of these communications to be modified globally for both emails and physical letters.
Claims Entry Preferences
This tab allows for customization and re-ordering of Summit’s default Claim Entry form at the global level to create a claim form that better suits your business needs.
For further information, please refer to the Reimbursement Settings section in FAQs.

chunks.content:
Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications
Summit allows users to customize and create notifications (letters and emails) to meet both TPA and Employer communication needs. This section covers Summit’s Premium Billing communication features, which support sending letters and email notifications between the TPA, Employers, Carriers, and Participants.
Table of Contents

To access Premium Billing Notifications & Communications:
Go to Settings.
Mouse over Premium Billing.
Click on Notifications & Communications.
Figure 1. Premium Billing Notifications & Communications

Figure 2. Notifications & Communications
The Notifications & Communications modal is divided into the following subsections:
Document Templates
Email Settings
Event Settings
Email Settings
The Email Settings section displays all email configuration details and allows users to add and edit email communications.
To edit Email Settings:
The email address in the From text box is read-only. This is the sending contact email address.
If desired, enter email addresses in the CC Recipients and BCC Recipients fields.
CC Recipients – Email addresses of copied recipients.
BCC Recipients – Email addresses of blind‑copied recipients.
To add an image to your notifications, click the Edit icon (pencil). A pop-up window will appear where you can select an image.
To remove the image, click the Delete icon (trash can)
Change the image Position by selecting the Left, Center, or Right radio button.
Click Save.
Figure 3. Email Settings
Document Templates
This section contains information about the document, including:
Name – The name of the template link.
Document Name – Name of the document.
Active – This column indicates whether the notification is active to be sent if the assigned event(s) occur. This is a read-only field.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications
chunks.content:
System Default – This column indicates if a system-default notification is enabled. This is a read-only field. Any user cannot delete a system-default notification, but it can be copied by saving the notice with a different title.
Figure 4. Document Templates
To download a template:
Clicking the link in the Name column. A pop-up will display.
Figure 5. Download Template Pop-up Window

Figure 6. Download Template Link

An event is an activity that must occur to produce a letter or email notification. This section will display the following Parameters:
Figure 11. Event Settings
Fulfillment – This is a radio button field with options “Manual Fulfillment” and “Datapath Fulfillment”. Select the fulfillment type and click save. This setting determines if the documents generated by the event are produced in a file for TPA download, printing, and mailing [Manual] or sent via DataPath’s mailing and fulfillment service.

Include Inactive events – When this checkbox is marked, all the inactive events will be included in the table.
+Add Event – This option can only be activated if no employer has been selected. When this link is clicked, an Add Custom Event UI will appear that allows the user to enter a custom Event Title, select and assign notification templates, and configure those notices notification settings. Custom Events that have been triggered will be included in the LOS Activity Report and the PB Mailing Report.
The pop-up window contains the following parameters,
Event Title – The Title is the name of an event.  The Title cannot be changed or modified by the User. The event title is a 60-character, alpha-numeric field.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications
chunks.content:
Active – This is a checkbox option. By checking this option, the event becomes active. New custom events will be “Active” by default. Note that if events are not “Active,” they will not be triggered. If a user deselects the Active checkbox, a warning message will display, informing the user “Making an event inactive will prevent the event from being triggered, which may have unexpected results.”
Approval Required – This checkbox option will be unchecked by default. When this checkbox is unchecked, the custom events will be flagged for auto-approval in Process Approvals.

Email Format – When this link is clicked, a PB Custom Event Notification Email UI will appear. Here, the user is allowed to customize the subject and content of Premium Billing Event email alerts. The user can add TPA, Employer, and Participant demographic merge fields to the communication as well as the template/notification’s name and a date merge field to indicate when the communication event was triggered. Additionally, the user can include the image uploaded in the Email Settings section as a merged logo in the email.
Also, the user can revert a communication’s body to the Summit defaults by the “Restore System Defaults” link, and communications generated subsequent to this revert will use the default text. Users can customize all non-custom event emails or use the TPA default email, per employer. TPA custom emails created for custom events will be used for all custom events, for all employers.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications
chunks.content:
All active English and Spanish notification templates will be available for selection to assign to the custom event. As with default PB Events, up to three templates may be associated with the event. Users may create custom templates to assign to custom events. These templates are restricted to the TPA, Employer, and Participant data sources.
The grid contains the following columns:
Document – In the English and Spanish document columns, the user will select the notification from the dropdown list.  The system will prepopulate the dropdown list with all English, Spanish, user-created, and system-default notifications.
Entity – This column contains a dropdown list that includes ‘Employer’, ‘Carrier’, and ‘Participant’. By checking the ‘Select all’ checkbox, all entities will be selected.
Send to Mailing Address – By checking this option, notifications will be sent to the Participant’s Mailing Address.
Send Email – This option is available only when the selected Entity is Participant. Selecting “E-mail” indicates that the User wants the system to send notifications via e-mail.
Send Letter If No Email – By checking this checkbox option, notifications will be sent by letter if no email address is assigned.
Send To Home Address – By checking this option, notifications will be sent to the Participant’s Home Address.
Send To Dependent Address – By checking this option, notifications will be sent to any or all Dependent Addresses.
Use Datapath Fulfillment – By checking this checkbox option, Datapath fulfillment will be selected.
After editing the required fields, click Save.
Event Settings Table – The following are the table parameters :
Name – This column will display the name of the event. By clicking on the link in the Name column, a pop-up window will appear that lists all documents assigned to the event and allows the user to add or remove notifications for each event.
Active – This read-only field indicates whether the event is active or not.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications
chunks.content:
System Default – This is also a read-only field, and it indicates whether the event is system-default or not.
Approval Required – If manual approval is required for triggering the event, a green checkmark will be shown here. Otherwise, a not icon will display.
Participant History – If checked, a green checkmark will be shown. Otherwise, a not icon will display.
Delete – The user will be able to delete custom events so long as it has not been triggered for a participant. If the custom event has been triggered for a participant and the user clicks the delete icon, they will receive a message informing them, “This event has been triggered for a participant and cannot be deleted.”
If you are looking for further information, please refer to the Premium Billing Notifications and Communications section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Premium Auto Draft Settings
chunks.content:
Premium Billing | Premium Auto Draft Settings
Premium Auto Draft Settings allows TPAs to draft premium payments from the checking accounts of participants who have opted in for auto‑drafted payments. Schedules are used to generate or post Premium Auto Drafts in batches.
Participants with default banking information who opt in to premium auto‑drafting will have their premium payments drafted for each billing period in which billing is available. If a participant has multiple coverages, premium payments will be drafted for all coverages that have available billing.
Table of Contents
Auto Draft Schedules
Heading Section
Scheduling Section
Calendar Section
Alerts Section
Pre-processing Alert
Manual Approval Alert
Post processing Alert
Employers Section
Additional rules:
 * Required fields appear in Red
To access Premium Auto Draft Settings,
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Premium Billing.
Click Premium Auto Draft Settings.
The Premium Auto Draft Settings page will appear.
Select a TPA from the dropdown list.
Auto Draft Schedules
To add a new schedule, click the +Add Schedule link on the right side. This opens the Add Premium Auto‑Draft Schedule modal.

To edit an existing schedule, click the linked Schedule Name in the table, which opens the Edit Premium Auto‑Draft Schedule modal.
The Add/Edit modals contain the following fields and settings:
Heading Section
Name –Enter the name of the auto‑draft schedule. When editing an existing schedule, this field becomes a dropdown list containing all Premium Auto‑Draft schedules, with the current schedule name auto‑selected.
Manual Approval Required – When checked, any payments generated by the auto‑draft schedule will appear on the Process Approvals UI for manual approval. This checkbox is selected by default.
When enabled, the user may select the Manual Approval Alert checkbox, Assign Users, and Additional Recipients fields.
When disabled:
The ACH payment file is generated immediately.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Premium Auto Draft Settings
chunks.content:
If using DataPath EFT services, payments will be drafted and processed automatically.
If manually processing ACH payments, Summit generates the ACH file for download under Processing > File Fulfillment (set Fulfillment Type to Manual Fulfillment).
ACH File Delivery – Determines how ACH files created by this schedule will be delivered:
Manually Download – Creates a NACHA file containing approved auto‑drafted payments and sends it to the File Fulfillment UI for download. If Manual Approval Required is enabled, individual auto‑drafts will appear in Process Approvals.
DataPath Fulfillment – Summit processes auto‑drafted payments through the DataPath Fulfillment process. This option is selected by default.
Scheduling Section
Premium Auto‑Draft schedules run based on the frequency, date/day, and time defined by the TPA user. Auto‑draft schedules currently support monthly billing frequencies, as Summit billing periods are monthly.
The Scheduling section includes:
Run Every – Configures how often and on which days the schedule should run. The value must be greater than 0.
Default: Run Every [1] [Week(s)] on [Monday]
Users may change this to any valid combination of:
Day(s)
Week(s)
Month(s)
Year(s)
Start Date – The first date the schedule will run. Defaults to the current date but may be set to a past or future date.
Exclude receipts within _ days of system date – When checked, the user may enter the number of days for which receipts should be excluded.
Time – Select the time of day the schedule should run.
Time Zone – A dropdown list of global time zones. Select the appropriate time zone for execution.
Account for US Banking Holidays – When checked, Summit avoids running auto‑draft processing on U.S. bank holidays.
Weekend/Holiday Processing – Determines how schedule dates falling on weekends/holidays are handled:
Before (default)
After
No Change
Status – New schedules default to Active. Existing schedules may be changed to Suspended or Inactive.
Calendar Section

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Premium Auto Draft Settings
chunks.content:
The Calendar section displays all scheduled run dates and allows users to:
Add extra run dates
Skip scheduled dates
This enables precise control over when the schedule runs in addition to the standard recurrence.
Alerts Section
Users may enable and configure email alerts:
Pre‑Processing Alert
Manual Approval Alert
Post‑Processing Alert
Pre-processing Alert
Notifies the user before the schedule runs.
To enable:
Check the Pre‑Processing Alert checkbox.
Click Assign to Additional TPA Users to open a pop‑up listing all users.
Select up to 10 users.
Users can also select when to receive the alert:
Same Day
1 Day Prior (default)
2 Days Prior
All selected email addresses appear in the recipient list.
Manual Approval Alert
Available only when Manual Approval Required is enabled.
Recipient selection works the same as for Pre‑Processing Alerts.
Post processing Alert
Triggers when the schedule completes processing.
Recipient assignment follows the same process as Pre‑Processing Alerts.
Employers Section
Employers who have opted in to premium auto‑drafting appear in the Employers list. These employers may be assigned to or removed from the schedule.
To modify employer assignments:
Click Add/Remove Employers.
A modal opens using the standard Summit assignment tool.
Employers that the user has permission to access will appear in the All Employers list.
Additional rules:
An employer may only exist in schedules of one ACH delivery type (Manually Download or DataPath Fulfillment).
They may exist in multiple schedules only if they share the same delivery type.
If the employer is assigned to a conflicting schedule:
A warning indicator appears next to the employer name.
A warning message displays if the employer is being added to a conflicting delivery‑type schedule.
If the user confirms, Summit automatically unassigns the employer from the conflicting schedule.
After entering all required information or making changes, click Save to create or update the schedule.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Premium Billing Default Settings
chunks.content:
Premium Billing | Premium Billing Default Settings
Summit allows users to configure premium billing plan default settings on this page. Users can set rate expiration alerts and view, modify, and create Employer Templates from this screen.
Table of Contents
Premium Billing Default Settings
Rate Expiration Alert Settings
Employer Templates
Employer Template Table
Add Template
To access Premium Billing Default Settings:
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Premium Billing.
Select Premium Billing Default Settings.
Premium Billing Default Settings
The Premium Billing Default Settings page is divided into two subsections. They are Rate Expiration Alert Settings and Employer Templates.
Rate Expiration Alert Settings
This section contains the parameters used to configure if, when, and to whom rate expiration alerts should be sent.
Send rate expiration alert __ days before rate expires – A checkbox option.
When selected, a numeric field appears allowing the user to enter the number of days before the rate expiration date that the alert should be triggered.
When this checkbox is enabled, the following fields appear:
Assigned Users – A multi-selector dropdown list allowing the user to select recipients for the rate expiration alert. Users can check the box next to each recipient’s name and email address. A Select All option is also available.
Additional Recipients – A text field where users can enter additional email addresses, separated by semicolons.
Set From address as – The email address entered here will appear as the From address in the alert email communication.
After configuring the settings, click Save.
Template Type – The Template Type multi-selector dropdown allows the user to choose any combination of template types. Only the selected template type(s) will appear in the Employer Templates and Benefit Templates sections.
A Select All option is also available.
The template types in the list are:
COBRA
Retiree
General Options
Direct Bill
Employer Templates

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Premium Billing Default Settings
chunks.content:
In this section, users can view, add, and edit Employer Templates. These templates can be associated with Employer plans, and the plan settings defined in a template will be reflected in any Employer plan assigned to that template.
Employer Template Table
Users may print each Employer Template by clicking the Print icon at the top of the page.
The Employer Template Table contains the following columns:
Template Type – Displays the type of Employer Template. Available types include COBRA, Retiree, General Options, and Direct Bill.
Template Name – Displays the name of the Employer Template. Summit auto-populates this value by default, but users may overwrite it. Default naming examples include:
Cobra Default 1 for COBRA templates
Retiree Default 1 for Retiree templates
Direct Bill Default 1 for Direct Bill templates
Default General Options for General Options templates
Template Description – Displays the description for the Employer Template. Descriptions must be unique within the same template type. Clicking the description opens the Employer Template with a grayed-out Template ID field. Users may edit template settings and update changes.
Status – Shows the current status of the template. Templates default to Active when created, but users may change the status to Inactive at any time.
Created Date – Displays the date the Employer Template was created.
Add Inactive Template(s) – A checkbox (unchecked by default). When selected, inactive Employer Templates are included in the Employer Template Table.
Add Template
To create a new Employer Template, click the Add Template button and select an option from the dropdown list.
The following template types may be created:
COBRA – Selecting COBRA opens an Employer Template modal with the COBRA Template Type.
Retiree – Selecting Retiree opens a template modal configured for Retiree plans.
General Options – Selecting General Options opens a modal for general Employer configuration.

chunks.title: Premium Billing | Premium Billing Default Settings
chunks.content:
Direct Bill – Selecting Direct Bill opens a modal for Direct Bill Employer Templates.
In each template modal, users can:
Add or edit the Template Description
Enable or disable the Allow Editing at Employer Level option
Set the template Status (Active or Inactive)
For additional information about configuring these templates, refer to the Employer Central Premium Billing page.

chunks.content:
Privacy Policy
Effective Date: January 1, 2019
Last Updated: 6/30/2025
DataPath, Inc. (“DataPath,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) respects the privacy of individuals who access and use our secure platform to manage benefits-related services and accounts. This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, disclose, and protect personal information processed through our web-based platforms.
This policy applies only to the platform and services accessible through authorized user login. It does not apply to our corporate website or any other external websites.
Information We Collect
We may collect the following types of personal information from users accessing our platform:
Name, username, and login credentials
Employer or plan administrator affiliation
Contact information (e.g., email address, mailing address)
Account activity, including benefit elections or reimbursement submissions
Device and browser information, IP address, session data
Security-related metadata (e.g., multi-factor authentication logs)
We do not directly offer services to individuals. Any personal information we process is on behalf of plan administrators, TPAs, financial institutions, or employers who engage us to provide platform services.
How We Use the Information
Personal information is used to:
Authenticate and manage platform access
Process account activity and benefits transactions
Maintain and improve the platform’s functionality and security
Support compliance with applicable laws, plan rules, and contractual obligations
Provide user support and respond to inquiries
Cookies and Tracking Technologies
Our platform uses limited cookies and similar technologies to:
Maintain secure login sessions
Track session activity for audit and compliance
Monitor platform performance and usage trends
We do not use third-party advertising cookies or track users across unrelated websites.
Sharing of Information
We may share personal information:

chunks.title: Privacy Policy
chunks.content:
With the authorized third-party administrator (TPA), plan sponsor, or financial institution managing your account
With contracted service providers who support platform operations (e.g., hosting, IT, fraud detection)
When required by law, regulation, legal process, or to protect our legal rights
We do not sell or share personal information for marketing or advertising purposes.
Data Security
We implement appropriate technical and administrative safeguards to protect personal information, including:
Encryption of data in transit and at rest
Role-based access controls
Multi-factor authentication
Intrusion detection and monitoring systems
Despite these measures, no system can be completely secure. Users are encouraged to safeguard their credentials and report any suspected unauthorized access.
Data Retention
We retain personal information as necessary to:
Provide ongoing platform services
Fulfill legal or regulatory retention requirements
Support audits, inquiries, and historical account resolution
Retention periods are determined in coordination with our clients and legal obligations.
Your Rights
Users may request to:
Access the personal information associated with their platform account
Correct inaccurate information
Request deletion (subject to plan sponsor approval and legal obligations)
Requests should be directed to your plan administrator or benefits provider. You may also contact us at [Insert Email Address] for assistance.
California Residents
If you reside in California, you have additional rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA), including:
The right to know what personal information is collected and for what purposes
The right to request deletion of your personal information
The right to opt out of any sale or sharing of your personal information (we do not sell or share data)

privacy@dpath.com

DataPath

1601 Westpark Drive, Suite 9
Little Rock, AR 72204
Children’s Privacy

However, in the course of providing services to businesses, we may receive limited personal information about dependents, including minors, as part of benefits enrollment or claims processing.
This information is collected and processed solely to fulfill our contractual obligations and in accordance with applicable privacy and security laws.

The Batch Transaction Entry screen allows the user to enter multiple transaction records in batches for processing. This screen will be disabled and hidden for CDH-only TPAs.
To access this screen:
Go to Processing and select Batch Transaction Entry from the dropdown menu.
The Batch Transaction Entry screen will display as shown below:
Transaction Type – This dropdown allows the user to select the type of transaction for batch entry. Currently, the following transaction type is available:
PB Premium Payment
PB Premium Payment
This Transaction Type allows the user to manually enter multiple Premium Billing receipt records and post all of the payments at once.
To add premium billing receipts to the grid, click the +Add Premium Payment link.
This will add a line to the grid for entry.
The grid will contain the following fields:
Participant – A lookup field that allows the user to search for and select a participant by first name, last name, participant system ID, or participant custom ID. When hovering over a participant’s name in the result list, the employer name will display to the side.
The employer name also appears in the search results popup, such as in the global participant search bar.
Total Amount Due – The employer name also appears in the search results popup, such as in the global participant search bar.
Employer – Read-only field that auto-populates the employer name associated with the selected participant.
Payor –Allows selection of a payor or addition of a new payor by clicking the +New link.
Signature – The name entered in the signature line of the payment.
Payee – Allows selection of Payee, Employer, or TPA.
Method – Allows selection of the payment method
Reference # – Optional field for entering a payment reference number.
Postmarked – Allows selection of the postmarked date.
Received – Allows selection of the payment received date.
Amount – The amount of the receipt

chunks.title: Processing | Batch Transaction Entry
chunks.content:
Memo – Optional field for entering a memo note.
Users can add as many records to the grid as needed by clicking +Add Premium Payment to add additional lines. Records can be removed by clicking the Delete (trash can) icon at the end of the record.
Once finished adding receipts, click the Post Payments button.
Posted payments will display on the Receipts tab for the respective participants.
A batch receipt report containing the entered receipts will appear in the download tray. (Ensure pop-up blockers are disabled before posting payments so the report can be generated.)
The Batch Transaction Entry Premium Payment feature is role-enabled. User roles with access to Receipt Entry will automatically include permissions for this feature.
PB Batch Receipt Post-Grace Warning
Post-Grace date validation is performed on batch receipts for participants with coverages in a premium billing status (COBRA, Direct Bill, QB, or Retiree) when there is an amount due for a previous billing period and the premium payment transaction’s Postmarked Date is after the billing period’s premium payment grace date.
A Post-Grace Warning icon appears next to the Postmarked Date when premium payments are entered after the grace date on the Batch Transaction Entry screen and fail grace date validation.
When hovering over the Post-Grace Warning icon, the following message displays:
An admin user may proceed and make the payment.

A deposit slip is a form that is used to itemize the checks and cash being deposited into a bank account. The form includes the name on the account, the account number, the amount of each check being deposited, and the amount of any bills and coins being deposited.
The TPA user may occasionally need a bank deposit slip that contains both a summary and the details of the receipts deposited into the bank account. Summit can generate deposit slips for the receipt deposit transactions in Cash Management.

Go to Processing.
Select Cash Management.
Select Receipt Deposit from the Transaction Type dropdown or Add Transaction link.
Receipt Deposit
Receipt Deposits are performed by choosing Receipt Deposit from the Transaction Type filter or by selecting Receipt Deposit from the Add Transaction link on the Cash Management page.
Add Receipt Deposit
By clicking Receipt Deposit from the Add Transaction list, the Add A Transaction modal will display.
TPA – Displays the TPA name.
Bank Account – Shows the selected bank account in a read-only field.
Type – Displays the transaction type as read-only.
Employer – The Employer dropdown lists all employers assigned to the bank account. By default, the system auto-selects all employers.
Deposited – Users can enter a deposit date in this field. The system auto-populates the current date as the default Deposit Date.
Items Selected – TDisplays the number of receipts selected for the receipt deposit.
Running Total – Shows the sum of the receipt amounts for the selected receipts.
Receipts Table
The Receipts table displays receipt information for all receipts that have not yet been included in a receipt deposit. Users can select one or more receipts from the table.

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management | Receipt Deposit
chunks.content:
Received – The system auto-populates the receipt’s payment received date in the Received Date field (display-only).
Postmarked – If the payment postmark date is included on the receipt, the system auto-populates it in the display-only Postmarked field.
Reference Number – If a reference number is included on the receipt, the system auto-populates it in the display-only Reference Number field.
Payment Method – The payment method for the participant receipt appears as a link. When clicked, the system opens the Edit/Reassign Receipt modal.
Amount – The system auto-populates the receipt’s payment amount in the display-only Amount field.
Employer Name – The system auto-populates the employer’s name in the read-only Employer field.
Participant Name – The system auto-populates the participant’s name in the display-only Participant Name field.
Custom ID – If the participant has a custom ID, the system auto-populates it in the read-only Custom ID field.
To associate a receipt with the transaction, the user must check the checkbox next to the desired receipt(s) and then click the Save button.
Edit/Reassign Receipt Modal
Participant – The participant’s name is auto-populated in the Participant field (display-only).
Payment Method – The receipt payment method is auto-populated in the Payment Method field (display-only).
Status – From this dropdown list, the user can choose the receipt status. If no status exists for the receipt, the default value will be Select One. Dropdown options include:
Void
NSF
Stop
Payable To – Auto-populated from the employer template in the Payable To field (display-only).
Check Date – Auto-populated in the Check Date field. The user can change the date; no date validations are performed.
Payor –Displays the payor name (read-only).
Reference Number – Auto-populated in the Reference Number field. The user can edit this field.
Date Received – Auto-populated in the Date Received field. The user can change the date. This is a mandatory field.

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management | Receipt Deposit
chunks.content:
Signature – Auto-populated from the receipt.
Amount – The receipt amount is auto-populated in the Amount field, as display-only.
Postmark Date – The postmark date is auto-populated in the Postmarked Date field.  The user can change the date.
Memo – Auto-populated from the receipt. The user can edit this field.
Deposit Date – Display-only date field.
Deposited – Display-only currency field. The system shall auto-populate blanks in the Deposited field.
Refunded Amount – The user can enter the refund amount for the receipt. The default value is zero.
Total Refunded – Display-only currency field. Auto-populated by the system.
Applied – The receipt’s applied amount will be auto-populated in the Applied field as display-only. When the user reassigns the coverage’s applied amount, the system adds the amounts and updates the field.  The system will save the updated Applied amount and will display the amount on the Receipts tab.  All applied amount changes will be saved for the receipt history.
Un-applied – The system will auto-populate the unapplied amount in the Unapplied field, as display-only. Calculated as Amount – (Applied + Refund).
Paid Through – Displays the paid-through date.
Billing Period Balance Due – Displays the balance due for the billing period.
After entering all mandatory fields, click Save.
View Receipt Deposit
When the user selects Receipt Deposit as the Transaction Type and then clicks the Search button, the system includes Premium Billing Receipt Deposit transactions in the Cash Management page transactions table.
Account Balance – The total amount of the bank account balance will auto-populate in this field as display-only.
Filtered Balance – When Receipt Deposit is selected as the transaction type, the filtered bank account balance includes the amount of receipt deposit transactions within the selected Start Date and To Date range.
Receipt Deposit Table
ID – Displays the receipt deposit ID as a link. Clicking the link opens the Edit Transaction modal.

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management | Receipt Deposit
chunks.content:
Display Date – Auto-populated with the receipt deposit date in the Display Date field.
Check – The Check Number field will be blank for receipt deposit transactions.
Filtered Amount – Displays the filtered amount in the Filtered Amount field.
Total Amount – Auto-populated with the receipt deposit amount in the Total Amount field.
Transaction Type – When the transaction type is Receipt Deposit, the system auto-populates Receipt Deposit in the Transaction field.
Employer Name – The Employer field displays the number of transactions included in the receipt deposit.
Participant Name – The Participant field displays the number of participants included in the receipt deposit.
Payee – When the transaction type is Receipt Deposit, the Payee field will be blank.
Edit Transaction
The Edit Transaction modal displays the same fields as the Add A Transaction modal described above: TPA, Bank Account, Type, Employer, Deposited, Items Selected, Running Total, and the Receipts table.
By selecting the Include Undeposited Receipts checkbox, undeposited receipts will appear in the Receipts table.
Clicking the arrow icon on the left side expands additional details, including Amount, Employer Name, Participant Name, Coverage, Period, Reference Number, and Type:
Amount – Displays the receipt amount.
Employer Name – Displays the employer name.
Participant Name – Displays the participant name.
Coverage – Displays the coverage.
Period – Displays the period.
Reference Number – Displays the reference number.
Type – Displays the transaction type.
Download Deposit Slip
The user can download the Receipt Deposit Slip by clicking the print icon at the right end of the table. A Receipt Deposit Slip is a form that is used to itemize the checks and cash is deposited into a bank account. The form contains the name on the account, account number, amount of each check being deposited, and the amount of any bills and coins being deposited.

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management | Receipt Deposit
chunks.content:
To delete a receipt, the user must click the delete icon and then click the Remove button in the Confirm Removal modal.
