chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management
chunks.content:
Processing | Cash Management
Cash Management is used to track balances and funds moving in and out of associated bank accounts in Summit. This module tracks deposits and debits from real bank accounts.
In the Cash Management module, the TPA can:
View balances of TPA bank accounts and any employer accounts
Add notional deposits to and withdrawals from these bank accounts
View individual transactions that have affected an account
Receive alerts when balances drop below a specified account threshold
Table of Contents
Cash Management
Add Transaction
Bank Account Deposit
Bank Account Withdrawal
Bank Account Adjustment
Receipt Deposit
Transactions Table
* Required fields appear in Red
To access Cash Management,
Go to Processing.
Select Cash Management from the dropdown list.
Cash Management
Cash Management transactions can be searched using the following criteria:
Account Owner – A radio button with TPA and Employer options.
When Employer is selected, the user can choose a single employer associated with the selected bank account. TPA is the default selection.
When TPA is selected, all employers associated with the TPA and the selected bank account are included in the search by default. Employers can also be selected individually from the Employer multiselector dropdown.
A dropdown list that includes all bank accounts associated with the TPA or selected employer. By default, an associated bank account will be pre-selected.
Employer –
If TPA is selected as Account Owner, the system auto-selects all employers associated with the TPA and the selected bank account.
If Employer is selected as Account Owner, this field appears as a dropdown list where the user can select a single employer.
Date Range – The Date Range Selectors allow the user to specify a date range for transactions to include in the query results.
Transaction Type – The Transaction Type dropdown allows filtering by specific transaction types. Select All is the default selection, but the user can choose any combination of transaction types.

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management
chunks.content:
See the Transactions Table section of this page for details on how results are displayed.
Add Transaction
By clicking the +Add Transaction link, the user can enter a new Bank Account Deposit, Bank Account Withdrawal, Bank Account Adjustment, or Receipt Deposit transaction.
Bank Account Deposit
If this option is selected, the user can add funds to a bank account by making a notional “deposit.” This will credit the bank account balance with a Bank Account Deposit transaction.
When the user clicks Bank Account Deposit, the Add A Transaction modal will display. Fields included in this modal are:
Bank Account – Display-only field showing the selected bank account name.
Transaction Type – The default value is based on the selected transaction menu. Users can select another transaction type if needed. This is a mandatory field.
Employer –
If TPA is selected as Account Owner, an Employer dropdown list will appear for selection.
If Employer is the Account Owner, the Employer dropdown will have the employer pre-selected and grayed out.
Event Date – A standard calendar field that defaults to the current date. Users can enter a different date or select one from the calendar. This represents the date the deposit was or will be made. This is a required field.
Check Number – Optional numeric field, blank by default. Users can enter the check number associated with the transaction.
Notes – Optional alphanumeric field for notes. Special characters are allowed. Blank by default.
Current Balance – Display-only field showing the current bank account balance.
Amount – Mandatory dollar value field. The entered amount must be greater than $0.00.
New Balance – When a value is entered in Amount, the system calculates and displays the new balance in this field.
After entering all required fields, click Submit to add the transaction.
Bank Account Withdrawal

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management
chunks.content:
The user can remove funds from a bank account by making a notional “withdrawal.” This will debit the bank account balance with a Bank Account Withdrawal transaction.
It is possible for a user to make a withdrawal that results in a negative account balance.
When entering a Bank Account Withdrawal, the user will have the same fields and business rules as a Bank Account Deposit, except for the Check Number field. Here, Check Number is not applicable and remains grayed out.
Bank Account Adjustment
An adjustment transaction is either a debit or credit that the TPA may use to adjust the balance of the associated bank account without corresponding to an actual deposit or withdrawal.
When entering an Adjustment, the user will have the same fields and business rules as a Bank Account Deposit, except for the Check Number and Amount fields:
Check Number – This field remains grayed out.
Amount – Follows the same formatting logic as described above. The difference is that the user can enter a negative amount by placing a “-” (negative sign) in front of the dollar value.
If the amount entered is negative, it will deduct from the account balance.
If the amount entered does not have a negative sign, it will increase the account balance.
Receipt Deposit
A deposit slip is a form used to itemize checks and cash deposited into a bank account. To learn more about this option, refer to Cash Management | Receipt Deposit.
Date Range – Enter or select a Start Date and End Date to filter the search results.
Transaction Type – A multi-selector dropdown list to filter transactions by type. Users can choose any combination of transaction types to display in the Transaction Table. An option to select all available transaction types by checking the Select All box is also provided.
The options available in the list are:
Bank Account Adjustment
Bank Account Deposit
Bank Account Withdrawal
Debit Card Settlement
Fee Transfer
NSF
Receipt Deposit
Receipt Refund
Reimbursement ACH
Reimbursement Check
Reimbursement Voided Check

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management
chunks.content:
Remittance ACH
Remittance Check
Voided Fee Transfer
Voided Receipt Refund
Voided Remittance
An option to select all the available transaction types by checking the Select all box is also present here.
Now click the Search button to display the results.
Account Balance – Display-only field showing the total balance of the selected bank account in dollars.
Filtered Balance – Displays the available bank balance in dollars within the selected date range (display-only).
Transactions Table
The filtered search results display in the Transactions table below the filter settings.
ID – Displays the transaction ID. For Bank Account Deposit and Receipt Deposit transaction types, the ID is a link that opens the Edit Transaction modal, where users can edit transaction details. The Edit Transaction modal is similar to the Add A Transaction modal. For more information, refer to Bank Account Deposit and Cash Management | Receipt Deposit.
Display Date – Auto-populated transaction date.
Check – Displays the check number for applicable transaction types.
Filtered Amount – Shows the filtered amount.
Total Amount – Displays the total transaction amount.
Transaction Type – Auto-populated transaction type.
Employer Name – Displays the employer name if only one employer is included in the transaction; otherwise, shows the number of transactions included in the entry.
Participant Name – Displays the participant name for applicable transaction types if only one participant is included; otherwise, shows the number of transactions included in the entry.
Payee – Displays the payee name for applicable transaction types.
Void – Available for some transaction types. Clicking this link opens a confirmation pop-up where the user can select Void and Recreate or Void and Reschedule.
Download and Delete – Available only for Receipt Deposit transactions.
To download the deposit slip, click the Print icon at the right end of the table.
To delete a receipt, click the Delete icon.

chunks.title: Processing | Cash Management
chunks.content:
Clicking the Delete icon will display a confirmation pop-up. Select Remove to confirm the removal.
In the Transactions Table, the user can see an arrow icon at the left end of each transaction. This is a dropdown arrow that displays details for each transaction included in the selected entry.
It includes the following fields:
Amount – Displays the transaction amount.
Employer Name – Auto-populated employer name (read-only).
Participant Name – Displays the participant name (read-only).
Coverage – Shows the coverage associated with the transaction.
Period – Displays the applicable period.
Reference Number – If included in the transaction, auto-populated in the display-only Reference Number field.
Type – Displays the transaction type.
Refresh – Clicking Refresh updates the search results on the screen if any filter has been added or modified.
Excel – Clicking Excel exports the Transactions Table to an Excel worksheet.
Print – Clicking Print opens the default print dialog box and allows the user to print the search results.
Print Visible – Similar to Print, but prints the search results exactly as displayed on the Cash Management screen.

chunks.title: Processing | Data Exchange
chunks.content:
Processing | Data Exchange
The purpose of Data Exchange is to facilitate the secure exchange of data between Summit and third-party systems via the Integration Manager. It supports integration with payroll systems, online enrollment platforms, custodial systems, and more—using SFTP and/or manual file uploads and downloads through the Integration Manager user interface.
TPAs and Partners can use flexible mapping tools to configure their data without needing to code to DataPath’s specifications.
Data Exchange is used for a wide range of purposes, from creating groups via import, to managing carrier claim feeds, to creating scheduled exports and reporting, report management, and more!
Due to the kinds of processes managed with Data Exchange, it is recommended that access is role-restricted to power users only.
Table of Contents
Entity Information
FTP Details
Imports/Responses
Exports
Process On Demand
File History
Schedules
Report Management
To access the Data Exchange:
Go to the Processing dropdown from the menu bar.
Click Data Exchange.
The Data Exchange page will display.
Entity Information
The Entity Information section displays read-only details for your TPA. This information is configured by DataPath Implementation during the setup of your TPA as an entity in Summit.
Entity Type – For TPAs, this will be set to Clients.
TPA Name – Populates automatically based on your entity setup in Summit.
Data Exchange Status – Indicates whether the entity has been granted Feature Access for Data Exchange. If your TPA has been set up and granted access, this field will display Active.
Email Notifications – TPA users may enter email addresses in the Email Notifications field in order to receive file processing alerts. Email addresses must be separated by a comma(,) with no space between the comma and the email addresses.

chunks.title: Processing | Data Exchange
chunks.content:
Header Password Required – In addition to the security inherent in SFTP and the option to encrypt the files themselves, TPAs can require a password to be included in any file sent or uploaded to the system.   When the Header Password Required field is checked, two fields will display; Password and Re-enter Password. If this option is checked, then the password must be included in the header record of files before Data Exchange will import the file.  This is a validation TPAs can add to ensure whichever person or system is sending a file to the system is in fact authorized to do so.  TPAs can turn this setting on or off at any time and can edit their password as often as they choose.
Restrict IP Addresses – If the Restrict IP Addresses checkbox is checked, then an IP Addresses field displays. The system will reject files from an IP address not entered in the IP Addresses field.
The Entity Information section can be displayed or collapsed using the Show/Hide link.
FTP Details
This tab allows users to configure the Secure FTP settings Summit will use to exchange data between clients and partners and the Summit platform. DataPath’s implementation team will work with TPAs to configure these settings.
Imports/Responses
This tab allows users to schedule the import of files and map those import files via templates to the applicable Summit File Type.
Exports
This tab allows users to create and configure exports of Summit data and other reports.
Process On Demand
This tab allows users to upload import files for processing on demand.
File History
This tab allows users to search for and view files that have been processed or are currently being processed, via Data Exchange.
Schedules
While Data Exchange allows for On Demand processing, Data Processing in Summit is primarily handled by scheduled processes. This tab allows users to set up schedules that Data Exchange processes, such as imports, exports, and report creation, may be associated with.
Report Management

chunks.title: Processing | Data Exchange
chunks.content:
This tab allows users to create and modify custom report templates that deviate from the DataPath Defaults. Additionally, users can run reports on demand from this tab, allowing them to test changes made to the report templates.

chunks.title: Processing | File Fulfillment
chunks.content:
Processing | File Fulfillment
Summit can produce files that are made available to TPAs on the File Fulfillment page. These files can be manually downloaded and sent to the TPA’s bank (e.g., Check/ACH files) for processing and participant reimbursement.
The objective of DataPath File Fulfillment is to provide TPAs with a way to utilize DataPath’s banking partner for the automated processing of files—eliminating the need for manual intervention.
Note: Any file fulfilled by DataPath will only be viewable via the DataPath Fulfillment view and will not appear in the Manual Fulfillment view.
Table of Contents
File Fulfillment
DataPath Fulfillment Files
Fulfillment Alert
Manual Fulfillment Files
Premium Billing File Fulfillment Editing
To access File Fulfillment,
Go to Processing.
Select the File Fulfillment menu from the dropdown list.
File Fulfillment
The File Fulfillment page will display.
The File Fulfillment page includes the following fields:
Fulfillment Type – Select a Fulfillment Type from the dropdown list. Available options:
DataPath Fulfillment
Manual Fulfillment
DataPath Fulfillment Files
Document Type – This is a multi-select dropdown list for choosing the type of documents to display.
The options available are:
ACH
CDH Check Fulfillment
CDH Communication
PB Check Fulfillment
Premium Billing Notification
You may also check the Select all box to include all document types.
Batch Status – This is a multi-select dropdown list used to filter documents by their current batch status. This option is available only when DataPath Fulfillment is selected.
The available options are:
Error – Indicates files that encountered an error during the fulfillment process. An alert icon will appear in the Batch Status column for these files.
Fulfilled – Indicates files that have been mailed and have received postmark dates.
Imaging Document Download Failed – Indicates files for which an image download failure has occurred.
Paused – Indicates files that have been paused in the fulfillment process.

chunks.title: Processing | File Fulfillment
chunks.content:
Queued – Indicates files that have been created but not yet transferred to the DataPath fulfillment vendor.
Sending – Indicates files that are in the process of being sent to the DataPath fulfillment vendor.
Sent – Indicates files that have been sent to the vendor but have not yet been mailed.
You may also check the Select all box to include all batch status options.
If the Fulfillment Type selected is DataPath Fulfillment, the user will be presented with a table of files that have been fulfilled by DataPath.
The table includes the following columns:
Status Date – The date on which the status of the file or file batch was changed to the current status.
Document Type –  Reflects the document type of the file or file batch. For an ACH file, the file name will be displayed here.
Batch Size – Represents the size of the file batch. [Note: There will be no batch size for ACH files.]
The value in this field is a clickable link that opens a pop-up displaying details of the files included in the selected batch.

The pop-up will display details of files included in the selected batch:
Payee Name
Employer
Original Document [Downloadable link]
Fulfilled Document [Downloadable link]
There are available options to refresh, export, and print this batch of files.
Batch Status –  Displays the current status of the file or file batch.
Actions – Here, there will be two options.
Queue Download / Download Queued / Download –
Clicking the Queue Download icon queues the file for download.
Once queued, a Download Queued icon appears.
When the file is ready, a Download icon replaces it.
Users can download files as often as needed [Note: The system does not track the user ID for downloads or re-downloads from this view.]
Hide/Show/Pause/Start – Icons are displayed based on the file or batch status. The user can hide, show, pause, or start a file or batch by clicking the respective icon. A notification message will confirm the action taken.

chunks.title: Processing | File Fulfillment
chunks.content:
Show Hidden – This is a checkbox that is unchecked by default. When selected, all hidden files/file batches are displayed in the table.
Manage Queued Documents – Opens a pop-up showing details of queued documents, including: Document Name, Name, Employer, Entity, Fulfillment, Created, and Actions. Also, there are available options to refresh, export, and print this list of files.
Refresh – The “Refresh” link will refresh the list of files on the screen if any filter is added or modified.
Excel – The “Excel” link will export the files list into an Excel worksheet.
Print – The “Print” link will open the default print dialogue box and allow the user to print the files list.
Fulfillment Alert
In DataPath Fulfillment, when a user clicks the Queue Download icon, the download will be queued. Once the download is ready, an alert will appear in the Alerts section on the Home page.
A user who logs into the summit will also see this alert in the Alert pop-up.
Manual Fulfillment Files
Document Type – This is a multi-selector dropdown list for choosing the types of documents to be displayed on the Manual File Fulfillment page.
The available options include:
ACH
Approval Letter
Check
Debit Card Transaction Edit
Denial Letter
MSP Reporting
Online Enrollment
Participant Communication
Premium Billing Notification
Premium Billing Remittance Checks
Provider Claim: $0.00 Payment
Provider Claim: Payment Calculated
Receipt Management
Request Letter
You may also check the Select all box to include all available document types.
Filter by – Filters results based on the selected date type. Options include Created Date and Downloaded Date.
Date Range – When a date type is selected, a date range selector appears. Users can enter a date range to filter results.
Only New Files – When this checkbox is selected, only files that have not yet been downloaded will be displayed.
The results table can be sorted by clicking any column heading (e.g., clicking File Name will sort results alphabetically by file name).

chunks.title: Processing | File Fulfillment
chunks.content:
The table includes the following columns:
Date – Displays the date the file was created. Sorted by default with the most recent date first.
File Name – Displays the file name using the standard naming convention.
File Type –  Indicates the type of file.
Download Date – Shows the date the file was downloaded. This is populated only if the user selects Open or Save after clicking Download. If Cancel is selected, this field remains blank.
Downloaded by – Displays the user ID of the person who downloaded the file.
Re-download Date – If the file is downloaded again, this field reflects the most recent re-download date. It remains blank if the user cancels the download.
Re-downloaded by – Shows the user ID of the person who last re-downloaded the file.
Sent Date – Indicates the date the file was sent.
Once a date is entered or selected from the calendar, it cannot be changed. A confirmation pop-up will appear to confirm the selected date.
Date Re-Sent – If the file was re-sent, this field shows the re-send date.
Like the Sent Date, this cannot be changed once saved. A confirmation pop-up will appear to confirm the selected date.
Download – Each row includes a Download link. Clicking it opens a pop-up with options:
Open – Opens the file for viewing or saving.
Save – Saves the file to the local network.
Cancel – Closes the pop-up without downloading.
Files can be downloaded multiple times. If a file has already been downloaded, clicking Download again will prompt a confirmation pop-up. Selecting Cancel will close the pop-up without updating the download history.
Premium Billing File Fulfillment Editing
Summit users are able to view, pause, edit, or delete Premium Billing Communications that are queued for processing prior to fulfillment. For information about editing Premium Billing communications, see this page.
Watch this short video for a step-by-step guide to the above instructions

chunks.title: Processing | On Demand Notices
chunks.content:
Processing | On Demand Notices
The On Demand Notices page allows users to generate various participant communications on demand, including:
Coupon Books
Initial Notices
Open Enrollment Notices
Rate Change Notices
Custom Notices
 Access Requirement: TPA users must have a role with Premium Billing access and the On Demand Notices feature enabled.
  * Required fields appear in Red
To access On Demand Notices,
Go to Processing.
Select On Demand Notices from the menu.
The On Demand Notices page will appear as shown below.
TPA – This dropdown selector is available only to TPA users with with access to multiple TPA entities. The TPA selected will determine the set of Employers available in the Employer dropdown. This is a mandatory field.
Employer – This dropdown selector lists all employers under the selected TPA that are enabled for Premium Billing. No employers will be selected by default. This is a mandatory field.
Events –Select one of the following event types from the dropdown (custom events are also supported):
ARPA Extended Election Notice
ARPA Subsidy Election Notice
ARPA Subsidy Expiration Notice
Covid-19 Extension
Open Enrollment Notice
Rate Change Notice
Send Coupon Book
Send Initial Notification
Send Initial Notification – Detailed Benefits
When Send Coupon Book is selected, an additional dropdown appears with the following options:
Send Coupon Book – Consolidated
Send Coupon Book – COBRA
Send Coupon Book – Direct Bill
Send Coupon Book – Retiree
If a Send Coupon Book – (Sub-LOS) event is selected for an employer not enabled for Sub-LOS coupon books, a warning will appear:
“The employer’s (Sub-LOS) Send by Line of Service option is not selected for the employer. No separate (Sub-LOS) coupons can be created on demand.”
After the user has selected an event, the appropriate filters for that event will display.

chunks.title: Processing | On Demand Notices
chunks.content:
As of Date and Through This Date – As of Date and Through This Date will be displayed, when ARPA Extended Election Notice, ARPA Subsidy Election Notice, ARPA Subsidy Expiration Notice, and Covid-19 Extension is the selected event. The user can either enter a date or select it from the associated calendar. The Covid-19 Extension notice will be sent to selected participants that were qualified beneficiaries during the user-specified date range.
Plan Year Start Date and Plan Year End Date – These fields will display when Open Enrollment Notice or Rate Change Notice is selected from the Events dropdown. The user can either key in a date or use the given calendar date selector. The Plan Year Start Date and End Date Rate Change Notice events and/or Open Enrollment Notice events will be triggered for the selected participants.
NOTE: No date options will be displayed when Send Coupon Book, Send Initial Notification, and Send Initial Notification – Detailed Benefits are selected. The Send Coupon Book event is triggered for the selected participants with COBRA/Direct Bill/Retiree status coverages with current billing.
Include only participants with AEI coverages – TFilters results to AEI-covered participants only.
Exclude terminated participants – Available for custom events to exclude participants with only terminated coverages.
Select Participants – The Select Participants option includes three radio buttons:
All (default) – Sends the notice to all participants of the selected employer.
Just These –  Displays a participant search box. Only selected participants will receive the notice.
Not These – Displays a participant search box. Selected participants will be excluded from the notice.
Once all selections are made, click the Generate Notices button to create and send the selected communications.
Watch this short video for a step-by-step guide to the above instructions
3:09

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Processing | Process Approvals
The Process Approvals section allows the user to view, approve, or reject various processes that require manual approval. These include ACH Returns, Contributions, Document Fulfillment, Election Changes, Events, Missing Information, Partner Messages, Premium Auto-Drafts, Online Enrollments, Reimbursements, Remittances, and Unapplied Receipts.
Table of Contents
Process Approvals
ACH Returns
Contributions
Document Fulfillment
Election Changes
Events
Missing Information
Premium Auto-Drafts
Online Enrollments
Reimbursements
Remittances
Unapplied Receipts
* Required fields appear in Red
To access Process Approvals,
Go to Processing.
Click Process Approvals from the dropdown menu.
Process Approvals
The Process Approvals screen displays all processes that require manual approval by the TPA. Users can select the type of process to review using the Process Type dropdown list.
Process Type – The Process Type dropdown is auto-populated with all process types available to the TPA.
The available options include:
ACH Returns
Contributions
Document Fulfillment

ACH Returns
When the user selects ACH Returns from the Process Type dropdown list, the page will display the following options:
Start Date/End Date – Allows the user to define a date range to filter ACH Return records.
A set of radio buttons enables the user to filter the results in the ACH Returns grid:
Show Only Unresolved (default) – Displays only unresolved ACH Returns. Checkboxes remain enabled for selection.
Show Only Resolved – Displays only resolved ACH Returns. Checkboxes are disabled to prevent selection.
Show All – Displays both resolved and unresolved ACH Returns. Checkboxes are disabled for resolved entries.
Click Refresh to apply the selected filters and update the ACH Returns table accordingly

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
ACH Returns Table – The ACH Returns Table displays ACH transactions that have been returned by the bank. These returns are specific to ACH transactions initiated by DataPath on behalf of the TPA.
ID – The ID of the original transaction.
Company Name –Displays the name of the company.
Employer Name – The employer associated with the ACH return.
Date Of Return – The date the ACH transaction was returned.
Transaction Type – Indicates the type of original transaction, such as:
Billing
Reimbursement
Pull of Funds for Premium
Debit Card Settlement
Amount – The amount of the returned transaction.
Account Owner – Name of the account owner (can be an employer, participant, or TPA).
Account Number  – The bank account number, masked except for the last four digits.
Bank Account Name – The name of the bank account.
Routing Number – The routing number associated with the bank account.
Return Reason –The reason the transaction was returned.
Return Code – The code corresponding to the return reason.
Resolved – Displays a checkmark if the ACH return has been resolved.
Resolved Date –The date the ACH return was marked as resolved.
NOTE: Premium Billing Chargebacks will be included in the ACH Returns list. These Credit/Debit Card chargebacks from Speedpay will be treated the same as ACH Returns. For information about handling chargebacks for Premium Billing payments, see our PB ACH Returns and Credit/Debit Card Chargeback Best Practices guide.
Once the return issue has been addressed, users can:
Select the record by enabling its checkbox.
Click Resolve to mark the return as resolved.
This table serves as a notification only. It does not trigger or replace any actions the TPA must take to re-issue payments.
Contributions
When the user selects Contributions from the Process Type dropdown list, the page will display the relevant contribution records.
Start Date/End Date – These fields allow the user to define a date range to filter the displayed records
The user can select a record by enabling its checkbox.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Click the Refresh button to apply the selected date range and update the table accordingly.
Contributions Table – The Contributions Table displays contribution records that require manual approval.
Process Date – The date on which the contribution process was run for the associated schedule.
Schedule/File Name – Displays the name of the contribution schedule.
Participant Funding – Shows the participant funding amount.
Employer Funding –Displays the employer funding amount.
Recurrence – Indicates the frequency of the contribution schedule.
Total Amount  – Displays the total contribution amount.. 
Clicking on the link icon at the right-hand side of each record will open a modal. This modal contains two sections:
Selected Contribution Schedule Run
Available Contribution Import Files
Clicking the arrow icon on the left-hand side of a record reveals additional employer-level details:
Employer
Participant Funding
Employer Funding
Employer Total
Clicking the arrow icon next to an employer reveals participant-level details:
Participant
Plan Name
Contribution Date
Participant Contribution
Employer Contribution
Participant Total
Clicking the participant’s name will open a contribution details pop-up as shown below:
Each record in the contribution table includes a checkbox. The user can select one or more records to take action.
After selecting records:
Click Approve to release the pended contributions and apply them to participant plans.
Click Decline to reject the selected contributions.
Document Fulfillment
When the user selects Document Fulfillment from the Process Type dropdown list, the page will display the relevant document fulfillment records.
From/To – These date fields allow the user to define a date range to filter the records.
Employer –  This mandatory multi-select dropdown auto-populates with all employers associated with the TPA. A Select All checkbox is available to quickly include all employers.
Fulfillment Status –  A multi-select dropdown containing the following options:
Select All
Mailed

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Not Mailed
Not Sent to Fulfillment
Events –  A multi-select dropdown listing all available events, with an option to Select All.
Document Fulfillment Table – The Document Fulfillment Table displays records related to document fulfillment processes. The table includes the following columns:
Process Date – Displays the date the fulfillment process was executed.
Event – Shows the name of the event as a clickable link. Clicking the link opens a pop-up displaying:
Event Name
Participant Name
Address Type
Letter
Email
Actions
Within the pop-up, clicking View allows the user to preview the document.
Employer Name – TDisplays the name of the employer associated with the fulfillment.
Participant Name – Displays the participant’s name as a clickable link. Clicking the link redirects the user to the participant’s Demographics page.
File Name – T Displays the file name as a clickable link. Clicking the link opens the file for viewing and downloading.
Sent Date – Displays the date the document was sent.
Status – Indicates the current status of the event.
Completed Date – Displays the date the fulfillment process was completed.
Election Changes
When the user selects Election Changes from the Process Type dropdown list, the Election Changes page will be displayed.
Start Date/End Date – These fields allow the user to define a date range to filter election change records.
Election Changes Table – The table includes the following columns. Users can select records by enabling the checkboxes next to them.
Change Date –The date the election change occurred. The table is sorted by this field.
Plan – Displays the name of the plan.
Eff Date – The effective date of the plan.
Participant – The name of the participant.
Current AE – The current annual election amount.
Current Per Period – The current per-period contribution amount.
New AE – The new annual election amount.
New Per Period – The new per-period contribution amount.
Reason – The reason for the election change.
Employer – Displays the employer name.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
After selecting one or more records, the user can:
Click Approve to approve all selected records.
Click Reject to reject all selected records.
Note: A record cannot be both approved and rejected at the same time.
Rejected Reason – A dropdown list where the user can select a reason for rejecting the records.
Add Reasons – Allows the user to add a new rejection reason. Clicking the link opens an Add Reason pop-up where the user can enter a new code and reason.
Do not send rejected letter to participant – When this checkbox is selected, the system will not send a rejection letter to the participant.
Events
When the user selects Events from the Process Type dropdown list, the page will display all premium billing events that require review.
Approval Type –A multi-select dropdown where the user must choose one or more approval types. Available options include:
Auto-Approved
Awaiting Approval
Manually Approved
Declined
A Select All checkbox is available to include all approval types.
From/To –Date fields used to define a date range for filtering event records.
User Type – A multi-select dropdown where the user selects one or more user types. Available options include:
Datapath
System
TPA
Broker
Employer
Participant
A Select All checkbox is also available.
Employer – A mandatory multi-select dropdown that auto-populates with all employers associated with the TPA. At least one employer must be selected. A Select All checkbox is available.
Events – A multi-select dropdown listing all available events. A Select All checkbox is available to include all events.
After entering all required fields, click the Search button to generate the Events Table based on the selected filters.
Events Table – The Events Table displays premium billing events based on the filters applied in the Events section. The table includes the following columns:
Process Date – The date on which the event occurred.
Event – The name of the event.
Employer Name – Displays the name of the employer associated with the event.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Participant Name – Displays the name of the participant involved in the event.
Status – Shows the current approval status of the event (e.g., Auto-Approved, Awaiting Approval, Manually Approved, Declined).
Completed Date – The date the event was completed.
Reviewed By – Displays the ID of the user who approved or declined the event. If the event was automatically processed, this field will show System.
Error Message – Displays any error that occurred during the event process. For example, if an issue occurs while sending the event to DataPath Fulfillment, the error message will indicate the issue and provide the user with an opportunity to retry sending the event.
By clicking the arrow icon on the left side of a record in the Events Table, the following additional fields will be displayed:
Coverage – Displays the participant’s coverage plan associated with the event.
Elected Tier – For Individually Rated Plans, this field shows the tier/level description entered in the Premium Billing Coverage Details UI. This is a freeform text field.
Covered Dependents – Lists the names of dependents covered under the participant’s plan.
Users can select one or more records by checking the corresponding checkboxes.
To view an event, click on its event name.
Now a pop-up will generate as shown below displaying:
Event Name
Participant Name
Address Type
Letter
Email
Actions
Within the pop-up, clicking Preview allows the user to view the associated document.
Click the Participant Name to navigate to the Participant’s Demographics page.
After selecting records, users can:
Click Approve to approve the selected events.
Click Decline to decline the selected events.
A record cannot be both approved and declined at the same time.
Custom events appear in Process Approvals and can be manually approved or declined just like system-default events.
If a custom event is awaiting approval and a new instance of the same event is triggered via the Run On Demand process, the new event will replace the previous one.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Missing Information
Summit alerts users when claims are missing required information that prevents them from being included in Provider Pay payment files.
These items will be listed under Missing Information, along with the number of claims that must be addressed.
An alert notification button will indicate when there are items in Pending Approvals & Actions that require attention.
Clicking the Missing Information link will take the user to the Process Approvals screen.
The page includes:
Start Date/End Date – These fields allow the user to define a date range to filter the records (same functionality as described in previous sections).
Missing Information Table – The table includes the following columns:
ID – The unique identifier of the record.
Date – The date on which the missing information was identified.
Employer – Displays the employer’s name as a clickable link. Clicking it redirects the user to the Employer | Reimbursement Settings page.
Transaction Type – Will display Missing Information as the transaction type.
Description – Provides a description of what specific information is missing from the claim.
Premium Auto-Drafts
When the user selects Premium Auto-Drafts from the Process Type dropdown, the page displays filters and a table of auto-draft records.
From/To – Date fields to filter records by date range.
Employer – A mandatory multi-select dropdown that auto-populates with all employers. A Select All option is available.
ACH File Delivery – A multi-select dropdown with the following options:
DataPath Fulfillment
Manually Download
After applying filters, click Search to generate the Premium Auto-Drafts Table.
Approve All – Clicking Approve All will approve all listed PB Auto Drafts and remove them from the Process Approvals UI once processing is complete.
Premium Auto-Drafts Table – Users can select records using checkboxes and click Approve or Decline. The table includes:
Participant – Name of the participant.
Employer – Name of the employer.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Auto-Draft Amount – The amount scheduled for auto-draft.
ACH File Delivery – Type of ACH file delivery.
Scheduled Date – The scheduled date for the next premium auto-draft.
Online Enrollments
Online Enrollment allows participants to self-enroll in available benefit offerings during the Open Enrollment period via the Participant Portal.
When the user selects Online Enrollments from the Process Type dropdown list, the page will display filters and enrollment data.
Line of Service – A multi-select dropdown with the following options.
Select all
CDH
PB
The Online Enrollment grid will populate based on the selection.
Employer – A dropdown that auto-populates with all employers in the TPA. The user can select one employer to include in the table.
SSN – Field to enter the participant’s Social Security Number.
 Open Enrollment Period – A dropdown with the following options:
Closed (default)
Open
All
Non-Enrolled Imports
Participant – A dropdown with All as the default selection.
Plan Type – Displays only plan types associated with pending online enrollments. Defaults to All. If no pending enrollments exist, it still defaults to All.
Plan Description – Displays only plan descriptions associated with pending online enrollments. Defaults to All.
After making the desired selections, click the Refresh button to update the enrollment grid.
CDH Online Enrollments Table – The CDH Online Enrollments Table displays participant-submitted enrollment records for CDH plans. Users can select records by checking the corresponding checkboxes.
Enrollment End – Displays the end date of the Open Enrollment period.
Plan Type – Shows the type of the plan.
Plan Description – Displays the description associated with the plan.
Effective – The effective date of the plan.
Participant Name – Displays the participant’s name as a clickable link. Clicking it redirects the user to the participant’s Demographics page.
SSN – Shows the last four digits of the participant’s Social Security Number.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Annual Election – Displays the annual election amount.
Per Period – Shows the per-period contribution amount.
Tier – Displays the tier name selected during online enrollment.
Employer – Displays the employer’s name.
Clicking the arrow icon on the left side of a record reveals dependent information, including:
Relationship
Dependent Name
SSN
Date of Birth
If a possible duplicate is detected, a warning icon will appear next to the record.
After selecting one or more records, users can:
Click Approve to approve the selected enrollments.
Click Decline to reject the selected enrollments.
A record cannot be both approved and declined at the same time.
Rejected Reason – Dropdown list to select a reason for rejection (same as described in previous sections).
Add Reasons – Allows users to add a new rejection reason via a pop-up.
Do not send rejected letter to participant – When selected, the system will not send a rejection letter to the participant..
PB Online Enrollments Table – PB Online Enrollments table contains the same columns as the CDH Online Enrollments table, except the “Annual Election” column. The user can choose records from the table by checking their checkboxes.
Reimbursements
When the user selects Reimbursements from the Process Type dropdown list, the page will display filters and a table of reimbursement records.
Start Date /End Date – Start Date / End Date – Date fields used to define a range for filtering reimbursement records (same functionality as described in previous sections).
Reimbursements Table – The table includes the following columns. Users can select records by checking the corresponding checkboxes:
Process Date – The date the reimbursement process was run for the associated schedule that now requires approval.
Schedule Name – The name of the reimbursement schedule.
Recurrence – The frequency associated with the schedule (e.g., weekly, monthly).
Check Total – Total reimbursement amount issued via check.
ACH Total – Total reimbursement amount issued via ACH.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Provider Pay Total – Total reimbursement amount issued via Provider Pay.
Total Amount – The combined total of Check Total and ACH Total.
Clicking the arrow icon on the left side of a record reveals employer-level details:
Employer Name
Check Total
ACH Total
Provider Pay Total
Total
Clicking the arrow icon next to an employer reveals participant-level details:
Participant Name
Reimbursement Amount
Reimbursement Method
After selecting one or more records, users can:
Click Decline to reject the selected reimbursements.
Click Validate to verify the selected records.
Click Approve to approve the selected reimbursements.
Remittances
This section allows users to view, approve, or reject premium billing payments before they are remitted.
Run Prepayment Register Report – The Prepayment Register is a report containing premium remittance information, intended for client finance teams. TPA users can run this report on-demand for all remittances awaiting approval.
When the Run Prepayment Register Report link is clicked from the Process Approvals UI, the system generates the default report.
This process functions similarly to how the Certificate of Mail report is generated in the File Fulfillment UI for manual fulfillment of premium billing notifications.
The report is available for download in PDF format by clicking the Run Prepayment Register Report link.
Remittances Table – This table displays remittances that are pending approval. Users can select records by checking the corresponding checkboxes.
Remit To – Indicates the recipient of the participant’s billed amount.
Amount – Displays the remitted amount.
Line of Service – Shows the associated line of service.
Clicking the arrow icon on the left side of a record reveals additional fields:
Participant
Employer
Amount
Coverage
Premium
Fee
Billing Cycle
Receipt Received
Clicking the Preview link on the right side of the grid allows the user to view the submitted document.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
The Dismiss button is used to remove overpayments from remittance processing. This is particularly useful when employer groups have low COBRA activity and overpayments may not be offset for some time.
Only negative receipts will display the Dismiss button.
When clicked, the system removes the selected negative amount from the remittance.
The dismissed receipt will not be included in the next scheduled remittance run.
After selecting one or more records, users can:
Click Approve to approve the selected remittances.
Click Decline to reject the selected remittances.
A record cannot be both approved and declined at the same time.
For more information, see the Processing | Process Approvals | Remittances page.
Unapplied Receipts
An unapplied amount can result from several scenarios, including:
Applying a receipt when the participant has no billing for the associated coverage.
Voiding a previously applied receipt.
Stopping payment on a previously applied receipt.
Marking a previously applied receipt as insufficient.
Summit allows users to reapply the unapplied portion of a receipt.
When the user selects Unapplied Receipts from the Process Type dropdown list, the page will display a table of receipts with unapplied amounts.
Each receipt in the table includes a checkbox. After selecting one or more records, the user can click the Reapply button to reapply the unapplied amount.
If the unapplied amount becomes zero, the receipt will be removed from the table.
If a partial amount is reapplied, the receipt will remain in the table with the updated unapplied balance.
Unapplied Receipts Table – The table includes the following columns:
Participant – Name of the participant associated with the receipt.
Participant Custom ID – Custom ID of the participant associated with the receipt.
Participant System ID – System ID of the participant associated with the receipt.
Employer – Name of the participant’s employer.
Employer Custom ID – Custom ID of the participant’s employer associated with the receipt.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Approvals
chunks.content:
Employer System ID – System ID of the participant’s employer associated with the receipt.
Payor – The payor associated with the receipt.
Reference Number – The reference number of the receipt.
Payment Method – The method used for the payment.
Amount – The receipt amount for each receipt that has an unapplied amount will be populated here.
Unapplied Amount – The remaining unapplied portion of the receipt.
For more information, please refer to the Process Approvals section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment
chunks.content:
Processing | Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment
The Participant Enrollment Renewal section is used to update and renew enrollment elections for participants. It allows users to review multiple participant enrollment elections on a single screen, make necessary changes, and renew those elections for the upcoming plan year.
Users can apply filters such as Employer, Division, Plan Type, Plan Name, and Status to narrow down the list of participants displayed.
Table of Contents
Participant Enrollment Renewal
Add Plan / Edit Plan
To access Participant Enrollment,
Go to Processing.
Select the Process Renewals menu.
Choose Participant Enrollment from the Renewal Types dropdown.
Participant Enrollment Renewal
When Participant Enrollment is selected from the Renewal Types dropdown, additional filtering fields will appear to help narrow down the participant list.
Employer – This dropdown is auto-populated with all the employers under the selected TPA. The user can select an employer to filter participants accordingly.
Division – This dropdown is populated with all divisions associated with the selected employer. Selecting a division will display only participants within that division.
Plan Type – This is a multi-select dropdown that allows the user to choose one or more plan types to include in the search.
The options populated in the list are:
DCA
FSA
HRA
HSA
LFSA
MERP
PRK
TRN
Other
An option to select all the available plan types in the list by clicking the “Select all” box is also present here.
Plan Name – This multi-select dropdown displays the plan names associated with the selected Plan Type(s). The user can select one, multiple, or all plan names from this list..
Enrolled Only – When the Enrolled Only checkbox is enabled, the system will display only participants who are currently enrolled in the selected Employer, Division, Plan Type, or Plan Name. If unchecked, the system will display all active (non-terminated) participants..

chunks.title: Processing | Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment
chunks.content:
Status – This is a multi-selector dropdown list showing different employment statuses. The user can choose all or any combination of status options to be included in the search.
After entering the required fields, click Search to display the Participant Enrollment Renewal table.
The table will include the following fields:
Participant Name – Displays the name of the participant.
Plan Type – Indicates the type of plan. This field includes a link that opens the Add Plan modal when clicked.
Plan Name – Displays the name of the plan.
Annual Election Amount – Shows the annual election amount for the plan. If the plan is tier-funded, this field will display “N/A.”
Contribution Amount – Displays the contribution amount. If the plan is tier-funded, this field will display “N/A.”
Funding Tier –
If the plan is not tier-funded, this field will display “N/A” and the Funding Tier selector will be disabled.
If the participant is currently enrolled in a tiered plan, their existing funding tier will be selected by default.
If the participant is not enrolled in the current plan but the new plan is tiered, the Employer plan tier options will be available for selection.
Election Type – Displays the election type for the plan.
To renew a participant’s enrollment, select the checkbox next to the participant’s name and click the Renew button.
Add Plan / Edit Plan
When the hyperlinked Plan Type is clicked, the Add Plan modal will appear.
The Add Plan modal is divided into two sections:
Enrolled Plans – Displays a list of plans in which the participant is currently enrolled.
Available Plans – Displays a list of plans available for the participant to enroll in.
To modify an existing enrollment, the user can click the Edit link located at the right end of each plan row in the Enrolled Plans section. Clicking this link opens the Edit Plan modal.
Funding Tier – This dropdown is auto-populated with available funding tiers. The user can select a different tier if needed.

chunks.title: Processing | Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment
chunks.content:
Funding Amount – Displays the funding amount. This field is read-only.
Plan Effective Date – To change the effective date, the user can enter a new date manually or select one using the calendar picker.
Audit History – This section displays the following read-only fields:
Created On
Edited On
Created By
Edited By
Election History –This section shows historical election data, including:
Original Funding Amount
Last Funding Amount
Original Funding Amount Updated By
Last Funding Amount Updated By details.
Click Save to update the changes made.
Similarly, users can edit fields in the Available Plans section by enabling the checkbox next to the desired plan and saving the changes.
Clicking the Plan Type link for any plan in either section (Enrolled Plans or Available Plans) will open the View Plan Detail modal.
For more information, refer to the Add Plan section of Participant Central | Plans.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Entry | Contribution Return
chunks.content:
Processing | Transaction Entry | Contribution Return
Contribution Returns provide TPAs the ability to retroactively correct HSA contribution errors. This includes specifying the source of the contribution, the contribution date, the applicable Tax Year, and the amount to be returned.
Table of Contents
Contribution Return
 * Required fields appear in Red
To perform a Contribution Return,
Go to Processing.
Select Transaction Entry from the dropdown menu.
Choose an Employer.
Select a search method from the Search By dropdown.
Search for or select the Participant based on the chosen method.
Plan details of the selected participant will appear as shown below.
From the Transaction Type dropdown, select Contribution Return.
Contribution Return
When Contribution Return is selected from the Transaction Type dropdown, the claim entry screen will display the following fields:
Contribution Search Date Range – This optional field identifies the date range during which the contribution(s) to be returned (in whole or in part) were made. If completed, Summit will display a list of contributions made within the selected range. The list includes the contribution date, source, amount, pre/post-tax status, and the tax year applied. Users can refresh, export, or print this list as needed.
Amount to Return – This required field allows the user to enter the total dollar amount of contributions to be returned. The default value is 0.00.
Contribution Source – This mandatory dropdown list includes various contribution sources.
Employer Contribution
Participant Pre-Tax – Contributions made via payroll deduction.
Participant Post-Tax – Contributions made directly from the participant account.
If the Contribution Source is Employer Contribution or Participant Pre-Tax, Summit will generate and send a request to the custodian platform to return funds to the employer. If the source is Participant Post-Tax, the request will be sent to return funds to the participant.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Entry | Contribution Return
chunks.content:
Tax Year – This required field allows the user to select the tax year to which the contribution was applied. Options include:
Current Tax Year — default
Previous Tax Year
Request Date – This mandatory field defaults to the current date. It represents the date on which the Return of Contribution(s) is requested.
Destination Plan – The user must manually select a Destination Plan to which the contribution return will be applied. This is a mandatory dropdown that lists plans based on the entered Original Contribution Date. The default value will be “Select One”, unless there is only one eligible plan—in that case, the plan will be auto-selected.
Display to participant – This is a checkbox that is selected by default. When checked, the transaction will be visible to the participant on the Participant Portal. If unchecked, the transaction will not be displayed.
Notes – In this text area field, the user can enter notes related to the contribution return.
Display note to participant – Enabling this checkbox will display the entered note to the Participant.
After entering all the mandatory information, click Save.
When the user saves the transaction, Summit will validate that the amount to be returned is equal to or less than the current HSA balance.
If the balance is less than the amount to be returned, then a message will display as a warning to the user that the return amount exceeds the balance. The user will have the option to cancel and return to the transaction page to change the amount or to continue with the transaction. If the user selects to continue, Summit will modify the amount of the request sent to the custodian platform so that it equals the remaining balance. The rest of the amount will be placed On Hold until additional contributions are posted.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Entry | Contribution Return
chunks.content:
In Participant Central and the Participant Portal, these transactions will appear as Contribution Return in the Transaction Type column of the Transactions list. This action will debit the total contribution amount returned and decrease the balance accordingly.
Summit updates balances in real time, but the transaction will initially have a Memo Posted status. This status remains until the transaction is completed by the custodian platform and a confirmation is received. Once confirmed, the Status will update to Completed.
By clicking the linked Participant name in the grid, the user can view the Contribution Return transaction details of the corresponding transaction as shown below.
On the Participant Portal, these transactions will display as Contribution Returns with the following statuses:
Awaiting Confirmation – for transactions in Memo Posted status
Approved – for transactions in Completed status
Users may search for Contribution Returns in Transaction Search by selecting Contribution Return from the Transaction Type filter list.
In CDH Transactions section , the user can view Contribution Returns as given below.
Clicking the Transaction Type link will open a Contribution Return Details pop-up for the corresponding transaction.
For further information, please refer to the Contributions section in FAQs.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Entry | Withdrawal
chunks.content:
Processing | Transaction Entry | Withdrawal
Some plans (typically an HSA) allow participants to request a distribution of funds from their plan without the need to justify the expense or submit receipts. This transaction type is known as Withdrawal. It is similar to a manual claim. When a withdrawal is entered, it reduces the balance of the participant and results in a check or direct deposit (ACH) to the participant. A withdrawal transaction does not need the review of TPA prior to the creation of the check or direct deposit.
Table of Contents
Withdrawal
  * Required fields appear in Red
To access Withdrawal:
Go to Processing.
Select Transaction Entry from the dropdown menu.
Choose an Employer.
Select an option from the Search By dropdown list to indicate the option by which the search should be carried out.
Search or select Participant.
A new page with plan details of the selected participant will appear.
Select the Withdrawal option from the Transaction Type dropdown list.
Withdrawal
When the user selects a Transaction Type > Withdrawal, the following fields will become available:
Withdrawal Amount – The user must enter a withdrawal amount in this mandatory field. The amount entered must be greater than $0.00.
Service Date – This field determines the service date of the withdrawal. It will auto-populate with the current date. A withdrawal will include only one service date. If needed, the user can choose another service date by clicking the calendar icon or simply typing the date.
Destination Plan – The user must manually select a destination plan from which the withdrawal will be pulled. The system will filter the plans available in the dropdown list based on the service date. Only those plans that the service date falls within will show here. The default value will be Select One unless there is only one possible plan. In such a case, that one plan will be auto-selected in the dropdown list. This is a mandatory field.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Entry | Withdrawal
chunks.content:
Distribution Method – The user can determine the distribution method by selecting an option from the given mandatory dropdown list.
The options in the list are:
Check – Default value
ACH
Payee  – This field indicates the payee.
The options available in the dropdown list are:
Participant
Claimant
Provider
The default value will be Participant.
Display claim to participant– This is a checkbox that is selected by default. When this box is checked, the withdrawal will appear to the participant on the Participant Portal. If it is not checked, the withdrawal will not be displayed.
Qualified Withdrawal – This is a checkbox to enable Qualified Withdrawal. It is also set as checked by default.
Notes – In this text area field, the user can enter notes.
Include note on participant communications/portal – Enabling this checkbox will include entered notes on participant communications/portal.
Click Save after entering all mandatory information. On saving a withdrawal transaction, the participant’s available balance and disbursable balance will be reduced by the withdrawal amount. Then a check file or ACH file will generate and a reimbursement to the participant will be created.

Processing | Transaction Entry
The Transaction Entry screen of Summit’s Processing module allows the user to enter a wide variety of transactions pertaining to a participant’s benefit plans or accounts. This screen will be disabled and hidden for Premium Billing-only TPAs. If the user is a CDH+PB TPA user with access to this screen, no transactions may be entered for participants who do not have a CDH plan.
Table of Contents
Transaction Types
The Transaction Entry screen can be accessed from the Processing dropdown.
The Transaction Entry screen contains a participant search feature that allows the user to find and select a participant to enter a transaction for.
TPA – This dropdown is only present if you are a user of a Master TPA with access to data of subordinate TPAs.
Employer – This dropdown contains a list of Employers associated with the selected TPA that the user has access to. Selecting an employer filters the participant results shown in the table. If no employer is selected, the query will include participants from all employers in the results.
Search By – This dropdown allows the user to select the Participant identifier (e.g., name, ID) by which the query will search. Available identifiers include:
ParticipantName
SSN
DataPathID
TpaID
HealthPlanID
PBMID
VisionID
DentalID
Participant – This dropdown search list allows the user to enter a Participant identifier and select from the matching names displayed in the dropdown list.
The results for the Participant search will display in the grid, with each participant name a hyperlink. Clicking the name will open the Transaction Entry form for that individual.
Transaction Types
The fields displayed on the Transaction Entry screen vary depending on the Transaction Type selected.
The following Transaction Types are available in Summit from the Processing | Transaction Entry screen:
Contribution Return
Credit
Manual Claim
Manual Contribution
Plan Repayment
Return of Withdrawal
Withdrawal

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Search
chunks.content:
Processing | Transaction Search
The Transaction Search tab provides users with a centralized view of transactions and a set of search filters to review transaction sets that meet their criteria.
Table of Contents
Transaction Search
Quick Search Options
Detailed Transaction Search
Transaction Search Result
Add Claim
To access Transaction Search,
Go to Processing.
Select Transaction Search menu from the dropdown list.
Transaction Search
The Transaction Search page consists of three sections:
Employer and Participant Search Options (top portion)
Various Search Filters (middle portion)
Search Result Table (bottom portion)
Employer –This is a dropdown list that auto-populates with all employers present under the TPA. Users must select an employer from this list either by searching based on Name or ID (System ID or TPA ID). The default value is All. Leaving the value set to All allows users to initiate a search for transactions across all employers. If users select a specific employer, the system will look for transactions specifically associated with participants under that selected employer only. 
Participant – By default, if the Employer selection is set to All, the Participant search field radio button will be set to ID. Users can enter an ID (System ID or TPA ID) of the participant to search for transactions specifically associated with that participant. If this field is left blank, the system will search for transactions across all participants.
If users select a specific employer from the Employer dropdown list, the Participant search field will default to the dropdown from which users can select a specific participant. The default value is All.
Quick Search Options

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Search
chunks.content:
In this section, users can enter a claim number to search for a specific transaction. If users enter a claim number and click the Search button, the system will search for any transactions within the TPA, for transactions of a participant (and any of their dependents) with a matching claim number. If the system finds a matching claim, it will produce the claim details. When users enter a value in the quick search field, the system will disallow the entry of data in any other search field as they are mutually exclusive. A radio button with options System ID and Custom ID is also present here.
If a specific employer/participant is selected and a claim number is searched, the system will look for a matching claim within that specified employer/participant only.
Detailed Transaction Search
The page also provides users with criteria to search for a particular transaction or a set of transactions. The search criteria include:
Claimant – This is a dropdown list available only when a specific participant is selected. It includes the name of the participant and any dependents of the participant, whether they are currently active and linked to the participant and any participant plans or not. The default selection is All.
If All is selected in the Claimant dropdown and the Transaction Type selection is All or Manual Claim, the search will return manual claim transactions that were entered for all claims matching the available claimants in the search. Users can also initiate a search with a specific dependent selected in the Claimant field and for a specific plan type, such as FSA. If the specified dependent was never linked to the participant’s FSA plan, the system will produce a search result of 0 transactions found.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Search
chunks.content:
Plan Type – This is a dropdown menu that lists all the plan types in the system, including any custom plan types created by the TPA. The default selection is All. If users retain the selection All in the Plan Type dropdown field, the search will return transactions applied to all plan types. If the selection is restricted to a particular plan type, it will return transactions that affected the selected plan type only.
The options available in the list are :
DCA
FSA
HRA
HSA
LFSA
MERP
Other
Transaction Type – This is another dropdown list that allows users to select transaction types. The default selection is All. If users retain the selection All, the search will return transactions of all types that meet other criteria. If a specific transaction type is selected, the system will return and display transactions of that specified type only.
The options given in the list are :
Contribution
Contribution Return
Credit
Debit Card
Debit Card Authorization
Debit Card Decline
Debit Card Return
Manual Claim
Overpayment
Plan Repayment
Withdrawal
Return Of Withdrawal
Fee
Adjustment
Interest
Investment Purchase
Investment Sale
Order
Premium Payments
Return of Contribution From HSA
Posted Plan Adjustment From HSA
Return of HSA Distribution
Reassignment of Purchase Return
DirectPay FSA Store
Status – This dropdown lists all claim review statuses for selection by the user. The default value is “All”.
Following are the options available in this list.
Additional Documentation Required
Approved
Auto Substantiated
Debit Card Return
Denied
Expense Denied
Ineligible
Pending
Pending Substantiation
Plan Satisfied
Posted
Receipt Overdue
Receipt Requested
Request
Return
Review
Card Number – In this field, the user can enter a card number to search for transactions. At least 4 characters of the card number must be entered here. When the card number is entered, the Transaction Type will default to Debit Card and will remain grayed out.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Search
chunks.content:
Decline Reason – By default, this dropdown is grayed out. When selecting the Transaction Type as Debit Card Decline, the Decline Reason dropdown will become available with All selected by default.
Entry Dates – Enabling this checkbox will display additional fields to enter/select From and To dates. By default, both date fields are blank. When users click the Search button, the system will produce all transactions that were entered on or after the start date and on or before the end date. If the end date is blank, the system will produce a list of transactions between the start date and those on or before the current date.
Reimbursement Dates – Selecting this checkbox will display additional fields named From and To to input a reimbursement date range. When users click the Search button, the system will produce all transactions whose Reimbursement Date fell on or after the start date and on or before the end date. If the end date is blank, the system will produce a list of transactions with Reimbursement Dates between the start date and those on or before the current date.
Service Dates – This is another date range users can set by enabling the checkbox. By default, both date fields are blank. When users click the Search button, the system will produce all transactions with a service date on or after the start date and on or before the end date. If the end date is blank, the system will produce a list of transactions between the start date and those on or before the current date.
When referring to debit card transactions, the service date of the transaction is the date the card is swiped (the authorization), which also happens to be the entry date.
Include/Exclude Tags – Users can search claims by selecting tags from Include/Exclude multi-selector dropdown lists.
After applying all the required filters, click Search to display search results.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Search
chunks.content:
Providers – Users may filter results by provider. When this checkbox is checked, only transactions associated with selected providers will be included in the query results. Users may also check the Show only Direct Pay Providers checkbox; when this is enabled, only DirectPay providers will be selected for inclusion in the results.
Transaction Search Result
This is the search result table that appears when users click the Search button.
Split claims will appear as a single record in the list view based on the ClaimDetailID rather than showing a record for each plan the payment was split across. Users may click to view the claim to see how the claim was applied to each plan.
Export To Excel – This link will allow the user to export the search results to an excel spreadsheet.
Export To PDF – By clicking this link, the user can export search results into a PDF.
The Search Results table includes the following information:
Participant Name – The name of the participant.
Claimant – The name of the claimant/cardholder entered during a claim entry will be displayed as a link. The claimant could be either the participant or a dependent. If it is a dependent, users can see a user icon along with the claimant’s name.
By clicking the Claimant name, a transaction detail modal specific to the transaction type will display. For more information, refer to the Claimant Link section of Participant Central Transactions.
Entry Date – This field reflects the date on which the claim was entered into the system. For card claims, it reflects the date on which the card swipe was done.
Dates of Service – These are the service start and service end dates of a claim. For card claims, it will be the date on which the card swipe was done.
Transaction Type – Reflects the type of transaction.
Plan Type – Displays the plan type of plan(s) a transaction was applied to. For split claims, each plan the payment was split across will display separated by commas.

chunks.title: Processing | Transaction Search
chunks.content:
Claim# /Contribution# /Payment# /Credit# /Plan Repayment# –  Based on the type of transactions, the claim number, contribution number, payment number, credit number, or plan repayment number are populated.
Status – This will be the current claim status.
Total Amount – Refers to the total claim amount.
Approved Amount – Displays the total approved amount.
Denied Amount – Displays the amount denied from the total claim amount.
OnHold/ Denied For Low Fund Amount –  Shows the amount kept on hold due to low plan balance.
Reimbursement Amount – Indicates the reimbursed amount.
Payment – Displays the amount of payment(s) done in dollars with its reimbursement method(s). For split claims, each payment will display separated by commas.
Check# – Claims that are entered and approved typically result in the production of a check or ACH. This field reflects the check number if the reimbursement method associated with the claim was check. For voided checks, the field will display as Voided.
Provider/ Merchant – Displays the name of the provider or merchant associated with the claim.
Add Claim
Clicking the “Add Claim” button will direct the user to the Manual Claim Transaction Entry page for entering new claims into the system.
For further information, please refer to FAQs.

chunks.title: Processing
chunks.content:
Processing
Processing covers a wide range of activities within Summit. Most administrative tasks that fall outside the scope of setting up entities and plan design are included under the umbrella of processing.
Processing tasks include manual claim entry and processing, importing and exporting, handling enrollment, and much more.
Table of Contents
Transaction Entry
Transaction Review
Batch Transaction Entry
Transaction Search
File Fulfillment
Process Approvals
Process Renewals
Data Exchange
Cash Management
On Demand Notices (Premium Billing)
The Processing subpages can be accessed from the Processing dropdown menu.
Additionally, any Processing subpage can be accessed by clicking the desired page from the top menu list displayed on all Processing pages.
Transaction Entry
The Transaction Entry screen allows for the manual entry of various transactions. For more information on Transaction Entry, visit the Transaction Entry page and the subpages for each of Summit’s available transaction types.
Transaction Review
The Transaction Review page allows users to review Debit Card transactions and Manually Entered Claims, as well as search for and associate Unassigned Images with claims.
Batch Transaction Entry
The Batch Transaction Entry page allows users to enter multiple transactions at once from a single point of entry. At this time, only Premium Billing Receipt entry may be done from the Batch Transaction Entry screen.
Transaction Search
The Transaction Search page contains tools that allow users to find and view transactions in Summit based on a wide range of criteria.
File Fulfillment
Summit can create files for use with bank integration, allowing for ACH payments, fulfillment of CDH checks and communications, and fulfillment of Premium Billing Checks and Notifications.
File created for these purposes may be accessed, viewed, and downloaded on the File Fulfillment page of Processing.
DataPath Fulfillment
Manual Fulfillment
Process Approvals

chunks.title: Processing
chunks.content:
Certain processes within Summit may require manual approval by an Administrator User to complete. The Process Approvals page allows users to view and either approve or reject processes that require administrative intervention.
These processes include:
Contributions
Document Fulfillment
Election Changes
Events
Missing Information
Premium Autodrafts
Online Enrollment
Reimbursements
Remittances
Unapplied Receipts
Process Renewals
The Process Renewals page is where you will be able to process Employer Plan Renewals and Participant Re-Enrollments.
Select a Renewal Type
Employer Plan Renewals
Participant Enrollment Renewals
Data Exchange
Data Exchange is one of the most powerful tools Summit offers. It allows for highly customizable exports and imports of data to and from Summit to meet a wide range of business needs.
Cash Management
Cash Management is used to track balances and funds in and out of the associated bank accounts configured in Summit. Summit can track deposits to and debits from real bank accounts.
From Cash Management, you can
View balances of TPA bank accounts and any employer accounts
Add notional deposits to and withdrawals
View individual transactions that have affected an account
Get alerts when balances drop below a specified threshold
On Demand Notices (Premium Billing)
At times, it may be necessary to create or recreate Premium Billing notices to participants on demand.
From this page, TPA users can:
Prompt coupon books to be sent to selected participants with Premium Billing coverage status within the selected plan year date range
Prompt Open Enrollment notices to be sent to selected participants within the selected plan year date range
Prompt rate change notices to be sent to selected participants within the selected plan year date range
Prompt initial notices to be sent to selected participants added during a calendar date range, with filters for dependents added during specific plan year start date and plan year end dates

chunks.content:
Select one or more participants for a specific employer to send the notices or coupon books
View the event on the Participant Central Events tab and the coverage’s Participant Portal Events tab.
