chunks.title: Quick Guide – How to Run the ARPA Extended Election Notice
chunks.content:
Quick Guide – How to Run the ARPA Extended Election Notice
The ARPA Extended Election Notice is now available to be generated via the On Demand user-interface.
A qualified beneficiary (QB) should receive the ARPA extended election notice if they:
Elected COBRA and:
Coverage was terminated on or after October 1, 2019 but before April 1, 2021, AND
The Qualified Beneficiary is still within their maximum COBRA period, AND
The Qualified Beneficiary’s qualifying event was loss of coverage due to Involuntary Termination or Reduction of Hours
Did Not Elect COBRA and:
Coverage was terminated on or after October 1, 2019 but before April 1, 2021, AND
The Qualified Beneficiary is still within their maximum COBRA period, AND
The Qualified Beneficiary’s qualifying event was loss of coverage due to Involuntary Termination or Reduction of Hours
The TPA can also send the ARPA extended election notice to a single participant not included in a previous distribution of the notice; for example, if a participant not identified by the employer as an Assistance Eligible Individual (AEI) thereafter calls the TPA to request treatment as an AEI.  The TPA should verify AEI coverage status prior to the subsidy assignment.
Viewing Previously-Generated Notices
To determine whether an ARPA extended election notice has already been generated for a participant, the user can run the LOS Activity report and select the ARPA Election Notice event.  The user can also select the event in Process Approvals and export the results to Excel.
Run LOS Activity Report
If the ARPA Extended Election Notice has been run previously on demand for an employer, run the LOS Activity report to determine the participants for whom the notices have already been triggered.
Figure 1 – Run LOS Activity Report User-Interface
Step 1.
To run the report for multiple employers, select Employers from the drop down list.

chunks.title: Quick Guide – How to Run the ARPA Extended Election Notice
chunks.content:
Note: If an employer has a large number of employees, we recommend that you run the LOS Activity report separately for the single employer to reduce processing time.  
  Step 2.
Select COBRA as the LOS using the drop-down menu.
 Step 3.
Enter a Start Date and End Date.
Notes:

Start Date:  If ARPA Extended Election Notices were generated previously for any of the selected employers, use the first date that notices were created as the start date. This will help to ensure that the participants for whom the notices were created previously will be included on the report, to prevent duplicate/multiple notices from being sent.

End Date:  If ARPA Extended Election Notices were generated previously for any of the selected employers, use the last date that notices were created as the end date. This will help to ensure that the participants for whom the notices were created previously will be included on the report, to prevent duplicate/multiple notices from being sent.
 Step 4.
Make sure thatthe ARPA Extended Election Notice is selected using the Events drop-down menu.  If the ARPA Extended Election Notice will also be generated/triggered on demand, and has previously been run on demand, the notice can be selected as well.
Step 5.
Include Only AEI Participants check box. When this option is checked, only participants that have AEI coverages will be included on the report.
NOTE: If the ARPA Extended Election Notice was run on demand previously with the Include Only AEI Participants option NOT checked, do NOT check the box now. In case the notices were sent to participants that did not have AEI coverages, those participants will appear on the LOS Activity report. However, if the ARPA Extended Election Notice was run on demand previously and the Include Only AEI Participants option was checked, the box should be checked for this run.
Step 6.
Select the Export Format for the file and click Run to export the LOS Activity Report.

chunks.title: Quick Guide – How to Run the ARPA Extended Election Notice
chunks.content:
NOTE: The CSV file format is recommended so that the report can be filtered and sorted by participant, employer, and event.
Figure 2 – LOS Activity Report
Process Approvals Event Excel Export
Step 1.
Make sure that all Approval Types are selected to ensure that all ARPA Extended Election Notice events will be included.
Step 2.
Enter the date of the first day and most recent date that the notices were run on demand, in the From and To date fields.
Step 3.
Select all user types that are applicable for the TPA in the User Type drop down list.
Step 4.
Select the employers for which the event was run on demand.
Step 5.
Select the ARPA Extended Election Notice event in the Events drop down list.
Step 6.
Select the Excel function.
Figure 3 – Process Approvals Excel Function
Step 7.
When the file is created, sort and filter as necessary to identify the participants for which the event had been previously triggered and manually approved, declined, auto-approved and/or declined.
Figure 4 – Process Approvals Excel Export Results
Generate ARPA Extended Election Notices
The On Demand user-interface will be used to generate/trigger the ARPA Extended Election Notices.
Figure 5 – On Demand Notices – Select All Participants
Step 1.
Select the Employer for which the notices are to be generated.
Step 2.
Select ARPA Extended Election Notice using the Notification drop-down menu.
Step 3.
Enter 04/01/2021 (ARPA subsidy start date)in the As of Date field.
Enter 09/30/2021 (ARPA subsidy end date) in the Through This Date field. 
NOTES

The ARPA Extended Election Notice event will be triggered if the participant elected COBRA coverage, the COBRA coverage was terminated before the As of Date, and the COBRA coverage expiration date was on the As of Date, on the Through This Date, between the two dates, or after the Through This Date.

chunks.title: Quick Guide – How to Run the ARPA Extended Election Notice
chunks.content:
The ARPA Extended Election Notice event will be triggered if the participant had a qualifying event but did not elect COBRA coverage before the As of Date, and the COBRA coverage expiration date was on the As of Date, on the Through This Date, between the two dates, or after the Through This Date.
Step 4.
To trigger notices only for participants with flagged AEI coverages, check the Include Only Participants with AEI Coverages option.
To trigger the notices for all participants that meet the As of Date/Through this Date criteria but do not have AEI coverages, do NOT check the option.
Step 5.
Choose a Select Participants radio button.
NOTES
If the notices are being run for the first time, it is recommended that you select the ALL button.
If the notices were run previously for some participants, select either Just These or Not These depending on the number of participants for whom notices are to be triggered. 
If there are fewer participants to include than exclude, select Just These and enter the names of the participants to receive the notices. 
If there are fewer participants to exclude than include, select Not These and enter the names of the participants that will not receive the notices.
Figure 6 – On Demand Notices – Select All Participants – Just These Participants
Step 6.
Click Generate Notices.

NOTE: If the On Demand process generates notices, On Demand Success! will display. If the process does not generate any notices, On Demand Notices – No participants selected will display.
View the ARPA Extended Election Notice Events
To view the generated/triggered ARPA Extended Election Notice events, open the Process Approvals user interface and select the ARPA Extended Election Notice event for the employers for which the notices have been run on demand.
NOTE: The Approval Required option is checked by default for the ARPA Extended Election Notice event.  
After verifying that the events were triggered for the appropriate participants, click Approve.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-11-4
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025-11-4
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.11.4. This release contains items pushed to production in November 2025 + the first week of December. For additional information on the Features and Enhancements, please see the What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
12/02/2025
11/20/2025
11/11/2025
11/4/2025
Enhancements
FTP Details – Exports to Use SFTP Irrespective of Port Number – Summit can now use SFTP regardless of Port selection.
Reimbursement Settings – Separate Account Assignment for ACH Reimbursements – We have added a new ACH Bank Account setting for both TPA and Employer-level Reimbursement Settings that will allow for the configuration of a separate bank account assignment for ACH Reimbursements.
 Participant Portal Security Image/Passphrase – The Security Image and Passphrase have been removed from the Participant Portal login process. The improved security offered by two-factor authentication obviates the need for these.
Side Tab – As part of our efforts to cleanup and streamline the Summit interface, we have removed the side tab that contained the Calendar, Favorites, Edit Role, and Help icons. Access to page-specific help can be found by going to Help (top of the screen), and clicking Page Help.
New PCOR Fee Rates – The IRS has published new PCOR rates [$3.84] for plans beginning on or before 10/1/2025 and ending before 10/1/2026. This new PCOR fee rate has been added to the Annual Rates & Limits table in Administrator Settings.
Receipt Distribution Details With Division Option – Additional Data Elements – We have updated the data set for the Receipt Distribution Details With Division Option report to include Supplemental Demographics values.
PB Continuation Participant Report With Division Option – Additional Data Elements – We have updated the data set for the PB Continuation Participant Report With Division Option to include Supplemental Demographic values.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-11-4
chunks.content:
CDH Invoice Report/Export Parameters – The CDH Invoice report parameters have been modified to allow for more flexible selections and better functionality.
Issues Addressed
12/02/2025
Duplicate CustomIDs for Participants and Dependents – An issue could occur where a participant and dependent shared the same CustomID value, which could result in validation issues when attempting to edit either record. This was occurring when dependent records were split from the original participant following a qualifying event; the dependent records would copy values from the original participant, including the CustomID. This has been corrected, and the creation of a split dependent record following a qualifying event no longer copies the CustomID value from the parent account.
TPA Fees Not Calculating Correctly Following Disability Extension – Following the beginning of a Disability Extension event, the system was not correctly calculating and collecting the TPA fee at the 50% rate. This has been corrected.
Age Rated PB Plans – An error occurred when users attempted to import age-rated Premium Billing tiers for new benefits. This has been corrected.
Coverage Details UI Error – When entering a PB plan for a participant, the Contribution Amount and Claim fields which are greyed out and should be unavailable could be unlocked by clicking on them, and users would receive an error when entering a value in these fields. This error would occur because these fields should be read-only, and entering a value created an exception. This has been resolved.
Payment Method Failing to Export – The Cash Management Export was failing to include the Payment Method field in the output results. This has been corrected.
ZIP Field Not Allowing Leading Zeroes – The validation on the Corporate ZIP field in the TPA Demographics section was preventing users from entering ZIP Codes with leading zeroes. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-11-4
chunks.content:
Enrollment Report Including Divisions Not Selected – When running the Enrollment Report with the By Divisions options selected, the report’s results were including divisions that had not been selected. This has been corrected, and only selected divisions will be included in query results.
Enrollment Option Missing for PB Plans – When renewing Premium Billing plans, the Enrollment Options would intermittently be missing from the form. This has been resolved.
Portal Images and FSA Store Banner – Banners were being inconsistently displayed in the Participant Portal, sometimes intermittently failing to display. This has been resolved.
Plan Repayments – When entering a repayment that was greater than the balance due to make an overpayment, the system was inappropriately allowing the user to select DirectPay as an option. This has been corrected, and DirectPay has been removed as an option for overpayments.
PB Event Dates Missing – Premium Billing Event Dates were missing from the first payment notices for 2nd Qualifying Events. This has been corrected, and the Event Dates are being included on these documents.
ACH Files Created Without Plan Overrides – The Plan Override setting was not using the specific bank when ACH payments were issued for the plan, rather using the primary employer bank. This has been corrected, and employers with plan overrides are functioning correctly.
Participant Claim Status Reverting From Approved to Request – The system was reverting claim statuses from “Approved” to “Request” upon saving. This has been resolved and affected claims have been patched.
Card Holds Not Working – An issue occurred where a card placed on hold due to a termination of plan could fail to be blocked. This has been addressed.
PB Import Error – Attempting to run a Premium Billing import for an employer that was both PB and CDH would result in a system error. This has been resolved.
11/20/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-11-4
chunks.content:
Logo Display Issues – Newly uploaded company logos were not displaying appropriately on Summit. This has been addressed, and images are displaying correctly.
11/11/2025
Employer Card Block – Expired Cards Reissuing – Expired cards were being reissued to participants despite an employer-level card block in place. This has been resolved.
11/4/2025
Terminated Plans Creating Rates – Terminated plans were creating rates for months that do not exist within the employer’s plan year. This has been corrected.
Employer Plan – Error Selecting Plan Year – Users would receive an error when selecting a new plan year after they had enabled CDH for Premium Billing-enabled plan. This has been corrected, and users can assign new plan years for all Lines of Service to associate with plans that had previously been Premium Billing-only.
On Demand Processing Permissions – A recent Premium Billing update to add Group Coverage Administration included changes to the permissions modules, resulting in users being unable to access On Demand Notices. Roles have been patched to address this issue.
Claims Not Restricting Plan Selection by Service Code – Users were able to enter claims and associate them with a plan that was not tied to a service category that was enabled by the employer-level benefit order. This has been corrected, and plan selection during claim entry is limited by available employer service codes.
Error When Editing/Importing Participants – An error occurred when editing or importing participants. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.12.3
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025.12.3
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.12.3. This release contains items pushed to production the 2nd– 4th week of December. For additional information on the Features and Enhancements, please see the What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Enhancements
Optimization
Issues Addressed
12/23/2025
12/18/2025
12/16/2025
12/09/2025
Enhancements
Premium Billing Online Elections “Step 2” Coverage Selection Grid – We have updated the “Step 2” screen of the Participant Portal’s online elections process to accommodate age-rate Sum Multiple Tier coverages.
Optimization
Reimbursement Setting Employer Selector – In order to address an issue with data loading on the Reimbursement Settings page, we have removed the default “—Select Employer—” option from the Employer dropdown selector. The Employer Reimbursement Settings page will load the session variable for the last selected Employer selected and that group’s data populated on the screen. If no employer is in the session variable, then no data will load on the pages until an employer has been selected.
Issues Addressed
12/23/2025
PB Import – Info Button Displaying Incorrect Information – When viewing and configuring the Premium Billing Import templates in Data Exchange, the Info button on the Employment Status field was not displaying the appropriate numeric values and corresponding status information. This has been corrected, and the Info button is now displaying the correct information.
Purse Not Including Contributions on Same Day as Posted – Under certain circumstances, purse values were not including contributions on the day they were posted. While the purse would update, it would subsequently revert before later updating to the correct amount. This could create a window where purchases would be declined despite the fact that funds should have been available. This has been addressed.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.12.3
chunks.content:
Payments to Terminated Plans – Participants were able to make payments to Premium Billing plans that had already been terminated. This has been corrected, and the system will no longer allow payments to be made for benefits in rehire or termed status.
Errors in HSA Plans – Users would receive errors when attempting to edit claims for groups with an HSA or when attempting to assign an HSA to a new participant. This has been resolved.
Error Processing Rate Change – Under certain circumstances, users would receive error messages when attempting to process rate changes. This has been resolved, and users are able to process rate changes without issue.
12/18/2025
Employer Subsidy Audit Report – The Employer Subsidy Audit Report was not populating query results. This has been corrected.
Transaction Display – The Add a Transaction dropdown menu item and the Add Transaction button on the Online Transactions screen were not displaying consistently. This has been corrected.
12/16/2025
Replacement Cards Issued With Old Name Information – If a participant’s name has changed since their original card was issued, replacement cards ordered following requests for new cards to replace lost/stolen cards were not being issued with the updated information. This has been corrected, and replacement cards will include updated participant names.
Disability Fee Split – When trying to update the fee percentage split for disability fees, the TPA fee split would not be affected if the employer fee split value was changed. This has been corrected and the fields correspond to one another when one or the other is modified.
Participant Portal Coverages Tab – The “Next Due Amount” in the Coverage tab of Participant Portal was not pulling the correct Amount Due value for Billing. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.12.3
chunks.content:
Participant Password Reset Link – The password reset emails sent to participants were incorrectly including links to the admin portal rather than the Participant Portal. This has been corrected, and the links included in the email direct to the Participant Portal.
Contribution Schedules Could Be Removed From Plans After Being Assigned to Participants – Contribution Schedules could be removed from employer plans after changing Plan Years even if those schedules had been assigned to Participant Plans. This has been corrected, and if a schedule has been assigned to a Participant Plan, it cannot be removed.
12/09/2025
Contribution History By Participant Report Omitting “Locked” Participants – The Contribution History by Participant Report was omitting participants that were in a “Locked” status. This has been corrected, and these participants are being included in the query results.
Next Check Number Erroneously Required – The Next Check Number field was being subject to validation and treated as a required field even when the “Let System Generate Next Check Number” option was disabled. This has been corrected, and the Next Check Number field will only be required if system generation of check numbers is enabled.
User Address Change Communications Merging Old Participant Addresses – When users updated their address, the resulting Address Change email communication was displaying the old address rather than the new one. This has been corrected, and the new address is displaying in the communication.
SSO Malfunction – An issue involving Single Sign-On was preventing participant users from accessing the Participant Portal from external links that relied on SAML passthru. This has been resolved, and users are able to access the Participant Portal through these links.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.12.3
chunks.content:
Claim Edit Missing Service Codes – When editing a claim, all applicable service codes were not being included for the selected service category. This was affecting service codes that had a copay value when “Bypass Deductible” was unchecked; this would result in the system failing to recognize the code as valid and would therefore omit it from the available service code list. This has been corrected, and all appropriate service codes are displaying for selection on the Claim Edit screen.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2026.01.4
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2026.01.4
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2026.01.4. This release contains items pushed to production the 1st through 4th week of January. For more information on new features and enhancements, see the January What’s New Guide.
Features
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
1/27/2026
1/20/2026
1/13/2026
1/06/2026
Features
Postpone Events in Process Approvals – Users can now postpone events in Process Approvals, delaying their processing until a later user–selected date.
Enhancements
Premium Billing Online Elections “Step 2” Coverage Selection Grid – We have updated the “Step 2” screen of the Participant Portal’s online elections process to accommodate age-rate Sum Multiple Tier coverages.
Process Renewals – Participant Enrollment – PRK/TRN Contribution Amount Validation – Participant Enrollment Renewals has been enhanced to include field validation for Contribution Amounts for Parking and Transit plan types.
Enrollment Report – Tier Name and Tier ID – The Tier Name and Tier ID data fields have been added to the data source for the Enrollment Report.
Participant Coverage Report – The Tier Name and Tier ID data fields have been added to the data source for the Participant Coverage Report.
“Summit” Verbiage Removed from 2FA Communications – The word “Summit” no longer appears in the Subject Line and Body of emails sent with the login verification code.
Issues Addressed
1/27/2026
Events Tab Show Deleted Events Filter Not Working – The Show Deleted Events filter toggle was not working correctly, and deleted events would not display when this option was enabled. This has been corrected, and the filter will control for display of deleted events.
Contributions Not Posting Correctly – When contributions were posted, the purse would appear to update then revert back to the original balance. This has been corrected and contributions are posting correctly.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2026.01.4
chunks.content:
Settlement Reconciliation Report – The Settlement Reconciliation report was erroneously returning results for periods during which the employer should have no card settlement data. If an employer was included in the report run for a date year prior to their start date, the report would include results from their first year of card activity when no results should have been included for that range. This has been corrected.
Delete Employer With Card History – The Delete Employer function was not working correctly for employers with Card Program history in Summit. An error would occur when deleting the employer. This has been corrected, and employers with cards history can be successfully deleted.
PB Import Error – An error would occur when attempting to run a premium billing import containing takeover retirees with the Entitled to Medicare as coverage expires rule enabled. This has been corrected.
Process Approvals: Remittances Erroneously Showing Minimum Message – The Minimum Check Amount message on negative offset payments were being included even if the Require Minimum Check Amount setting was disabled. This has been corrected and the message will not display if Require Minimum Check Amount is disabled.
Carryover Amount Not Being Included in Participant Balances – If a participant elected $0 for a benefit, the participant’s balance was not including the previous year’s carryover if available. This has been corrected.
Balance Due Amounts Not Populating For Partially Denied Card Claims – The Balance Due Amount was not populating for partially denied
1/20/2026
Contribution Amount Not Displaying – Contribution Amounts were not displaying if the user had selected a contribution schedule in the plan which had not previously had any schedules assigned to it. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2026.01.4
chunks.content:
Non-Discrimination Testing Failing – Non-Discrimination Testing would fail if participants under a single employer group had the same name. This has been addressed, and the system will now use the SSN value to disambiguate between participants within the group.
Participant Entered Receipts Alert – Participant Entered Receipts alerts were being generated for the Pending Approvals and Actions screen despite no pending receipts being present Cash Management. The underlying issue that resulted in these alerts has been resolved and erroneous alerts have been removed.
Imported Files Showing With Incomplete Status – Imported files were showing with an incomplete status, and no response file was being generated if the file contained an incorrect data type in at least one column of every row. This has been corrected, and the file will process and produce a results file.
Previously Terminated Participants Not Included in Active Lives Invoice – An issue occurred where participants who had been previously terminated and subsequently reinstated were not being included in the Active Lives Invoice Fee. This has been corrected and the invoice is including these individuals in fee calculations.
Third Party Payor Coverage Assignment Display Issue – Due to a refresh display issue, the selections made under Premium Billing | Third Party Payors was not displaying the most recently saved settings. This has been corrected, and the selections are displaying properly after saving.
Negative Contribution Adjustments Generated for Contributions – Negative contribution adjustments were being generated for contributions that were made prior to the effective date of the new election amounts. This has been corrected and these negative contribution adjustments will not apply to contributions made before the effective date of the new election amount.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2026.01.4
chunks.content:
Process Renewals – Participant Enrollment – When viewing Participant Enrollment Renewals in Processing | Process Renewals, plans that had already expired would not return any participant results. This has been addressed and the query would include these participants in the results on the Process Renewals screen.
Reissued Cards Displaying Old Card Packages – If a participant had a card under an employer’s previous card package and a new card package was implemented and that participant’s card was reported lost or stolen, the new card would appear in the Cards tab associated with the old card package instead of the new card package. This has been corrected.
Data Exchange Files Stuck in Pending Status – In some instances, files uploaded to Data Exchange would become stuck in a Pending status, requiring the file to be manually removed and reuploaded. This has been addressed and files are processing correctly.
CDH Checks Secondary Signatures – DataPath Fulfillment – CDH check templates have been updated to correctly merge Secondary Signature images when sent to DataPath Fulfillment.
Payments Unable to Process – Some payments generated for claims prevented TPAs from being able to generate a file from the payment. This has been addressed and resolved.
Receipt Distribution Details Report – The Receipt Distribution Details Report had an incorrect fee total calculation in the Summary section. This has been corrected and the summary fee total is calculating correctly.
Data Exchange PB Import – Premium Billing Plans were failing to add when imported through Data Exchange. This has been resolved.
1/13/2026
Participant Account Balance Report – The Year To Date Payments included in the Participant Account Balance Report were not calculating correctly and were failing to match the payments in Summit’s UI. The report was erroneously including Purchase Returns and Plan Adjustments in the YTD totals. This has been addressed and the YTD payments are calculating correctly in the report output.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2026.01.4
chunks.content:
Debit Card Transactions by Participant – Declined debit card transactions were erroneously being included in the Debit Card Transactions by Participant report. This has been corrected and these transaction types are being excluded from the results.
Dependent Split Off Missing Setup Checklist Steps – When dependents were split off from a participant account following a Qualifying Event, the system was not including the participant setup checklist steps in the dependent’s records, which would result in the system failing to send the welcome notice email. This would require users to manually setup the dependent account. This has been resolved and dependent accounts are being successfully spun off of participant accounts following QEs.
On Demand Reimbursements – When selecting a payment that was for $1000 or more under On Demand Reimbursement, the total button was not displaying the dollar amount. This has been corrected.
Participants Not Displaying in Participant Central – Participants were failing to display and list in Participant Central. This has been corrected, and participants are once again loading on the Participant Central screen.
1/06/2026
Receipt Management Emails Failing to Generate – Receipt Management emails were not being sent consistently for all transactions. This has been addressed and resolved.
Error Undoing Changes to Plans – Users would experience an error when attempting to undo changes to plans if the EmployerFundingTierID value was null. This has been resolved, and the Undo function can be performed without error.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2026.01.4
chunks.content:
Debit Card Transactions at Grocery/Pharmacy Not Processing Correctly – Debit card transactions at certain pharmacies and grocery stores were not applying to the correct plans, going balance due, or failing to autosubstantiate. Issues were affecting 5912 and 5411 MCCs as these require IIAS or 90% Merchant flag data to properly calculate; absence of these values would lead to discrepancies in how the Claim Calculator handled these transactions and could result in the claim being misapplied. We have updated the claim calculation logic to address scenarios where the claim would process transactions from these MCCs incorrectly.
Password Reset Error – An error would occur when attempting to reset a Participant user’s password using the Reset User link on the participant’s profile screen in the admin system. This has been corrected, and users may manually reset participant users’ accounts without issue.
On Demand Processing Exclusion Filter – The option to exclude terminated participants when configuring an On Demand Custom Event was excluding any participants who had a terminated plan rather than excluding participants for whom all plans had been terminated. This has been corrected, and this exclusion filter is only excluding participants for whom all coverage has been terminated.
Mandatory Field Validation For Dependents – Validation of mandatory fields for participants in Summit created issues for Premium Billing Administrators, as many carrier feed files do not typically include for dependents the demographic values that were flagged as required in Administrator Settings | Participant Demographics [eg. Gender, SSNs and DOBs]. While these values may still be flagged as Required for primary participants, these fields will NOT be validated for dependents.

chunks.content:
Release Notes 2026.02.2
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2026.02.2. This release contains items pushed to production the 2nd week of February.
Issues Addressed 2/10/2026
Claims Made Balance Due when Prior Claims Edited – An issue was occurring where autosubstantiated claims would go balance due after prior claims were edited. This has been corrected, and a data patch has been applied to affected autosubstantiated cards.

No Valid COBRA Time Period Message – Users would receive a “No valid COBRA time period” error message when performing rate changes on participants’ FSA plans that had an Active status. This has been corrected and users are able to successfully save rate changes for plans in Active status.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2026.02.2

Duplicate TPA Default Portal Settings For New Employers – An issue was occurring where upon creation of a new employer group, the TPA default Participant Portal settings would create duplicate entry that would be assigned to that employer as employer level settings rather than simply apply the TPA defaults to the employer. chunks.title: Reporting | MSP Reporting
chunks.content:
Reporting | MSP Reporting
Medicare Secondary Payor (MSP) Reporting is a mandated report to Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) of individuals covered by a Health Reimbursement Arrangement (HRA). The goal is to identify individuals covered by Medicare and an HRA for which a covered individual can be reimbursed 5000.00 or more for a plan year. Those individuals will be designated as covered by Medicare as a secondary payor, meaning the HRA should be exhausted before Medicare pays any claims.
Table of Contents
To access MSP Reporting
MSP Input File
MSP Input TIN File Format
Response File Format
* Required fields appear in Red
To access MSP Reporting
Enter the MSP Reporting RRE ID and select the MSP Reporting Submission Period from the Demographics tab in Administrator Central.
MSP Reporting RRE ID – The MSP RRE ID is an identifier assigned to the Required Reporting Entity by CMS and is included in the MSP Input file, Header Record, submitted to CMS each submission period. It is included in the response files received from CMS.
MSP Reporting Submission Period – The MSP Submission Period field identifies when the file must be submitted to CMS. The Submission Period is assigned by CMS when the Required Reporting Entity (RRE) registers. The Submission Period is seven days long and occurs once per quarter. The file can be submitted at any time during the submission period, but may not be submitted before the first day of the Submission Period.
Clicking the ‘information icon’ will display the Submission Period List pop-up.
The complete list of submission periods is listed below. The user will choose the appropriate Submission period from the MSP Reporting Submission Period dropdown based on the submission period assigned by CMS.

Total Employee Count – The user must select a value from this dropdown list. The default is “Select Employee Count”. The dropdown options are “1-19”, “20-99”, and “100+”.
Tax ID – The user must enter a valid Tax ID in this field. This is the tax id that will be submitted to CMS for the employer and any MSP reportable plans.
Add/Edit an HRA or MERP plan from the Benefit plans tab to access MSP Reporting options.
Report this plan to CMS – The “Report this Plan to CMS” checkbox must be checked for a benefit to be included in the MSP file. Selecting the Report this plan to CMS identifies this plan as one that can reimburse an individual $5000.00 or more for the plan year. If the checkbox is selected, Summit will report all covered participants that meet the criteria: DOB calculates to age 45 and older, a gender selection, a relationship selection to the employee, and a Social Security Number.

The available types are:

chunks.title: Reporting | MSP Reporting
chunks.content:
Enter all the required fields including SSN, Date of Birth, Gender, HICN and ESRD fields in the Participant Central Demographics tab.
SSN – The user can enter the Social Security Number (SSN) in this numeric field. The SSN is a required data element for reporting to CMS.
Date of Birth – Enter the date of birth. The system will calculate the participant and covered dependents’ age and will include anyone 45 years or older.
Gender – Select the gender of the participant and dependents. Gender is a required data element for reporting to CMS.
Male
Female
Other
HICN –Enter the Health Insurance Claim Number (HICN) of participant or dependent if provided. This is not required for reporting to CMS. If the individual reported is a current Medicare Beneficiary CMS will respond with the individuals HICN.
ESRD – Selecting this checkbox indicates that the participant is an End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) patient. ESRD patients are covered by Medicare regardless of age. Selecting this option will include the individual in the CMS report regardless of their age.
Assign the participant to MSP Reporting enabled plan from the Participant Central Plans page. For more details, refer Participant | Participant Central | Plans.
Go to the MSP Reporting page of Reporting menu.
This page includes:
Tax ID – The Tax ID of TPA which is a read only field.
File – The dropdown lists past and upcoming quarterly submissions. Select the submission period to view the detail of the file.
Plans/Participants/Employers tabs – Plans selected as reportable will display on the Plans tab while participants assigned to the identified plans will display on the Participants tab and employers with reportable plans will display on the Employers tab. The Participants tab provides an option to filter participants based on employers and plans as shown below.
After making the required selections, click the Create File button to generate the MSP report.

chunks.title: Reporting | MSP Reporting
chunks.content:
The generated MSP report can be viewed at the MSP Reporting section of Processing | File Fulfillment.
For more details, refer Processing | File Fulfillment page.
MSP Input File
The MSP Input File includes participants covered by a plan identified as reportable to CMS that also have an SSN, gender, relationship, and a DOB that calculates their age to 45 or older.  The MSP input file will also include individuals returned as Medicare Beneficiaries who have had their reportable coverage terminated. Summit will generate the contents of the file by first looking at Benefit Plans identified as MSP Reportable (i.e. that have the ‘Report this plan to CMS’ selected, along with an MSP Coverage Type, during the query period); Summit will then determine which participants, i.e. the employee and any covered dependents, are currently covered by those plans that also meet the required data elements, i.e. have a Social Security Number, have a Date of Birth that calculates the participant to be 45 years of age or older, have a Gender assigned, i.e. Male or Female, and have a Relationship identified, i.e. Spouse, Child, etc. A participant can also be included if the HICN field is populated even if they are less than 45 years of age. For more information about the MSP Input File Layout, refer to MSP Reporting.
MSP Input TIN File Format
The TIN file includes a record for each Employer whose participants are included in the Input file. The TIN file also includes one record for the reporting TPA. Required data elements are Tax ID, Name, Address, City, State, Zip Code, and the TIN Indicator. The TIN Indicator is a single letter that identifies the record as belonging to an Employer (E) or to the TPA (I). There are also Header and Trailer records that precede and follow the TIN Detail records. The TIN file is included in the Input file following the Detail Trailer record. For more details, refer to the MSP Input TIN File Format section of MSP Reporting.
Response File Format

chunks.title: Reporting | MSP Reporting
chunks.content:
A response file is generated, by CMS, for every Input and TIN file submitted.
The response file contains the Disposition Code that identifies a submitted individual as a Medicare Beneficiary. Covered participants returned as Medicare Beneficiaries will be excluded from future Input files until their reportable coverage is terminated, deleted, not renewed, or the balance goes to 0.00. Other Disposition Codes and Error Codes will give direction for action to be taken before the next submission period.
For detail regarding the Response File Format, refer to MSP Reporting.
Also, please refer to the Reporting section in FAQs for further information.

To access Report Editor,
Go to Processing and select the menu Data Exchange.
Open the Report Management tab, locate the desired report and click the  “Edit” link to access the report editor.
The advanced report editor will open in a new tab as shown below.
Report Editor Overview
The Report Editor will contain a Template Name, Report Design Surface, and various tools to design the report. 
Template Name – In this field, the name of the report template which is being edited will be shown. This is a mandatory field.
Design Surface – Report Design Surface displays the structure and contents of the report.
Menu – This button at the top left-hand side of the screen is used to manage and set up reports. Clicking the button will expand and display available menus.
Main Toolbar – From this toolbar, the user can access various report editing commands. This section is just above the Report Design Surface.
Toolbox – This is another toolbox on the left-hand side of the screen from which the user can add available controls to the design surface.
Properties – Properties panel provides different controls to customize the report and report element properties. This panel is located on the right-hand side of the screen.
The Properties panel includes some or all of the following categories. The list of available categories is dependent on what item the user has selected within the Design Surface.
Actions

chunks.title: Reporting | Reports | Report Editor
chunks.content:
Styles
Appearance
Behavior
Data
Design
Layout
Navigation

Field List – This panel displays the schema of the report data source and enables the user to manage report data sources and parameters. This panel is located on the right-hand side of the screen. Data elements can be added to the report Design Surface from this Field List. This panel is located on the right-hand side of the screen.
Modifying a Report Template
Label
Label control is used to insert plain text into the report.
Add – To add a Label to the report, drag the label icon from the toolbox and place it in the report. By double-clicking the label, the user can insert the desired text into the label or enter the desired text in the “Text” property field of the Actions category.
Edit – Double-clicking the label allows the user to change the text inside the label or enter the desired text in the “Text” property field.
Delete – For deleting a label from the report, select the label and click the Delete icon or press the Delete button on the keyboard.
Move – To move a label, the user must select the label and then drag it to the desired location.
Width – The user may drag the anchor point of the label to adjust its width.
Also, the user can use “Auto Width” to adjust width automatically, “Can Grow” to grow the label size according to the text, “Can Shrink” to shrink the label size according to the text, and “Word Wrap” to wrap the text inside the label.
Data Field
The user can view the available data fields in the Field List tab.
Add – To add a Data Field, drag the desired data field from the Field List and place it in the report.
Delete – To delete a data field from the report, select the data field and click the Delete icon or press the Delete button on the keyboard.
Move – To move a data field, the user must select the data field and then drag it to the desired location.
Width – The user may drag the anchor point of the data field to adjust its width.

chunks.title: Reporting | Reports | Report Editor
chunks.content:
Also, the user can use “Auto Width” to adjust width automatically, “Can Grow” to grow the data field size according to the text, “Can Shrink” to shrink the data field size according to the text, and “Word Wrap” to wrap the text inside the data field.
Header/Footer
The Report Header is the report’s first band and is used to display the report’s name, company logo, date of creation, username, etc. The Report Footer is used for report summaries or conclusions.
Add – The user can add text to the header/footer by dragging the label to the report header/footer band.
Drag Page Info control into report’s header/footer band and choose an option from the “Page Information” property of Actions category to insert User Name, Page Count, Page Number, Current Date and Time, and “Current of Total” Page Number to the report.
Edit – Double-clicking the label allows the user to change the text inside the label or enter the desired text in the “Text” property field. From the “Page Information” property, the user can choose the desired property.
Delete – To delete, select the tool and click the Delete icon or press the Delete button on the keyboard.
Fonts
Font properties can be accessed from the Appearance category of the Properties panel.
Font Name – From this dropdown list, the user can choose a font.
Size – The user can enter the size of the text in this field.
Style – The user can apply styles to the text by clicking the preferred style.
Font Color – Font color can be changed by selecting the label/data field and then choosing a color from the “Foreground Color” property.
Picture  
Using the Picture Box control the user can embed a picture (logo image) into the report.
Add the Picture Box control onto the report’s area by dragging it from the Toolbox on the left-hand side of the screen.
Click the “Image” property’s marker in the Actions category of Properties panel and select an image to upload.
Now using the “Sizing” property, specify the position of the uploaded image in the Picture Box.

By moving and placing labels and data fields in desired locations, the user can perfectly align them in the report easily.

This category belongs to the Properties panel of Report Editor.

By selecting one of the options given, the user can specify the orientation of the report page. Also, there is available an option to reset the selection.
Page Width and Page Height
In these fields, the user can set the width and height of a report page respectively. It will appear clickable only when the option selected in the Paper Kind field is “Custom”. Options to reset entered values are also present here.
Cut/Copy/Paste
These are commonly used tools available in the Main Toolbar section.
Cut – This tool cuts the selected control to the clipboard.
Copy – This will copy the selected control to the clipboard.
Paste – Pastes a control from the clipboard onto the selected report band.

Preview a Report – By clicking the preview button on the main toolbar, the user can view the preview of a report before printing the same.
Print a Report – In Preview mode, the user can print out the report using the appropriate tools.
Return to Editor – When the Designer tool on the top of the Preview page is clicked, the user can go back to the report editor page.
Undo/Redo
By clicking the Undo arrow on the main toolbar, the user can cancel the last change made in the report whereas they can reverse the last change by clicking the Redo arrow.
Zoom
The user can Zoom In a document by clicking the plus icon (+) on the main toolbar whereas they can Zoom Out it by clicking the minus icon (-). If needed, an option to choose a specific zoom level from the Zoom Factor dropdown is also present here.

chunks.title: Reporting | Reports | Report Editor
chunks.content:
Save – The user can update the report template currently being edited by clicking the “Save” option available in the Menu on the top left-hand side of the screen. The Save button will only be available when editing a TPA customized template. Summit default templates may not be modified and updated by TPA users.
Save As – By clicking “Save As”, a pop-up will appear as shown below with an option to rename the report. This will create a modified version of the report being edited.  The user may use Save As on Summit default report templates and on TPA customized templates.
Sorting a Report’s data
The user can sort the data on the report using the following steps:
From the Properties panel on the right-hand side of the screen, select the “Detail Band”.
Expand the Sort Fields section under the Actions category and select the required data field from the “Sort By” dropdown list.
Click the up-arrow to sort in ascending order and the down-arrow for descending order.
For multiple sort fields, click Add icon, so that a new sort field can be added to the “Then By” field.
Subreports
Subreport control is used to embed detail reports into the master report. It is possible to have multiple detail reports attached to the same master report.
Master Report – This is the main report where all the detail reports are embedded. The user can create or open an existing report to use it as a master report. By binding the report to a data table and dragging the required data fields from the Field List, a master report can be created.

chunks.title: Reporting | Reports | Report Editor
chunks.content:
Detail Report – Detail report is a report with hierarchically linked data. The user can create a blank report to use it as a detail report. After creating the report, bind it to the same master report data source or to a different data source containing the required information. Then drag the necessary data fields from the Field List into the detail report. To filter a detail report, there should be a common filter criterion (column) for both master and detail reports. By adding parameters, filter criteria can be given.
Embedding the Subreport
Open a master report and create its detail report templates separately.
From the toolbox, drag the Subreport control and place it into the desired location of the master report.
Once the creation of detail report templates is complete, it will bind to the Report Source URL dropdown of Actions category. Choose the required detail report for the selected Subreport control.
Data Filtering
There should be a common filter criterion for both master and detail reports to filter the data. By adding parameters, the user can define these criteria.
To add a parameter, click the Add parameter button in the Field List of detail report.
Then click on the edit button of the created parameter and specify the Name and Type of the parameter.
Save the detail report.
To bind the created parameter, select the inserted subreport control in the master report and open the Data category of the Properties panel. Now the Parameter Bindings section will appear.
Expand the section and choose the parameter name and binding from the given dropdown menus.
After saving the master report, go back to the detail report and click on the ellipsis button of the Filter String property.

In the invoked Filter Editor, construct an expression where the required data field is compared to the created parameter. To access the parameter, invoke the dropdown list on the right-hand side and select the option “Parameter”. It will display a list of created parameters. Choose the required one.

chunks.title: Reports | Nondiscrimination Testing
chunks.content:
Reports | Nondiscrimination Testing
Nondiscrimination Testing is a value-added feature that enables TPAs and Employers to verify whether their benefit plans comply with discrimination policies. Plans falling under various sections of the IRS tax code must meet Nondiscrimination mandates. These policies generally ensure that a plan does not favor highly compensated and key employees over other employees.
Table of Contents
Nondiscrimination Testing Parameters
Select Test and Criteria
Section 125 Key Employee 25% Concentration Test
Section 129 More than 5% Owner 25% Concentration Test
Section 129 Dependent Care 55% Average Benefits Test
Choose Data Source
Summit Participant and Plan Data
Summit Data plus Uploaded POP Amounts
Update Compensation Limits
To access Nondiscrimination Testing,
Go to Reporting.
Select Nondiscrimination Testing.
The Nondiscrimination Testing page displays several parameters. The Nondiscrimination test module of Summit guides users through a series of steps to process Nondiscrimination testing for certain Section 125 and Section 129 benefit plans.
Nondiscrimination Testing Parameters
Select Test and Criteria
In this section, the system displays three available tests as checkbox options, all initially deselected:
Section 125 Key Employee 25% Concentration Test
Section 129 More than 5% Owner 25% Concentration Test
Section 129 Dependent Care 55% Average Benefits Test
Section 125 Key Employee 25% Concentration Test
When this checkbox option is selected, the section expands to display two radio button options:
Key Employees are identified using the Key Employee field – This option is selected by default. 
Calculate my Key Employees based on the participant demographics – If the user selects this option, the Officer prior year compensation field will be enabled. If a user edits this field, the value will be saved for that particular user. Otherwise, the default initial value will be used. The initial value of the Officer prior year compensation is $170,000.

chunks.title: Reports | Nondiscrimination Testing
chunks.content:
Section 129 More than 5% Owner 25% Concentration Test
When this checkbox is selected, the section expands to display the Excluded Employees options. There are three checkbox options under the Excluded Employees label, all deselected by default:
Employees under collective bargaining not participating in a 129 plan
Less than 1 year of service
Under age 21
Section 129 Dependent Care 55% Average Benefits Test
When this checkbox is selected, the section expands to display two radio buttons and the Excluded Employee options:
HCEs are identified by Highly Compensated Employee field – This option is checked by default.
Calculate HCEs using the participant demographic data – If the user selects this radio button option, the HCE prior year compensation field and And in the top 20% highest paid employees checkbox options will be enabled. If a user edits this field, the value will be saved for that particular user. Otherwise, the default initial value will be used. The initial value of the HCE prior year compensation is $120,000.
Excluded Employees: This section contains four checkbox options:
Compensation less than $25,000
Employees under collective bargaining not participating in a 129 plan
Less than 1 year of service
Under age 21.
Choose Data Source
The Choose Data Source section of the Nondiscrimination Testing page allows users to select or import test data and validate that all required information is available. Users can choose to test data stored within Summit, Summit data plus uploaded Premium Only Plan (POP) amounts, or upload a properly formatted file containing all necessary data for the selected tests.
The three options available in this section include:
Summit Participant and Plan Data
Summit Data plus Uploaded POP Amounts
Uploaded Data File
Summit Participant and Plan Data
If the user selects this option, the following options will display:

The file layouts are identical; however, the template downloaded when Summit Plus Upload is selected includes an Instruction tab, which provides definitions for each field and indicates whether the field is required.
The data should be grouped by the employer and sorted alphabetically by employer name, participant last name, and participant first name in the system-created data file.
The Upload button will prompt the user to select the completed file for upload, validation, and processing.

chunks.title: Screen Customization | Dashboard
chunks.content:
Screen Customization | Dashboard
For Summit employer users, an employer dashboard is an alternative landing page to a traditional home page. On this page, a user can customize the employer dashboard screen by configuring its widget background color and adding/removing individual widgets. The system will automatically adjust the placement of widgets when they are added or removed.
If the employer dashboard feature is enabled for the TPA via the Feature Access page, the TPA can choose to enable the dashboard and set it as the landing page for users of selected (or all) employers via the Summit Customization Screen.
Table of Contents
Screen Customization Page
Employer Dashboard
 * Required fields appear in Red
To access Dashboard Screen Customization,
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Screen Customization.
Select the Dashboard menu.
Screen Customization Page
By selecting the Dashboard menu, the screen customization page will display as follows. Here, the user can customize the employer dashboard at both the TPA level and the Employer level. The settings configured at the TPA level will be automatically applied to all existing and new employers added to the system under that particular TPA.
Employer – This is a dropdown list that will auto-populate with all the employers present under the TPA. For a TPA level configuration, no Employer selection is required.
If the user wants to customize the dashboard for a specific Employer at the Employer level, select an Employer from this dropdown list and uncheck the checkbox that links the Employer to Administrator Defaults. By deselecting this checkbox, the user can customize an employer dashboard for the selected Employer. As long as this box remains checked, changes updated at the TPA level will be reflected at the Employer level.
To reassign the Employer to Administrator Defaults, reselect this checkbox.

chunks.title: Screen Customization | Dashboard
chunks.content:
Enable – TThis is a checkbox option to enable the employer dashboard. The user can check this box only if the TPA has access to the dashboard via the Feature Access page. If the TPA does not have Feature Access to the dashboard, this box will remain unchecked and grayed out. By default, this is an unchecked box.
At the Employer level, this checkbox will remain grayed out.
Background Color – This is a color picker field where the user can choose a background color for widgets. The selected color can be previewed in the preview box positioned here.
An information icon shows where this background color will be reflected on the dashboard.
Add Widget – As the name indicates, this is a dropdown list to select and add additional widgets to the dashboard.
The available widgets in the dropdown list are:
Current Orders
Past Orders
Upload a File
Recently Viewed
Approved Events
When the dashboard is enabled by the TPA, it will have Participant Search, Plan Details, Banking Information, Documents, and Pending Approvals widgets by default. However, any actual content will not be included in them.
Each widget shown on the customization screen will include an “X” icon. When this icon is clicked, the system will remove the selected widget from the screen and re-organize the remaining widgets. Each widget will be shifted up and to the left of the page.
Similarly, when the user selects a widget from the dropdown list, the screen will update and add the selected widget to the lower right of the existing widgets on the page.
After completing all these customizations, click “Save” to configure or update the employer dashboard.
Employer Dashboard
An employer user can view the configured employer dashboard if the TPA has access to the dashboard via the Feature Access page, enabled the dashboard in the Dashboard Screen Customization page, and set it as the landing page for the selected employer via the Summit Customization screen.

The Mobile Screen Customization page allows the TPA user to customize the look of the Summit mobile application. TPAs can upload logos and customize the colors of certain texts and areas of the screen.

Mobile Screen Customization
By clicking on the Mobile option, the following customization page will display:
Assign to Administrator Default – When this checkbox is selected, it indicates that the employer is assigned to the TPA default settings, and changes to the Mobile Screen Customizations at the TPA level will apply to this employer. To customize settings for a particular employer, the user must first deselect this checkbox. This option is checked by default for new employers.
When this box is deselected, a warning popup will appear. Press the Continue button to proceed.
Once the employer has been delinked from the TPA default settings, the employer-specific screen customization settings may be applied on this page.

Android
iPhone

chunks.title: Screen Customization | Mobile
chunks.content:
Page Header Logo – By pressing the Change Photo button, the user can upload the Page Header Logo for the Summit mobile application. chunks.title: Screen Customization | Participant Portal
chunks.content:

All design elements are listed on the page with a sample of their associated color. Next to each element/color is a color palette icon that the user can select to produce a color palette. The user can select a standard color from the palette or input the RGB values directly for the desired color.
The design elements included in this section are:
Top Navigation Bar – This navigation bar currently represents the “Support”, “Documents”, and “Logout” buttons. The user can update the color of the bar (collection of those buttons).

Main Navigation Bar Highlight – When a user hovers over or clicks an option on the main navigation bar, that option is highlighted in a distinct color (by default, a lighter shade of blue). The user can customize the color of this highlight.
Page Background – This represents the top portion of the page (where the top navigation bar and images sit) as well as the side borders of the page. The user can customize the color of the background.
Header & Sub-Header text – This text indicates to the user which page of the system they are currently on. The user can update the color of this text. Updating this text will have no impact on the text in the body of the page, which is a static color.

chunks.title: Screen Customization | Participant Portal
chunks.content:

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Employer Invoicing
chunks.content:
Administrator Settings | Employer Invoicing
A TPA’s revenue comes from being able to charge their employer clients a series of fees for administering their group benefits. They typically charge their clients a flat fee for every active participant in the system plus some additional ancillary fees. Summit’s invoicing module allows for TPAs to configure these fees within Summit, using the settings and data within Summit to create invoicing for employer groups.
Table of Contents
Employer Invoice Set Up
To access Employer Invoicing CDH:
Go to Settings.
Mouse-over Administrator Settings.
Click on the Employer Invoicing menu.
Figure 1. Administrator Settings – Employer Invoicing
The Employer Invoicing page will display (Fig. 2).
Figure 2. Employer Invoicing Page
Employer Invoice Set Up
You can set up invoicing settings per employer or as TPA-default settings. To set up invoice settings for a specific employer:
Select an Employer using the drop-down menu. An “Assigned to Administrator Default” checkbox will appear.
NOTE: If no employer is selected from the drop-down, invoice settings configured on this page will be used as the TPA-default settings.
2. Select the Assigned to Administrator Default checkbox to use the TPA default settings to generate the employer’s invoicing.
3. Create custom invoicing for the employer group by unselecting the box. When unselected, the settings configured on this page will be applied to this employer only.
Figure 3. Employer Invoice Settings
4. To enable Summit invoicing for the employer, select the Enable checkbox. If you will be handling your employer invoicing outside of Summit, unselect the Enable checkbox.
NOTE: If invoicing for only a particular employer is being handled outside of Summit, select that employer from the Employer drop-down. Make sure that Assign to Administrator Default is unselected and then unselect Enable. This will disable Summit invoicing for the selected employer.

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Employer Invoicing
chunks.content:
