chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
Summit allows participants to enroll in benefit plans online via the Participant Portal.  The online enrollment process is determined by the settings configured on the Administrator Settings Online Enrollment page. TPAs may configure their Online Enrollment settings globally or assign specific settings to individual employers that are not assigned to the TPA default.
The purpose of this document is to outline and define the Online Enrollment Settings and explain their impact on participants’ online enrollment process.
Table of Contents
Online Enrollment Tab
Online Enrollment
Communications
Enrollment Options
Associated Employers
Associated Plan Types
Associated CDH Benefits
Associated PB Benefits
Plan Coordination Rules
Exclusive Plan Rules
Inclusive Plan Rules
Benefits Resource Page [Enrollment Resources]
Election Changes Tab
Communication Settings
Election Change Approval Notice
Communication Methods
Election Change Rejection Notice
Communication Methods
Alerts of Pending Process Approvals
 * Required fields appear in Red
Online Enrollment Tab
Online Enrollment Settings can be applied at the TPA level as the TPA default or to individual employers. The online enrollment screen includes an employer selector that allows users to choose an employer for configuring online enrollment settings. To configure the TPA default Online Enrollment settings, leave the Employer selection on this dropdown as “–Select Employer–.” The TPA level settings are applied to all employers associated with the TPA default. Select a specific employer to apply specific enrollment criteria to that employer.
Online Enrollment
Online Enrollment LOS – The Online Enrollment LOS option is divided into CDH and Premium Billing. This allows TPAs to control Open Enrollment based on whether the functionality is enabled for CDH plans, Premium Billing plans, or both.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
When an employer is selected, the LOS enabled for that employer will be displayed. “CDH” and “Premium Billing” will be displayed when there is no employer is selected.
When the Premium Billing checkbox is checked, PB participants can enroll in the associated benefits during the open enrollment period from the Participant Portal. Note that Premium Billing online open enrollment is limited to non-FSA COBRA coverages.
Communications Only – While employers may be enrolling participants via paper forms, TPAs can still take advantage of Summit’s online enrollment suite of communications to inform participants of important enrollment dates and system details. When this option is selected, only features under the Communication Settings will be enabled.
Email Settings
Image Settings
CDH Open Enrollment Notice
PB Open Enrollment Reminder
CDH Open Enrollment Reminder
PB Rejected Enrollment Notice
CDH Rejected Enrollment Notice
Open Ended Plan Notice
Alerts of Pending Process Approvals
All Features – When this option is selected, the communications described above and all features under the Enrollment Options section will be enabled.
Customize Welcome Text – Displays on the first page of Online Enrollment.
Waiver Text – Displays on Step 4. Review Information, if there are benefits not elected by the participant.
Confirmation Text – Displays confirmation details.
CDH and PB Email Confirmation of Enrollment – Sends email confirmations for CDH and Premium Billing enrollments.
Enforce Plan Eligibility Restrictions – Ensures that plan eligibility restrictions are applied.
Participant Type –The Participant Type dropdown allows the user to define who may access online enrollment and who will receive communications.
Known Participants – Participants already existing in Summit.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Known Participants and Unregistered Enrollees – This setting extends open enrollment access to both known participants in Summit and those not yet registered but who have the required Employer Code. Only known participants will receive system enrollment communications.
Census Import – Only individuals imported via the online enrollment census import will have access to online enrollment. This option is available only for selected employers and is not applicable if the Admin Default setting is used. Note that even existing participants in Summit must be included in the census to access online enrollment features and communications.
Require an enrollment code of – When checked, the enrollment code becomes a required field. This code will be available as a merge field that can be included in online enrollment communications. The enrollment code can be set as a TPA default or for individual employers not associated with the default.
Require approval of online enrollments for –This option sends all online enrollments to the Online Enrollment Process Approvals queue for approval before the elections are accepted for administration. Online enrollments can be rejected during this process. The dropdown includes options for CDH, Premium Billing, and CDH + Premium Billing:
CDH: CDH enrollment selections require approval.
Premium Billing: Premium Billing enrollment selections require approval.
CDH + Premium Billing: Both CDH and Premium Billing enrollment selections require approval.
Communications
Set from address as – This field specifies the “from” email address for all online enrollment emails sent from Summit for the TPA or selected employer. It ensures that emails are sent from a recognizable address, and replies will be directed to this address. This is a required field.
Auto-forward a copy of all communications to – When checked, Summit will forward copies of all online enrollment emails to the email address entered in the “forward to” textbox.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Image Settings – Image settings allow TPAs to brand their enrollment communications. Users can upload an image to be displayed in online enrollment communications. Click the Pencil icon to open the dialog box and select the image you wish to use. Acceptable formats are GIF, JPG, or PNG. The Left, Center, and Right Image Location radio buttons indicate the position of the image on the communication. To delete the uploaded image, click the delete icon.
Communications Table – This table includes CDH and PB enrollment notices with their communication options as described below.
Enable – This checkbox will be displayed for each listed notice.
Communication – Displays CDH and PB communications, including:
CDH Open Enrollment Notice
PB Open Enrollment Reminder
CDH Open Enrollment Reminder
PB Rejected Enrollment Notice
CDH Rejected Enrollment Notice
Open Ended Plan Notice
Send Days Before Enrollment Starts/Ends – Contains a Starts/Ends field for CDH Open Enrollment Notice, PB Open Enrollment Reminder, and CDH Open Enrollment Reminder.
Email – This checkbox will be displayed for each enabled notice. When checked, the communication will be sent by email if an email address is available.
Mailed Letter – This checkbox option will be displayed for each enabled notice. When checked, the communication will be sent by letter if a participant mailing address is available. If the Mailed Letter option is selected, the DataPath Fulfillment checkbox will be displayed for the notice.
DataPath Fulfillment – The DataPath Fulfillment checkbox will be displayed for each enabled notice that is also enabled for Mailed Letter. This will flag the notices to be generated and mailed via DataPath’s fulfillment service. When checked, the DataPath Fulfillment popup agreement will display, and the user must elect to turn on the DataPath Fulfillment feature.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Send Letter If No Email Address – This checkbox will be displayed for each enabled notice. When checked, Summit will generate the notice as a letter if no email address is on record for the participant.
Portal Mobile – The Portal Mobile checkbox will be displayed for each enabled notice. When checked, the communication will display for the participant on the Participant Portal.
Push As Alert – The Push As Alert checkbox will be displayed for each enabled notice. When checked, the participant will be notified of the communication in an alert when they next log in to the Portal.
Format – Users can view the Email, Letter, and Portal formats of enabled communications by selecting the links in the Format column.
Note: There is a setting in Settings | Administrator Settings | Participant Portal Settings | General Settings | Account Registration that allows the selection of which Employer ID should be used during registration. The options are Employer System ID or Employer Custom ID. The selection affects all registration regardless of where the notice is initiated, (eg. Welcome Notice or open enrollment notice, or registration notice from an import census.)
Due to the behavior of certain plans (e.g., HSAs are evergreen and Open Ended, even though a participant’s HDHP is an annual benefit), whether or not a participant receives an open enrollment communication may vary. For instance, if the benefit is Open Ended and has no annual component with open enrollment, the participant would receive no communications.
The table below illustrates the logic dictating how and which participants should receive communications when those communication types are enabled and which Participant Type has been selected.
Participant Type Plan Other Required Settings Who should get a communication
    Annual with Open Enrollment Period Open Ended Participant Communications | Welcome Notice| Include Participants Enrolled Online

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Known Yes Yes   All active participants in the Summit system should receive the Open Enrollment Notice only
Known Yes No   All active participants in the Summit system should receive the Open Enrollment Notice only
Known No Yes   No communications should be sent
Known No No   No communications should be sent
All Yes Yes   All active participants in the Summit system should receive the Open Enrollment Notice only
All Yes No   All active participants in the Summit system should receive the Open Enrollment Notice only
All No Yes   No communications should be sent
All No No   No communications should be sent
Census Import Yes Yes Yes Individuals in the Online Enrollment Import Census file should receive both Open Enrollment and Open Ended Plan Notices
Census Import Yes Yes No Individuals in the Online Enrollment Import Census file should receive the Open Enrollment Notice but not the Open Ended Plan Notice
Census Import Yes No Yes Individuals in the Online Enrollment Import Census file should receive the Open Enrollment Notice only
Census Import Yes No No Individuals in the Online Enrollment Import Census file should receive the Open Enrollment Notice only
Census Import No Yes Yes Individuals in the Online Enrollment Import Census file should receive the Open Ended Plan Notice only
Census Import No Yes No No communications should be sent
Census Import No No Yes No communications should be sent
Alerts of Pending Process Approvals – Users assigned here will receive email notifications of Online Enrollments that require process approval.
Send to all TPA Users with Role Access – Sends emails to all TPA users with Process Approvals access.
Send to all Employer Users with Role Access – Sends emails to all employer users with Process Approvals access.
Assign Additional TPA Users – Additional addresses may be added in the “Assign Additional TPA Users” field.
Enrollment Options

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
The Enrollment Options section allows TPAs to customize the text that appears within the Online Enrollment module on the Participant Portal. DataPath provides default text for each field, but TPAs can modify these texts as needed.
The Enrollment Options include:
Welcome Text – The Welcome Text appears to Participant users on the Participant Portal when logging in for online enrollment. The default text can be unlocked and customized by checking the Customize Welcome Text checkbox.
Require Waiver of Non-Elected Benefits –This text and the required waiver acknowledgment appear on the Review Information step of the Online Enrollment Process when this checkbox is enabled. The default text of this field will be unlocked for editing when the checkbox is selected. If this option is enabled, the participant must check a checkbox to waive unselected benefits.
Confirmation Text – This text will display on the Enrollment Complete step of the online enrollment process when this checkbox is enabled. The default text of this field will be unlocked for editing when the checkbox is selected.
The CDH Confirmation of Enrollment Email and PB Confirmation of Enrollment Email checkboxes enable communications specific to CDH and PB participants, respectively. The content and format of these communications can be customized by clicking the Email Format link.
Enforce Plan Eligibility Restrictions – When this checkbox is checked, enrollment in a plan will be restricted if the participant does not match the plan’s eligibility selections. These eligibility fields are set at the TPA Default Plans level and/or the Eligibility modal of the Employer level Plan screen.
The following eligibility selections are taken into consideration:
Allow Dependent Enrollment + Maximum Dependent Age – Allows dependent enrollment up to the maximum age.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Require Agreement – A Dependent Disclaimer that must be acknowledged will display on the Dependent step of Online enrollment. The language is hardcoded to: “You are required to provide documentation of eligibility for new dependents whether added during the Open Enrollment process or due to a Qualifying Life Event and whether enrolled online or manually. Failure to do so may cancel dependent’s coverage. Setting dependent to inactive suspends dependent claim processing and enrollment in benefit plans. For more information about Qualifying Life Events, visit http://changeofstatus.com/.”
Allow Participant to enroll dependent – This option at the Plan level allows participants to enroll dependents via the Participant Portal for plans that permit dependent enrollment. 
Allow Key Employees – A Yes or No option that corresponds with the identification of whether the participant is a key employee. If Key Employees are disallowed, a participant flagged as a Key Employee will not be permitted to enroll in the benefit.
Associated Employers
The Associated Employers section will be displayed when no employer is selected.  PB employers will be included in the All Employers list when PB-only or CDH + PB is selected for the online enrollment LOS.  The CDH employers that were previously selected will be selected by default.
Associated Plan Types
The Associated Plan Types section will be displayed when no employer is selected. When CDH and PB LOS are selected, the All Plan Types list will contain CDH and PB plan types. When only CDH or PB is selected, the respective LOS plan types will be displayed in the list. The CDH plan types that were previously selected for TPA will be selected by default.
Associated CDH Benefits
An Associated CDH Benefits section will be displayed when a CDH-only or CDH + PB employer is selected, and the CDH LOS is selected. The CDH plans that were previously selected for an employer will be selected by default.
Associated PB Benefits

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
An Associated Premium Billing Plans section will contain a list of all Premium Billing plans that may be associated with the online enrollment defaults when the employer is PB-only, CDH + PB, and when the Premium Billing LOS is selected. Note that this list will only contain non-FSA COBRA coverages, even if those coverages are available for CDH Online Open Enrollment.
Plan Coordination Rules
While Plan Coordination Rules are not configured on the Online Enrollment screen, they are considered when determining which benefits a participant may enroll in via Online Enrollment.
Federal regulations prohibit concurrent enrollment in certain plans, such as HSA and full-purpose FSA, or full-purpose FSA and limited-purpose FSA.
Additionally, some employer plan designs require that enrollment in one plan automatically enrolls the participant in one or more other specified plans. For example, a participant enrolled in HRA1 will also always be enrolled in HRA2.
Plans can be structured to be either exclusive (enrollment in plan 1 or plan 2, but not both) or inclusive (enrollment in plan 1 automatically enrolls the participant in plan 3).
Furthermore, some employers design plans such that grouped plans share annual or monthly contribution or spending limits.
In general, these characteristics may be referred to as Plan Coordination.
Plan Coordination Rules are established at the Employer level through Employer Central | Benefit Plans and the Plan Details UI.
A grid will display containing the Rule Name for any added rule along with edit and delete icons. New rules may be added by clicking the +Add Rule link.
The +Add Rule link will open an Add Plan Coordination Rule modal. Rules may have a name up to 30 alphanumeric (and printable special) characters in length.
Below the Name field is an Enrollment option radio button which allows the user to determine whether the rule is Exclusive or Inclusive.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Beneath the Enrollment selection, a grid of all the employer’s CDH and CDH/PB plans will display with Name, Type, and Plan Year/Effective Date. The user may check these plans to be affected by the rule.
The plan list may be filtered to include Inactive/Terminated Plans. Plans that are inactive and terminated as of the current system date will display when this filter option is selected.
Exclusive Plan Rules
Plans may be restricted to prevent enrollment of a participant into more than one plan with the same rule. Summit will evaluate the participant’s currently elected plans when determining how each enrollment-enabled plan should display on the Choose Your Benefits Page.
Plans excluded from a participant due to the Plan Coordination Rules will be unavailable for selection by the participant on the Choose Your Benefits page.
Inclusive Plan Rules
When plans are associated via an Inclusive Enrollment rule, a participant electing and enrolling in any one of the associated plans will automatically enroll them in all other plans associated with the rule. When the Enrollment selection is set to Inclusive, the plans assigned to the rule will be bundled for online enrollment purposes.
Benefits Resource Page [Enrollment Resources]
DataPath has produced a set of videos to assist participants during Online Enrollment. These videos include general participant-focused content, such as the Captain Contributor series, which explains various types of benefits and how they work, as well as other benefit overview presentations.
These videos are hosted on Summit and can be enabled for viewing on the Participant Portal. TPAs can configure which videos will display for participants via the Benefit Resource Center Settings tab located under Administrator Settings | Participant Portal Settings.
The videos will be listed on a sortable grid with three columns: Title, Description, and Topics Covered.
The title of each video is a hyperlink that opens the video in a viewer.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Each video will have DataPath-assigned tags (e.g., “FSA”, “HSA”, “DCAP”) that determine which videos are accessed from the Learn More link on the Participant Online Enrollment pages.
The Benefit Resource Center Settings page can also be accessed from the Online Enrollment Settings page located via Settings | Administrator Settings | Online Enrollment.
When a TPA selects videos from the Benefit Resource Center to display on the Participant Portal, a Learn More link(s) will appear on the Online Enrollment Choose Your Benefits page. The link will appear under each benefit listed for which there is a video selected with a tag that matches the benefit’s plan type.
For example, if the TPA has selected videos tagged for FSA, DCA, and HRA but not Transit or Parking, and FSA, DCA, HRA, Transit, and Parking benefits are available for online enrollment, the links will ONLY display under the FSA, DCA, and HRA plans.
Clicking the Learn More link will take the participant to a new Benefit Resource Center page where they can view the available videos or, if there is only one video available for that benefit type, be taken directly to the video viewer.
Election Changes Tab
While many benefit elections are tied to annual elections and cannot be changed during the plan year, participants are allowed to make election changes to certain benefits that are not tied to plan years, such as Parking and Transit benefits, and individually owned accounts like HSAs.
The Online Enrollment settings on the Election Changes tab allow TPAs to enable participants to submit changes to these elections through the Participant Portal, rather than requiring them to manually contact their administrators for mid-year adjustments to elections and contributions.
Additionally, TPAs can dictate whether changes to elections may be automatically processed or require administrator approval.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
If the Employer selector is set to Select Employer, all settings on this tab will be applied globally to all employers linked to the TPA default.
To make changes to these settings for a specific employer, select an employer from the Employer dropdown selector. Note that the Assign to Administrator Defaults setting for the Election Changes tab is independent from the Assign to Administrator Defaults setting for the Online Enrollment tab.
Enable Election Changes – When this checkbox is selected, participants may make online election changes to their benefits of the type(s) selected from the Benefit Plan Types dropdown selector.
Benefit Plan Types – Participants can make online changes to the elections of the selected benefit type(s) when the Enable Election Changes checkbox is checked. Due to IRS regulations governing annual elections for certain benefits and plan types, only Transit and Parking Plans and HSAs may be selected to allow for mid-year changes to elections.
Frequency – Currently, the only available frequency is Monthly, meaning participants may only make changes to their election once a month if the Enable Election Changes checkbox is checked.
Cut-Off Day – The Cut-Off Day determines when the election change must be completed to be effective the following month. If the election change occurs after the cut-off day, the change will be effective at the beginning of the second month after the election change is made.
For example: If the Cut-Off Day is set to 25 and the participant enters an election change on September 15, the new election will be effective on October 1, the first day of the following month. However, if the participant makes the change on September 26, the new election will be effective on November 1.
Require Approval of Election Changes – If the Require Approval of Election Changes checkbox is enabled, changes submitted by participants through the Participant Portal will require administrator approval.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Election Change requests will appear in Processing | Process Approvals with the “Election Change” Process Type.
If the approval is made after the first pay period following the effective date, the system will post a catch-up contribution as it would if the election change were made manually by the TPA.
Communication Settings
The Communication Settings section allows TPAs to configure the communications sent to participants making election changes via the Participant Portal.
Set from address as – Communications generated by Summit will use the value set in this field as the “From” address. This is a required field and must be designated by DataPath personnel. Please contact DataPath support to have this value entered or changed.
Auto-Forward a copy of all communications to – This setting allows you to designate additional email addresses to forward copies of communications sent to participants. When this checkbox is selected, the user must enter an email address in the “Forward to” field.
Image Settings – This allows users to upload an image or logo that will be included in the communication and designate the image’s alignment.
Election Change Approval Notice
You can enable a communication to be sent to participants when an Election Change is processed for approval by checking the Enabled checkbox in this section.
Communication Methods
When enabled, the Election Change Approval Notice can be sent by any combination of Letter, Email, or Portal/Mobile notification by checking the respective checkbox in the Communications Method subsection.
Additionally, if the communication is enabled for Portal/Mobile, you have the option to push the communication as an alert that will pop up when the user next logs in by checking the Push as Alert checkbox, which is enabled when the Portal/Mobile option is checked.
As with all communications in Summit, the format can be customized distinctly for each method by clicking the respective Format link.

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
The default text of the communication is as follows:
Dear ##PARTICIPANT_NAME,

Your election change submitted ##ELECTION_CHANGE_SUBMITTED_DATE to ##BENEFIT_PLAN_NAME has been approved.
Thank you,

##REVIEWER_SOURCE_NAME
Send letter if there is no email address on file – By checking this box, the system will default the communication method to letter when the participant’s email address is not present.
Election Change Rejection Notice
You can enable a communication to be sent to participants when an Election Change is rejected in Process Approvals by checking the Enabled checkbox in this section.
Communication Methods
When enabled, the Election Change Rejection Notice can be sent by any combination of Letter, Email, or Portal/Mobile notification by checking the respective checkbox in the Communications Method subsection.
Additionally, if the communication is enabled for Portal/Mobile, you have the option to push the communication as an alert that will pop up when the user next logs in by checking the Push as Alert checkbox, which is enabled when the Portal/Mobile option is checked.
As with all communications in Summit, the format can be customized distinctly for each method by clicking the respective Format link.
The default text of the communication is as follows:
Dear ##PARTICIPANT_NAME,

Your election changes submitted ##ELECTION_CHANGE_SUBMITTED_DATE to ##BENEFIT_PLAN_NAME has been rejected.
The reason for rejection is ##ELECTION_CHANGE_REJECT_REASON. If you have questions please contact ##REVIEWER_SOURCE_NAME at ##REVIEWER_SOURCE_PHONENUMBER or ##REVIEWER_SOURCE_EMAIL.
Thank you,

##REVIEWER_SOURCE_NAME
Send letter if there is no email address on file – By checking this box, the system will default the communication method to letter when the participant’s email address is not present.
Alerts of Pending Process Approvals

chunks.title: Summit Online Enrollment Configuration
chunks.content:
Send to all Employer users with Role access – When this option is enabled, pending process approvals alerts will be sent to all employer users with process approvals role access.
For further information, please refer to the FAQs.

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Users
chunks.content:
Administrator Settings | Users
Table of Contents
Creating a User
Editing a User
Searching for Users
User Search Results
  * Required fields appear in Red
As a multi-layered platform offering a wide range of services and views for multiple stakeholders and entities, Summit can accommodate many different users with different roles and levels of access.
The Users modal allows TPAs to create and modify Summit user accounts and assign roles to those users, including TPA Administrator users, Agency/Broker users, Employer (HR) users, and Participant Users.
Creating a User
Go to Settings >> Administrator Settings >> Users.
Select the tab for the user type you want to create, Administrators, Brokers, Employers, and/or Participants.
NOTE: If creating a Broker or an Employer user, you will need to select the appropriate entity from the “Select Agency” [Broker] or “Select Employer” [Employer] dropdown before proceeding.
Select Agency
Select Employer
Press the green Add User button.
The Create User modal will appear.
Enter the user information. The following fields are required:
First
Last
User ID
Email
NOTE: The User ID must be unique and 8-25 characters in length. This ID cannot be modified once the user profile is saved.
The following are optional security features for first-time login:
If “Require user to contact you directly for Access” is selected, a user Password field and an Admin Phone field will appear as required fields.
If “Require initial security question” is selected, “Enter Question” and “Enter Answer” fields will appear as required fields to contain a login challenge question.
Assign a role to the user from the Role dropdown.
An optional user profile photo may be uploaded and attached to the profile.
Click the edit icon under the photo box.

Browse for a profile picture and click Open.
Press the Save button.
Summit will send two emails once the user profile has been saved. One will contain the username and the second will contain a temporary password.
Editing a User

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Users
chunks.content:
Go to Settings >> Administrator Settings >> Users.
Select the tab for the user type you want to edit, either Administrators, Brokers, Employers or Participants.
If you are editing a Broker, an Employer, or a Participant User, select the appropriate entity from the “Select Agency” [Broker] or “Select Employer” [Employer or Participant] dropdown before proceeding.
Select Agency
Select Employer
Use the Search User box and desired filters or click the “Show All” or the “Show Currently Logged In” link.

User names will display in the grid.
To update the status of one or multiple users, select the checkbox next to the user name, and click the “Active”, “Inactive”, or “Locked” button to update all the selected users.
To make detailed changes to an individual user’s profile, click the name of the user you wish to edit.
You may make changes to the user’s profile info and/or change the User Account Status.
Allows you to manually reset/unlock a user’s account that has become locked.
Allows you to deactivate or reactivate a user’s account.
Press the Save button when done.
Searching for Users
Each tab of the Administrator Settings | Users page includes a search section that will allow users to search for, view, and edit Summit users.
Each tab allows you to search for users of a particular type [Administrators, Brokers, Employers, Participants]. Many of the search filters and features are standard across each tab, however, there are certain filters that are specific to a tab and user type.
Administrators
A TPA selector dropdown will be present if the user is part of a master TPA with access to associated TPAs. This selector will determine which TPA-level set of user data will be searched. This is included on each tab.
The Brokers tab contains a Select Agency dropdown which will contain a list of all brokers associated with your TPA. The User Search list results will be filtered by the selected agency.

chunks.title: Administrator Settings | Users
chunks.content:
Both the Employer tab and the Participant tab contain a Select Employer dropdown. On the Employer tab, this filters the results to Employer-level users associated with the selected Employer. On the Participant tab, this filters the results to participant users that are associated with the selected employer.
Employer Tab
Participant Tab
The Search User bar is a dropdown that allows text entry. If the Contains checkbox is selected, Summit will return any results containing the string entered in the search bar.
Clicking on the Search User bar will cause a list of available users to dropdown for selection.
The Participants tab has a series of radio buttons that changes the categories of information you can look for in the Search User bar.
Participant Name – Search User will search for participant users by the Participant Name.
SSN – Search User will search for participant users by Social Security Number
DataPathID – Search User will search for participant users by the unique Summit ID assigned by DataPath.
TpaID – Search User will search for participant users by the TPA ID assigned to the participant.
You can press the Show All button, and all Active users will display.
NOTE: For Brokers, the Show All selection will show all users within the selected agency. For employers, Show All will show all users within the selected employer. For participants, Show All will show all participant users for the selected employer or all participants for your TPA if no employer is selected in the –Select Employer– filter.
If search results are displaying, the Show All button will display as a link above the results.
The Employer tab’s search tools have a special “Assigned Admin Users” link that will display a popup of all Administrator-level and Broker-level users that have access to the selected employer.
User Search Results

“What’s New” Guide – 2025-11
Table of Contents
Enhancements
FTP Details – Exports to Use SFTP Irrespective of Port Number

Enhancements
FTP Details – Exports to Use SFTP Irrespective of Port Number
We have made changes to how Summit handles its SFTP settings.
Previously, the system would only use SFTP when Port 22 was designated in the FTP Details for exports. This could create issues for TPAs that require a different Port number AND SFTP.
Summit can now use SFTP regardless of the Port selected in the FTP Details settings.
Reimbursement Settings – Separate Account Assignment for ACH Reimbursements
We have added a new ACH Bank Account setting for both TPA and Employer-level Reimbursement Settings that will allow for the configuration of a separate bank account assignment for ACH Reimbursements.
The Default Reimbursement Account label on the Reimbursement Settings | Banking/Checking tab has been renamed to “Default Check Reimbursement Account.”
TPA Level
Employer Level
Below this section, we have added a new Default ACH Reimbursement Account section.
TPA Level
Employer Level
The Default ACH Reimbursement Account section includes a “Same Setup as Checks” checkbox in addition to all fields and options available in the Default Check Reimbursement Account section.
When the Same Setup as Checks checkbox is checked, information from the Default Check Reimbursement Account section will populate in the Default ACH Reimbursement Account section, and fields and selections will display as read only. When this checkbox is unchecked, the fields and selections are unlocked for editing. This checkbox is checked by default.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide – 2025-11
chunks.content:
Selections made for the Default ACH Reimbursement Accounts at the TPA level will populate for Employers assigned to administrator defaults.
The ACH creation process will use the account information designated in the Default ACH Reimbursement Account when issuing payments.
Participant Portal Security Image/Passphrase
The Security Image and Passphrase have been removed from the Participant Portal login and registration process. The improved security offered by two-factor authentication obviates the need for these.
Side Tab
As part of our efforts to cleanup and streamline the Summit interface, we have removed the side tab that contained the Calendar, Favorites, Edit Role, and Help icons.
Access to page-specific help can be found by going to Help (top of the screen), and clcking Page Help.
New PCOR Fee Rates
The IRS has published new PCOR rates [$3.84] for plans beginning on or before 10/1/2025 and ending before 10/1/2026. This new PCOR fee rate has been added to the Annual Rates & Limits table in Administrator Settings.
Receipt Distribution Details With Division Option – Additional Data Elements
We have updated the data set for the Receipt Distribution Details With Division Option report to include the following Supplemental Demographics values:
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Job Title
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Job Code
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Dept Code
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Branch Code 
PB Continuation Participant Report With Division Option – Additional Data Elements
We have updated the data set for the PB Continuation Participant Report With Division Option to include the following Supplemental Demographic values:
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Job Title
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Job Code
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Dept Code
Supplemental Demographics – FIELD: Branch Code  
CDH Invoice Report/Export Parameters
The CDH Invoice report parameters have been modified to allow for more flexible selections and better functionality.

chunks.title: What’s New Guide 2026-01
chunks.content:
What’s New Guide 2026-01
Features
Postpone Events in Process Approvals
Process Approvals | Events
Updated Events
Participant Events Tab
Enhancements
Premium Billing Online Elections “Step 2” Coverage Selection Grid
Process Renewals – Participant Enrollment – PRK/TRN Contribution Amount Validation
Enrollment Report – Tier Name and Tier ID
Participant Coverage Report – Tier Name and Tier ID
“Summit” Verbiage Removed from 2FA Communications
Features
Postpone Events in Process Approvals
Users now have the ability to postpone events in Process Approvals, delaying their processing until a later user-selected date.
Process Approvals | Events
The Process Approvals | Events UI will now be divided into Non-Postponed Events and Postponed Events. The Non-Postponed Events table includes a Postpone button in addition to the Approve and Decline buttons that were already present.
Clicking the Postpone button will postpone any of the selected events in the table.
For each selected event, a Postpone Event popup will display, allowing the user to enter a date. The event will not be released for processing until the Postpone End Date.
Postponed events will be moved from the Non-Postponed Events table to the Postponed Events table as shown below.
The events will be held until the selected postponement date, however users may manually release postponed events for processing by selecting them and clicking the Release button.
After confirming, the events will be moved back to the Non-Postponed Events table.
Updated Events

chunks.title: What’s New Guide 2026-01
chunks.content:
When notice events are postponed, the notice itself will be updated if subsequent changes to the participant’s account (eg. Qualifying Events or rate changes) would result in updates to the postponed event notice. Postponed events that have been updated and overwritten will be released and reverted to “Awaiting Approval” if the event requires manual approval or “Approved” if the event does not require approval. If the postponed event is deleted by an updated event, it will be released and revert to “Awaiting Approval” or “Approved” based on whether the event requires manual approval.
Participant Events Tab
The Participant Events tab has been updated to allow users to filter for postponed events. Normally, postponed events will not display. If the Show Postponed Events checkbox is checked, postponed events will display.
Postponed events will display with a Pause icon when the Show Postponed Events option is enabled.
Enhancements
Premium Billing Online Elections “Step 2” Coverage Selection Grid
We have updated the “Step 2” screen of the Participant Portal’s online elections process to accommodate age-rate Sum Multiple Tier coverages.
Previously, participants were only able to select a single dependent with the same age range. Participants are now able to select multiple dependents within the same age range up to the tier’s validation limit.
Tier selections will be validated against dependent relationship if the tier is relationship-restricted.
Process Renewals – Participant Enrollment – PRK/TRN Contribution Amount Validation
Participant Enrollment Renewals has been enhanced to include field validation for Contribution Amounts for Parking and Transit plan types.
If an amount that is greater than the plan limits is entered, an “Amount is invalid” warning will display along with a growler message displaying the plan’s contribution limits. Users will only be able to save and process the enrollment if the Contribution Amount falls within the valid range for the plan.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-08
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025-08
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.8.1. This release contains items pushed to production in August 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the August What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Enhancements
Optimization
Issues Addressed
8/26/2025
8/20/2025
8/12/2025
8/5/2025
Enhancements
 Process On Demand | Records Processed Status – The Imports table on the Processing | Data Exchange | Process On Demand tab has been updated to include a Records Processed column that will display the number of records in the import file that have been processed since the file was uploaded. The Records Processed count will update in real time as imported records are added into the system.
Premium Billing Chargebacks – Premium Billing Chargebacks will now be included in the ACH Returns list. Chargebacks will create an ACH Return alert notification on the Summit Homepage and appear on the Alert Notifications popup so that users may address them in Process Approvals. These Credit/Debit Card chargebacks from Speedpay will be treated the same as ACH Returns.
Receipt Dismissal Audit Report – We have created a “PB Dismissed Receipt Report” and a “PB Dismissed Receipts Division Report” that contain a list of receipts that have been dismissed within the queried date range so that users can more easily review dismissed receipts that are no longer listing under Remittance in Process Approvals.
Claims by Provider Report – We have created a new Claims by Provider Report that will list the payments and claims included within the payments associated with the selected provider(s).
Mask TPA Bank Accounts For Employer Users – TPA Bank Account Numbers will now be masked on the Employer-level.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-08
chunks.content:
PB Receipt Distribution Report – Employer and Participant Custom ID and System ID – The PB Receipt Distribution Details Report and Receipt Distribution Details with Division Option Report have been updated to include both the SystemID and CustomID values for both Employer and Participants included in the query results and are viewable on the CSV report format.
PB Continuation Participant Report With Division – The PB Continuation Participant Report With Division has been updated to include both the SystemID and CustomID values for both Employer and Participants included in the query results and are viewable on the CSV report format.
Optimization
Process Renewals – Search Performance – The Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment search query has been optimized to return results much faster.
HSA Monthly Statements – We have archived old data in the snapshot detail table to improve the time it takes for HSA Monthly Statements to load on the Participant Portal.
Issues Addressed
8/26/2025
Provider Not Saving During Claim Entry – The provider was not saving during claim entry on the Transaction Entry screen. This has been corrected, and the provider is saving to claims.
Addressee2 Field Not Merging on Initial Notices – The Addressee2 Field was not merging onto Premium Billing Initial Notices. This has been corrected, and the values are merging correctly.
Future Start Date on Employer Plans – Future Start dates on employer plans did not allow employer–level subsidies to be applied. The system would be unable to locate the plan for the subsidy to apply to. This has been corrected, and subsidies may be applied to plans with future start dates.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-08
chunks.content:
Open Enrollment Notices – Tier Information displayed blank if no option had been selected for the smoker status in the participant demographics for QBs and COBRA Participant if the plan included “By Smoker status” in its rates calculation. Now, if there is demographic information missing that is needed to calculate the rates for the benefit, the Open Enrollment notice will merge “Please contact your TPA for this coverage’s rates,” instead of displaying blank rates.
Participant Access Settings – FAQ – An error would occur when attempting to save an FAQ in Administrator Settings | Participant Access Settings that contained more than 175 characters in the Answer field. This has been addressed, and users can save Answers with up to 400 characters. Field overtype validation will prevent users from entering more than 400 characters in the Answer field.
Role Selection Error – Users would receive a system error when TPA level roles in the Settings | Roles | Administrators tab. This has been resolved, and users are able to select, view, and modify TPA-level Summit roles.
Unable to Edit Employer Global Role Templates – The Save button was disabled for employer role Global Templates, preventing users from saving changes to these roles. This has been corrected, and users are able to save changes made to the Global Template.
PB Qualifying Event Tracking Report – Last Day to Accept COBRA Incorrect – The PB Qualifying Event Tracking Report was not showing the correct date for the Last Day to Accept COBRA, populating with the last day of the month for the first Qualifying Event rather than retrieving the correct value from the tables. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-08
chunks.content:
Debit/Credit Card PB Payment Verbiage – The verbiage was incorrect on the Participant Portal’s Make a Payment page for making Debit/Credit Card payments. The screen would read “Draft funds from my personal bank account” when Debit/Credit Card was selected. This has been corrected, and the following verbiage displays: “By selecting this box and clicking Submit, I acknowledge that I will be redirected to a third-party payment service, ACI Speedpay, to complete my premium payment using a credit or debit card. The payment will be processed by ACI Speedpay on behalf of [TPA Name].”
8/20/2025
Subsidy Information Not Showing on COBRA Election Form – If multiple premium billing plans with subsidies associated with them were assigned to a Qualified Beneficiary, the COBRA Election Form was not showing the Subsidy information for those benefits. This has been corrected.
Debit Card Declines – Debit Cards were declining due to an issue with purse values failing to sync correctly. This could occur due to delays occurring during the nightly synchronization process resulting in a failure to update all purse values for all accounts. This has been addressed, and the nightly process has been optimized to ensure correct synchronization of cards and purses, and monitoring has been put into place to verify that all spend limits have been processed.
Welcome Notice Email Link – Participant Users were receiving error messages when following the Registration Link in the Welcome Notice email. This has been resolved, and participant users are able to login and complete their registration in Participant Portal.
Error When Editing Contributions – Users would receive an error when editing contributions. This has been corrected, and users can save changes to contributions.
Error When Deleting Contributions – Users would receive an error when trying to delete contributions when an offset was in place. This has been corrected, and contributions can be deleted without an error.
8/12/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-08
chunks.content:
Turning Off Debit Cards At Plan Level Not Reducing Card Purses – Turning off debit cards at the plan level was not zeroing out the card purse values for the plan within the card system. This has been addressed, and card purse values for the plan will be set to zero when debit cards are turned off at the plan level for benefits.
Offset Reversal History – Previously, if a claim was offset and the offset was subsequently removed due to a claim recalculation, the offset record would be deleted from the ClaimProcessOffset record. The system will now track the history of offsets that have been reversed due to a claim recalculation, showing the initial offset as well as the reversal in ClaimProcessOffset.
Unable to Delete Employer Plans – Users were unable to delete employer plans when the Override TPA Bank Account option was selected on the Employer Reimbursement Settings Banking/Checking tab. Users would receive a system error when attempting to delete the plan. This has been corrected.
Employer Listing Report Not Including Agency – The Employer Listing Report was failing to include the Agency assigned to employers. This has been corrected, and if an Agency is associated with the employer, it will be reflected in the Employer Listing Report’s query results.
Card Claim Status Changing to Ineligible When Denying Partial Amounts – When a card swipe had a partial amount denied, the entire card claim’s status was being changed to “Ineligible.” This has been corrected, and the Claim Status will remain Approved, reflecting the approval of the partial amount.
8/5/2025
Participant Portal Settings Audit History – The audit history on Participant Portal Settings was not displaying correctly. Modifications were appearing with the users listed as “Created by,” and the “Edited by” value would display as “N/A.” This has been corrected, and the page’s audit history is updating properly.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-08
chunks.content:
Employer Report Repository Email – Employer Report Repository emails were not generating properly Assigned to System Defaults had been checked. This has been corrected.
Report Repository Not Defaulting All Employer Settings – Some employer groups were not automatically assigned to the default entity communication settings. This has been corrected, and we have implemented a data patch to assign all employer groups without custom settings to the default entity communication settings.
Termination End of COBRA Event Effective Date Incorrect – Under circumstances when plans had mid-month coverage expiration, the Termination – End of COBRA Event’s Effective Date was populating as the first day of the following month rather than the expiration date. This has been corrected, and the event’s Effective Date is calculating correctly.
Premium Amount Incorrect in Check Detains for SMT Plans – The premium amounts were incorrectly calculating for remittances if the rates were Sum Multiple Tiers. The generated checks were multiplying the remittance amount by the total number of tiers associated with the plan. This has been corrected, and the check details show a single entry for each remittance.
Categories

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-09
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025-09
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.9.1. This release contains items pushed to production in September 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the September What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Features
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
9/25/2025
9/16/2025
9/9/2025
9/3/2025
Features
Administrator Central | Email UI & Technical Settings – We have added a new Email Domains tab to Administrator Central to allow for more efficient handling of the technical settings pertaining to email domain management for communications generated by Summit.
Enhancements
PB Status Change Notice Event – We have created a PB Status Change Notice event that will trigger the Employer Notice of Status Change and Carrier Notice of Status Change letters..
Issues Addressed
9/25/2025
Bank Routing Number Imports – Bank Routing Number Validation was not being applied to imports. Participants could be imported with a bank routing number of 8 digits rather than 9. This has been addressed, and routing numbers with fewer than 9 digits will create an exception when imported.
Participant Listing Report Name Fields Incorrect – The Name column in the Participant Listing Report was incorrectly returning the Participant Status rather than the participant’s name. This has been resolved.
PB Invoice Monthly Schedule – The Monthly Schedule selector was not functioning correctly for the PB Invoice report and was calculating an incorrect start date. This has been addressed.
Custom Employer CDH Payment Register with Division Option – Users were unable to save changes made to custom report exports of the Employer CDH Payment Register with Division Option. This has been corrected, and custom exports based on this template are saving correctly.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-09
chunks.content:
CDH-Only TPAs Could Not Terminate Participants – Due to Certain TPAs that were CDH-only were unable to terminate participants’ Employment Status. The selectors and options on the Participant Employment Change screen would be greed out.
Tier Display Order – Tier Groups were sorting in display by name rather than by Tier Level value. This has been corrected.
Premium Billing COBRA Template Setting Not Saving on Premium Billing Tab – COBRA templates were not saving for some employer groups under certain circumstances. This has been corrected and the COBRA Template Settings are saving correctly.
9/16/2025
New Payments Unable To Process – Under certain circumstances, payments generated on claims were created with an IsClaimProcessed value set to 1, preventing TPAs from being able to generate a file from the payment. In some cases, where payment was exactly twice the amount of the claim, the system erroneously created overpayments and placed the claim in a Balance Due state. This was occurring for claims that had already issued at least once payment and a subsequent payment was issued due to an On Hold amount or other claim recalculation occurring (such as a plan tier change). We have addressed these issues and payments are generating properly.
Card Logo – An incorrect Card Logo was erroneously assigned to multiple TPA groups. This has been addressed and the logo has been removed from the card packages.
Employer Card Page – Assign Mailer and Logo Missing – The option to select a logo or mailer had been erroneously removed from the Employer Card Settings page. This has been addressed and the options have been restored to the employer level configuration page.
Plan Enrollment Import – The Plan Enrollment Import process was incorrectly enrolling participant dependents without regards to their termination dates and statuses. This has been corrected and terminated dependents are not being enrolled during the plan import process.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-09
chunks.content:
Employer Central Division Save – When the “Not Applicable” checkbox was checked in Division Tab of the employer account screen, the save button on the tab would be disabled, preventing users from saving the selection on the tab. This has been corrected.
Runout Days – Users were unable to set the Runout Days to 0 for either the Runout Calculation for Active Participant Plans or the Runout Calculation for Terminated Participant Plans when Runout was enabled. Validation of the Runout Days fields has been updated to allow for a value of 0 to be entered and saved.
9/9/2025
Secondary Signature Not Merging on Remittance Checks – Premium Billing Remittance Checks lacked a merge field to include a Secondary Signature image. PB Check formats have been updated so that the image assigned to the Secondary Signature in the Premium Billing | Remittance Settings | Banking/Checking tab UI can be successfully merged onto remittance checks.
Data Exchange – Extraneous Data Validation – Data Exchange File Validation was not skipping data elements that had been flagged as Extraneous Data, which would cause exceptions when importing files. This has been corrected, and the import / validation process is skipping positions in the import files that have been flagged as Extraneous Data.
Imported Custom Billing Schedules – Imported Custom Billing Schedules were failing to be applied to participants’ Direct Bill coverages. This has been corrected.
Card Settings Removed for Associated Employers – Under certain circumstances, global changes to card packages would result in Employer-level card settings being removed, resulting in failed creation of cards for these groups. This has been addressed and resolved, and all affected TPA and Employer settings data has been patched and restored to configurations prior to 7/31/2025.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-09
chunks.content:
PB ACH Fees Reset by Changes to Participant Portal Settings – The ACH Fee for Premium Billing Payments would be reset to the system default of $5 whenever an employer was removed from default Participant Portal Settings. This has been corrected, and unchecking the Assigned to TPA Defaults checkbox will not reset the Premium Billing Options ACH fee amount values.
9/3/2025
Rehire Fees Not Included in Invoices – The Rehire Status Fee was not being included in Premium Billing Invoices. This has been corrected.
Deductible Amounts Doubling – When two HRA plans had consecutive plan years and deductibles, claims entered during the grace period for the earlier plan would display as applying to the deductible of both plans. This will now display in the Plan Details table as applying to the Deductible of the prior plan year but reflect in the Family YTD Out of Pocket for both plans in the Active Plans table.
Benefit Order Name Error – An error would occur when a user attempted to enter and save a Benefit Order Name that was more than 30 characters. Summit will now validate the field to limit the field length to 30 characters rather than throw an error when a user attempts to enter a name longer than the maximum field length.
PB COBRA Plan Coverage Months Changing on Edit – Under certain circumstances, the Plan Coverage Months on COBRA Plans were changing from 36 months to 18 months when a user edited the plan. If the user selected a Qualifying Event action, changed the action to a different option, then selected QE Dependent Status Loss, the Months would change from 36 to 18 months. This has been corrected, and the Coverage Months for QE Dependent Status Loss calculates as 36 months.
Participant Portal Settings – Making changes to the default Participant Portal Settings would result in a system error. This has been resolved.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-09
chunks.content:
Participant Account Balance Report – Plans included in the Participant Account Balance Report were appearing with Inactive Dates despite being active. This has been corrected, and plans included in the query results are showing with an Active Status.
Participant Portal Settings – TPA Default – TPA Default Participant Portal Settings were erroneously being returned to the system defaults whenever an employer was removed from the TPA default for these settings. This has been addressed.
Remittances Disabled for Amounts < $1 – Remittance checkboxes in Process Approvals were greyed out for amounts below $1 despite the minimum check amount option being disabled. This has been corrected, and the remittance option will be available in Process Approvals for any amounts if the Minimum Check Amount option has not been enabled.
Categories

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-10
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025-10
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.10.1. This release contains items pushed to production in October 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the October What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Features
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
10/28/2025
10/22/2025
10/14/2025
9/30/2025
Features
On Demand Processing | Premium Billing Group Coverage Administration – We have made substantial changes to Processing | On Demand Processing to allow for Group Coverage Administration for Premium Billing. TPAs may now use Group Coverage Administration on the On Demand Processing page to terminate coverages and undo selected grouped terminations, bypassing Process Approvals. The On Demand UI has been updated to include a History table of group coverage changes. Role Permissions have been updated to account for the necessary On Demand Processing permissions for Premium Billing users.
Duplicate Import File Process Approval – Summit has been updated to include duplicate handling during the import process. Now, when a file is imported, the system will compare it to previously imported files. If it appears to be a duplicate of one or more files, the system will not import the records contained in the file. Instead, it will display the new file in Process Approvals for review. There, the user will see the new file and the previous file(s) suspected of being identical to the new file. The user will have the option of accepting or rejecting the new file. Choosing to accept the new file will result in its records being imported into the system. The Process Approvals page has been updated to include a new “Duplicate Import Files” Process Type where these files and records may be reviewed and subject to approval. Duplicate Import Files will appear in the Pending Approvals and Actions alerts window with a link to the Process Approvals | Duplicate Import Files screen.
Enhancements

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-10
chunks.content:
Edit PB-Only Plans’ Enrollment Date – User may now make changes to the enrollment dates of Premium Billing-only benefit plans.
ACH Participant Receipt Refund Generation – Participants may now be issued receipt refunds by ACH in lieu of receiving a paper check.
Gender, Custom ID, and DOB Added to Dependents Table – The Dependents table on Participant accounts’ Dependent tab has been updated to include dependents’ Custom ID, Date of Birth, and Gender. The Dependent ID column has been renamed “Dependent System ID.”
Employer and Participant Custom and System ID Added to Process Approvals Unapplied Receipts UI – Process Approvals has been updated so that when the Unapplied Receipts process is selected, the Employer and Participant Custom ID and System ID values are now included in columns in the table.
Processing UI Access – We have made changes to how Summit handles access to various portions of the Processing module based on Line of Service access. Certain Processing screens that are irrelevant a particular TPA’s book of business will now be hidden if those Lines of Service are not enabled.
Employer Benefit Plans Tab: Division, Location, and Union Info – We have enhanced the Employer | Benefit Plans tab to include additional information pertaining to employer plans and their assignment relationship to Divisions, Locations, and Unions. The Employer | Divisions tab will also now reflect the benefits that have been associated with Divisions, Locations, and Unions for that employer group.
PB Payments Received Report – The data set for the PB Payments Received Report has been updated to include the Receipt System Key Value. Note that the formatted report output has not be changed.
Issues Addressed
10/28/2025
Dependent Card Issuance – Dependent cards were being sent to the primary participant’s address. This has been corrected, and dependent cards are being mailed to the dependent address on file when it is different from the primary participant address.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-10
chunks.content:
Secondary Check Signatures – Secondary Signature images were failing to merge onto CDH checks. This has been corrected.
PB Subsidy Detail Report – The Premium Billing Subsidy Detail Report was not displaying correct tiers, pulling from the tier assigned when the participant was placed in QB status rather than the elected tier for the PB status. This has been corrected.
Settlement Emails Missing Default From Address – When Settlement Emails were enabled for TPAs or Employers, the From Address was not defaulting, which could result in the emails to fail to be sent. This has been corrected and the communications@summitwith.us default email address is populating in this field.
Data Exchange Output File Error – If the ImportPlanID value was invalid, a system error would occur when viewing the output file rather than an exception message being created. This has been corrected.
10/22/2025
Purse Not Updating Contributions Correctly – Purse values in Summit were not updating correctly when a contribution was posted for a contribution-funded plan. Purses would appear to update then revert to the previous balance. This has been addressed, and balances are updating correctly.
Receipt Distribution / Receipt Distribution Details Reports – The Receipt Distribution Report was not working correctly when output to CSV. The fee values were not being calculated correctly. This has been resolved.
ClaimsVault Not Displaying Correctly – If the default payment type in Employer | Reimbursement Settings was set to “None,” participants would be unable to access the ClaimsVault. The ClaimsVault would display for the participant user as a blank screen. This has been corrected.
Issue Previewing ACH Remittance DDA – A system error would occur when trying to preview ACH Remittance Direct Deposit Advices in Process Approvals | Remittances. This has been corrected, and users can preview the Remittance DDAs.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-10
chunks.content:
Company Entry Description Not Merging on PB Remittance ACH Files – The Company Entry Description for remittance ACHs was not merging into the file. This has been corrected.
Transaction Review: Dependent Care Receipts – If a Dependent Care claim had an attachment and a subsequent receipt was added by the participant online, that additional receipt was failing to show up in Transaction Review when looking for claims with recently uploaded attachments. This has been resolved.
Adding General Settings Rules in Communications – A validation issue was occurring when users attempted add a General Settings rule for a TPA that had the same name as an existing General Settings rule that had already been applied to an Employer group. These rules are no longer flagged as duplicates due to the name match so long as they are entered for different entities.
10/14/2025
Claim Import Issue – If multiple providers in the system have the same Tax ID, the import process was failing to use the NPI value when included in the claim import record to distinguish the correct provider identity. This would result in the claim failing to process because the system was unable to identify a provider to associate with the claim. This has been corrected, and if the NPI value is included in the file, claim processing will use it to disambiguate providers that share a Tax ID value.
Process Approvals Error – A system error was occurring when users attempted to access the Election Change or Online Enrollment process types in Process Approvals. This has been resolved.
COBRA Termination Notice Events – If a previous COBRA Termination Notice event was declined, subsequent plan terminations would result in the subsequent COBRA Termination Notice event being decline and unable to be processed for the terminated plan. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-10
chunks.content:
Special Characters in Dependent Names For Cards – When adding a participant’s dependent through the Wizard, users were able save dependent names with special characters. This would result in issues with creation of the dependent cards. The Dependent Name field will now be validated to prevent inclusion of special characters.
COBRA Termination Notice – Incorrect Reason – Incorrect Reasons could be included on COBRA Termination Notices for rehires that were subsequently terminated. For example, a prior Open Enrollment New Benefit termination reason would be listed on COBRA Termination Notices instead of the Timely Payment Failure reason following a termination for failure to make timely payment.
Payment Breakdown Report – The Payment Breakdown Report was erroneously omitting some payments from the query results that should have been included. This has been addressed and resolved.
Minimum Check Amount Message on Remittances – Remittances in Process Approvals were showing the Minimum Check Amount warning message on negative offset payments when the Require Minimum Check Amount option was disabled. This has been corrected, and the message will not display if Require Minimum Check Amount is turned offer under the Remittance Settings.
Participant Demographics Street Address – Updates to the participant’s Street Address were failing to save on participants’ account pages. This has been corrected.
Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment – Enrolled Only Filter – When the Enrolled Only filter was unchecked in Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment, participants who were not currently assigned to a plan would display but users were unable to add plans to those individuals. This has been corrected, and users may assign plans through the Process Renewals interface.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-10
chunks.content:
Process Renewals – Plan Appearing Multiple Times – If a participant had multiple plan years of the same plan, those plans would appear multiple times in Process Renewals | Participant Enrollment, one for each year. This has been corrected, and each plan is only displaying once for renewal regardless of how many plan years were associated with it.
Payment Received Notices – Under certain circumstances, the Premium Billing Payment Received Notice was not always generating when a receipt was entered. This has been corrected, and receipt entry consistently generates this notice.
Process Renewals – Tier Funding – Non-tiered plans such as FSA and DCAP were displaying in Process Renewals with a dropdown selector for Funding Tiers in Process Renewals. Field validation was preventing the selection of None from dropdown, preventing users from saving the plan. This has been addressed, and the Funding Tier dropdown no longer displays for level-funded plans in Process Renewals.
9/30/2025
Claim Note Not Populating on the Reimbursement Check – Claim notes were not merging onto the details section of Reimbursement Checks. This has been corrected, and notes are populating in the details portion of check formats that include a detail section.
Invalid PB Coverage Periods for FSA Benefits – When processing a qualifying event for an FSA coverage, there would be a coverage period that extended beyond the FSA’s actual plan year. This could result in the participant being enrolled in a subsequent plan year’s FSA for which they were not eligible to enroll. This has been addressed, and Qualifying Events in circumstances where the QE occurs at the end of the year for FSA benefits will have a “No Valid COBRA Time Period” denial reason rather than allowing the participant to elect into the subsequent plan year.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-10
chunks.content:
Plan Repayments Not Displaying in Summit – Plan Repayment Transactions for Balance Due claims were displaying with blank/null fields in the Plan Repayment Details screen. This has been corrected, and Plan Repayment Transaction Details are populating.
Error Changing Participant Plan Status – Users would receive an error when changing a participant plan’s status to Active in circumstances where the participant’s Employment Status had been changed to Terminated if the effective date of the Plan Status Activation was prior to the effective date of the Employment Status Termination. This has been corrected, and users are able to save the change of the coverage status for participants whose Employment Status has been changed to Terminated.
Participant Portal – Debit/Credit Card PB Payment Verbiage – Incorrect verbiage was displaying on the Participant Portal page when making a Debit/Credit Card Premium Billing payment. When the Debit/Credit Card Payment Method was selected, the text erroneously displayed “Draft funds from my personal bank account.” This has been corrected, and appropriate text regarding card payments made through ACI Speedpay is displaying.
Open Enrollment Dates Cleared – Open Enrollment dates were being cleared when the Plan End Date was edited. This could result in errors when participants elected COBRA for those plans. This has been corrected.

Communication – This field contains the name of the communication as a hyperlink that will take the user to the page in Summit where the communication may be viewed/configured. Note that this functionality will only work for the user if the user has role access to the page in Summit where the communication may be configured.

Processing | File Fulfillment Manual Fulfillment Filter Options
The Processing | File Fulfillment page has been enhanced to allow users to more easily find and view documents.
The File Fulfillment page will now display results for Manual Fulfillment in a table based on the query filter parameters the users enter.
When the Manual Fulfillment Fulfillment Type is selected, the user can filter by:
Document Type – Allows for the selection of one, multiple or all Document Types to be included in the query.
Filter By – This option controls the parameter used to determine whether a file falls within the selected date range. Users may select Created By or Downloaded Date. Files whose selected date type fall within the From – To date range will be included in the results table.
Once the desired parameters have been entered, clicking Search will populate the results table.
The results in the table may be sorted by any criteria by clicking the column heading of the results table [eg., clicking File Name will sort results alphabetically by File Name value.)

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-01
chunks.content:
Service Charge for NSF, Voided, and Stopped Payments on PB Receipts
TPAs now have the ability to add service charges for PB receipts submitted that are flagged NSF, become Voided, or are Stopped Payments, allowing them to recoup from the participant the service charges that are assessed on the receipt.
The Edit/Reassign Receipt UI has been updated to include a Service Charge field, which will allow the user to enter an amount between 0.00 and 999.99 when selecting NSF, Void, or Stop for the receipt Status.
If the receipt Status is changed to NSF, Void, or Stop, the Service Charge field will become available for the user to enter a value.
Additionally, once the Status is changed to one of those values, the following message will display:
“Changing the receipt’s status may result in an event being added to, changed in, or removed from Process Approvals.”
Users will be unable to make changes to a receipt’s status once it has been approved in Process Approvals to ensure that the event and receipt history match for reconciliation purposes.
Once approved, receipt Status fields will be read only, and the following message will display:
“The receipt’s status has an approved event in Process Approvals. The receipt status and service charge cannot be changed.”
The Receipts grid on the Participant account screen’s Receipts tab has been updated to include the date on which a service charge was added or changed. The date and amount of the charge will display as a tooltip when moving the cursor over the Status:
“The receipt status was changed on <<StatusChangeDate>>. The service charge amount is $<<ServiceChargeAmount>>.”
Users will not be able to delete receipts for which NSF, Void, and Stopped events have been approved in Process Approvals. The delete icon cannot be selected for these receipts, and a tooltip will display when moving the cursor over the trashcan icon:
“The receipt cannot be deleted. The event has been approved in Process Approvals.”

Stop Payment Notice Event
A Stop Payment Notice event has been added that will trigger when the receipt status updated to “Stop”. This event is a System Default event. This event has “Approval Required” disabled by default and will appear in Process Approvals when the “Auto-Approved” Approval Type option is selected. The event will display in the participant’s history. 
The Stop Payment notice is associated with the event by default with the Participant as the selected entity and Send to Mailing Address as the default distribution method.

A Void Receipt event has been added that will trigger when the receipt status updated to “Void”. This event is a System Default event. This event has “Approval Required” disabled by default and will appear in Process Approvals when the “Auto-Approved” Approval Type option is selected. The Event will display in the participant’s history.
The Void Receipt event is associated with the event by default with the Participant as the selected entity and Send to Mailing Address as the default distribution method.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-01
chunks.content:
When making a change to a participant’s Plan Election through the Participant Plan Edit, entering a future Effective Date would be recorded in the database.  The system would apply the change to the participant’s plan via an automated process on the appropriate effective date.  This was and is working correctly.  However, users were unable to see that future-dated election changes had been recorded until after the future date had passed.
The Participant Plans tab has been updated to include a Pending Plan Changes (to be applied on Effective Date) section which will record the pending future-dated plan changes.
The Pending Plan Changes table includes all columns as the Plans table above, allowing the user to compare the details of the current plan with the pending changes to the plan.
The future dated records in the Pending Plan Changes table may be viewed by clicking the linked Plan name.
The Participant Plan Details will display as follows. The pending changes may be deleted from this screen by clicking the Delete Participant Plan link, however any other changes must be made by opening the original plan’s Plan Details screen and making those changes there.
Changes made to the original plan with a future effective date will override the pending plan change with a new pending plan change. If there is already a pending change for a plan, the user will receive a warning message after making a change with a future effective date, confirming that they wish to override the previous change.

The Coverage Status Change options in the Coverage Details UI have been restricted to role-based permissions to prevent HR and Broker users from performing certain status change actions incorrectly [such as performing a Takeover QB rather than activating the coverage then processing a Qualifying Event for it].

Default Remittance Schedules for New Employers
