Features
Reset User Registration
Previously, when a user initiates the Forgot Password option, if they did not know the answer to their security questions, it required developer involvement to regain access to the account. We have added a User Reset Registration feature that will allow a user who has been locked out of their account to be reset to an unregistered state so that they may reregister for their Summit account.
The Reset User Registration tool has been added in the following locations:
Administrator Central | Users
Administrators | User Account
Employers | User Account
Brokers | User Account
Partners | User Account
Participants | User Account
Participant Central | Participant Account
On the Administrator Central | Users pages, the User table has been updated to include a Reset User column with a button that may be clicked to initiate the reset for users with Summit logins.
The link will only be present for participants who have Summit logins.
The Reset User link will be present on the Participant account’s User Account screen if the participant is registered on Summit.
Note that the tool will NOT be available for the user account that is currently logged in.
Reset Process
To reset the account, click the Reset Registration link for the user account from Administrator Central. The user will be prompted to confirm that they wish to reset the user’s registration:
Clicking Continue will remove the previous registration for the account and trigger an email notification to the user informing them that their account has been reset.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-03
chunks.content:
Note: If resetting registration from the Participant’s Account screen in Participant Central, no warning will be displayed; the reset will be immediate and the user will be resent the Welcome Notice.
Participants
For participant users whose account has been reset, the user will be sent a Welcome Notice to the participant’s email on file. The user will no longer be able to login with their previous credentials and will be prompted to create a new login.
Admin Portal Users
When an Admin Portal user’s account is reset, they will be sent the User Account Creation emails containing a User ID and Temporary Password to the email address on file.
The user’s password and security questions only will be reset.
User Role Access
Access to the Reset Registration tool is governed by the read/write permissions to Participant Central | User Accounts and the Administrator Central | Users pagers.
TPA users with read/write access to TPAs, Brokers, Partners, Employers, and Participants will be able to view and perform the Reset for the respective entities assigned to their user role.
Broker users with read/write access to will be able to view and perform the reset for Broker, Employer, and Participant users for the respective entities assigned to their user role.
Partner users with read/write access will be able to view and perform the reset for Partners, Brokers, Employers, and Participant users for the respective entities assigned to their user role.
Employer users with read/write access will be able to view and perform the reset for Employer and Participant users within their group.
Users with read-only permissions for entities will see but be unable to use the Reset Registration tool
Enhancements
Claim Entry Confirmation Message
An alert will now display on the Admin portal if any unsaved claim details on the Transaction Entry screen are present when the user attempts to close or click away from the page.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-03
chunks.content:
The alert will inform the user that changes may not be saved and prompt the user to click “Leave,” which will allow the user to leave the page, or “Cancel,” which will prevent the user from leaving the page, allowing them to complete and save the claim form.
Participant Portal Duplicate Premium Payment Warning
In some cases, Participants were making duplicate premium payments on the Participant Portal because posted payments were not immediately visible. In order to address this, we have added a warning message to inform participant users that they may have submitted a duplicate payment. Duplicate payment matching logic will check the payment amount, bank account, and date. If the participant has entered payment information and all three values match a previously made payment (One-Time, Recurring, or auto-draft Pending Approval Payments), the participant will be presented with the following warning message:
“A payment from the selected bank account, for the same amount, has already been made for the same payment date. Press “Continue” to make the payment that was entered, or press “Cancel” to exit the payment process. Go to Scheduled Transactions to view payments made but not posted, or go to Transactions to view payments that have posted.”
Edit Recurring Payment – Remove Message
The warning message “Adding recurring payments will result in the cancellation of any future scheduled premium payments upon completion of the recurring payment setup.” has been removed from the Edit Recurring Payment UI, as this information only applies to adding recurring payments.
PB Mailing Summary Report – Divisions

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-03
chunks.content:
A new version of the PB Mailing Summary Report has been created that includes Division functionality. This new report, PB Mailing Summary with Division Option, is available in the DataExchange Report Management list and will contain all information in the PB Mailing Summary Report with the results subgrouped by division within each selected employer. Each division within each selected employer group will display as its own sub-section with the division name and ID in the subheader.
Participants not assigned to any division will be grouped in a separate subsection after all divisions within each selected employer group. Results for employers without divisions will display without division subgroupings.
Users with access to the PB Mailing Summary Report will also have access to the PB Mailing Summary with Division Option report.
Mutual Fund Names Updated
Some of the mutual funds in which investment-enabled accounts may be invested have undergone name changes. We have updated the listings in the Participant Portal to reflect the new names of these funds.
HSA Terms & Conditions Popup
We have added a Terms & Conditions popup that HSA account holders must acknowledge and agree to when an HSA owner logs into the Participant Portal. Users will only need to acknowledge the Terms & Conditions once and will not be notified on subsequent logins unless we have updated the Terms & Conditions, in which case the user must acknowledge the new Terms & Conditions.

chunks.content:
“What’s New” Guide 2025-03 Mobile App
Table of Contents
Enhancements

Enhancements
Mobile App – Liquidate to Savings
We have added a Liquidate to Savings option to the Summit Mobile App, allowing investment-enabled HSA owners to perform the Liquidate to Savings action on invested funds.
The Investment screen of the Summit Mobile App has been updated to include a “Liquidate to Savings” options in the I Want To menu. Participants with investment-enabled accounts can process liquidations of funds from the Mobile App by selecting this option.
The user will be taken to the Liquidate to Savings screen. Here they will be informed of their invested amount and be able to enter an amount to be liquidated up that invested amount.
Liquidated investment shares will be prorated based on the percentage of the corresponding market values in the account owner’s portfolio. Example: Fund A has $10,000, Fund B has $10,000, and Fund C has $20,000; the account owner chooses to liquidate $400 to savings; $100 from Fund A, $100 from Fund B, and $200 from Fund C will be liquidated to the participant’s cash account.
The user may tap Cancel to back out or Save Investment Order to proceed.
If the user tapped Save Investment Order, they will be taken to a Liquidate To Savings Confirmation screen with the details of the transaction. From this screen, they may download the confirmation as a pdf by clicking the Download Confirmation link.
Mobile App – Finish Later
Users entering claims via the Summit Mobile App can now save a claim to finish it later.
A Finish Later link has been added to the claim form. When the user taps this link, the completed fields of the claim will be saved, though the claim will not be submitted. The claim will be placed under Unfinished Claims where it may be completed later.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-03 Mobile App
chunks.content:
To complete an unfinished claim, the user will tap Enter a Claim from the I Want To list, and then tap the Unfinished Claims link in the upper right corner of the screen.
This will open the Unfinished Claims screen that will list all unfinished claims that have been saved but not yet submitted. Tapping one of the claims on this screen will open the claim form, allowing the user to complete and submit the claim form. Note that unfinished claims may only be saved and edited once; they cannot be saved again once opened from the Unfinished Claims list.
The user may delete an unfinished claim if it is no longer needed by tapping the Delete button.
Click Continue to delete the claim.

Features
Include Non-Active Employers and Participants in Reports
We have enhanced Summit’s participant-based reports to allow for the inclusion of non-Active Employers and Participants.
Report query parameters have been updated to include filter options that will allow users to include both Active and Inactive participants, include only active participants, include only a certain combination of active or inactive participants based on either employment or Summit user status, or include only non-active participants when generating results.
Reports that include an Employer dropdown selector now also present an Include Inactive Employer checkbox. When this checkbox is checked, Employers with an inactive status will display as available for selection to be included in query results. This checkbox is unchecked by default.
Reports that include a Participant dropdown selector now also include User Status and Employment Status multi-select dropdown selectors that will filter results by status.
The User Status dropdown includes all user statuses and applies to participants’ system status as a user in Summit. All User Statuses will be selected by default.
The Employment Status dropdown includes all user statuses and applies to participants’ employment status. The following statuses are selected by default for inclusion:

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-04
chunks.content:
Employed – Full Time
Employed – Part Time
Employed – Season
Employed – Contract
Note that the Status selectors will determine which participants in the Participant selector are pre-selected for inclusion; they do NOT affect the participant pool included for selection within the dropdown selector.
IDV Failure Notes
Identity Verification failure messages for participants applying for HSAs will be sent to the TPA users as a Pending Approvals & Actions notification and will display for participants on the Participant Portal.  These notifications are generated and sent by DataPath Financial Services (DFS) as an email to the participant when an HSA applicant has failed to pass the necessary Identity Verification process for any reason. The notices include instructions on the actions necessary to pass the verification process. Admin users can view these notices, as well as subsequent pass validation notices, in Processing | Process Approvals as a Partner Message type. In addition to receiving an email, the Participant users will see these notices in the Participant Portal.
Admin
When a participant must provide additional information to open their Health Saving Account, and their ID Verification fails, Summit will create a notice in the Pending Approvals & Actions alert/notifications queue as a Partner Message.
The notice(s) for participants whose ID Verification failed will be included in Process Approvals | Partner Messages. The table can be filtered by Message Type, with “Identity Verification Failed” displaying the failure notices.
The user can view the message details by clicking the linked text of the “Subject” field.
The message includes the specific reasons for the failure and how the participant might address the ID Verification failure.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-04
chunks.content:
The “Suppress Passed Identity Validation Failures” filter will hide notifications of Identity Validation Failures that have since been resolved. [Note that even once an ID Validation issue has been resolved, the failure notice will remain in history and will still be available for viewing.]
This option will allow the user to see only the Failures which have not been resolved when the Identity Verification Failed filter is checked.
TPA users will only receive Identity Validation Passed notices if an attempt at validation failed and the participant subsequently resolves the issue which caused the verification to fail. These notes will simply indicate that the IDV passed validation, and the account has been approved.
Participant
The participant will be shown the ID Validation Failure alert on the Participant Portal home page. This alert will contain the same information that is shown to the TPA in the admin portal, i.e. details of why the failure occurred and how the participant may address and resolve the issue that prevented ID Validation.
Once DFS has received the additional documentation requested and ID Validation has been passed, the IDV Passed message will display for the participant on the Alerts section of the Participant Portal home page.
Designated Default Remittance Schedules
TPAs may now designate a default Remittance Schedule to which all newly added employers in Summit will be assigned.
Note that the Default Remittance Schedule will ONLY be applied to newly-added employers. Changing the Default Remittance Schedule will not reassign the new schedule to any existing employers, even if they are assigned to the TPA defaults and were assigned the Default Remittance Schedule when created.
Add Remittance Schedule – Default Remittance Schedule Checkbox
The Add Remittance Schedule UI has been updated to include an option to designate a schedule as the default schedule which will be automatically assigned to new employers.
chunks.section: Add Remittance Schedule – Default Remittance Schedule Checkbox

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-04
chunks.content:
Checking the Default Remittance Schedule checkbox will designate the newly-added Remittance Schedule as the default for all newly-added Employers. Note that this selection will also override any previously designated Default Remittance Schedule.
Premium Billing | Remittance Settings | Schedules tab
The TPA Schedules tab has been updated to include a Default Remittance Schedule dropdown list. This list will contain the available Remittance Schedules with the schedule currently selected as the default selected. The user may designate a new default Remittance Schedule by selecting an available schedule from this dropdown list and clicking the Save button.
Enhancements
Verify $0.00 Premium Amounts for Individually Rated Plans
We have implemented validation on the Premium Amount field which will no longer default a 0.00 value for Non-FSA Premium Billing plans.
When entering individually rated Medical, Dental, or Vision plans into Summit, the Individual Rate field used for calculating premiums would default as 0.00. If this amount was saved, then the user needed to perform a rate change to add the premium amount before a qualifying event could be performed.
The Premium field will now default as blank and will be validated as a required field to ensure that the desired value is added before the coverage can be saved. This will prevent benefits from being incorrectly saved with, and have billing generated for, a $0.00 Premium amount if the coverage was not meant to have a $0.00 Premium.
If the coverages are imported via file, warnings will display in the results file if the file contains either spaces [a null value] or a $0.00 value for the Premium Amount.
Null/spaces – If Null value or spaces are present, the results file will include a warning “The coverage premium amount is spaces.”
Zeroes – If a $0.00 is present, the results file will include a warning “The coverage premium amount is zeroes.”
Remittance Minimum Check Amount.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-04
chunks.content:
Process Approvals will now display a validation warning message for check remittances if a check remittance amount is less than the minimum check amount threshold when the Require minimum check amount setting has been enabled.
If the check amount is zero, a “Minimum check amount must be greater than $0.00” warning will display.
If the check amount is below the designated Minimum Check Amount, a “Check remittance amount is less than the remittance check minimum allowed amount” warning will display.
The Remittance Settings UI has been updated to move the Require minimum check amount checkbox and the Minimum Check Amount field closer together.
[Note, the Minimum Check Amount field had previously been labelled Min Check Amount.]
PB Check Templates
We have updated PB Check Templates to include additional data elements in their data source. No changes have been made to physically printed checks, however these values will be included in report exports of these templates.
The following data elements have been added to Premium Billing Check Templates:
PPT System ID
Employer Name
Coverage Tier
Division Name
Division ID
These will help carriers identify members associated with remittance payments in absence of an accurate group number as well as help administrators identify members when generating refund checks.
Document Manager Improvements
The Document Manager in Summit has undergone code optimization to significantly improve performance. In addition to this code optimization, we have added the ability for users to save documents that include special characters in the DocumentName field, and whenever a document is added to the Document Manager, the Globally Available option will be unchecked by default.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-04
chunks.content:

This new report, PB Employer Benefit Detail Report with Division Option, is available in the DataExchange Report Management list and will contain all information in the PB Mailing Summary Report with the results subgrouped by division within each selected employer. Users with access to the PB Employer Benefit Detail Report will also have access to the PB Employer Benefit Detail with Division Option report.
Assigned Account for Direct Deposit Contributions Report (HSA)
We have created an Assigned Account for Direct Deposit Contributions report that shows all real bank account routing and account numbers associated with HSAs for participants whose employers utilize direct deposits as HSA’s Contribution Method. This report can be run for one or multiple employers and will display the real bank name, account number, and routing number for the bank utilized for direct deposit HSA Contributions.
LOS Activity Report – Employer Plan Name and Employer Plan ID
The LOS Activity Report has been enhanced to include the Employer Plan Name and Employer Plan ID to the data source. The Report itself has been updated to include the Employer Plan Name in the query results.

A summaries subsection will report the totals by employer plan year for each plan year within the query’s date range.

Signature File Validation on PB Remittances
Premium Billing Banking/Checking tabs will now validate the presence of signature files to ensure that check files are printed with a signature.
The Premium Billing | Remittance Settings | Banking/Checking tab and the Employer Account | Premium Billing tab will no longer allow a user to save when DataPath Fulfillment is selected as the Default Check File Delivery method unless a signature file has been uploaded. If no file is uploaded, a “Signature file is not assigned” validation message will display when attempting to save.
This validation message will also display if the user changes the Default Check File Delivery method from Manually Downloaded to DataPath Fulfillment.
Process Approvals | Remittances has been updated to prevent users from checking the approval checkbox if a signature file is missing from the TPA/Employer level Remittance Settings and the Default Check File Delivery method is set to DataPath Fulfillment. A “Signature file is not assigned” validation message will display for the remittance record.
Additionally, check generation for remittances and refunds will be blocked if the next check number = 0 on the associated Remittance account.
Any instances of remittances and refunds that are pending check generation due to a missing signature file or a check number = 0 will appear as “Missing information” items in Process Approvals and will appear in the Alerts & Notifications popup.
Coverages by Carrier Reports
We have added a Coverages by Carrier report and a Coverages by Carrier – Division report that will aid TPAs in determining which carriers should be paid when participants make premium payments.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-06
chunks.content:
These reports which can be run from Processing | DataExchange | Report Manager display the participants with coverages that are assigned a carrier.
Users will be able to configure the following query parameters:
Employer – One, multiple, or all.
LOS – COBRA, Direct Bill, Retiree; at least one LOS must be selected
Start Date / End Date – The date range will be used to determine whether a participant record should be included in the query results based on whether the selected Date Type falls within the selected range.
Filter by Date Type – Whether the query will use the Event Date or the Processed Date to determine whether the record falls within the selected date range.
Event Date – Participants will be included on the report that had an event date for the selected Plan Type falling on or within the selected dates.
Processed Date – Participants will be included on the report that had a processed date for the selected Plan Type falling on or within the selected dates.
Coverage Plan Type – The user can select one or multiple Coverage Plan Types [Eg. Dental, HRA, Medical, etc.].
The report includes the following details:
Participant Last Name
Participant First Name
Participant Middle Name
Participant SSN
Participant Date of Birth
Participant Custom ID
Coverage’s Qualifying Event Date
Coverage’s Start Date
Coverage’s End Date [if coverage is non-expiring, “does not expire” will display]
Coverage/Benefit name
Elected coverage/benefit tier
Covered Dependents
Covered Dependents SSN
Covered Dependents DOB
Covered Dependents Custom ID
The reports are sorted alphabetically by Employer if more than one is selected in the query parameters.
The Coverages by Carrier -Divisions report sorts by Division within each Employer group.
The reports contain a header with the report title and the employer name(s) and a footer with the TPA Name, report date & time, and page number.

Features
Two Factor Authentication – Participant Portal
The Summit Participant Portal and Mobile App now use Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) to better secure participant login and access.
Participant users logging into their account through the Summit landing page will see a screen regarding authentication following the sign in process, by which they may have a verification code sent to a phone number or email address associated with their account.
Desktop Web View
Note: Users logging into Summit via an Employer login portal utilizing SSO integration will not be prompted to input 2FA.
Mobile App View
If the participant has one or more phone numbers saved in their demographics, they will be allowed to select to receive an authentication code by text message. All associated phone numbers for the participant will display for selection, allowing the user to designate the number/device to which verification should be sent.
If the participant has an email address saved in their demographics, they will be allowed to select to receive an authentication code by email.
If the participant does not have an email address or phone number present in their demographic information, the user will be unable to proceed and will receive the following message: “An email address or a phone number capable of receiving text messages must be provided for Two Factor Authentication. Please contact your administrator.”
Once a delivery method has been selected, the user can click the Send Code button.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-07
chunks.content:
A 6-digit code will be sent to the designated number/email.
Once the code has been received and entered, the user may click the Verify button to proceed.
Checking the Remember this device for 30 days checkbox will allow the user to subsequently log into the app without requiring 2FA for 30 days.
A verification code may be requested multiple times. Only the most recently requested verification code will be valid. Verification codes will expire after 10 minutes.
If the user enters a code which has expired, the app will inform the user that the code has expired and they must request a new code. Additionally, entering an invalid or expired code 3 times will result in a temporary [10 minute] account lock.
Summit HSA Identity Verification Checks [Compliance to DFS Custodian BSA/AML]
Summit will now place contributions and distributions as pending until the account holder passes the ID Verification check. Until the account holder passes the IDV check, cards will be blocked and distributions will be prohibited.
Participants with HSAs will now be assigned an Account Status, which will contain one of the following values:
Application Received
Account Open
On Hold
Account Closed
The Account Status will automatically be set by the custodial platform and reflected in Summit.
Whenever a new account holder is added into the system by any method, they will be assigned an Account Status of “Application Received.” Their status will only be updated to “Account Open” once the account holder has passed ID Verification.
If the ID Verification fails, the Account Status will be updated to “On Hold” and a note will be added to that more information is needed to open the account. The reason for the failure will be displayed in the Notes tab for the participant.
Until the account has been updated to an Account Open status, debit card transactions will not be approved, and distribution requests will be disallowed. Contributions will remain in a pending status.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-07
chunks.content:
Once the account has been updated to an Account Open status, any contributions that were pending will be credited to the account.
If an account remains in an “Application Received” or “On Hold” status (that is, the account is not updated to “Account Open” following ID Verification), after 90 days, any contributions made on behalf of the account holder are refunded to the entity who made the contributions.
Accounts that are marked “Account Closed” are unable to use debit cards associated with the account, and no further contributions or distributions may be made or requested.
In Participant Central | Plans Tab | View Plan Detail, the account status is listed as follows:
An Opened Account will display “Open”; a closed account will show the status as “closed”.
A newly added HSA will show “Application Received” until the account holder passes the identity verification process.  When the individual is successfully identified, the account status will change to “Open”.
During the time the account is in “Application Received” status, the effective date, contribution effective date, and coverage end date will be set to 12/31/9999, 12/31/9999, and 01/01/1900, which makes the accounts pend contributions.  This also prohibits the account holder from making a distribution request or debit card transaction until the identity verification process is successful.
Once the account moves from “Application Received” to “Open” the contributions will post, the debit card will be usable, and distribution requests can be made.
ID Verification Notes On Participant Account Pages
Participant ID Verification notes will now be included in the Notes tab of the Participant’s Account screen.
If a participant has passed ID Verification, an “IDV Pass, Account Opened” note will display in the participant’s Notes tab that corresponds to completion of the verification process.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-07
chunks.content:
If the participant has failed ID Verification, a note will display containing the full body of the IDV failure email notification sent to the participant that includes instructions on how to successfully pass IDV to complete opening their HSA.
These notes are only visible to TPA users with read access to the participant in Participant Central and to the Participants themselves in the Participant Portal. Employer/HR/Broker users will not have access to IDV participant notes.
TPA Portal Participant Central | Notes Tab
Click on the subject and the entire communication that was sent to the participant will be displayed.
In the Participant Portal, the account holder will see the email body in their Alerts section:

Ability to Change Tax Treatments and Tax Years of HSA Contributions
We have introduced the ability to make changes to the tax treatment and tax years of HSA Contribution transactions.
The Contribution Details screen for HSA Contribution transactions has been updated to include a pre-tax/post-tax Tax Treatment selector and a Tax Year selector.

Edit Plan Year Start/End Date
Users are now able to edit the earliest Plan Year Start Date and most recent Plan Year End Date for Premium Billing-Only plans. [Note that if a plan is CDH-only or CDH+PB, the Plan Year dates cannot be edited.]

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-07
chunks.content:
The Employer Benefit Plans tab has been updated to allow the earliest and latest plan years to be edited to correct plan year dates for Premium Billing benefits.
The tab displays benefits’ latest plan year and allows the user to select and edit Plan Year Start Date and End Dates of active PB-only benefits.
The benefit’s latest plan year, including its start and end date, will display in the Benefit Plans table when the user expands the benefit list.
Only Active PB-Only plans will allow the user to select the plan year for editing the start and end dates.
Changes made to plan years’ start and end dates will be recorded in the table’s audit information, including the prior dates, the date on which the change was enacted, and the User ID of the Summit User who made the change.
Start Date
The user may change the Plan Year Start Date to a date that is on or before the benefit’s billing effective dates [i.e., if a participant is assigned to the benefit and has billing effective dates, the Plan Year Start Date may not be changed to later than the billing effective date]. If a previous plan year exists, the Plan Year Start Date may not be changed in such a way that would create a gap between the previous and current plan year.
If a Plan Year Start Date is edited, the following warning message will display:
“Billing changes and other adjustments may automatically be applied, and manual adjustments may be necessary for any participants enrolled in coverages during the changed plan year.”
End Date
The user may change the Plan Year End Date only for the most recent Plan Year, and only for active benefits. If a benefit assigned to the plan year is in an Inactive status, the user will be unable to make changes to the Plan Year End Date.
If a Plan Year End Date is edited, the following warning message will display:
“Manual adjustments may be necessary for participants enrolled in coverages during the edited plan year.”
PB Plan Year Date Change Audit Report

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-07
chunks.content:
We have added an audit report for the purpose of tracking changes to Plan Year dates changed using the new PB Plan Year Edit feature. The report lists all participants that have a PB Status Coverage during the plan year that was edited.
Whenever a benefit plan year start date and/or end date are edited, an audit report will display.
This report will include the Employer’s name, the system date, Coverage Name, and updated Plan Year Start/End Date in the header and list all affected participants’ names (Last name, First) along with their Custom ID.
Bank Routing Number Metadata
We have updated the bank metadata with the most recent set of banks and their respective routing numbers to reflect changes and acquisitions throughout the banking industry. This will address discrepancies and ambiguities some participants may have encountered when entering routing numbers on the Participant Portal

chunks.content:
“What’s New” Guide – 2025-07 Mobile App
Table of Contents
Features
Two Factor Authentication – Mobile App
Enhancements
Privacy Policy Update
Features
Two Factor Authentication – Mobile App
The Summit Mobile App now uses Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) to better secure participant login and access.
Users will see a screen regarding authentication following the sign in process, by which they may have a verification code sent to a phone number or email address associated with their account.
If the participant has one or more phone numbers saved in their demographics, they will be allowed to select to receive an authentication code by text message. All associated phone numbers for the participant will be displayed for selection, allowing the user to designate the number/device to which verification should be sent.
If the participant has an email address saved in their demographics, they will be allowed to select to receive an authentication code by email.
If the participant does not have an email address or phone number present in their demographic information, the user will be unable to proceed and will receive the following message: “An email address or a phone number capable of receiving text messages must be provided for Two Factor Authentication. Please contact your administrator.”
Once a delivery method has been selected, the user can click the Send Code button.
A 6-digit code will be sent to the designated number/email.
Once the code has been received and entered, the user may click the Verify button to proceed.
Checking the Remember this device for 30 days checkbox will allow the user to subsequently log into the app without requiring 2FA for 30 days.
A verification code may be requested multiple times. Only the most recently requested verification code will be valid. Verification codes will expire after 10 minutes.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide – 2025-07 Mobile App
chunks.content:
If the user enters a code which has expired, the app will inform the user that the code has expired, and they must request a new code. Additionally, entering an invalid or expired code 3 times will result in a temporary [10 minute] account lock.
Enhancements
Privacy Policy Update
The Privacy Policy on the Summit Mobile App has been updated.

Enhancements
Process On Demand | Records Processed Status

Premium Billing Chargebacks
Premium Billing Chargebacks will now be included in the ACH Returns list. Chargebacks will create an ACH Return alert notification on the Summit Homepage and appear on the Alert Notifications popup so that users may address them in Process Approvals. These Credit/Debit Card chargebacks from Speedpay will be treated the same as ACH Returns.
Receipt Dismissal Audit Report
We have created a “PB Dismissed Receipt Report” and a “PB Dismissed Receipts Division Report” that contain a list of receipts that have been dismissed within the queried date range so that users can more easily review dismissed receipts that are no longer listing under Remittance in Process Approvals.
This report is available in Data Exchange’s Report Manager and contains the following parameters:
Include Inactive Employers – When this checkbox is checked, the Employer dropdown will include inactive employer groups for selection. This checkbox is unchecked by default.
Employer – One or multiple Employers may be selected.
Coverage Type – One or multiple coverage types may be selected
LOS – One or multiple Premium Billing SubLOS may be selected
Filter By Date Type

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide – 2025-08

Receipt Created Date – Query will use the date the receipt was created to determine if a receipt falls within the selected date range.
Receipt Dismissed Date – Query will use the date the receipt was dismissed to determine if a receipt falls within the selected date range.
Start Date/End Date
Results are grouped alphabetically by Employer, and each Employer will include subtotals of the total number of participants who have had dismissed receipts during the queried timeframe as well as the total dismissed receipt amounts. The “PB Dismissed Receipts Division Report” version of the report further subgroups results within each selected employer by division, with a subgrouping at the end of each employer section for participants not assigned to a division.
The results include:

Remit To

Dismissed Receipt

Employer – Payments and claims will sort subgrouped by Employer; additionally, they will sort alphabetically by provider within the employer subgrouping.
Provider – Payments and claims will sort subgrouped by Provider; additionally, they will sort alphabetically by employer within the provider subgrouping.
The report includes the following fields in the query results:

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide – 2025-08

Each record in the report represents a single payment. If a claim was paid via multiple checks, each check will display in the results with the claim’s details included in each check record.
Each subsection will include totals of the Check Amount, Amount Approved, and Amount Paid.
When sorted by employer, each employer subsection will include totals with the sum paid to each provider. When sorted by provider, each provider subsection will include totals by employer.

Employer Reimbursement Settings

The PB Receipt Distribution Details Report and Receipt Distribution Details with Division Option Report have been updated to include both the SystemID and CustomID values for both Employer and Participants included in the query results and are viewable on the CSV report format.

Features
Administrator Central | Email UI & Technical Settings
We have added a new Email Domains tab to Administrator Central to allow for more efficient handling of the technical settings pertaining to email domain management for communications generated by Summit. While the functionality of this tab will be primarily accessible to DataPath users only, TPA users will have read access to the information in this tab. The Communications | General Settings email settings have been integrated with this newly added tab. Additionally, access to the Administrator Central | Technical Settings tab is now controlled by Role permissions.
Role Access
Technical Settings and Email Domain Management have been added as feature access modules in Summit’s Role Management Permissions grid.
TPA Roles may have Read/Update access to the Technical Settings module.
TPA Roles may only have Read access to the Email Domain Management module.
Existing TPA Roles and Role Templates that have access to TPA Central and TPA Central | Demographics have been patched to apply their corresponding Read or Read/Update access to new Technical Settings module; users with Read or Read/Update access have been patched to apply Read access to the new Email Domain Management modules.
Email Domains
The Email Domains tab contains a table of Email Domain values with the following columns:
Domain Name
Status –
Pending – When Domains are added, they will appear with a Status of Pending. Domains will remain in Pending status until they have been marked as Approved.
Approved – Once approved, the record will indicate the Approved Date and the user who approved the domain in the Approved By field in the Email Domain Detail modal.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide – 2025-09
chunks.content:
Inactive -Indicates the domain is no longer in use and should not be used for emails. [Such domains may be removed from the system].
Created By – The DataPath User that created the record.
Created Date – The Date the record was created.
Status Changed By – The DataPath User that performed the most recent status change for the domain record.
Status Change Date – The Date the most recent status change was performed.
Default Domain –Indicates that the domain will be used as the default for generating emails; only domains with a Status of “Approved” may be designated as the Default Domain
View – Clicking this icon will open the Domain Name Details window.
DataPath users will be able to manage email domain information for TPAs on this page.
TPA users with Read access can view the email domain information associated with their TPA.
Clicking the View icon will open the Email Domain Details modal that includes the following details for the Domain:
Domain Name
Status
Default Domain [checkbox]
Created By
Created Date
Approved By
Approved Date
Status Changed By
Status Changed By Date
Modified By
Modified Date
Communications | General Settings
The Communications | General Settings page has been updated to include two new fields on General Settings Details modal:
From Mailbox – This is a text field. A value must be entered here to save an email address.
From Email Domain – This is a dropdown selector that will include the active/approved email domains. An Email Domain that has been designated as the default will be selected here by default, but a user with sufficient Role permissions can select one of the other available active/approved domains. If there are no domains currently in approved status, this selector will display “None available.” If there are no domains available, the email address will populate with the default “communications@summitwith.us.”
The From Email Address field will display the email address entered as “[From Mailbox value]@[selected From Email Domain]”

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide – 2025-09

PB Status Change Notice Event
We have created a PB Status Change Notice event that will trigger the Employer Notice of Status Change and Carrier Notice of Status Change letters.
While these letters existed in Summit, there was no event directly associated with them by default.
As part of this enhancement, the Carrier Notice of Status Change has been renamed PB Carrier Status Change Notice and the Employer Notice of Status Change has been renamed PB Employer Status Change Notice, and both of these are now associated with the new PB Status Change event. These notices have had references to COBRA removed from the templates to make them general purpose PB notices.
The PB Status Change event will trigger whenever a participant’s coverage tier changes, whenever a covered member or qualified beneficiary is added to a coverage, or whenever a covered member or qualified beneficiary is removed from a coverage.
The PB Status Change event has been added to Invoicing, the LOS Activity Report, and the PB Detail Mailing Report.

chunks.content:
“What’s New” Guide 2025-10
Table of Contents
Features
Premium Billing Group Coverage Administration

Enhancements
Edit PB-Only Plans’ Enrollment Date
ACH Participant Receipt Refund Generation

Employer Benefit Plans Tab: Division, Location, and Union Info.

Features
Premium Billing Group Coverage Administration
We have added new tools to Processing | On Demand to allow users to perform Group Coverage Administration for Premium Billing benefits. Users with role permission will be able to perform terminations en masse for groups as well as undo, bypassing Process Approvals.
Changes to Processing | On Demand
As part of this enhancement, the On Demand Notices UI has been renamed On Demand Processing to better reflect the expanded functionality of this Summit module.
Group Coverage Administration functionality has been moved to Processing | On Demand Processing.
A “Process Type” dropdown selector has been added to On Demand Processing.
The Process Type dropdown will allow the user to select either “Event Notifications” or “Group Coverage Administration.”
The Generate Notices button has been renamed and is now the Perform Processing button.
On Demand Event Notifications
The previously existing On Demand Notification processes and functionality will be available when “Event Notifications” is selected as the Process Type. Employer and Event Notification fields as well as participant selection filter options will display when “Event Notifications” is selected.
Group Coverage Administration Process Type
When the Group Coverage Administration Process Type is selected, options relevant to Premium Billing Group Coverage Administration will be displayed on the Processing | On Demand screen.
The Group Coverage Administration Process Type includes the following options:

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
LOS – At this time, the only options available are “Select One” and Premium Billing. When Premium Billing is selected, the following fields will be available:
Coverage –All of the selected employer’s coverages that are neither inactive nor terminated will be included in this dropdown list (unless “Include Inactive/Terminated Plans” is checked). “Select One” will be selected by default. Only one coverage may be selected for the action. Selecting a coverage will allow the user to complete the Coverage Status, Action, Reason, and Effective Date fields.
Coverage Status – This dropdown list includes the Active, COBRA, Direct Bill, Retiree, Qualified Beneficiary, Qualified Direct Bill, and Qualified Retiree Premium Billing coverage statuses. “Select One” will be selected by default. Only one coverage status may be selected for the action.
Action – This dropdown list will include actions to be performed by the Group Coverage Administration. The only actions that may be selected are “Termination” and “Undo.” Other Premium Billing actions will be made available in subsequent phases of development.
Reason – The Reason dropdown list will populate with appropriate reasons depending upon the selected Coverage Status. “Select One” will be selected by default regardless of the Coverage Status. The same Reasons that are available for the selected coverage status Action on the Coverage Details page will be available for each group coverage administration action.
Effective Date – The date selected here will be used as the effective date for the Group Coverage Administration action taken.
Participants will display in a table with a selection checkbox column and Name and Custom ID and System ID columns. Participants will be sorted by Last Name, First Name, and Middle Initial. All participants for the employer will be checked by default. Checking or unchecking the box will select or deselect all participants in the table.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
Note that only up to 1,000 participants may be selected for a single batch Group Coverage Administration action at a time.
GCA Audit Report
Summit will generate a downloadable audit report for Group Coverage actions that will contain the selected Employer, LOS, Participants, Coverage, Coverage Status, Reason, Effective Date, and Process Date for the action performed.
Undo
Performing the Undo action for a previously performed Group Coverage Administration action will have the same effect as performing an Undo on an individual participant’s Coverage Details, reversing the last coverage action for all selected participants.
When the “Undo” Action is selected, the Reason option and Effective Date field will be hidden as they are not applicable.
All participants meeting the coverage and coverage status criteria will be included in the Participant grid for selection. All participants selected will have the previous group coverage administration action reversed when the Group Coverage Undo is performed.
Summit will generate a downloadable audit report for Group Coverage actions that will contain the selected Employer, LOS, Participants, Coverage, Coverage Status, Reason, Effective Date, and Process Date for the action performed.
History Grid
We have added a grid that contains the selected group coverage actions, reason, coverages, process dates, effective dates, results, coverage, and User IDs for each participant which met the group coverage selection criteria.
The On Demand Processing UI has been updated to include collapsible History section and Filters subsection that will display when the Group Coverage Administration Process Type is selected.
The table will be populated with participants for the selected employer’s Group Coverage Administration actions, filtered by the criteria selected in the History subsection’s filter options.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
The available filters for the History table will display when the Show Filters checkbox option is checked. The filters in this subsection are as follows:
Coverages – This dropdown multiselector will include all available coverages for the selected Employer group. All coverages will be selected by default. Participants for whom a batch process was run for a selected coverage will be listed in the History table if all other filter criteria are met.
Coverage Status – This dropdown multiselector includes all coverage statuses. All statuses will be selected by default. Participants that were included in a batch process with one of the selected coverage statuses will be listed in the History table if all other filter criteria are met.
Process Dates – Participants included in a batch process with process dates on or within the designated date range will be listed in the History table if all other filter criteria are met.
Effective Dates – Participants included in a batch process whose coverage actions include Effective Dates that fall on or within the designated date range will be listed in the History table if all other filter criteria are met.
Actions – This dropdown multiselector includes all available action types. All Action types will be selected by default. Participants included in a batch process whose coverage action is one of the selected action types will be listed in the History table if all other filter criteria are met.
Reason – This dropdown multiselector includes all available coverage action reasons. All reasons will be selected by default. Participants included in a batch with one of the selected reasons will be listed in the History table if all other filter criteria are met.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
Results – This option section includes checkboxes for Completed and Error results status. Depending on the selection, the table will either include or exclude participant listings based on whether the Group Coverage Action completed successfully or an error was reported for the individual’s action.
User IDs – This dropdown multiselector will include a list of TPA Users by User ID. All Users are selected by default. Participants that were included in a batch process that was created by the selected user(s) will be listed in the History table if all other filter criteria are met.
A Reset Filters link will restore the default settings of the filter selectors.
An Apply Filters link will apply the updated filter selections to the History table below.
Results based on the filter selection will populate in the History table, which may be exported or printed.
The History table contains the following columns:
Process Date – The process date for the selected actions will populate here.
Participant – The participant’s name [Last name, First name, Middle Initial] will populate here. This name will be a hyperlink that will open the participant’s account screen in Participant Central.
Custom ID – The participant’s Custom ID value will populate here.
Coverage – The coverage that was processed for the selected action will populate here.
Coverage Status – The coverage’s beginning coverage status prior to the Group Coverage Administration action will populate here.
Action – The Group Coverage Administration action that was performed for the coverage will populate here.
Reason – The Group Coverage Administration reason that was processed for each action will populate here.
Effective Date – The effective date of the processed Group Coverage Administration action will populate here.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
Results – “Completed” will populate in each listed record when the Group Coverage Administration action was successfully completed. “Error” will populate in each listed record when the Group Coverage Administration action was not completed due to an error.
User ID – The Summit User ID of the user that submitted the action will populate here.
Permissions For On Demand Processing PB Processing Types
We have updated Summit’s Role Permissions to include On Demand Processing permissions subsections that will control Premium Billing Processing Types.
An Events Notifications permission subsection and a Group Coverage Administration permission subsection have been added to the On Demand Processing Administrator Setting Permissions grid.
The Group Coverage Administration subsection includes permission for the “Terminate” and “Undo” coverage actions. TPA, Employer, Partner, and Broker roles will have Read/Update access to the Terminate action.
The Group Coverage Administration page has been updated to include a warning message that will display next to the Action field noting that some Actions are role-based and may require permissions to process.
If a user selects an Action they do not have role permissions for, they will receive a “Your role does not permit this Action” warning message.
User permissions for the On Demand Processing UI will be applied to the Events Notifications and the Group Coverage Administration Process Types. If a user has role permission for On Demand Processing, they will be able to select Event Notification or Group Coverage Administration as a Process Type.
All user roles that have access to the Events processing type have been patched to continue to have permission to process events.
Duplicate Import File Process Approval

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
Summit has been updated to include duplicate handling during the import process. Now, when a file is imported, the system will compare it to previously imported files. If it appears to be a duplicate of one or more files, the system will not import the records contained in the file. Instead, it will display the new file in Process Approvals for review. There, the user will see the new file and the previous file(s) suspected of being identical to the new file. The user will have the option of accepting or rejecting the new file. Choosing to accept the new file will result in its records being imported into the system. Process Approvals has been updated to include a new “Imported Files” Process Type where these files and records may be reviewed and subject to approval. Duplicate Import Files will appear in the Pending Approvals and Actions alerts window with a link to the Process Approvals | Imported Files screen.
Duplicate Checking
When a file is received for import, the system will calculate a CheckSum based on the content of the file, comparing the CheckSum value of the file for import against the CheckSum value of previously imported files for the same EntityID.
If the CheckSum value does not match, the file will be imported normally.
If the CheckSum value matches, the new file will be moved to a review queue in Process Approvals as a potential duplicate.
Pending Approvals & Actions
Files that are determined to be potential duplicates will create alerts in the Pending Approvals & Actions screen. A file count representing the number of potential duplicates awaiting review will display on the Pending Approvals & Actions screen along with a link to Imported Files that will open the Processing | Process Approvals screen with the Imported Files Process Type selected.
Process Approvals | Imported Files

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
In addition to going through the Alerts screen, the Imported Files screen can also be reached by going to Processing | Process Approvals and selecting the new Process Type, Imported Files.
When Imported Files is selected, a read-only Import Approval Type field will display, populated with “Duplicate Import Files Pending Approval.”
If there are potential duplicates, they will populate in the table.
The Duplicate Import Files Pending Approval table is divided into a File on Hold section and a Duplicate Files section, where the imported file and the potential duplicates can be reviewed:
File On Hold
File Name – The filename of the imported file with potential duplicates will display as linked text. Clicking the link will open a read-only popup allowing the user to preview the file’s contents.
Received Date
Uploaded By
Template Name
Dup Count
Duplicate Files
Name of previous file(s) / potential Duplicate File(s) – If an import file has a potential duplicate file, the duplicate will display here as a text link that will open a read-only popup window for viewing the file’s contents. If there are multiple potential duplicates, a “View” link will expand the grid to show a list of all potential duplicate files. The “View” link will become a “Hide” link that can collapse the expanded grid details when clicked.
Received Date of previous file(s)
Uploaded by (of previous file(s)
Status (of previous file(s)) – If a file has a status of “Hold” due to its CheckSum matching a previously received file, the held file will appear in the Pending Approval table.
The page includes Reject and Import buttons at the bottom of the screen. All files that were selected by clicking the corresponding checkbox will be either rejected or imported depending on the button pressed.
If the user selects a file and clicks the Import action, the file status will be changed from “Hold” to “Approved” and placed into normal queue for processing.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
If the user selects a file and clicks the Reject action, a popup will display confirming the user wishes to reject the file.
Clicking Continue will update the file’s status to Rejected, and the file will not be processed and will not be reconsidered for future import.
Permissions
Role Permissions have been updated to include a permissions sub-module for the Import Approvals page. All existing roles that have access to the Process Approvals module will be granted access to the new Import Approvals sub-module.
Enhancements
Edit PB-Only Plans’ Enrollment Date
User may now make changes to the enrollment dates of Premium Billing-only benefit plans.
The Open Enrollment Start and End dates will display on the Plan Year Edit UI for plan years with open enrollment enabled. Users that have Read/Update access to Plan Years will be able to edit the latest plan year’s open enrollment dates for PB-only plans that are in an Active status.
Click the Edit action button on the Plan Year date to open the Plan Year Edit UI and make changes to the Open Enrollment date fields.
Normal validation rules for the edited Open Enrollment dates will apply to the edited dates.
Plan Year Audit Report
The Plan Year Audit Report will now display updated Open Enrollment Start/End Dates in the header if it has been changed for the plan year. If no date change has been made, the report’s header will include N/A for the unchanged date field.
The report will list the names of all participants that have a PB-status coverage during the plan year for which an Open Enrollment date was changed.
Role Access
We have added Process Renewal as a specific role permission to prevent users without CDH access from mistakenly processing CDH open enrollment renewals.
All user roles that have access to the Processing module have been patched to include access to Process Renewals.
ACH Participant Receipt Refund Generation
Participants may now be issued receipt refunds by ACH in lieu of receiving a paper check.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
When an Employer-level remittance schedule is run at its appointed time or if it is run manually using the Run Now option, participants with refunds included in the schedule will have those payments remitted by either ACH or Check based on their individual settings on the Reimbursement Method field on the Banking tab.
Refunds processed for the participant through their Receipt tab will issue payment by ACH or Check based on the settings in their Banking tab.
Gender, Custom ID, and DOB Added to Dependents Table
The Dependents table on Participant accounts’ Dependent tab has been updated to include dependents’ Custom ID, Date of Birth, and Gender. The Dependent ID column has been renamed “Dependent System ID.”
Employer and Participant Custom and System ID Added to Process Approvals Unapplied Receipts UI
Process Approvals has been updated so that when the Unapplied Receipts process is selected, the Employer and Participant Custom ID and System ID values are now included in columns in the table.
Processing UI Access
We have made changes to how Summit handles access to various portions of the Processing module based on Line of Service access. Certain Processing screens that are irrelevant a particular TPA’s book of business will now be hidden if those Lines of Service are not enabled.
Transaction Entry – The Processing | Transaction Entry screen will now be disabled and hidden for Premium Billing-only TPAs. If you are a CDH+PB TPA user with access to this screen, no transactions may be entered for participants that do not have a CDH plan.
Transaction Review – The Processing | Transaction Review screen will now be disabled and hidden for Premium Billing-only TPAs.
Process Renewal – The Processing | Process Renewal screen will now be disabled and hidden for Premium Billing-only TPAs.
Batch Transaction Entry – The Processing | Batch Transaction Entry screen will now be disabled and hidden for CDH-only TPAs.
Employer Benefit Plans Tab: Division, Location, and Union Info.

chunks.title: “What’s New” Guide 2025-10
chunks.content:
We have enhanced the Employer | Benefit Plans tab to include additional information pertaining to employer plans and their assignment relationship to Divisions, Locations, and Unions. The Employer | Divisions tab will also now reflect the benefits that have been associated with Divisions, Locations, and Unions for that employer group.
Employer | Benefit Plans
The Employer | Benefit Plans tab has been updated to include a grid displaying the Divisions, Locations, and Unions that have been assigned to benefits. These grids will display subgrouped by plan year. To view the associated DLUs, click the expand button for the plan year. As shown below. All associated DLUs will be listed in their respective columns.
Employer | Divisions tab
The Employer | Divisions tab has been updated to include a grid displaying the plans assigned to each Division, Location, or Union for the most recent plan year. Click the expand detail button for any DLU on the tab to display a list of all benefits associated with the most recent plan year.
PB Payments Received Report
The data set for the PB Payments Received Report has been updated to include the Receipt System Key Value. Note that the formatted report output has not been changed.
