chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.02.01
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025.02.01
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.2.1. This release contains items pushed to production in February 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the February What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
Issues Addressed 2/25/2025
Issues Addressed 2/18/2025
Issues Addressed 2/11/2025
Issues Addressed 2/4/2025
Enhancements
Default Remittance Schedules for New Employers – We have added an option to automatically assign newly added employers to a designated remittance schedule.
HSA Account Number on Participant Portal – The HSA Account Number associated with a participant’s HSA will now be viewable on the Participant Portal. The account number will display on the coverages screen next to the HSA benefit.
Card Package Valid Time Frame – The “Valid Time Frame” value for all active default card packages has been updated from 39 to 60 months.
Hide Detail Tab Under HSA Coverage on Participant Portal – Whereas the information included on the Coverages Details tab is not relevant to HSA-only participants, the Details tab will now be suppressed on the Participant Portal for participants that only have an HSA coverage and no other coverages.
Deductible & Responsibility Information Removed From Participant Portal for HSA-Only Participants – Whereas the Deductible and Plan/Participant Responsibility information displayed is not pertinent for HSA-only participants, this information will be suppressed on the Participant Portal’s Coverages screen for participants that only have an HSA coverage and no other coverages.
PB Subsidy Detail Report – A new version of the PB Subsidy Detail Report has been created that includes Division functionality.
PB Term for Failure to Pay Conflicts – Division – A new version of the PB Term for Failure to Pay Conflicts Report has been created that includes Division functionality.
Issues Addressed

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.02.01
chunks.content:
Issues Addressed 2/25/2025
Bank Account Permissions – TPA Bank Account access was not respecting role permissions for TPA level users, allowing users without Bank Account Access to select the TPA-level Bank Accounts Tab. This has been corrected and users without the appropriate role access permissions will be unable to select and access the Bank Accounts Tab.
Claim Denial Letters – Claims that were in Transaction Review that included a denied amount but were not yet approved were generating Denial Letters. This has been corrected, and Denial Letters are only being generated for claims with a denied amount that have been processed.
Error Viewing Participant From Administrator Settings Page – A system error would occur when attempting to view a participant account from the Administrator Settings page. This has been corrected.
Issues Addressed 2/18/2025
MSP Reporting – An issue resulted in MSP Reporting files not submitting and processing. This has been addressed and MSP files are processing correctly.
Deactivated Cards Not Reactivating – Cards that had been deactivated due to an overdue receipt were not being reactivated once the transaction had been approved. This has been corrected and the cards are reactivating once a request claim has been approved.
User Unable to Deselect “Send Letter if no email” – If an employer was selected as the entity for an event in Premium Billing | Notifications & Communications, users were unable to deselect the “Send letter if no email” checkbox option. This has been corrected.
PB Remittances Going to Manual Rather Than DataPath Fulfillment – A recent issue resulted in remittance checks that were being directed to use DataPath fulfillment were instead using manual fulfillment. This has been corrected.
Error Deleting Employers – Users were receiving an error when attempting to delete an employer in Employer Central if that employer had custom Participant Portal settings or a security email block in place. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.02.01
chunks.content:
Unable to Assign Plan Template – When building a new benefit in Summit, users were unable to select a plan template. This has been corrected.
Contribution Schedules Calculating Incorrectly – A recent issue resulted in Contribution Schedules calculating incorrectly if edited. This has been addressed and we have implemented a data patch to correct affected accounts.
Editing Claim – Claimant – Users were unable to change the claimant when editing a claim. When the claim was saved, it would revert to the original claimant. This has been corrected and changes to claimants are saving correctly.
Issues Addressed 2/11/2025
Terminated Employer Receiving Settlement Emails – An issue was occurring where settlement emails were being sent to employers for whom the “Send Employer Settlement Emails” Debit Card Settlement Setting option was disabled. This has been corrected, and the system will check to confirm an employer’s status is Active before sending an email.
Debit Card Claim Missing After Changing Destination Plans – An issue could occur when if a participant had two consecutive plan years with card-enabled FSA plans, changing the Service Start and End Dates for a card transaction in the current year to fall within the previous year, the claim will not appear in the participant’s Transaction tab; the amount debited from the current year’s plan will be returned to the plan but the previous year’s plan will not be deducted. This has been corrected, and the transactions will deduct from the appropriate plan year and are displaying in the Transactions tab.
Error When Editing Contribution – Under certain circumstances, users would receive an error when attempting to make contributions to Plan after claims had been entered against it. This has been corrected and users can make edits without receiving an error.
Issues Addressed 2/4/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.02.01
chunks.content:
Access to Corrected Tax Forms for HSA – Corrected 1099, 5498, and 8889 Tax forms for HSAs may now be found in Summit for participants who have been issued corrected forms. These forms will display and be available for download on the Participant Portal from the Account Statements widget on the Coverages UI.
Summit Hanging When Downloading Excel Files – Summit would hang when users attempted to download Excel files, preventing the user from successfully completing the download. This has been corrected.
Data Exchange: Row Numbers Not Provided in Errors Only Response Files – Response files that were output in Data Exchange when the import settings were configured to produce an “Errors Only” response file were not including row numbers. This has been corrected, and the results files are including the row number values.
Document Template Name Field Allowing Special Characters – Users were able to save Premium Billing document templates with special characters in the name, which could result in an error occurring when a “\” character was used. This has been addressed. While users are still able to enter special characters in Document Template names, Summit will now parse these characters when generating the file, preventing issues and errors related to the special character being interpreted as a file folder delineator.
PB Notifications and Communications – Error Changing From and CC Fields – A system error would occur when attempting to make changes to the From and CC fields on the Premium Billing Notifications page. This has been corrected and users are able to save changes to these fields.
Categories

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.03.01
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025.03.01
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.3.1. This release contains items pushed to production in March 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the March What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Features
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
Issues Addressed 3/25/2025
Issues Addressed 3/17/2025
Issues Addressed 3/12/2025
Issues Addressed 3/4/2025
Features
Reset User Registration – Users with appropriate role access may now reset the Summit User Registration of both Admin Portal and Participant Portal users who are unable to login to their Summit account.
Enhancements
Claim Entry Confirmation Message – An alert will now display on the Admin portal if any unsaved claim details on the Transaction Entry screen are present when the user attempts to close or click away from the page.
Participant Portal Duplicate Premium Payment Warning – We have added a warning message that will display when a premium payment entered by a participant on the Participant Portal appears to match an identical payment made the same day so as to prevent participants from accidentally submitting premium payments twice.
Edit Recurring Payment – Remove Message – The warning message “Adding recurring payments will result in the cancellation of any future scheduled premium payments upon completion of the recurring payment setup,” has been removed from the Edit Recurring Payment UI, as this information only applies to adding recurring payments.
PB Mailing Summary – Division – A new version of the PB Mailing Summary report that groups results by division has been added to Summit.
Mutual Fund Names Updated – Some of the mutual funds in which investment-enabled accounts may be invested have undergone name changes. We have updated the listings in the Participant Portal to reflect the new names of these funds.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.03.01
chunks.content:
HSA Terms & Conditions Popup – We have added a Terms & Conditions popup that HSA account holders must acknowledge and agree to when an HSA owner logs into the Participant Portal. Users will only need to acknowledge the Terms & Conditions once and will not be notified on subsequent logins unless we have updated the Terms & Conditions, in which case the user must acknowledge the new Terms & Conditions.
Issues Addressed
Issues Addressed 3/25/2025
Premium Billing Check Format Division Fields – The Premium Billing Check Format data source has been updated to include the Division Name and Division ID. Note that the check report templates themselves have not been updated.
Participant Wizard – PB Plans – Users were unable to select Premium Billing Plans when setting up participants through the Participant Wizard. This has been corrected.
Expected Contributions Report – Employer Summary – The Employer Summary section at the bottom of the Expected Contributions report was not itemizing totals by plan type/name. This has been corrected and the report is now including the list of plan with a breakdown of the dollar value by plan in addition to the total of all plans in the Employer Summary section.
HSA Excess Contribution Report – The HSA Excess Contribution Report was listing contribution excess amounts incorrectly. This has been corrected, and these amounts are displaying proper amounts.
Contact Us Phone Number – The phone number value being populated in the Contact Us section on the Participant Portal was displaying with an additional hyphen. This has been corrected and phone numbers are populating in a proper format on the Portal.
Receipt Deposit Slip – Receipt Deposit Slips were generating with the current date rather than the date the deposit was made. This has been corrected and the dates are merging correctly.
Issues Addressed 3/17/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.03.01
chunks.content:
Trigger Send COBRA Election Form Event for All Qualifying Events – The Send COBRA Election Form event was not being triggered for FSA Plan Type qualifying events. This has been addressed, and the Send COBA election form event will be triggered for all qualifying events.
PB Refunds – Receipt is over paid – In certain circumstances, users editing the applied amount of premium billing receipts when attempting to apply a refund would receive a “Receipt is over paid” warning. A rounding error in how values were calculating would sometime lead to a $0.01 value being overpaid. This has been addressed.
Unable to Delete “Elect COBRA” Action – Users were unable to delete an “Elect COBRA” Action in the coverage’s event history if the coverage had been terminated and then added after a rehire. An error would occur, preventing the user from completing the deletion. This has been corrected.
Purchase Returns Not Crediting Plans – Some purchase return transactions were failing to credit back the plan. This has been corrected and transactions affected by this issue have been patched to correct the data.
Send Initial Notice Event Approval Settings – The Send Initial Notice Event Approval Settings were using the TPA Default settings rather than the employer settings. This has been corrected and Employer-level settings will be used for those groups not assigned to the TPA default.
Report Repository – CDH Invoice Report Not Generating Correctly – When generating the CDH Invoice Report, the version sent to the Report Repository was generating with no results even though a correct version was output to File History. This has been corrected and this report is generating correctly in both locations.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.03.01
chunks.content:
TPA Report Repository Error When Exporting to DPSupport Users – Exports to the TPA Report Repository were failing due to an error when the “except selected” option was used and no users were selected. This would create an exception due to the process attempting to send emails to users without email addresses. The process will now skip users without an email address and successfully generate the report.
Post Processing Alerts Delayed – Some Post Processing Alerts were being delayed or in some cases not sending at all. This has been corrected, and Post Processing Alerts are sending as expected.
Issues Addressed 3/12/2025
Edited Claims Paying Out Incorrectly – After claims were edited, they could potentially pay out more than the monthly spending limit set on the plan. This has been corrected and plans with a Monthly Limit will figure the set limit into reimbursements create by edited claims.
Employer Role Templates – When created, Employer Role Templates were being saved globally for all TPAs. This has been corrected, and only roles created by and for a TPA will appear in their Employer Role list. Additionally, we have implemented a data patch removing all Employer Role Templates from TPA environments that were not created by that TPA entity.
Active Plans Displaying Ended Plans – The Active Plans table on participants’ account pages was erroneously including plans that had ended. This has been corrected.
Unable to Dismiss Negative Amount For a Refund – An error would occur when a user attempted to dismiss a negative amount for a refund of applied PB receipts. This has been addressed and refunded receipts can be dismissed.
Issues Addressed 3/4/2025
Remittance Emails – Remittance Schedules were failing to generate and sent TPA/Employer Remittance Emails. This has been corrected, and remittance notification emails are being sent to designated users.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.03.01
chunks.content:
Split Claim Payments – Payments on debit card claims that were applied to multiple plans including an HSA were debiting payments for more than the amount of the actual claim. While the claim would be split properly through the two plans, the claim would be recalculated and the full amount would apply to the HSA plan despite there being insufficient funds AND the split amount would apply to the other plan, resulting in a payment greater than the amount of the original claim. This has been corrected, and split claims involving an HSA plan are calculating and paying out properly.
Categories

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.03.01 Mobile App
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025.03.01 Mobile App
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit Mobile App solution, Release 2025.03.1. This release contains items pushed to production in March 2025. For more information about the following changes, please see the Summit Release 2025.03.1 Mobile App “What’s New” Guide.
Enhancements
Mobile App – Liquidate to Savings – We have added a Liquidate to Savings option to the Summit Mobile App, allowing investment-enabled HSA owners to perform the Liquidate to Savings action on invested funds.
Mobile App – Finish Later – Users entering claims via the Summit Mobile App can now save a claim and finish it later.
Issues Addressed
Mobile App Push Notifications Not Received – Under certain circumstances, users were not receiving push notifications to their mobile devices. This was occurring because push notifications were only being sent to the last device used to log into the participant account irrespective of how many devices the participant has used to log into account. This has been addressed, and push notifications will be sent to all devices the participant uses.
Mobile App – New IOS Users Unable to Register – Participants were unable to setup their account via the Mobile App on iOS devices. They would receive an alert message informing them they could not complete their registration. This has been corrected and iOS users are able to register via the Mobile App.
Categories

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.04.01
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025.04.01
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.4.1. This release contains items pushed to production in April 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the April What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Features
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
4/22/2025
4/08/2025
4/1/2025
Features
Include Non-Active Employers and Participants in Reports – Summit’s participant-based reports now allow for the inclusion of non-Active Employers and Participants, and also allows filtering by Participant Employment status
IDV Failure Notes – Identity Verification failure messages for participants applying for HSAs will be sent to the TPA users as a Pending Approvals & Actions notification and will display for participants on the Participant Portal.
Designated Default Remittance Schedules – TPAs may now designate a default Premium Billing Remittance Schedule to which all newly-added employer in Summit will be assigned.
Enhancements
Verify $0.00 Premium Amounts for Individually Rated Plans – We have implemented validation on the Premium Amount field which will no longer default to a 0.00 value for Non-FSA Premium Billing plans.
Remittance Minimum Check Amount Validation Warnings – Process Approvals will now display a validation warning message for check remittances if a check remittance amount is less than the minimum check amount threshold when the Require minimum check amount setting has been enabled.
PB Check Templates – We have updated PB Check Templates to include additional data elements in their data source. No changes have been made to physically printed checks, however these values will be included in report exports of these templates.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.04.01
chunks.content:
Document Manager Improvements – The Document Manager in Summit has undergone code optimization to significantly improve performance. In addition to this code optimization, we have added the ability for users to save documents that include special characters in the DocumentName field, and whenever a document is added to the Document Manager, the Globally Available option will be unchecked by default.
PB Employer Benefit Detail Report with Division Option – A new version of the PB Employer Benefit Detail Report has been created that includes Division functionality.
Assigned Account for Direct Deposit Contributions Report (HSA) – We have created an Assigned Account for Direct Deposit Contributions report that shows all real bank account routing and account numbers associated with HSAs for participants whose employers utilize direct deposits as HSA’s Contribution Method. This report can be run for one or multiple employers and will display the real bank name, account number, and routing number for the bank utilized for direct deposit HSA Contributions.
LOS Activity Report – Employer Plan Name and Employer Plan ID – The LOS Activity Report has been enhanced to include the Employer Plan Name and Employer Plan ID to the data source. The Report itself has been updated to include the Employer Plan Name in the query results.
Contribution History by Participant – Totals and Summary – The Contribution History by Participant report has been updated to include totals and summaries. The report will now include totals information for each participant plan/year, and for the employer. A summaries subsection will report the totals by employer plan year for each plan year within the query’s date range.
Issues Addressed
4/22/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.04.01
chunks.content:
Unable to Process COBRA Rehire – Due to how field validation calculated dates, users were unable to process rehires of individuals whose COBRA had expired. Users would receive a warning that “Rehire Effective Date must come before the Expiration Date” and be unable to save. This has been corrected and rehires who have had COBRA expire at some point prior to their rehire may be processed.
Void and Reissue Not Working on Claims with Edited Plans – If a participant had at least two plans and a claim had been edited to target the new plan after the first payment had been issued, users were unable to void and reissue payment properly and no new payment would be pending in On Demand Reimbursements. This has been corrected, and the Void and Reissue process is working for claims whose target plan was changed during a claim edit.
Premium Grace Letters – Premium Grace Letters were generating for each plan with total amounts due rather than generating a consolidated Premium Grace Letter for all plans. This has been corrected.
Split Claims Recalculating Incorrectly – When claims were edited, payments were not calculating correctly when the claim was split between two plans. The full amount of the claim would be applied to both plans, potentially resulting in the claim going Balance Due. This has been corrected.
DataExchange PB Import Fails to Update Employment Status – The PB Import was failing to update the Employment Status for participants. This has been corrected, and the import is successfully updating the Employment Status value in Summit.
Life Insurance Rate Changes Not Calculating Correctly – The premium amounts entered for Life Insurance Plans were not calculating correctly following rate changes. This has been resolved.
Amount Not Displaying for Remittances – Participant receipt details were not showing in Process Approvals | Remittances if there were multiple refunds. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.04.01
chunks.content:
Total Period Amount Totals Incorrect – Summit was including totals for all plans on an account in the PB coverages Total Period Amount on the Participant Portal. This has been corrected and now only billing details for active plans are being included in the totals.
Coinsurances Changing – An issue was occurring where edits made to a plan with tiers could result in the coinsurance settings being erroneously changed, leading to payment issues. This has been resolved, and the coinsurance tables remain fixed unless the user makes changes to the coinsurance when editing the plan. Additionally, we have implemented a data patch to correct the affected plans and payments.
Missing Form 5498-SA – Form 5498-SAs were not generating for HSA owners for whom no contributions had been made during the tax year. This has been corrected.
Undeposited Receipts – When receipts were undeposited from a receipt deposit batch, the deposit date was not removed from the receipt on the participant’s account. This has been corrected.
Participant Plans Missing Funding Tier Assignment – We recently changed the methodology by which Summit funds plans, removing the Level Funding method and converting all plans to a Tiered Funding method. While a patch was implemented to convert all plans, some participant plans were missing their funding tier assignments and were producing “No funding tier found for tier-funded plan” errors. We have manually corrected the affected plans and have made changes to the database to prevent plans from being saved with a null funding method.
Employer Role Templates – When created, Employer Role Templates were being saved globally for all TPAs. This has been corrected, and only roles created by and for a TPA will appear in their Employer Role list. Additionally, we have implemented a data patch removing all Employer Role Templates from TPA environments that were not created by that TPA entity.
4/08/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.04.01
chunks.content:
Deleting Employer Without Permissions – Users with read-only permissions were able to delete an employer group. This has been corrected, and only users with read/write permissions for the employer group can delete it.
PB LOS Settings Defaulting to Inactive Template – New employers created in Summit were defaulting to an inactive COBRA Default1 template in the COBRA tab rather than the correct COBRA Default. This has been corrected, and newly created groups are being assigned to the correct default template.
4/1/2025
Track By Age – 1st Day of Plan Year On or After Birthday Option Not Applying – Under circumstances where an individual’s date of birth was the same as the plan start date when enrolling into plans with Age Rated tiers, the “Track By Age” with “1st Day of the Plan Year On or After Birthday” options were not applying correctly. This has been resolved, and appropriate tiers are available for that individual.
Report Repository Exports – Exports sent to the TPA Report Repository were disappearing after a few minutes. This has been corrected and exports sent to the repository are populating and available for viewing and download.
Error Deleting Elect COBRA Action – Users would receive an error when attempting to delete the last coverage action when it was “Elect COBRA.” This has been corrected, and users are able to delete Elect COBRA actions without encountering an error.
Categories

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.05.01
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025.05.01
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.5.1. This release contains items pushed to production in May 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the May What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
Issues Addressed 5/27/2025
Issues Addressed 5/21/2025
Issues Addressed 5/13/2025
Issues Addressed 5/06/2025
Issues Addressed 4/29/2025
Enhancements
Document Fulfillment Process Approvals Alerts – The Pending Approvals & Actions Alerts & Notifications screen has been updated to include Documents Fulfillment link to show documents that are pending in Process Approvals Document Fulfillment.
Permanent Card Blocks – Employer Level Card Blocks for Card Program Terminated will now ensure that no new cards are issued to replace expiring current cards.
Gross Misconduct Qualifying Event Reason – Gross Misconduct is now available to select as a Qualifying Event Reason.
PB Employer Benefit Division Report – A new version of the PB Employer Benefit Report has been created that includes Division functionality.
PB Prepayment Register with Division Option – Employer Fields – The PB Prepayment Register with Division Option has been updated to include the Employer systemID and Employer Custom ID to the report data source. No changes have been made to the report template.
Void Check Option Removed – The “Void” option has been removed from the Claim Detail modal for claims that have been paid by check. Note that the “Void and Reissue” remains available.
Issues Addressed
Issues Addressed 5/27/2025
Claims Not Returning to Transaction View – When a claim that had previously been reviewed was edited, Summit was updating the claim review status to pending and then returning it transaction review to be approved again.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.05.01
chunks.content:
Users With Read-Only Access Able to Delete Participants – An issue resulted in users with read-only access to an employer group being able to delete a participant account. This has been addressed.
HSA Plan Adjustments Appearing Twice in Transactions Tab – An issue was occurring where HSA Plan Adjustments were showing up twice under the Transactions tabs, one as a plan adjustment and one as a credit. This has been resolved and only the Plan Adjustment is displaying in the tab.
Unable to Undo COBRA Elections – When Allow Dependent-Only Elections was enabled, users were unable to undo COBRA Election events. When attempting to delete a COBRA Election event from a participant with dependents who had separate accounts, an error would occur. This has been corrected, and these elections can be deleted.
Dependents Missing from MSP File – Under certain conditions, when a participant and their dependent both had ages greater than 45, the dependent was not being included in the MSP Reporting File. This has been corrected.
Issues Addressed 5/21/2025
HSA Contribution Adjustments created Incorrectly – An issue occurred where when a participant’s per period HSA contribution amount was changed to $0, the system erroneously created a contribution adjustment.
Carrier Mails Not Sent to Carrier Contacts – Carrier emails were only being sent to Carrier Primary Contacts; additional Carrier Contacts were not receiving emails. This has been corrected, and all assigned contacts are receiving email notifications.
Participant Gender Data Not Pulling in Reports – Premium Billing reports were failing to pull gender data from participants when outputting query results. This has been corrected.
PCOR Fee Report Error – An error would occur when running the PCOR Fee Report. This has been addressed and the PCOR Fee Report is generating correctly.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.05.01
chunks.content:
Premium Grace Letters Sent When 0.00 Balance Due – Premium Billing Grace Letters were incorrectly generating and sending to participants when there was no balance due. This has been resolved.
Missing Payment Records – An issue occurred where some card transactions for HSA payments were failing to generate payment records and were deducting funds from Employer Settlement accounts rather than the participants’ HSAs. This has been addressed and resolved.
Incorrect Tiers Displaying During QE Entry – When entering a qualifying event on a participant’s plan, the tier would show incorrectly if the employer plan had tiers with the same level. For example: a participant is on an active plan with Employee + Spouse and Employee + Child assigned as the same tier level in the plan design; if the participant was assigned to Employee + Spouse and the TPA edited the plan to process a qualifying event, Summit would select the other tier of the same level and the user would be unable to change it. This has been corrected.
Unapplied Receipts – If there was no billing available to which unapplied receipt amounts could be applied, the unapplied amount was showing as 0.00 in Process Approvals. This has been corrected and the available amount for future application is displaying correctly.
Premium Billing Notification Sent Dates – The Sent Date on the Manual Fulfillment UI incorrectly displayed as one day prior to the actual date entered. Note that this was only affecting the display on Processing | File Fulfillment | Manual Fulfillment, and the correct mailed date was present on the Participant Events tab and on the PB Mailing Detail Report. This issue has been resolved, and the correct date appears on the Processing screen.
Reissue Card Fees Charged for Expired Cards – Card Reissue fees were being charged for cards sent to replace expired cards. This has been corrected, and the Reissue Fee is only being applied to cards that have been reported lost or stolen.
Issues Addressed 5/13/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.05.01
chunks.content:
Denied Amounts Not Updating – When claims were denied during Transaction Review, the Denied Amount was not automatically updated on the claim form. This has been corrected, and the Denied Amount is updated automatically regardless of whether the claim is denied while being edited or in the Review queue.
Custom Plan Type Errors – When setting up Custom Plan Types, if the user left the Plan Type Description blank, an error would occur when saving. The Plan Type Description field will now be validated and display a validation warning if it is left blank instead of generating a system error.
Error Adding HSA Plan via Wizard – When attempting to an HSA plan for an employer via the wizard, an error would occur when attempting to save. This has been corrected, and HSA plans can be saved when entered through the wizard.
Disabling IIAS for Plan Not Resetting IIAS Subtotals – Under circumstances where a plan was enabled with IIAS turned on and then later edited to have IIAS turned off, the IIAS subtotal would remain the previously entered amount rather than reverting to null. This would result in the IIAS remaining enabled in the card system for card swipes against the plan. This has been corrected, and disabling IIAS for a plan will automatically clear the IIAS sub-total value.
Issues Addressed 5/06/2025
Login Error for User IDs Starting with a Space – The Summit User creation process allowed users to save User IDs that contained a leading space character; these users were unable to login to the Participant Portal as an error would occur. Summit will now validate User IDs to prevent User IDs from being saved if they contain a leading space character.
Employer Account Screen Menu Bar – The menu bar containing employer-specific sub menu items was no longer displaying on Employer account pages. This has been addressed, and the menu is displaying correctly.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.05.01
chunks.content:
Plan Setup Grace Issue – An issue was affecting clients attempting to set up new plans. If Grace was enabled at any point during the benefit setup, the user could not deselect Grace and were unable to save the plan. Additionally, an error would occur if the user attempted to bypass this issue by saving with Grace enabled and Grace Days = 0. This has been resolved, and users can disable Grace, after selecting it, before saving the plan details. Additionally, we have implemented validation on the Grace Days field; users will receive a validation message that 0 is an invalid number for Grace Days rather than a system error.
HSA Excess Contribution Report – The amounts of Excess Contributions listed in the HSA Excess Contributions Report were not reconciling with the amounts reported by the Custodian platform. This has been resolved, and the report is calculating excess contribution amounts correctly.
Denying Claim Resulted in Negative Plan Balance. – An issue occurred where the system could overapply claims to one plan while the participant still had funds available in a different plan. This occurred when card claims that were split over multiple plans or plan years of carryover that had been denied were recalculated. This could result in one plan having a negative balance while the other plan would have an inflated balance which could potentially be overspent. This issue has been addressed.
Edited Card Transactions Not Crediting/Debiting HSAToday Correctly – Edited card transactions in Summit that changed the target plan to or from an HSA were not applying the changes correctly to the HSA account on the custodian platform. This has been resolved, and adjustments are applying correctly to the account. Additionally, we have implemented a data patch to correct balances of affected accounts.
Issues Addressed 4/29/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.05.01
chunks.content:
Plan Repaid Amount Appearing as Offset Amount – When a card transaction was denied and went balance due, amounts repaid by a plan repayment transaction appeared as an Offset amount rather than a Plan Repaid amount. This has been corrected.
COBRA Template Note Saving – Users were unable to save COBRA Template settings for employers with custom premium billing templates. This has been corrected.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.06.01
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025.06.01
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.6.1. This release contains items pushed to production in June 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the June What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Enhancements
Optimization
Issues Addressed
6/24/2025
6/17/2025
6/10/2025
6/3/2025
Enhancements
Signature File Validation on PB Remittances – Premium Billing Banking/Checking tabs will now validate the presence of signature files to ensure that check files are printed with a signature.
Coverages by Carrier Reports – We have added a Coverages by Carrier report and a Coverages by Carrier – Division report that will aid TPAs in determining which carriers should be paid when participants make premium payments.
Pending Approval Growler Message – We have added a new growler message that will appear at the top of the browser each time a TPA user logs on and one or more items are awaiting action in Processing | Pending Approvals.
Provider Search – The Advanced Plan Design | Provider Networks page has been enhanced to include a search bar.
2024 PCOR Rate – The IRS has released the PCOR rates for PCOR reporting for plans ending on or after 9/30/2024. The Administrator Settings | Rates and Limits page has been updated to include the new $3.47 PCOR Fee Rate.
Optimization
Participant Plan Card Balance Update Service – The Participant Plan Card Balance Update Service has been optimized to improve performance.
Partner Integration Batch Service Process Contributions – The Partner Integration Batch Service for Processing Contributions has been optimized to improve performance.
Issues Addressed
6/24/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.06.01
chunks.content:
Participant Central/Transaction Search: Debit Plan Adjustment Type – Queries on the Transaction Search and Participant Central search tools were failing to grab transactions with a “Debit” Plan Adjustment Type. This has been corrected and these transactions are being picked up by search queries.
Qualifying Events Could be Processed with Effective Dates Prior to Event Dates – An issue occurred where while processing a participants QE if the system had an event record processed with an effective date after the QE date, the system would complete the action but fail to write certain records due to the date mismatch. This would typically happen when a qualifying event was processed following a rate change where the QE date is prior to the rate change. This has been corrected and the proper records for the QE are being written to Summit’s tables when the QE is processed.
DataPath Fulfillment – Manage Queued Documents – The search tool in Processing | File Fulfillment | Manage Queued Documents for documents fulfilled by DataPath Fulfillment was not including documents created on the specified End Date. This has been corrected and the search logic has been updated to be inclusive of the End Date in search range.
Administrator Central Agency Error – An error would occur when a user clicked on an agency in Administrator Central. This has been corrected.
Premium Billing – Send Initial Notification Event Error – Running the Send Initial Notification Event for new participants was causing an error upon generation when the participant had no Email on file and the Event Notification Entity was set to Participant Only. This has been addressed and the notice can be successfully generated.
6/17/2025
Debit Card Return Declined – Some participants were affected by an issue where a debit card return would appear in the system as a decline, resulting in the plan not being credited for the return amount. This has been addressed, and affected accounts have been patched.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.06.01
chunks.content:
Funding Method Field Validation – A validation issue on the Employer Funding Method field prevented users from saving existing HRA plans that had been added to the COBRA line of service. Changing lines of service for a plan would reset the Employer Funding Method to Null; this would allow the user to reset the Employer Funding Method, however this created an issue as the Funding Method field becomes locked when participants have been assigned to the plan. Summit will no longer clear the Employer Funding Method when the LOS is updated if participants have been assigned to the plan.
FSA Premium Amounts Displaying as $0.00 – FSA Premium Amounts on FSA Election Forms were displaying as $0.00 when the Qualifying Event was processed from the Employment Status Change screen. This has been corrected, and the premium is displaying as the plan amount.
Error Editing Third Party Payor – Users would receive an error when attempting to add or edit a Third Party Payor on the Premium Billing tab of employers’ account screens. This has been corrected.
Claims with MOP None Issued Checks Transferred to HSA – An issue occurred with imported claims that included Method of Payment = None. These claims did not pay from the destination plan but instead transferred to HSA plans. While the None payment method is disallowed for HSA plans, the import transfer claims bypassed this, which erroneously resulted in the creation of checks. This has been addressed, and imported claims with MOP=None can no longer be transferred to HSA plans.
HSA Contribution Schedules Erroring During Processing – TPA users would receive errors when attempting to run scheduled batches of HSA Contributions, forcing them to process these contributions manually. This has been corrected, and scheduled contributions are working properly.
6/10/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.06.01
chunks.content:
Premium Billing Amount Due Calculating Incorrectly – When a participant had multiple premium billing plans and had partially paid the next month’s premium for one plan in advance, the amount due for that next month was calculating incorrectly. This has been resolved, and premium billing amounts due are calculating correctly to account for prepayment of future billing.
MSP Reporting Option Not Displaying for Custom HRA Plans – When editing a custom HRA plan, the MSP Reporting checkbox was not displaying, preventing users from being able to designate a newly-created plan for MSP Reporting if the checkbox was not checked at the time the plan was first created. This has been corrected, and the MSP Reporting checkbox is now displaying on the Edit Benefit Plan screen.
Duplicated Imported Contributions – Contribution files imported into DataExchange were sometimes processing twice despite only having been uploaded once, resulting in duplicate contributions to plans. This has been addressed.
PB Remittance Check Dates – Reissued Premium Billing Remittance checks were incorrectly using the original issue date of the first check rather than the date of the recreated check. This has been corrected, and the reissued checks are issued with the correct date.
Employer CDH Payment Register with Division Options Error – If an overpayment had been processed into a check or ACH file and the payment created date fell within the report’s query parameters, a system error would occur when attempting to run the Employer Payment Register with Division Option report. This has been corrected.
6/3/2025

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025.06.01
chunks.content:
Posted Card Swipes with Decline Codes Not Included in Settlement Pulls – Debit card transactions with decline codes were missing from the Settlement database and failing to be included in the Debit Card Reconciliation report despite appearing on participants’ accounts. This was occurring due to the card system sending a decline reason code of 2 when no decline reason code should have been sent. This issue of false declines has been resolved.
Reports Removed from Data Exchange – The following reports have been removed from the DataExchange Reports list, as they are tied to specific processes and should not be run on demand:
Certificate of Mailing – The Certificate of Mailing report is run from Fulfillment when the sent date is added to the file.

PB Premium Auto Draft Audit Report – The auto-draft report is generated when the auto-draft is approved in Process Approvals.

Employer Subsidy Audit Report – The employer subsidy audit report is generated when a subsidy is edited.
Gas Station Transactions Balance Due on LSA Plans – Transactions at Gas Stations were going Balance Due for LSA Plans due to the holds placed on card swipes. This has been corrected.
Screen Customization Settings – Dashboard – Clicking on the Dashboard link on Screen Customizations would result in a system error. This has been corrected, and users may once again access the Dashboard customizations from Screen Customizations.
Lost/Stolen Card Showing Active – Cards reported Lost/Stolen were reverting to active after the new card request record was created. This has been corrected.
HSA Partner – Previously the partner’s name when setting up partner-integrated HSAs on Summit was shown as “HSATODAY.” The partner for these integrated plans will now appear as DFS [DataPath Financial Services].
Faxes Missing from Unassigned Images – Due to a recent issue, faxes being sent to Summit were not appearing in the Unassigned Images queue. This has been corrected and faxed images are working again.
Categories

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-07
chunks.content:
Release Notes 2025-07
We are pleased to announce the latest release of the DataPath Summit online solution, Release 2025.7.1. This release contains items pushed to production in July 2025. For more information on the Features and Enhancements included in this release, see the July What’s New Guide.
Table of Contents
Features
Enhancements
Issues Addressed
7/29/25
7/22/25
7/15/25
7/9/25
7/1/25
Features
Two-Factor Authentication – We have implemented Two-Factor Authentication to participant login to Participant Portal and the Summit Mobile App. Upon login, participants will be required to enter an additional verification code that may be sent either by SMS to the participant’s phone or by email.
Summit HSA Identity Verification – Summit will now place contributions and distributions in a pending status until the account holder passes the ID Verification check. Until the account holder passes the IDV check, cards will be blocked and distributions will be prohibited. The Participant Account Screen’s Notes tab will include ID Verification notes, indicating the verification status of the participant’s account. Process Approvals | Partner Messages has been updated to include search criteria for Identity Verification Notes.
Enhancements
Ability to Change Tax Treatments and Tax Years of HSA Contributions – Users can now make changes to the tax treatment and tax years of HSA Contribution transactions.
Plan Year Claims Paid by Claimant Report – We have created a report that includes Year-to-Date claims paid per claimant.
Edit Plan Year Start/End Date – Users are now able to edit the earliest Plan Year Start Date and most recent Plan Year End Date for Premium Billing-Only plans. An audit report is available which will display a list of affected participants.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-07
chunks.content:
Bank Routing Number Metadata – We have updated the bank metadata with the most recent set of banks and their respective routing numbers to reflect changes and acquisitions throughout the banking industry. This will address discrepancies and ambiguities some participants may have encountered when entering routing numbers on the Participant Portal.
Issues Addressed
7/29/25
Individually Rated Retired and Direct Bill Coverages Failing to Create Billing When Imported – Imported Retiree and Direct Bill coverages that were individually rated were failing to create billing periods for the enrolled participant. This has been corrected.
Secondary Participants Not Removed from Participant Listing – When certain Qualifying Events occur that entitle dependents to their own separate election, Summit will split these dependents off and create their own independent participant records. However, undoing the coverage action that would have created and split off these secondary participants was not removing these accounts from the Participant list. This has been addressed and undoing the coverage action that created secondary participant records for eligible Qualified Beneficiaries will now also remove the secondary participant entry records from the participant list.
Edited Claims Not Going to Transaction Review – If a claim that was previously marked for review was later edited, the system would update the claim’s review status to “pending” and the claim would not be sent to Transaction Review for subsequent approval. This has been corrected, and claims that were designated for Review will be sent back to Transaction Review for subsequent approval if they are edited at any point.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-07
chunks.content:
Contribution Import Response Files – Contribution Import Response files were incorrectly reporting that there were Invalid Contribution Amounts even though the contribution import was successful. This has been addressed, and the response file will no longer show failed/validation messages for successfully imported contributions.
Entity Comm Including Non-Repository Email Settings – Certain General Settings were available for selection in the TPA Report Repository section of Entity Communications that should not have been available. This has been corrected, and only Report Repository-relevant General Settings are available for selection in Entity Communications.
Certificate of Mailing Address – The Address Order was not displayed correctly on Certificate of Mailing documents. The City was displayed before the street address. This has been corrected.
7/22/25
Broker User Search – The global search was not finding broker users correctly. TPA users whose employer access was configured to “All now and in the future except selected ones” were unable to find broker users from the global search bar (they were still able to find users within the Administrator Settings | Users search tools). This has been addressed, and the global search bar is returning broker username results.
Paid Through Dates Showing Incorrectly – Paid Through dates were erroneously shown on the participant’s Billing tab as being prior to the Billing Star Date for the first billing cycle when no premiums had been paid. For example, if billing began on 03/01/2025, the Paid Through date was displayed as 2/28/2025 even if no payments had been made. This erroneous paid through date was also being included in reporting that pulled Paid Through Date data. This has been corrected, and the Paid Through date will appear as “N/A” if no payment has been made yet.

chunks.title: Release Notes 2025-07
chunks.content:
Participant Account Balance Report – Plans were listed twice in the Participant Account Balance Report if there was a pending plan change with a future effective date. This has been corrected.
7/15/25
Process Approvals – Participant Receipts – Employer users were able to view the unapplied receipts of participants associated with other employers in process approvals. This has been addressed.
7/9/25
Recurring Payment Premium Billing Receipts Applying to Same Billing Period – An issue occurred in circumstances when a participant made a manual premium billing payment immediately after setting up recurring payments online. This scenario would result in the first recurring payment and the manually entered payment both applying to the same billing period, which would cause a negative balance due for premiums. This has been addressed, and if multiple payments are made, the first payment to process will apply to the currently outstanding billing period and the second payment to process will apply to subsequent billing period.
7/1/25
Reimbursement Date Changed to Payment Date on Participant Portal – The Participant Portal view of Transaction Detail has been updated to change the “Reimbursement Date” to display as “Payment Date” to better reflect the participant’s understanding of the process (i.e., the payment of the claim). No other change has been made, and this field still displays the date the reimbursement was created.
Online Enrollment Error – A system error would occur when attempting to approve participant PB enrollments in Process Approvals. This has been corrected.
Categories

chunks.title: Summit Premium Billing - Sample File Layouts & Import Reference
chunks.content:
This document provides reference information for importing data into Summit Premium Billing.
It covers file layouts, required fields, sample data, import codes, and lookup values.


## PB Importing Basics
(17 rows x 18 columns)

General Importing Information:
•  File Type must be selected which determines the purpose of the Import (EX: PB Import)
•  File Format must be selected (Comma Delimited is most common and can be created in Excel as a .csv file)
•  When using comma delimited files, all commas should be removed from the file (Find and Replace with 'blank')
•  Date Format must be selected (YYYYMMDD works well with .csv documents as leading zeroes do not work well)
•  Data Elements can be ordered as needed provided that the final data element of each row is populated
•  File name prefix must match the name of the template followed by an underscore and unique suffix (EX: StandardTemplate_XXXXXXX)
•  Employer Custom ID or Employer System ID are mandatory
PB-Specific Importing Information:
•  Employees and Dependents are imported on the same file with one dependent per row; the number of rows will be determined by the number of dependents
•  PPT Custom ID and Dependent Custom ID values are mandatory
•  Same as Participant Address Y or N field should be populated to import dependent records; If 'N' is entered dependent address fields should be populated
•  Dependent Qualifying Events will require that the new primary be imported as the Employee with the employment status of "Non-Employee" (11)
•  Importing coverages requires that rows are included with each dependent that should be enrolled using the appropriate Action and Reason Codes from the Import Code Matrix
•  Multiple coverages are to be listed on separate rows; the number of rows will be contingent upon the number of dependents to be assigned

chunks.title: Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
chunks.content:
Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
This guide is applicable when selecting the “Tiered Funding” Coverage Type option.  It is in this “Coverage Tiers” section that funding amounts, carry over values, deductibles, and limits are configured for a plan.  These are common attributes of HRA plans.  It is important to note that not all attributes will be applicable to each HRA plan that is built.  Populate only those fields that are necessary and leave those that don’t apply as blank.  (EX: First Dollar HRAs do not require deductibles to be met, so those fields are irrelevant.)
Select the Tiered Funding option from the Coverage Type dropdown menu.  The Coverage Tiers link will appear.
Required Fields
Tier Name – (Required) Naming convention used to identify a tier; this is the value that we be selected when assigning coverage to a member; can be configured globally or created independently at the plan level
Tier ID – (Required) Unique value used to identify a tier value; this is the value to be used when importing enrollments
Funding Amount – (Required) Total value of the plan tier; this is the total dollar amount that can be paid out during the plan year (minus any carry over dollars)
Carry-over
Plan Year Carryover Cap – (Optional) Amount indicating the limit of unspent dollars during a plan year that can be carried over to the next plan year
Accumulated Carryover Cap – (Optional) The Accumulated Carryover Cap acts as a limit on the total accumulation of carryover funds for all plan years preceding and including the selected plan year. The Accumulated Carryover that is carried over into the following plan year will not exceed the selected plan year’s Accumulated Carryover Cap value.
Default Tier
Default – (Optional) An indicator that allows Summit to pre-select a tier value when assigning coverage to employees; Note:  the tier selection can be overridden when assigning coverage
Deductibles

chunks.title: Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
chunks.content:
Family Deductible – (Optional) Total value of claims submitted by members in a family unit that must be reached prior to any reimbursements from the plan; *Note:  Serves as a cap for the total amount accumulated when used in conjunction with Individual Deductibles
Individual Deductible – (Optional) Total values of claims submitted by an individual that must be reached prior to any reimbursements from the plan
Ind. Ded. Per Family Member – (Optional) Indicates that each covered family member must accumulate claim values equal to the value entered in the Individual Deductible field prior to any reimbursements from the plan
No. of Ind. Deductibles – (Optional) Indication of the number of covered family members that must accumulate claim values equal to the value entered in the Individual Deductible field prior to any reimbursements from the plan; Note:  Ind. Ded. Per Family Member box must be deselected
Aggregated Ded. Amount – (Optional) Aggregate total amount of claims submitted by remainder of family members once a single Individual deductible is met
Limits
Embedded Limit Amount – (Optional) The total value of reimbursements allotted to each covered family member. (E.g. Claimant Reimbursement Limit)
Service Category Limits – (Optional) Limits that can be configured to cap reimbursements per service category (EX: medical, dental, etc.)
Family Maximum Out of Pocket – (Optional) Aggregator that combines the total value of claims submitted, copays, and coinsurance* for the entire family.
* Note: Coinsurance is applicable when combined with per family member deductibles)
Claimant Maximum Out of Pocket – (Optional) Aggregator that combines the total value of claims submitted, copays, and coinsurance* for each individual family member.
* Note: Coinsurance is applicable when combined with per family member deductibles)
Coinsurance

chunks.title: Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
chunks.content:
Adding Coinsurance – (Optional) Add coinsurance values to a tier by expanding the details of that tier.  Additional Bands can be added which require dollar amount ranges and plan vs. participant responsibility to be entered.
Make Coinsurance Consistent Across Tiers – (Optional) Applies coinsurance values to all tiers; eliminates the need to configure coinsurance values for each tier independently
Coinsurance Accumulator – (Family vs. Individual)
Family Coinsurance – When this option is selected, the benefit’s coinsurance will be accumulated and summed for the participant and the dependents that are enrolled in the benefit. This option will be selected by default. When the Family Coinsurance maximum is met, all claims are paid at 100% until the maximum benefit value has been reimbursed. (E.g. a single/aggregated coinsurance)
Individual Coinsurance – When this option is selected, the benefit’s coinsurance will be accumulated separately for the participant and for each dependent enrolled in the benefit. When the Individual Coinsurance is met, claims submitted by the individual that has met their coinsurance threshold will be paid at 100% until the maximum benefit value has been reimbursed. (E.g. per claimant coinsurance)
**Note – The options above are configurable on the main “Add Plan” screen for plans that are “Level Funded” as opposed to “Tier Funded”.  Enable attributes in order to display the text boxes.

chunks.title: Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
chunks.content:
Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
This guide is applicable when selecting the “Tiered Funding” Coverage Type option.  It is in this “Coverage Tiers” section that funding amounts, carry over values, deductibles, and limits are configured for a plan.  These are common attributes of HRA plans.  It is important to note that not all attributes will be applicable to each HRA plan that is built.  Populate only those fields that are necessary and leave those that don’t apply as blank.  (EX: First Dollar HRAs do not require deductibles to be met, so those fields are irrelevant.)
Select the Tiered Funding option from the Coverage Type dropdown menu.  The Coverage Tiers link will appear.
Required Fields
Tier Name – (Required) Naming convention used to identify a tier; this is the value that we be selected when assigning coverage to a member; can be configured globally or created independently at the plan level
Tier ID – (Required) Unique value used to identify a tier value; this is the value to be used when importing enrollments
Funding Amount – (Required) Total value of the plan tier; this is the total dollar amount that can be paid out during the plan year (minus any carry over dollars)
Carry-over
Plan Year Carryover Cap – (Optional) Amount indicating the limit of unspent dollars during a plan year that can be carried over to the next plan year
Accumulated Carryover Cap – (Optional) The Accumulated Carryover Cap acts as a limit on the total accumulation of carryover funds for all plan years preceding and including the selected plan year. The Accumulated Carryover that is carried over into the following plan year will not exceed the selected plan year’s Accumulated Carryover Cap value.
Default Tier
Default – (Optional) An indicator that allows Summit to pre-select a tier value when assigning coverage to employees; Note:  the tier selection can be overridden when assigning coverage
Deductibles

chunks.title: Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
chunks.content:
Family Deductible – (Optional) Total value of claims submitted by members in a family unit that must be reached prior to any reimbursements from the plan; *Note:  Serves as a cap for the total amount accumulated when used in conjunction with Individual Deductibles
Individual Deductible – (Optional) Total values of claims submitted by an individual that must be reached prior to any reimbursements from the plan
Ind. Ded. Per Family Member – (Optional) Indicates that each covered family member must accumulate claim values equal to the value entered in the Individual Deductible field prior to any reimbursements from the plan
No. of Ind. Deductibles – (Optional) Indication of the number of covered family members that must accumulate claim values equal to the value entered in the Individual Deductible field prior to any reimbursements from the plan; Note:  Ind. Ded. Per Family Member box must be deselected
Aggregated Ded. Amount – (Optional) Aggregate total amount of claims submitted by remainder of family members once a single Individual deductible is met
Limits
Embedded Limit Amount – (Optional) The total value of reimbursements allotted to each covered family member. (E.g. Claimant Reimbursement Limit)
Service Category Limits – (Optional) Limits that can be configured to cap reimbursements per service category (EX: medical, dental, etc.)
Family Maximum Out of Pocket – (Optional) Aggregator that combines the total value of claims submitted, copays, and coinsurance* for the entire family.
* Note: Coinsurance is applicable when combined with per family member deductibles)
Claimant Maximum Out of Pocket – (Optional) Aggregator that combines the total value of claims submitted, copays, and coinsurance* for each individual family member.
* Note: Coinsurance is applicable when combined with per family member deductibles)
Coinsurance

chunks.title: Summit Plan with Tiered Funding Guide
chunks.content:
Adding Coinsurance – (Optional) Add coinsurance values to a tier by expanding the details of that tier.  Additional Bands can be added which require dollar amount ranges and plan vs. participant responsibility to be entered.
Make Coinsurance Consistent Across Tiers – (Optional) Applies coinsurance values to all tiers; eliminates the need to configure coinsurance values for each tier independently
Coinsurance Accumulator – (Family vs. Individual)
Family Coinsurance – When this option is selected, the benefit’s coinsurance will be accumulated and summed for the participant and the dependents that are enrolled in the benefit. This option will be selected by default. When the Family Coinsurance maximum is met, all claims are paid at 100% until the maximum benefit value has been reimbursed. (E.g. a single/aggregated coinsurance)
Individual Coinsurance – When this option is selected, the benefit’s coinsurance will be accumulated separately for the participant and for each dependent enrolled in the benefit. When the Individual Coinsurance is met, claims submitted by the individual that has met their coinsurance threshold will be paid at 100% until the maximum benefit value has been reimbursed. (E.g. per claimant coinsurance)
**Note – The options above are configurable on the main “Add Plan” screen for plans that are “Level Funded” as opposed to “Tier Funded”.  Enable attributes in order to display the text boxes.
